DayZ was a game concept that really sparked my imagination. I put nearly 700 hours into this game before installing it, so was it worth the money? Hell, yes. Ultimately though, I lost interest in the game. Looking back, I can put this down to two main reasons...
The first is that there was not enough players on the map. The crux of the game is that encounters with other players are exciting because they are infrequent, after all, this is a desolate post apocalyptic land, right? But a maximum of 40 players meant encounters were just TOO infrequent for my liking. Because of this, many players are just hanging around the same old towns on the coast. When travelling inland and exploring the vastness of the map, it is quite common to go hours without encountering anybody, which, after a while, can get, well.... boring. The developers did eventually increase the maximum sever population to 50, which brings me onto the second reason that I uninstalled...
The development of the game in fundamental areas was taking too long for me, and made me lose optimism that the game would ever be completely finished to my satisfaction. The general consensus is that if you raise these complaints, you are likely to get shot down with comments like "It's alpha, you knew what you were buying into, so what do you expect??" and "The point of alpha is not to fix anything, it's just to add the enhancements. Bug fixing is for beta!!"
But these statements become flawed when you look at the details. The fact is that Bohemia ARE issuing bug fixes with every patch despite it being in alpha. But is it a lot of simple bug fixes usually. What they are NOT doing is showing competence to fix the major issues. The 2 big issues for me are performance and persistence. Despite multiple cryptic "performance enhancement" change logs, the fact is that the 50 man servers run like dogs and show no improvement whatsoever. Lag is so bad that combat is often compromised so that it is more of a luck fest. Which is frustrating to die like that after wandering around for hours not seeing anybody! Also persistence. Bohemia started to introduce persistence integration around 9 months ago. Since then there has been one bug after another, so much so that even today persistence is being switched off with the new patches due to bugs.
All of this, together with the new focus on console development, leaves me very skeptical about the abilty of the developers to fix the core issues in a timely and competent manner. Bohemia have issued a timeline on when they expect the game to go into beta stage and when it will be completed. Looking at the sheer amount of bugs and major engine issues that the game suffers with at the moment, I would probably say that they should be doubling that timeline and then adding another half to be anywhere close.
A great game that spawned a wave of clones. Just a shame that the development cycle was so frustrating for me.  If they could only fix the performance problems and be able to offer 75 or 100 man servers. Then we would have a map which is sparsely populated enough to be immersive, but also raise the encounters across the map, which would be much more fun in my opinion.

It is hard to talk about this game without spoiling too much, but it definitely went viral for a reason.
The music, characters, and bullet hell turn based combat system are amazing and I would easily play this game for those reasons alone. But what really makes this game shine is its story, and how the game changes according to how you play it.
There are two major paths, Pacifist or Genocide. They feel COMPLETELEY different, changing events and the world drastically. The game truly makes you feel the path you are taking. Doing a Genocide run after the Pacifist path is a trip, and may not be for the faint of heart.
Note that the game knows what you did, even if you load a previous save.
I loved playing this game, and I would highly recommend it. Definitely go for the extreme endings to get a true feel for it. There are a few spoiler free guides that you can use to get a gist of each path if you need.

Posting this now that I have the same amount of time played on Rust as I do on DayZ (7 hours).
I compare the two because they are similar in their survival aspects, although totally different in many regards.
Pros for Rust:
1) Unlike DayZ, the devs have made what appear to be constant improvements. I have friends that have played both at start up and where as DayZ was better 2 years ago than it is now, Rust is not. Rust devs continue to add new content and make improvements.
2) Lots of stuff to do. For me, there was no progression in DayZ. You spawn, you find stuff, you shoot people and die. With Rust there is base building, blueprint gathering, resources, there is always something you should be doing.
3) Stability. Compared to DayZ, Rust is a triple A game. I have only had a few moments where my lag spiked. I haven't fallen through any floors (yet). I haven't dropped 2 feet from a set of stairs and broken my legs (DayZ).
Cons:
1) Sometimes the animals bug out.
Pretty fun game. Do not waste your money on DayZ like I did when you can play this game which is cheaper and 1000% better.

After the most recent patch playing Dayz has gotten much harder, but there are some good things from this patch:
-After 8 hours of searching I have yet to find a box of Mosin or SKS ammo
-Melee weapons are useless against zombie
-Zombie are incredibly fast and strong now and must be killed with guns or locked into buildings.
-Simple loot like weapon cleaning kits and sewing kits are almost impossible to find, but completely needed now that zombies are super strong.
-Loot could respawn a little quicker, but make military loot less abundant
-hunting is now more important than ever.  Hunting use to be ignored, but now it is more important due to the decreased amount of food found.
-The coast isn’t the only place people go now.  Inner towns and cities use to be dead, but now that central loot has been implemented the inland towns are getting more traffic.
- Some ammo like .307, .380, .45 ammo still can be found fairly easily.
-You no longer can go from being a new spawn to Rambo in 20 minutes of looting.  Loot being scarcer makes the game more survival based and not just a coastline camp fest.
-Although zombies are too strong, they are now actually something that needs to be watched out for when looting.  Not like before where zombies were no issue at all and were easily ignored.
-Go inland
-High Traffic areas = low loot   Low Traffic = high loot
-Dusk and early morning is best server time to loot.  Zombies have a harder time seeing you
-Crouch around zombies they are less likely to agro due to new stealth UI
-Loot every building (I have found the best loot in the smallest buildings)
-Carry a knife, water purification tablets and seeds in case you need to hunt farm or fill your water bottle from a pond.
Enjoy playing and I will see you all in Chernarus.

Undertale is a great game and I absolutely recommend it. The game deals with morality in games in a new way. Without spoiling too much, this game is very different from traditional RPGs in that for every encounter in the game, you can resolve the fight peacefully or violently. Which resolution you pick changes your experience greatly.
In terms of gameplay, Undertale uses a simplified of traditional RPG combat. Instead of learning new moves to attack with, you find new armor and weapons to boost your ATK or DEF. When an enemy attacks you, you have the chance to avoid damage not by RNG but by a bullet hell-esque situation where you literally must dodge the attacks.
This game is much better when played without prior knowledge so instead of continuing to write a review, I'll just recommend that you play it. It really is a great game and is definitely worth playing.

Undertale is a great game and I absolutely recommend it. The game deals with morality in games in a new way. Without spoiling too much, this game is very different from traditional RPGs in that for every encounter in the game, you can resolve the fight peacefully or violently. Which resolution you pick changes your experience greatly.
In terms of gameplay, Undertale uses a simplified of traditional RPG combat. Instead of learning new moves to attack with, you find new armor and weapons to boost your ATK or DEF. When an enemy attacks you, you have the chance to avoid damage not by RNG but by a bullet hell-esque situation where you literally must dodge the attacks.
This game is much better when played without prior knowledge so instead of continuing to write a review, I'll just recommend that you play it. It really is a great game and is definitely worth playing.

I finally bought Undertale about a week ago and managed to finish the game all the way to the True Pacifist ending and... wow... what a journey.
I had read about Undertale about a month ago and was becoming intrigued by its concept. As many who've also read about it and/or played it, this is a game that gives the player the choice to either befriend your "enemies", or kill them off like one usually would do in most games. While playing through the game sparing every monster, it surprised me to see how, what at first is presented to you as an enemy, after coming to terms, can be seen as a friend. With characters such as
, you don't perceive it, but with
, who's a character that despises humans and upon your encounter with
wants to kill you, it was surprising and rewarding.
The big surprise though actually came near the "ending". When finally I thought I would spare
, everyone's favorite sunflower popped up and after finishing him off, when I saw the game close... I was (1) unsettled, (2) freaked out; but despite this I had to open it up again. What a surprise it was to be greeted in a way that felt like the very game was talking directly to me; directly to the player. And then... the psychological scar. I was not ready to see a boss like that. Not only was its attacks hard to evade, but its sight also had me on edge (I couldn't sleep that night D: ).
Once overcoming that challenge, yet feeling like I missed something, the game presents you with a chance to go all the way to the true end (if you're doing true pacifist run of course). Here's where one learns of the remaining part of the plot and it's one filled with revelations, but most of all emotions. The feels after the final battle were cathartic and it made me feel good having spared all the monsters and seeing them enjoy their lives on the surface.
I admit I spoiled myself checking up on the genocide run and, reading how the gameplay changed all the way to the ending felt almost as if I was reading about a different game. The true pacifist ending was enough to convince me that that was the way to finish the game. Reading on the genocide convinced me even more that true pacifist was the way to go.
Thanks Toby Fox for this video game masterpiece! :D The moral lesson is well taught.

This is the ultimate survivalist experiance. F*ck H1Z1, that game is for kids and streamers. DayZ is for people looking for a challenge, people looking for something else. Although there have been many patches fixing certain glitches. It might take a while until it's finished.
I personally liked the game very much. But after a while you start to notice the bugs, the glitches and so on. The 20 hours i have i sort of the limit on how much i could play. Although i didn't stop enjoying the game, i simply couldn't take spawning in the middle of nowhere with no map, no way of making markers (Like in the old game on ARMA 2) and especially the world/server hopping. This game is far from finished by still ahead of any other game on the early access part. Further more, the game was not ment to be finished in a day. They strive for perfection, not "almost finished" like H1Z1 or other competitors. It's true that you might end up dying a lot, and not meeting many people, but when you do, you don't just run up to them like in the other games, you hide, observe and you might both just have found a friend to survive the hellish nightmare that you both are stuck in.
The other competitors might have the finished product and the player base. But when this game releases, it's gonna wipe the floor with everything else, even though it might seem far away. The game itself contains with a lot of features already, you might end up running through the forest with only a flashlight, or you might be running through a city with a fierce helicopter behind you. Now with the vehicles update a lot more players have decided to join the "Battlefield" and it's been a lot of more active servers with kindhearted people, not just loot-leechers.
I personally would recommend the game to any gamer that wants a challenge, a place to explore, a place to thrive and the obvious, find odd friendships.

Ah Rust. As we all know, steam is very much oversaturated with survival crafting mmo's. however, Rust is by far the most immersive and rewarding experience i've had so far. the game in and of itself is pretty simple. harvest, craft, build, survive. while harvesting and exploring are two fun yet critical components in the game, pvp is inevitable, and is in fact a primary staple of the game. Pvp is the reason for the game's intense difficulty and the sense of panic and paranoia when you know you're being stalked from afar.
In truth, the game is what you make it. the beautiful visuals and environment makes playing for immersion possible. sometimes you just want to get by in your little shack that you've outfitted with spikes and traps and a balcony that you stand guard at defending your home with a bow and arrow. or perhaps you're the type that enjoys banding together with a small gang of raiders armed with revolvers and bone armor, going base to base, busting down walls with your preciously scarce c4 you spent forever crafting. or hell, maybe you're a clan guy, belonging to a large heavily armed compound nestled in a valley rich in resources, keeping your phone close by in case you get a text while you're offline saying that your clan's fortress is getting raided by a rival clan and they need you online now.
just remember, you will rage after losing your base that you spent 3 real life days building. every time you get raided, learn from it. adapt, grow, and improve. its a man eat man world, literally, and you'll realize that after you watch yourself become the manhunter you never thought you'd be.

Undertale;
A game stylized to fit the classic RPGs of the Super Nintendo days. Games similar to Earthbound, Final Fantasy, Mario RPG, the lists go on for a long while, but I will say it flat out.
Undertale fits into a pile of genres, be it classic RPG, adventure/Point&Click, even platformer, and puzzle at many points. But what is the most important isn't the game designs, elements, and sounds.
It's the content.
In Undertale, you play as a Human, uder the name the PLAYER chooses, who has fallen into the Underground, a place where Monsters had long ago been sealed after a war between Humans & Monsters. Through the course of the game, you're met with a handful of choices. Many small, but one large one, that could impact not only the game greatly, but yourself.
Do you befriend the Monsters you meet through your adventure...
Or slay them?
Throughout the beginning of the game, you're taught be a Mother-Figure, to love all those you meet, treat them kindly, with respect, and to never give in to anger. Most importantly, of all of those; Stay Determined.
With these words, you're taken from the world you fall into, and explore further into the Underground, seeking a way to escape the caverns of the Monster's home, to the Surface to live happily with other Humans, or to find a way to bring peace to the Underground, and stay with the Monsters who you have met along the way.
Many characters each having their own flaws, features, and ideas.
Some simply wanting to share their friendship with others, keep them happy.
While others wish to destroy the Humans, which have caused their kind pain in the past.
But as long as you stay DETERMINED, you will make it through, and gain some friends along the way.
With each friendship, you will learn what each character you meet have on their minds, what haunt them, their sorrows, joy, and love.
Just what makes the character them. Each having their own drastically different ideas and personalities.
It will be hard not to get attached to each one as you go along with the story.
As the ramble I have posted is a bit off-topic, it still stands. I would HIGHLY recommend Undertale to everyone.
Be it from the simple "RPG Nerd", to the "Next-Gen Gamers". This game will appeal to almost everyone, if you give it a try.

This game is multiplayer. It's incredible how many people seem to forget that while playing. Rust is the first and only survival game I've ever played. It was hard at first adjusting to the new gameplay, along with the glitches I had to learn through, but now it's one of my most played games. I've made a ton of friends and haven't been this entertained by a game like this for years. You have to either have friends to play with or be prepared to play at a disadvantage. But one of the best things about this game is that even if you start out solo you can make friends and alliances and as long as you dedicate time to the game you'll do just fine. Hackers are still a bit of a problem, though just about any game will have hackers. And if you rage or get salty easily or have issues with losing things, this may not be the game for you. One of the most difficult things to get used to is when you die, unless you can get back to your body and loot it then your♥♥♥♥♥♥is gone. You learn by losing, you learn by being killed and getting raided and glitches killing you. The best way you're gonna learn is by mistake, so get ready for some infuriating moments, just remember it's still in alpha. Though one thing this game does really well is player interaction. While a lot of people will run around and just kill people, or just farm and hide in base, don't be surprised if a group of nakeds run up to you and start screaming for their gods to smite the armored one. Or if you're trying to raid a base and the defenders end up being able to do nothing but throw grenades out the window and chant for the greak Helk to save them.  The player interaction in this game is unlike any other game I've ever played, it's amazing to see how people react to others in relaxed and extreme circumstances. If you can play a game without raging at every loss and learn to adapt, then I absolutely reccomend this game.

After four playthroughs and all three routes done, I can finally review this game.
If you've been on the internet at all the past couple of months you've heard of Undertale and its praise, aswell as its comparions to other RPGs such as Earthbound, which I have yet to play. Now, I can't say anything about the comparisons, but Undertale fully deserves the praise it has gotten. While not the best game I've ever played, it's surely up there.
Pros:
+ The gameplay is unique and never gets boring. despite the fight scenes getting repetitive they manage to be different each time.
+ The soundtrack is AMAZING. Many of the themes are remixed versions of each other, for example: CORE and Death by Glamour. Many songs tell a lot about the situation and character, such as Heartache and ASGORE.
+ The jokes are great. Some would say otherwise, but it really depends on your sense of humor.
+ Everything you do matters. Your choices change the ending and the game remembers everything you do.
+ A well written storyline with multiple paths. The game doesn't try to force you to feel anything, it actually makes you feel. Many other games try way too hard to evoke emotion. "PRESS F TO PAY RESPECTS"
+ The characters are amazing. They all have unique personalities and dialogue. The sprites, both overworld and battle, are well made. All the main NPCs are extremely memorable, one example being Papyrus.
+ The controls are simple and tight.
+ Really good and rewarding boss fights. The Neutral and No Mercy final bosses are some of my favorites. Do not search them up to avoid spoilers.
Cons:
- The player character's design clashes with the artstyle A LOT. I get that Toby wanted to make them gender ambigious, but the fact that the sprite is terrible and so emotionless doesn't help. We have all these unique and colorful sprites and then there's this stupid yellow blob walking around going -_-. "Woah that fish is trying to kill me... -_-"
- While I like how the game remembers your choices from previous runs, many people like to start from scratch.
- The beginning, while not bad, is slow and boring, and can cause a lot of people to stop before Snowdin.
- The community. While it's not the game's fault, and it's not the worst out there and not as bad as others such as FNAF, it still detracts from the game because you almost don't want to talk about in public because of how bad it's becoming.
- Zero settings. While graphic options aren't needed in this game, I'd love to change up the volume.
Final Verdict:
Undertale is one of the best RPGs I've ever played and one of the best games in general.
I have to give it a 10/10. If you haven't, play it now, and hope you go in blind.

Well, I managed to wait a few months, unspoiled, until I played Undertale, and honestly, I was surprised.
Gameplay-wise, the game is an old-school 16-bit-look-alike RPG blended in with bullet hell elements. If you don't like bullet hells, I will note that the difficulty might scale a bit too high for the people who want to fully complete the game.
The bullet hell element is present in the combat section of the game, in which you will muck about plenty. The combat options, as will be presented very early on in the game, will give you chances to complete fights peacefully.
The soundtrack is inspired by the SNES-era games, and it's fairly competent to be listened to even outside the game. If you purchase the soundtrack, my only gripe is that some pieces are too short, and sometimes, some are just there ... just because. Like some other backtracks. For example there is a track with an elevator-esque noise for 20 seconds; if you're an elevator noise fan, there's the track just for you!
I don't have much to complain about the overall sound design, the only element which slightly annoyed me was a waterfall effect repeating too much in one of the rooms; but that's about it, one room out of a few hundreds.
The game offers a number of endings depending on your choices, and game elements also change depending on how you "game" the game. This game will twist your senses around, and whenever you think you made a witty move, the game will snap back at you for doing that.
The story is decent, it offers a lot of various characters, from the kind-hearted doof to the overzealous warrior, from the maternal figure to the ditzy scientist, there are enough characters to go along with, and you will probably find a character which you can relate with.
The story is fairly varied, it contains humor, deep aspects, character development, and all the feelings or lack of them you may want.
If you like how the game looks, and are into a change of pace, give Undertale a whirl.
If you dislike how the game looks, but you are into for some challenges, you may also want to try Undertale.
If you don't like how this game looks, and dislike everything I mentioned in this review, give Undertale a try. It's an interesting experience, and it's a shame if you were not to go once fully through it.

Probably one of the most polished survival games available. The devs are very good about updating and fixing bugs. Usually see a new content patch about once and month and bug fixes are quicker than that. If you like survival games you won't be disappointed with Rust. Below are some basic Pros and Cons to the game.
Pro:
Large community - very easy to find someone or a clan/group to play with
Crafting system - over 150 craftable items
Building system - Building system is very inuitive, game forces you to build your base carefuly to avoid being an "easy raid"
No leveling system - No grinding experience
PvP combat - armor and part of the body hit influence damage taken
Modding - Game is very mod friendly
Official servers - many official servers are available for different regions/countries

This game is multiplayer. It's incredible how many people seem to forget that while playing. Rust is the first and only survival game I've ever played. It was hard at first adjusting to the new gameplay, along with the glitches I had to learn through, but now it's one of my most played games. I've made a ton of friends and haven't been this entertained by a game like this for years. You have to either have friends to play with or be prepared to play at a disadvantage. But one of the best things about this game is that even if you start out solo you can make friends and alliances and as long as you dedicate time to the game you'll do just fine. Hackers are still a bit of a problem, though just about any game will have hackers. And if you rage or get salty easily or have issues with losing things, this may not be the game for you. One of the most difficult things to get used to is when you die, unless you can get back to your body and loot it then your♥♥♥♥♥♥is gone. You learn by losing, you learn by being killed and getting raided and glitches killing you. The best way you're gonna learn is by mistake, so get ready for some infuriating moments, just remember it's still in alpha. Though one thing this game does really well is player interaction. While a lot of people will run around and just kill people, or just farm and hide in base, don't be surprised if a group of nakeds run up to you and start screaming for their gods to smite the armored one. Or if you're trying to raid a base and the defenders end up being able to do nothing but throw grenades out the window and chant for the greak Helk to save them.  The player interaction in this game is unlike any other game I've ever played, it's amazing to see how people react to others in relaxed and extreme circumstances. If you can play a game without raging at every loss and learn to adapt, then I absolutely reccomend this game.

I'm probably late in writing a review for this, and it probably won't be seen anyway. Eh, screw it, I'll do it anyway.
What can I say about this game that others haven't already? Probably not much. What I will say is that you don't simply play Undertale; you
it. And it is the best experience I have had from a game in a very long time, quite possibly ever. A combination of interesting gameplay (JRPG/bullet hell), great story, lovable characters, and a fantastic soundtrack managed to suck me in and surprise me with how much I ended up loving this game. Above all else, this game taught me that I am nowhere near as cold and cynical as I imagined myself to be, which actually made me quite happy.
All that said, this game is certainly not for everybody. If you have a low tolerance for the kind of quirkiness and sentiment that comes from the likes of Earthbound and other such things, this game is probably not for you. If you're not into JRPGs, this game is probably not for you. If you prefer your games to be super long with tons of sidequests and other things to do, this game is probably not for you. If you are truly a cold and cynical ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, this game is probably not for you.
For those to who do not fall within those demographics, I strongly urge you to play Undertale. For me it was the best $10 I ever spent, and while I can't say the same for you, I'm fairly certain you will not be disappointed.

Undertale is an amazing game, to put it simply. A Kickstarted project back in 2013, released in late 2015, also (possibly) going through earlier stages of development. After playing Undertale thoroughly and beating every ending, I can write a valid positive review.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
For those who were living under rocks during the duration of late 2015 and early 2016, Undertale is a story-driven RPG  game designed by Tobyfox on the GamerMaker engine.
You play as the 'Human' who falls into an underground world unseen by humans of the modern era. This underground world contains dangerous monsters out for any human who falls into their world. Your goal is to escape, but everything becomes so much more than just trying to get out without missing a leg or a few fingers and toes as you make friends along the way and find out the dark secrets in the reknown game, Undertale.
--------------------------------------------------------------------
The gameplay of Undertale stands out by defining what it means to be innovative with a restrictive but powerful engine, combining Final Fantasy RPG elements with a very unique take on the bullet hell genre. A task accomplished by few game developers.
Although the difficulty of the game is pretty casual, you can't help but try to take on every monster and see what kind of battle you're going to get.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
this is what everybody praises about Undertale, it's exmplary story. I'm not going to lie the story in this game is ♥♥♥♥ing great. Although I was spoiled here and there,
Playing this game without paying attention to the story would certainly leave you with a Butterscotch-Cinnamon Pie with about half of your pie already eaten, and the pie is kind of cold in the center. Personally, I praise the story and would love to see it expanded in future installments.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
What can I say that hasn't already been said about the soundtrack? Undertale's iconic soundtrack couple of new bars and is just flat out awesome. Undertale uses a mix of MIDI and 8-bit/16-bit music to create an wide array of music. The defining soundtracks being the boss battle songs, such as the iconic 'Megalovania' (sans's theme) and the well known 'Hopes and Dreams'
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Undertale uses a 16-Bit graphics and art-style to paint the world around you. Although using the 16-Bit art style does have some of it's drawbacks, it really suits the game entirely and allowed the game to keep in touch with it's simplistic RPG elements and gameplay. Also lets anything, even Android phones (look for the Unofficial fan port to Android), run the game.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
For everything that is holy and pure, avoid it like it's the ♥♥♥♥ing plague. Stay. The. ♥♥♥♥. Away.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Undertale proved games can become reknown for being developed on something so simple like the GameMaker engine with a lot of heart, ethic, and effort in place. Undertale will always have a special place in my library of favorite games, also being more than just a game in some aspects.

I'm probably late in writing a review for this, and it probably won't be seen anyway. Eh, screw it, I'll do it anyway.
What can I say about this game that others haven't already? Probably not much. What I will say is that you don't simply play Undertale; you
it. And it is the best experience I have had from a game in a very long time, quite possibly ever. A combination of interesting gameplay (JRPG/bullet hell), great story, lovable characters, and a fantastic soundtrack managed to suck me in and surprise me with how much I ended up loving this game. Above all else, this game taught me that I am nowhere near as cold and cynical as I imagined myself to be, which actually made me quite happy.
All that said, this game is certainly not for everybody. If you have a low tolerance for the kind of quirkiness and sentiment that comes from the likes of Earthbound and other such things, this game is probably not for you. If you're not into JRPGs, this game is probably not for you. If you prefer your games to be super long with tons of sidequests and other things to do, this game is probably not for you. If you are truly a cold and cynical ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, this game is probably not for you.
For those to who do not fall within those demographics, I strongly urge you to play Undertale. For me it was the best $10 I ever spent, and while I can't say the same for you, I'm fairly certain you will not be disappointed.

A brick is building material used to make walls, pavements and other elements in masonry construction. Traditionally, the term brick referred to unit composed of clay, but it is now used to denote any rectangular units laid in mortar. A brick can be composed of clay-bearing soil, sand and lime, or concrete materials. Bricks are produced in numerous classes, types, materials, and sizes which vary with region and time period, and are produced in bulk quantities. Two basic categories of bricks are fired and non-fired bricks.
Block is a similar term referring to a rectangular building unit composed of similar materials, but is usually larger than a brick. Lightweight bricks (also called "lightweight blocks") are made from expanded clay aggregate.
Fired bricks are one of the longest-lasting and strongest building materials, sometimes referred to as artificial stone, and have been used since circa 5000 BC. Air-dried bricks, also known as mudbricks, have a history older than fired bricks, and have an additional ingredient of a mechanical binder such as straw.
Bricks are laid in courses and numerous patterns known as bonds, collectively known as brickwork, and may be laid in various kinds of mortar to hold the bricks together to make a durable structure.

Alright so, Undertale, lots of hype and LOVE but does it stand up? I went straight into the game with an analytical attitude and the intention to have a good time. In my opinion, yes, it stands up and it stands out for good reasons.
1: The game is clever: The writing, dialogue and humor is fantastic, they did a really good job creating a quirky setting and filling it with memorable characters. Unique in a lot of ways; It's interesting and fun to see how they interact with you as the protagonist and with each other in this bizarre yet fun setting.
2: Save game mechanics: Not going too much into detail here as I'm not trying to spoil the game, but Undertale pulls off some crazy stunts with your game save that I didn't think possible and at times had my jaw drop down and go "Wait, WHAT!?"
3: "Combat": Random encounters and scripted boss fights make up this game's combat system. Once combat has been initiated, the usual RPG Turn based staples appear (Fight, Item, Run Away), but then there's an extra "Act" option. Once selected, "Act" will open another menu with options that vary for every single monster you come across, simple roleplaying options like "Talk, Flex, Sing, etc". The purpose of these actions are to appease and gain favor with your enemy so that you might "Spare" them and end combat without their death. I found these combat sections to be surprisingly fun and had a blast with them as they behave like a puzzle to solve (Assuming you aren't all murdery). This is perfect for people like me as I would prefer to make friends than kill a potential ally.
4: Gameplay: While the actual game itself will last around 8 hours for your first play through, several different endings and secrets easily increase that to an easy 20 hours (At least). It's a pretty fast game with a strong sense of momentum and as you're lost in your enjoyment of the game the ending might feel like it comes quick.
The game has at least two awesome final boss fights (Based on your ending) with their own quirky mechanics that make them memorable. I just unlocked the "True" ending recently and it alone brought my thoughts on the game from the previous default ending of "Yeah, that was really cool, I enjoyed it" to "HOLY CRAP THIS IS AWESOME I LOVE THIS LET'S DO THIS!".....Needless to say, the "True" ending and final fight moved me deeply (I was in tears).
In all honesty, with how the game moved me at the end I find it easy to score this game an 10/10. Granted, I'm not scrutinizing the game over every single little aspect, but it gave me what I wanted, what I didn't even know I wanted, pleasantly surprised me and will stand out as the game with the greatest final boss battle I've ever experienced. LOVE is what this offers and LOVE is all I have in return for it. Take the game for what it is, enjoy it for what it has to offer and chances are, you'll come out smiling too.

Of all the RPG gaming that I've played out there, this game is giving feels and a lot of feels throughout the gameplay. However, this game is like the baby brother of the Mother series. Not to mention that this game takes you on a different route. The road to pacifist or the road of genocide. The genocide part is too ugly, even if you have what it takes to search and destroy until the end, but on that route, Sans will kick your♥♥♥♥♥so badly and he'll try to troll you many times whether you're having a bad time.
On the pacifist route, you needed to be merciful to others because this game is all about problems and solutions. It's like counseling or whatsoever. There are others who wanted to be your friend, and you needed to keep your heart warm, until you'll reach the true ending of this game.
The only character you'll control is a lonely human who wanted to go back to the surface, and your only weapon and armor that you'll depend and to protect yourself is YOUR HEART. Again this isn't Kingdom Hearts, I mean this would literary put yourself to the test to show how merciful and good of a person that you are. It's bonerific to know that your heart is an important thing that you can trust.
But I can tell you this much, but remember: There are many people that can be a good person and a good heart, but there is evil that only lies in the hearts of men.
Choose your own path, and let that path take you forward!
But in any case, I find this game interesting, because you feel like you have a heart inside of you to play this game.

The only character you'll control is a lonely human who wanted to go back to the surface, and your only weapon and armor that you'll depend and to protect yourself is YOUR HEART. Again this isn't Kingdom Hearts, I mean this would literary put yourself to the test to show how merciful and good of a person that you are. It's bonerific to know that your heart is an important thing that you can trust.
But I can tell you this much, but remember: There are many people that can be a good person and a good heart, but there is evil that only lies in the hearts of men.
Choose your own path, and let that path take you forward!
But in any case, I find this game interesting, because you feel like you have a heart inside of you to play this game.

Undertale's uniqueness is one of its biggest strengths (out of many huge strengths.) It is a very story driven rpg that changes up the genre enough to make it fresh again. Overall, it has very few flaws that can come to mind (being just one flaw) and is easily one of the best indie, if not general, releases seen this year. Check it out and feel ready to be determined.

Undertale has so much charm, so much story, so much replay value. This is my review of it.
Graphics:
Apparently most of the graphics were don in paint surprisingly, they are very lo-fi yet charming. I could only liken these graphics to a show like south park, it has its own charm. Though it may not have the graphics of Halo 5 theyre definately charming.
Gameplay:
The gameplay is remiscent of Earthbound and other old-school JRPGs, but the battle system with the dodging is extremely creative and definately holds up. Though the game can be completed under an hour it has high replay value, you'll want to make different desiscions. And sometimes shorter=better, if this had the length of Final Fantasy III noone would be playing it as much.
Story:
You play as a young girl trying to escape the underground, there are so many memorable characters and areas. The ending is very rewarding (no spoils tho)
Soundtrack:
The soundtrack on this one is purely amazing, you can hear it in the backround of "LeafyIsHere's" videos and "Pyrocynical" too. Its amazing chiptune that doesn't get old. Generally I listen to music while playing these games but for this one I wanted to listen, actually no, there was this one time where I listened to "The Weeknd's" "House of Balloons" Mixtape over it (you cant turn off music i think) lets just say it was a unique experience.
Final Verdict:
Undertale is a fun game that reminds us of what games are supposed to be FUN, many games in the past years have just been trying to impress people with their amazing graphics or 5270526758905 hour long gamIteplay but lack in fun. Undertale doesn't have a single flaw, the game isn't too hard, graphics are charming, fun battle system, great story, good message, Sick soundtrack. NOTHING is wrong with this game.

This is going to be odd, but I must say that I liked my time in undertale. The story, characters, and soundtrack are all rather strong. However, even with those points I wouldn't recommend this game because once you've gotten the true pacifist ending, there isn't much in my opinion to go for. Neutral runs don't have much to offer and the genocide run looks boring on account of the grinding. Resetting from square one to chase down a less satisfying ending isn't anything I'd like to do when the gameplay isn't stellar. Gameplay is executed with simple Fight, Act, Items, and Mercy commands. Fight has you time your press for extra damage. Act has you do various things including scanning enemies and actions that lead to sparing an opponent. Item needs no explanation. Mercy has spare and run away. After your turn is up the enemies attack you in a bullethell style minigame to avoid damage with each enemy having their own attacks. The reason I say this isn't great is mostly because once you've got patterns down the game is pretty easy, with exception of some boss fights. Once I did my true pacifist run my desire to play zeroed out because I couldn't bring myself to reset from the best ending just to find out what happens if I kill everyone or just specific characters, especially when I like these characters. In conclusion, Undertale is a great experience, but not one I care to do again. I'd recommend watching others play, that way you can experience the important aspects while being free to do something else too.

Pros:
- Fun game to play with some friends for a few hours a day.
- Intense PVP gunfights.
- Lots of lovely RP opportunities.
- Radtowns and LOOOOOOT.
- A couple interesting PVE encounters (Heli & Bradley APC) - More to come.
- Great building mechanics, easy to learn and use. (probably one of the best in the survival game genre)
- Although some would disagree, the gunplay in this game is pretty decent and easy to pick up.
- Awesome Developers who update every week with new content to play around with.
Cons:
- If you don't have much time on your hands you may have a hard time getting much done in this game without either, your base disappearing or it being raided. Playing in a group is advised.
- Game can be slow at times, framerate can be very inconsistent but if you have a high end PC you shouldn't notice much.
- The community can be VERY toxic. If you are someone who is put off by that then this game is not for you. LOL
-The game can be hard for new players when you are just starting out. There are a few tips ingame to help you out but for the most part it is very hard starting out for the first time, especially if you are solo.
- Survival aspects in this game are not very, "survivaly". There are times where you do feel like you aren't just trying to survive against other people, but that is usually very short lived as you can find food and water easily around the map.
Conclusion:
I don't have as much fun in this game as I used to but maybe that's just because I have played it to death and have become quite bored of its repeatitive nature beyond early game. I still recommend it as it is one of my all time favourite games, and I still look forward for the future of the game.

Dying from glitches/errors/resets/hackers is not acceptable at this point. This game has been too long in development for it to STILL be having these issues.
This game would be my #1 favorite game if they fixed the glitches and the hackers FIRST.
If you want to spend HOURS of your life COLLECTING virtual survival gear only to die the MOMENT you are fully geared out by a GLITCH or a HACKER then this is the game for you.

I absolutely refuse to play this game until these issues are fixed FIRST.

Okay so my last review I felt was a little unfair to the game so honest review time
DayZ: Open world, MMO, Zombie survival game we should all know that by now.
FAQ:
Q: Is it fun?
A: yes at times the game can be fun if you can look past some bugs the game needs to work out, it's not as far as people think from being done, but still has it's glitchy, bug-riddled moments.
Q: Is it worth the $35.00?
A: Honestly no, but with Steam's new refund policy it's now worth giving it a try if it's risk-free to an extent just make sure you play under 2 hours of it then give an opinion.
Q: I want the game but I dont want spend the $35.00 what should I do?
A: Wait for the game to go on sale, then give an opinion, less money is lost this way if you don't like it.
So out of 10 for generic game review catagories here's what I give this game and reasons why;
Gameplay: 6/10 "Game is very addicting at first but once fully geared it can kinda get boring and you'll just end up going to a PvP server and want to murder innocent new-spawns on the coast. Yes this game has bugs, bugs that should have been worked out since before development but what do you expect from a low buget 5 or 6 man team working on a game like this. Yes it's no excuse but thats what trademarks DayZ as a game."
Graphics: 9/10 "If you have a high powered PC then this game will look beautiful in 1080p max graphics not much else to say, good job Bohemia Interactive."
User-Interface friendliness: 7/10 "I'm not a big fan of the new inventory customization system simply because it requires me to drop my gear and put it back on in the order I want it in and that's just too risky for me. But other than that the menus and the inventory is responsive under the circumstance you're not desyncing everywhere and lagging."
Lasting appeal: 4/10 "I'd love to say even with all the hours I have on this game I still play it but really every new patch I play it for a day or two then get bored of the game and wait for something exciting to come out in a newer patch. So for now until base-building, Steam Workshop content, and DayZ Epoch for the standalone come out, this game isn't going to be very appealing to play every day."

So after calculating the scores this game is a 6/10 which is above the margin for me to recommend a game but not enough to say claim this "Game-of-the-year" which is far from what it actually is but is still appealing on some level.

Truly a masterpiece of a game. I don't really know what to say about it other than that.
Pros:
- Great characters, each is extremely unique and individual, even characters that are only in one part of the game. They are all designed very uniquely and look nice.
- A great soundtrack (although what did I expect, this guy did like 75% of the music for Homestuck and the music is the best part of homestuck)

- Interesting gameplay, particularly the fighting method and all that.
Cons:
- A bit lengthier than I was expecting (I read online that it's supposed to be like a 5-6 hour game so that might jut be false data), but that might just be because I'm bad at it and died a lot

- A bit expensive for the hours of gameplay you get out of it, but it's well worth the price. Undertale fit more into 12 hours of gameplay than Skyrim has into 120.
Overall, a fantastic game that will definitly stick with me for a long time. It was an experience that I wasn't expecting (I will admit, with all the hype, I was worried I would be disapointed but no, it is exacly as good as everyone is saying it is), but an experience I needed, if that makes any sense.

I personally never wanted to try this game following its release, I figured a game made by someone who took part in Homestuck kind of bothered me. It was only a matter of time before people would start overcrowding the fanbase of this game with saturated memes and r34 (I guess maybe the r34 isn't that bad, r34 has never ruined anything for me.) The memes would eventually lead up to me judging a book by it's cover (come on, we are all guilty of this at some point.) Though upon the Steam Winter Sale, I decided I should give this game a try.
I didn't like it to begin with, mostly because just about everything I did would remind me of all the memes I saw. The whole determination thing was kind of annoying, and after
I decided to take a break from the game. Frustrated as I was, I began to feel upset as if I haven't given the game a chance.
Upon trying it again I began to really enjoy the game as it has been one of the first times in a long time I have felt attached to the characters. Characters seem very memorable and have personality that can mess with my emotions, which I can last remember happening when I played Pokemon Emerald over 10 years ago. This game is pretty vivid, and has some neat soundtrack that goes along with every move perfectly. Sure it's not the most graphically advanced or has the most awe-inspiring gameplay, but it makes up for that with its intriguing story. Everything just seems right. It does feel like a tribute to Earthbound, but its fresh and anew. It also has the same childhood humor that I grew up with in cartoons, which is another thing I really like about the game. (I am aware that some don't and that's perfectly fine!)
My main goal of this review was more-so to get people who haven't tried this game before to try it. For something so amazing, it's cheap. I can easily say this was one of my favorite games this year. Sure there will be people who pick on this game for having bad gameplay or see it as not advancing the gaming industry, but this goes to proof that retro games can still exist and be just as successful as a highly advanced game. The sad truth is it seems to point out that retro games used to have so much to offer because game developers would focus on adding neat things in there and secrets to make people play the game longer, instead of just dumping their funds to make the graphics as highly advanced as possible. I guess this is controversial to say, but realize it is only my opinion.
I think the least I can give this game is a 9/10, I would go 10/10 but I feel I haven't played the game long enough to give it this review. I am unsure whether it merits any replay value, but I shall play the game again sometime.
Word of advice to people who play this game... DO NOT KILL ANYONE! You will feel bad for doing so.

Undertale is a game for everyone. As an RPG you can experiment with it to get different endings, different banter and different sides of stories. I've played through both the Pacifist and the Genocide playthroughs (despite never finishing the Sans fight). Of course when you finish the game you may get momentarily bored. This happend to me when I finished all paths (except for the Genocide due to ol' Sansy). Because of this I was short of anything to do and I needed some time off to forget about Undertale and then come back to it like a new game for some nostalgic recollection rather than playing it over and over and eventually never playing it again until, what, a year goes past. That tends to happen to all my games.
Other than that, the battles are interesting and the story/content can be sad, funny and even scary at times. It's definitly worth a shot.

The absurd level of hype surrounding this game probably had a part in why I didn't enjoy it. It almost made me continue playing just to find out what all the fuss is about. Admittedly with the amount of games I've yet to try this year I wasn't ready to give Undertale a lot of time to pull me in and since it didn't do it right away, I decided to move on to other games.

While I don't personally recommend the game, it's probably best to try this one out for yourself.

Undertale is a redifining game in the modern game industry, relying on older concepts seen with gems such as Earthbound/Mother. The game itself, while not being the longest, is one of the best story-driven RPGs, maybe even video game I've played in quite a long time. Putting yourself as the lone human to fall into the Underground, the home of monsters, the game does an incredible job of throwing the player between moodswings simply due to the minimalistic things like music, environmental objects, and expression. The game also gives a unique battle system, either giving the player a hostile approach of attacking and gaining EXP, or finishing battles through acting, both of which can give the player entirely different endings based on their decisions to fight, or to act. While giving sheer differences some endings, the main three can be described as following the Genocidal Path, the True Pacifist, and the Neutral (a general mix of both), almost all required to understand the full circle of the pre-game story, as well as whats going on around you in the Underground. Undertale may not be the longest JRPG that's available to the Steam consumer, but it is for sure one of the most promising and charming games that I've played in years for sure. Definitely woluld recommend picking it up while its on sale right now.

The trailer makes Rust look like a PS2 game.  The trailer oversells it.
As soon as you install the game,
, a fact that is not mentioned anywhere in the Steam store page.  If you agree to that, you will be greeted by the Flash wrapper that surrounds the actual game.  If you agree to use the flash wrapper, you will be dropped into a world of mashed potatoes that very roughly reflects a post-apocalyptic earth.
This world of mashed potatoes doesn't have a tutorial, documentation, or even any action other than 'throw your rock away'.  (Literally, that is all you can do by default.  There is a rock in your hands.  You can throw it -
.  Then, it has left your hands and no button of the mouse does anything anymore.)  Yet it has microtransactions to purchase guns
you've already bought this game.  They're good to go on microtransactions.  Man, there are so many microtransactions.
There is an inventory screen ripped off of Minecraft at the bottom of the screen.  However, it is superfluous, seeing as you can't pick up items.
But there is a crafting system.  You will be able to tell this by the sheer number of ten-story-tall swastikas that dot the landscape.  (The $20 early access fee doesn't cover moderation, it seems.)  These swastikas are the only straight lines you'll find in the mashedpotatoverse.
The only thing I can say in this game's favor is that it doesn't have audio chat.
If you're looking for a beautiful survival game, go preorder The Long Dark.  In that game, you can pick things up
use them, two innovations that Rust is not quite ready to tackle yet.

I never review games on Steam but this one I just had to. I didn't expect too much when I got it because I'm pretty cynical when it comes to the quality of games that others recommend but this one just blew me away. It has been one of the most story and choice driven games I've ever played and I just couldn't get enough. To start off, if you do not wanna cry because of a video game, do not buy this. (But buy it anyways, it the experience of tearing up makes the game much better for emotional attachment to certain characters)
If you are interested in Earthbound, Adventure Time, dogs, skeletons, a great soundtrack, and an emotional attachment to fictional characters; this game is perfect for you. To summarise the story, you're a boy/girl (genderless? It doesn't matter) that some how accidentally falls down a sacred hole to the underground where monsters live. Your goal is get out and return to your people. I'll leave it their to not ruin other people's playthroughs. Anyways, the graphics do feel like old SNES era graphics, but is it that bad? The areas, characters, NPC's, and backgrounds have a very nice color scheme to go along with the tone of the game. Besides graphics, the fighting and defence mechanics are extremely unique, which is hard to find in RPG's now a days. The characters are very well detailed and elaborted when going on the lines of personality and identity. The multiple endings and decisions give the games a high replay value as well. Even the soundtrack sounds like the development team actually took a while to cook up. The corky humor, non-repetitive fights, and the world around you as you play is very well executed accompanying everything I stated above.
This game is just beautiful.

In all of my time in gaming i have not seen a game like rust. It a very well executed and put together first person survival shooter. You are placed into an unknown world with just a rock and a torch, and put up against the dangers of wild animals, the elements, and other humans. You must fight and build to survive, growing stronger and stronger as you play more and more. And yet that can all be lost in the matter of seconds, to a few raiders and some c4.
Rust, in my opinion, has paved a new road in gaming. Opening doors for new survival games with its innovative crafting, building, and survival systems. It is a very intricate and fun game, and i would strongly reccomend you purchasing it. Many say that the old rust was better, although many of them only played a few hours of it. Legacy rust was very fun, but the new rust is just as fun, if not even more fun. It has a large space to grow and develope into a phenominal game. And with facepunch, garry, and his team of devs behind this game, i think it will become one of the greatest games of its time.

At first, I thought the game will be boring, another post apocalypse game.
After watching videos, reading about the game and it's features I decided to purchase it along with my friends.
After I started playing (the original Rust game) I got to know it and liked it.
From starting with nothing, building 1X1 "houses" to huge buildings and Complex structures it was a lot of fun.
I loved that there are different kinds of construction parts the difficulty of gathering enough resources to build what I want.
Unfortunely, the variety of wepons in the game was very small from each kind, and although I know it's a survival game, I think there should have been more.
Perhaps I don't have the best PC for gaming but graphics are important to me as equal to the game play itself and in Rust it was really nice, and it just got better from there.
I never hosted my own Rust server but giving the option to decide the settings and options of the game is amazing, you can choose the way you want to play it, whether it will be easy or challenging, short gameplay or a long one.
I have no ideas how to do it in an online open world game but I would love it if there was the possibility to do Quests given by auto-generated NPC's that completing them will grant rewards or something like that.
They don't have to talk but make some "story" side to game which will be some intresting addition to Rust.
After the "new" Rust version which I didn't like was released I stopped playing, my friends too and right now I'm probably not updated with the improvements they made to it but I like the main idea so I do recommend playing the game.

Great idea, bad actions
Rust is a survival game meant to display the actions in which players portray in a hostile wasteland. On its release, Rust found it to be in many gamers hearts, due to its fresh style and play that it brought with it to the gaming world, in fact it inspired many others to develop their own survival games. (H1N1, Unturned, etc) It was new, fresh, and unlike any other game that came before it, but it took an unlikely turn.
The development team decided it was best to scrap the whole game and redo it into a better coded system, which was understandable at the time, but the thing that made Rust, once a fantastic and exciting game, into a kill on sight shooter is the lack of interaction within players. I feel that this game could of been better with a better community that engages with one another instead of killing each other.
What happened to the communities within this game? Ever since the development team decided to scrap the game, I've noticed that many players started to be more hostile to each other, could it be the bigger map, more weapons, lack of interaction between the community and development team, I don't really know. But what I do know is that this once fantastic game, is now just another shooter.

Undertale is "one of those" surprisingly immersive, beautifully-crafted worlds that doesn't give all its cards away at once. I say "one of those", when what I really mean is "it's singlehandedly given an entire genre a much needed sping cleaning".
You've doubtless already heard this before (and if so, what are you doing here, reading this review?) but Undertale is a game best played knowing the least possible about it. Rest assured that it won't disappoint you. Every time you think you've got it figured out - prepare for a curveball or two.

Rust is a great game for two reasons:
I've played this game for a long time, and I've watched it update along the way. At first, the game was great, I really enjoyed it. Then the updates started rolling in, and eventually it just got so boring that I stopped playing it for a long time. I started up again, however, and it is great again. This is because the developers are constantly listening to the community on things that they like/don't like. They should be role models for Valve and other game companies on working with the community.
The only thing to complain about is getting raided, and how when you're offline someone can just take your base without ever putting up a fight. On most Minecraft factions (yes, I know, Minecraft is stupid and for kids), to raid someone's base, you first have to kill them lots of times to get their rating down or something like that. Basically, for someone to raid you, you have to be online. And for a game like Rust this wouldn't make much since, sense Rust is a lot more realistic than Minecraft.
However, Rust has a "backup" to when you get raided and go from 100 to 0 within an hour. This is the blueprint system. If you get killed, raided, and killed again, you can always rely on your Blueprints. Overall it's a great game and I would reccommend it to anyone. It is especially fun if you have a group of friends with which you can make a huge base and rule the server.

Rust is a great game for two reasons:
I've played this game for a long time, and I've watched it update along the way. At first, the game was great, I really enjoyed it. Then the updates started rolling in, and eventually it just got so boring that I stopped playing it for a long time. I started up again, however, and it is great again. This is because the developers are constantly listening to the community on things that they like/don't like. They should be role models for Valve and other game companies on working with the community.
The only thing to complain about is getting raided, and how when you're offline someone can just take your base without ever putting up a fight. On most Minecraft factions (yes, I know, Minecraft is stupid and for kids), to raid someone's base, you first have to kill them lots of times to get their rating down or something like that. Basically, for someone to raid you, you have to be online. And for a game like Rust this wouldn't make much since, sense Rust is a lot more realistic than Minecraft.
However, Rust has a "backup" to when you get raided and go from 100 to 0 within an hour. This is the blueprint system. If you get killed, raided, and killed again, you can always rely on your Blueprints. Overall it's a great game and I would reccommend it to anyone. It is especially fun if you have a group of friends with which you can make a huge base and rule the server.

I fell in love with DayZ when it was still a mod. Times were good, it was new, fresh and people were genuinely interested in exploring and having fun. The zombies gave the game the right amount of tension, and there was always something to do. By do, I mean holding an area, creating a camp or even building a bus!
As a mod it was raw, but fun! 3 years down the track, and it's a standalone game now, very little has changed. It had its problems with griefers, but the main problem now is lack of progress, most of the bugs of the mod have been nicely ported to the standalone. And the game has less readily available weapons, while that may give it a higher level of difficulty, and more realism, it makes for a boring, buggy game.
Overall, it's a trainwreck. Such little progress, in such a large amount of time.
Avoid!

Without a doubt, Undertale has earned its place as a bookmark in gaming history. From its well-designed bullet hell mechanics, to its loveable cast of characters that draw you into a story that proves that you do not need to follow Tolkien in order to introduce fantasy elements into a mainstream audience, and a phenomenal soundtrack that would leave you paralyzed should you be asked to pick your favourite song.
Undertale does have one drawback—while I would argue that the story and characters are loveable, the entire game hinges on the notion that the player
finds them endearing so
if you do not grow attached to the main characters the greatness of the game becomes moot. However, anyone who has ever adopted favourite characters from other story-based games should have the capacity to grow fond of what Undertale has to offer.
Bring your tissues, whether to wipe tears or blood (perhaps someone else's) from your face, and check out Undertale. For what Undertale gives you, the price is a steal.
Edit: btw, I want to lick Asriel

There are so many things to be said about this game but the majority of them would spoil to much.
The best description I could think of is that Undertale is a game that goes out of it's way to try to supvert the expectations of rpg players: At a lot of times for humor, sometimes for drama and at others just to mess with you.
The game is written well, especially character banter. Undertale remembers choices and actions the player takes, changing moments, character reactions, and endings accourdingly.  Sometimes a thing as simple as how many times you petted a specific dog will change a how many snow figures he tries to build shortly after. That change has no plot relavences at all but little touches like that are everywhere and add so much to the charm of the experience.
The only gripe I can think of is that some may find the humor grating on the nervoues. It uses a lot of puns and repetition  based comedy.  On some game routes there is a decent sized chunk of gameplay where the player is consistantly inturupted with phone messages.
These were things that I didn't mind much, being a pun fan myself but I know several who a bit annoyed by those elements.

I fell in love with DayZ when it was still a mod. Times were good, it was new, fresh and people were genuinely interested in exploring and having fun. The zombies gave the game the right amount of tension, and there was always something to do. By do, I mean holding an area, creating a camp or even building a bus!
As a mod it was raw, but fun! 3 years down the track, and it's a standalone game now, very little has changed. It had its problems with griefers, but the main problem now is lack of progress, most of the bugs of the mod have been nicely ported to the standalone. And the game has less readily available weapons, while that may give it a higher level of difficulty, and more realism, it makes for a boring, buggy game.
Overall, it's a trainwreck. Such little progress, in such a large amount of time.
Avoid!

I whole-heartedly recommend this game. However, I must make a point. There is two distinct peronalities that someone can approach this game from. No, I am not talking about two of the commonly associated routes. I am talking about if you like to be nice in video games, or not.
If you like being nice in video games, you will LOVE this game. The story and characters will mean a lot to you, and you will WANT these characters to survive. Also, if you do kill some one, it will carry actual emotional weight. I would go into further detail, but to do so would be spoilers. However, the only thing I might mention that may detract from your experience is the difficulty, but even then, this can be cured (there is an item that acts as an "easy mode" for people that may have trouble, although I would recommend not using it if you can avoid it).
However, if you are the type of person that, in video games, likes to feel like the evil bad guy, you will not like this game. Not only will you not find the game challenging, you will feel like the game is made for the people who try to be nice. I would try to explain in what ways, but again, pesky spoilers. You may play the game, but just know it is not meant for you. You will not get as much out of it as a nice person would.You may even feel like the game's attempts to make You want to be nice annoying. You will not understand the hype surrounding it. There is nothing wrong with that way of playing games. In fact, I would go so far as to avoid it if you only intend to be evil. The one glimmer of redemption lies where you truly want to be nice after being evil. And not just in that "I heard it was a better ending" kind of way, but rather a "I kind of WANT to be nice to them now" way.
Keep in mind, there is a LOT of grey area between these two, but I find these two the easiest to gauge.

Graphics, they looked ok at the start, now it's much better. With the new Enfusion engine, the game is becoming better by the updates. New graphics, new sounds, new loot economy and soon to be new animations.

+ Solid survival gameplay
+ High grade realism
+ Potential for roleplay

I woke up naked on the beach, and started exploring the area around me. I learned to harvest wood and stone to create some basic tools, which made the bolder I started with obsolete. I absolutly love the hemp "pot" plants that grow all over. Too bad it's only usable as cloth. (Note to the devs: maybe you can ad another use for it)
The first thing I did was make some clothes, as it was raining and I was cold. I made a bow & some arrows and got a few wild pigs for food and leather (and cloth) . I came across a dusty road that led be to an airfield.  It was then I noticed there was someone else in the world besides me. Luckily, he was friendly and agreed to show me the ropes.
With his help I quicly learned the basics of building and crafting better items.  By now, I had the Rust bug.
Fast forward a couple of weeks, and I was starting to build a small compound of my own. Again, on a relatively empty server.  I discovered lots of blueprints, built a large furnace and began mining and smelting metal and sulfer. I has a nice stash of goods I had collected over the past couple of days and was feeling pretty good. Then, the unthinkable happened - I was raided. My doors and walls blown up, all my hard earned loot and supplies stolen. The perpetrator left a message on my sign - HI - was all it said.  With that, I rebuilt, added locks and the next day, robbed again - they blew up the box. The last straw, they blew my doors off, and killed me in my sleep.  I know, it's a pvp world out there, but killing someone while they are asleep?? That's just mean.  Now it's time to plot my revenge, as it told me whole killed me while I slept.
I still enjoy playing - it's a blast. And having an enemy beside that damn helicopter makes it more personal.  I now know I need to rebuild in a more secluded area.  I'll be waiting for you ...
To the Devs, if you are open to suggestions and/or ideas I have plenty.  I'll save that for a diferent post.  I like this game, and I'll keep playing. I say, get it - it is fun, especially if you like killing and crafting.
Happy hunting!

DayZ Standalone is ultimately a disapointing title, the primary reason being the player base. Due to the way the game was developed its similary concern from the get go was being a bandit, mainly because there was nothing better to do. Now anyone who has played the mod will know surviving/being a bandit is just one of the things you can do with your time on DayZ mod, but for at least the first year of the Standalone is was entirely all you could do. This has had the effect of educating the player base into banditry and as such the game is now primarilly Shoot on sight, this makes the game very unforgiving as you can spend an hour gathering gear just to have someone kill you for the sake of it, now i know this is something to expect on DayZ, but when the person is using a shotgun and wont get any real reward from your body as shotguns tend to ruin all loot, this makes the practice pointless. It would be preferable to be held hostage, which at the very least would be entertaining, but due to the bad habits ingrained in the player base it is preferable to kill for the sake of killing, since there is nothing better to do.
The rather unique health system has its drawbacks also, mostly the rather unforgiving food system, your character has to eat constantly to survive, it becomes habit to litterally eat everything in sight, which leaves new spawns struggling to find food and as such dying of starvation within the first half hour of gameplay. This also makes the game unrewarding as despite picking and eating 7 fresh apples my character still starved within half a hour. The game prides itself on realism and i can assure you id not starve to death within 20 minutes of eating a pound of fruit.
Early in development attempts by the studio to stop players switching from server to server looting military caches was implimented, a cooldown on server switching, this has done nothing to stop this particular habit and infact punishes genuine players trying to find a stable server. The developers need to find a means to counter this bad habit that doesnt punish everyone, just those responsible. It would be preferable if your loot was bound to the server you grabbed it on.
Ultimately DayZ standalone fails to even match the mod in any way. While it still is in development and all credit to the studio they do release regular updates, the departure of Rocket(Dean Hall, creator of the mod who litterally took the money and ran) leaves the standalone a poor alternative to the mod or even some of the other survival games out there currently. A unrewarding waste of time

Rust is a survival game created by Facepunch Studios. Inspired by games like DayZ, Minecraft and Stalker – Rust aims to create a hostile environment in which emergent gameplay can flourish. The aim of the game is to survive. To do this the player should gather resources. Hitting a tree with a rock will give you wood, hitting a rock with a rock will give you rock and ore. You can then craft a hatchet from the wood and rock, allowing you to gather faster. You can go out and hunt a variety of wildlife such as boars, chickens, rabbits, bears, wolves and deer. Once you have killed an animal you can butcher it to gather its meat and skin. You can craft a fire using wood and cook the meat inside the fire. Then you can eat. You face two major dangers in game. Rust is a multiplayer game, so there will be other players trying to survive in the same way that you are. Unfortunately for you they can find you, kill you and take your stuff. Fortunately for you – you can kill them and take their stuff. Or maybe you can make friends and help each other survive. Rust’s world is harsh – so you might need to make friends to survive. The environment is not kind. Bears and wolves will chase and kill you. Falling from a height will kill you. Being exposed to radiation for an extended period will kill you. Starving will kill you. Being cold will kill you.

This game is described by the developers as a survival/crafting game and the graphics are absolutely gorgeous but it is so heavily biased towards murdering psychopaths I doubt it will ever be anything but a mass murder simulator. Largely because after two years in Early Access, the developers have shown absolutely no interest in fixing the horribly broken gameplay, which goes like this:
Every few weeks the entire map is reset because the servers can't cope with all the buildings and items hoarded by the first few players who joined. These very first few players who had the time to play non-stop for 20 hours after the last wipe got to hoard some automatic weapons and build inpenetrable fortresses of steel and stone. After this, they spend the next few weeks sniping naked would-be players who try to join the game. See, the established players spawn inside their fortress next to their chest full of armor, weapons and medkits while everyone else spawn naked on a beach holding a rock which will fall apart if you try to hit a tree more than a few dozen times. Collecting wood will ofcourse get you nowhere because you need cloth (which is pretty rare), stone (which is nearly impossible to come by) and animal fat (easiest to obtain by killing yourself) to craft a simple furnace, smelt 100 units of metal which can then be used to craft a combination lock which can be used to lock... well, whatever you would have had to lock if you hadn't been killed a LONG time ago at this point.
Because of this, the game quickly devolves into a bunch of desperate, frustrated naked guys pummeling eachother with rocks instead of "surviving" and "crafting". All of this is accompanied by the inspiring sound of microphone-toting teenage misfits telling you to f**k yourself in poor english while dismembering your corpse with a rock. If you can play this game for a week without completely losing faith in humanity, you simply haven't been paying attention.
