Undertale is a 8Bit-ish stroy based RPG if looked at from an objective perspective.
From a subjective perspective however it is a masterpiece that will blow your mind with plot twists, great characters, kickass music (suck on that, Duck Tales' moon level!) and probably the most unique fighting mechanic any RPG that was created in this century has to offer.
Even though it is very story based, this game still manages to let you control about everything you want to control. You wanna avoid fighting an enemy? DO IT! You wanna goof around and look if anything cool happens? DO IT! You wanna FEEL how everything you do can change worlds? JUST DO IT!
But seriously, here are the PROs and CONs this game has (warning opinion!)
PRO:
- Offers a great, yet somewhat disturbing atmosphere. I guarantee you'll find at least one character you'll LOVE
- As I said, the music is amazing. The only game I ever wanted to by the soundtrack of really badly
- Great fighting mechanic that offers you to do everything the way you want: hostile or peaceful
- A very nice humor (as nice as it gets without breaking the atmosphere of the story)
- Replay value is given, I can almost guarantee you wanna play through it at least twice
- The Story is just amazing, I stopped counting the amazing ideas, plot twist ect... just too many
- There are some backstory hints scattered around the game for theorists to discover
- The only game besides Pokémon Mystery Dungeon that almost made my face leak
- The Puzzles and Secrets are neither too hard nor too easy
CON:
- Pretty short (you can easily end the game in 2 hours without calling it a speed run)

Even though it is very story based, this game still manages to let you control about everything you want to control. You wanna avoid fighting an enemy? DO IT! You wanna goof around and look if anything cool happens? DO IT! You wanna FEEL how everything you do can change worlds? JUST DO IT!
But seriously, here are the PROs and CONs this game has (warning opinion!)
PRO:
- Offers a great, yet somewhat disturbing atmosphere. I guarantee you'll find at least one character you'll LOVE
- As I said, the music is amazing. The only game I ever wanted to by the soundtrack of really badly
- Great fighting mechanic that offers you to do everything the way you want: hostile or peaceful
- A very nice humor (as nice as it gets without breaking the atmosphere of the story)
- Replay value is given, I can almost guarantee you wanna play through it at least twice
- The Story is just amazing, I stopped counting the amazing ideas, plot twist ect... just too many
- There are some backstory hints scattered around the game for theorists to discover
- The only game besides Pokémon Mystery Dungeon that almost made my face leak
- The Puzzles and Secrets are neither too hard nor too easy

This review is  my opinion and my opinion only - sorry if it's not what you'd like to hear.
GRAPHICS
-----------
Yes, graphics of a game are important when judging it by its aesthetics and whatnot - and despite me having some troublesome issues with setting it to high or low; I still find this game quite beautiful. Eye candy if you'd like! There are some performance issues, however, seeing how people say that this game gives them very low FPS on high-end PCs. I am inclined to say that this isn't the case for me, but I do see where they're getting at. It's a CPU intensive game which isn't optimized to the fullest yet.
GAMEPLAY
-----------
A lot of walking, I'll give you that. The gun mechanics are realistic and fun but not as greatly developed as its predessecor; ARMA 2: DayZ. There's zombies, kind of glitchy but are killable - sometimes glitching through you and slicing you, causing you to bleed. The scavenging loot part of this is definetely better than before! It allows you to access the inner-areas of buildings, houses and this time; destroyed cars. Overall I believe this is a great factor that allows this game to be fun, however it does need to get a bit more upgrades...*cough* Zombies *cough*.
DEVELOPEMENT
-----------------
While the two above are great categories to sit this game into, this however isn't. It grows slowly, even more so then when Rocket ( Dean Hall ) left the making of this game. It has been over a year and yet barely any progress. Step up your game, DayZ. This isn't that fraction I bought the game for - we all want more focus being put into this game so we can be pleased with this game.
TL;DR -> Buy with caution. If you want to play this game and expect slow updates, lots of bugs and glitchy mechanics - by all means do so. It's still fun and has lots of good features. ( Beware of FPS issues )

I decided to wait some days before giving my final review of Undertale, after I finished my 3rd and last run of the game. And here is my final opinion: if you’re still hesitating to play this game, buy it and play it now. Because you might miss what I consider as one of the best game that as ever landed on our little gaming countries.
This little pearl has a lot to offer, but the major one is probably its game design. Undertale offers you one intriguing possibility for an RPG: you can simply discus with your opponents, laugh with them, maybe even flirt with them… and end the battle like this. Undertale allows you to not fight your enemies, but instead to find a way to solve everything without any battle. And the way you use this feature might totally change the way the story will evolve and, inevitably, end.
This same story is full of appealing characters, that you might find strange at first sight for some, but that you will probably (nearly) all love at some point. What is interesting is that all the characters you fight in this game, even regular monsters, are characters that you might chit-chat with at some other point. You’re not fighting and killing/sparing people you won’t meet again: everyone has a place in Undertale. And, to be honest, I nearly never, in any other game, bounded so much with nearly all the main characters. Trust me: it was a pain for me to leave the game after having this short, yet immersive adventure with all of them. My special favorite there is probably Sans, one of the main characters in the game, which I found totally fun and cool to be honest.
The story and those characters will make you have some impressing emotional lifts. It amazed me how, while you think everything is over and clear, a little something happen and make you question everything again. And, as I kinda said earlier, I nearly never have been as immersed in a game as I was nearly feeling alongside the hero in the hardest moments, especially the final battles. And I think that’s the first game that made me want to stop it because I didn’t want, for instance, to kill one character that I liked way too much after some runs.
Because it was not enough, Toby Fox, not only a great designer, is a freaking badass at music. The OST of Undertale is a gem of this generation. From old sounding tunes to epic electronic battle music, everything is perfect. Oh well, no. You know what, in reality, “Waterfall” was a pain for me to hear in the end. You ruined my game experience Toby Fox, damn you. (Sorry, I heard it was fashionable to let one bad commentary on Undertale.) Well, to be honest, except this tune, I heard there some of the most memorable music of this gaming era. As a video game music lover, I’m not kidding with those words.
Some people might be repeled by the graphics. To be honest, I don’t think Undertale would have been as cool with more recents and beautiful graphics (though I would be curious to see the result. Wait and see). If you’re not someone who like retro stuff like me, you still should be accustomed pretty quickly to the game. Don’t worry, the rest of the game should make you forget it.
Undertale is not only a game. It’s an experience. An experience of a game that is maybe, in the end, more playing with you than you’re playing with it. 10€ for that game which gave me way more sensations than 60€ games. Sincerely, thanks Toby Fox. No wonder Undertale is GOTY. What you did there was for me a great boost in the way of becoming a game designer.
Gameplay : 10/10
Story : 10/10
Music : 9.5/10 (you’re gonna pay for that Waterfall)
Characters : 10/10
Graphics : I am not sure myself how to note this one, so I’ll pass.
Overall : 10/10

Undertale deserves all the credit and awards it has received over the year, Undertale is one of those games which you want to stop after a lengthy palythrough, but can't stop playing. Even with its very simplistic graphics and music, it can tell you so much. So much so, that is one of the very few games that made me regret the choices I made while playing more than any other game that has better mechanics and graphics than this
Undertale breaks the boundary of normal regular RPG's and adds its own sweetner into the mix. With the combat, which is one of the most ingenious bits of combat I have seen so far in a game, the combat mixes turn based with bullet hell elements, and it succeeds prefectly. But, you don't have to fight the monsters in Undertale, you can; chat, play, joke and even flirt with most of the enemies you encounter in the Underground
The music is amazing, not once did I find the music annoying or abnoxious, although you can hear the loops in the music, it was so well produced that you ignore that fact and just keep on playing
The storytelling is brilliant and told very well, however there are so many loopholes, plot twists, etc... that I cannot really talk about the story element in Undertale without having the risk of spoiling something... the level of comedy that Undertale offers is off the hook, every single time I met one of the regular characters, I just giggled inside with the silly slapstick comedy it had to offer
What intrigued me the most was the level of interaction between the game and the player, the amount of fourth walls and references to pop culture really hooked me in
Although the game make look simplistic, it isn't. The amount and love that went into the game is incredible, from the multiple different endings, the brilliant combat system, brilliant writing and storytelling and music, Undertale is one of the best indie RPG games to come out for this century!
And if you see my playtime, which is six hours and say, "Is that it!?", trust me, this game delves deeper than any other game I have played thus far!
It may not impress a lot of people, but trust me, once you play it, there is no way you will close the executable down!
Undertale is simply amazing!

It has all the good elements of a classic RPG, and it reminds me of Earthbound. The humour in this game is pretty good, too.
I recommend it to anyone who loves RPGs, or wants to try a unique spin on an established genre.

The following review is based on my completion of the "normal" path.
I'll start with the good. The characters are quirky and likeable for the most part. The music is excellent. And some of the flavor text is genuinely funny. The game combines RPG elements with a bullet hell dodge mechanic that increases in difficulty as the game progresses. I personally hate bullet hell, but I list it as a positive because to my knowledge it has not been done before. So props to the dev for trying something new.
Now the bad... This game is soaked from start to finish in heavy-handed "randomness" and clumsy fourth wall breaks. If that's your type of humor then you will enjoy it. For me it was unoriginal and cringeworthy. I will not include spoilers, but there was a very critical part of the plot that made absolutely no sense to me because of this randomness. And although I thought it may be explained later, it was not. I would also like to point out that the aforementioned likeable characters are not developed well at all. That's because this game is very short. This may be a mercy when you consider how tedious the combat is. There is no strategy whatsoever. You either attack or try to resolve the conflict peacefully(or stall until it can be resolved) and then you dodge. That's it. Every turn. No special attacks, very little variation in gear, no combo system, no nothing.
In conclusion: Undertale is game that tries too hard to be different, and forgets to be fun.

The DayZ Mod for Arma II was incredibly well received by many people, and rightfully so. For a mod, it was tons of fun, and had a lot of potential. It then become a standalone game, and the early access alpha version of this was released on the 16th December 2013, and it looked quite decent, despite being in early access.
Everything seemed like it was going well in the beginning, but 17 months later and very little development progress has been made. For the entirety of it's release, it has been considered a 'Walking Simulator' by many, and that is essentially what it is. There's very little to do other than walk and kill the occasional zombie. As you can imagine, it gets extremely boring after playing for a short period of time.
The fact the game isn't even in beta yet is absolutely ridiculous. I get that games can take a long time to develop, but there has been so little progress throughout the time it's been available for purchase that I believe the development team is just lazy and doesn't care much. Not to mention, they're greedy - they upped the cost in order to use the previous price as a sale price!
It's also very poorly optimized and a lot of users with perfectly decent machines are unable to run it properly, even with low graphic settings.
That said, there is one positive about the current state of DayZ - the players. While messing around on various different servers, you're bound to meet some interesting people, some of which can be absolutely hilarious. However, funny people on online multiplayer is certainly not a valid reason to recommend a game.
To sum it up: DayZ has been in early access alpha with very little progress for way too long, there's very little to do besides walk, and the developers are greedy. It has the potential to become a pretty good game eventually, but I'm not the slightest bit impressed with how it's been handled since release. 2/10.

I woke up naked on the beach with nothing but a rock and a torch. Someone shot me.
I woke up naked on the beach with nothing but a rock and a torch. I snuck past other people and planned to stay away from people in general. I was cold, naked, and starving, when a bear mauled me to death.
I woke up naked on the beach with nothing but a rock and a torch. After defending myself against a naked madman armed with a rock and a torch, I found myself in a place of plenty. I gathered resources, made myself a makeshift hatchet, and even clothed myself. I was well fed and had quenched my thirst well. There was wild game, hemp, everything a man could need. When a far better equipped rival chased me away I found myself on a narrow ledge, half way down a sheer cliff wall. Sadly, I lost my footing and fell to my demise.
I woke up naked on the beach with nothing but a rock and a torch.....
_
Seriously though.
The game is fun.
There's a definitive learning curve, but it's not so much regarding the basics of how to play, but more an issue of how to survive.
You gather resources, you eat, you drink, you upgrade your tools, you gather more resources, you explore, you find out how to make bigger and better things, you sometimes find truly amazing things, and the scenery is breathtaking.
You build yourself a home base and fill it with all the things you can't carry around with you all the time because your inventory is limited and you don't want to end up having to sacrifice something you want for something you want slightly more.
You hoard resources.
You hoard clothes and armor.
You hoard guns and ammo.
You grow food and hoard that too.
You go offline and pray to whatever gods of gaming there may be that you get to keep at least some of your stuff.
You log back in.
And here comes what makes or breaks the game for me.
Do you wake up in your own home, with all your gear intact?
Do you wake up in your own home, only with all your stuff gone?
Do you wake up in your own home, with all your stuff gone, your rights to build removed, and surrounded by solid walls rendering the home useless?
Do you wake up in your own home, with most of the walls gone, your rights to build removed, all your stuff gone, and traps EVERYWHERE?
Were you raided by a fellow player? Or maybe... the person you teamed up with?
Will you be allowed to rebuild?
Will you find someone stalking your base, killing you if you dare try to rebuild it?
What makes or breaks this game isn't the game, not for me... it's the players.
This game has taught me a few things.
1. Trust No One!
2. There is no such thing as too many barricades.
3. There is no such thing as "safe".
The game has turned me into a paranoid crotchety hermit.
And I still wanna play.
... just wish I had people who I know in person to team up with so I could slap them, in person, should the turn around and stab me in the back while I sleep.

All right, I've written a handful reviews for this game in the past, with each subsequent playthrough, I had new things to say. As I near my final run, I realized I've played my fair share of the game, now it's time to give it a full review.
Undertale is an amazing game, there's really no other words that can describe my feelings towards it. I wouldn't be surprised if this lingering in our hearts and minds for a long time. It's got a fresh combat style, turned based combat with the ability to manually dodge and not leave it up to chance, interacting with the enemies, seeing how they tick to certain actions (even though in many cases it feels a rather limited). Using your sheer charm to defuse the combat situation.
A major contributing factor is the soundtrack, it sounds awesome, but what REALLY makes the soundtrack, is the nostalgia you get from it. It's a little weird to say that, but it's true. Although the journey was rather short (6-7 hours for me), something just ticked for me when I heard the Ruin's theme after my first run, the game just makes that much of an impression.
Minor Spoiler:
My final score for Undertale, is a 10/10. That's a score that may get tossed around a lot in the reviews of other games, but it's especially true for Undertale.

The game has not made much progress in the last year and at this point I have a feeling they will just eventually "release" it by slapping a 1.0 on the version. I'm amazed people aren't rioting in the streets over this. They have failed to deliver in just about every way possible.
Do not buy this game until it's fully released and has been thoroughly reviewed (if that ever even happens). Fantastic concept, absolutely no followthrough from the developer.
EDIT, 8/2016: Checking back in 14 months after writing the review above. Little has changed, the game is still fundamentally unplayable. No loot or Zombies in any of the online servers, still a pain to join a server, still missing most promised features, still buggy and horribly optimized.
This isn't a game in early access that's just broken cause it's in development, it's not even possible to playtest and clearly lacks strong leadership or direciton.

I feel like it would take an unhealthy amount of masochism for me to go for "the true pacifist" route. In two sentences, I would describe the plot as this -- some weird creatures repeatedly ambush and try to murder a 5-year-old either because they are racist, or to do a human sacrifice. I just want to get back home; also I am somehow supposed to feel bad about defending myself, srsly? :/
For example, there is a giant spider in the game, who explains how she'll make a batch of pastries out of me. I had to listed for over 15-minute long speech about how many things she and her fellow spiders will buy with this fortune that they'll make on selling my soul. All while trying to kill me and feed me to her pet with little spiders dancing around her. And then she receives a letter, changes her mind and says she is sorry. So I suppose it's all OK then, because she, uh, apologized? :/
On top of that I had to become friends with several main characters. I think the game is supposed to be empathetic and all, but I hardly can see myself going out of my way and befriending the equivalent of these characters in real life:
- the goat mom, who tried to beat me up (for my own good, according to her) when I attempt leave her house
- two skeletons, both annoying as hell
- the robot who repeatedly tried to murder me to get more viewers
- the fish who REALLY hates me
- the nerdy scientist (the least repulsive of them all, but still tries to deceive me)
In short, I feel it's really hard to empathize with characters in this game. I see it like majority of characters being♥♥♥♥♥♥♥to me, and then acting passive-aggressively (by guilt-tripping me) when I don't go to great lengths and make them feel better about themselves. IRL version of this is called abusive relationship. There is no way I can enjoy it :(

Note: This review may contain spoilers, atleast to some people. If you haven't played it or seen something about it, go buy it!
How many times in the game
have you nearly killed Balrog, when he just hops away, waiting for you in the next area? How many times in
have you killed Bowser, but it turns out another Bowser somehow made it to the other castle? How about in
how come the Super Mutant population never seems to go down?
asks the question, "What if you kill a character and they never come back?" If you kill a main character, such as the goatmom Toriel, they won't respawn and you won't be able to get them back. Pretty dark. But, of course, the game is stapled with the fact that you don't need to kill anything!
Instead of having crappy RPG characters do nothing but attack turtles and innocent bystanders with no way out of actually killing them,
has a new feature that not a lot of RPGs nowadays have, in which you can interact with the enemy, and attempt to spare them. If you don't hurt anything at all throughout the game, it's how you get the best endings possible throughout. Of course, if you don't want to use this feature, you can also do another path in which you murder everything that comes in your way, wether it'd be frogs, or a snowflake that wants to be a comedian. If you do that, it will give you the worst endings possible. Interesting, right? There's also more that this RPG has to offer than just a new spare feature.
also has some memorable characters, such as a comedic skeleton, or a killer robot with a thirst for human blood! Every character (or atleast, every main character) has memorable quotes, and once you do a pacifist run and don't kill anything, you pretty much develop a like towards the main characters and you don't want to kill them (even though doing a pacifist run first and a genocide run next is the preferable way to play) which means you probably won't do a genocide run.
Aside from having memorable characters and a mercy feature, this game also offers more than just an RPG. You can also date a skeleton, a fish, and a dinosaur rat... thing? Besides that, it also has some minigames thrown in the mix, such as a puzzle involving playing a piano to get a special item, and another minigame involving a cooking show with a killer robot. Again, this makes more memorable moments in this game, and that just makes many people including myself enjoy it even more than before.
I may have been a little bit depressed in my life, (I know this might sound cliche) but
really did change the way I look at things both in video games and in real life. It taught me that violence isn't the answer, and spaghetti cooked by a skeleton sucks.
Of course, every game has it's pros and cons, and I should list it's cons right about here. One of them is that the game is just too short. From what I have heard, the game was actually supposed to be 2 hours long! Can you belive that? Instead, it's roughly about 6 hours. That's how long it took me to get the true ending. Another con about the game is that, even though it's an awesome game, it isn't planned to have a sequel. Although it IS having a sequel named
, it's probably going to be nothing like
(from what I've heard, anyway) but I am still highly anticipated for this game. Other than that, the only other complain I can think about that's bad is that it's $10. I'd probably sell this game for $5 for it's length, but of course, it's a great game and I'd definently recommend picking it up if you haven't yet.
TL;DR: A memorable RPG game that memorable characters, the function of giving enemies and characters mercy, and special, fun minigames thrown in the mix. If anything, I would vote this game as game of the year, because it's better than any other moneygrab games like

After 18 months as standalone (not including all the time it spent as a mod) Dayz is still unplayable. The controls and movement feel terrible and are unintuitive, combat is impossible, and navigating inventory and menus is still a pain.

Do not buy this game until it's fully released and has been thoroughly reviewed (if that ever even happens). Fantastic concept, absolutely no followthrough from the developer.

This isn't a game in early access that's just broken cause it's in development, it's not even possible to playtest and clearly lacks strong leadership or direciton.

I originally posted this review on the 5th of April 2015, can you believe it's been just over two whole years since that point? It's been a long road for this game certainly and out of respect for the times I've had with it, the brilliant memories and the things I have learnt from it which I will carry on into the future, I'd like to simply edit my review now by writing you a story.
"DayZ Standalone was on its initial release a fresh faced survivor, bright and hopeful for the future and the paths they'd take going forward. The future itself was grim and the prospects of getting things done would take more effort than anyone had put in before it, but they were determined to see it through.
Somewhere along the line, DayZ was bitten and never told a soul. So we watched slowly as our new comrade got sicker, became paler, more frail and less people began to hang around them for fear that they might indeed be infected. Those same people moved on to newer communities, healthier people.
All the while our friend DayZ eventually succumbed to their infection and while twitches of life still remain, and it mimics the behaviours it once had in life. We all need to come to the realisation that, that fresh faced friend we met years ago is gone and is never likely to live the life we'd hoped and dreamed for them from the very beginning."
That is not to say that there might never be a cure for our survivor, but for now DayZ is in a latent state of development that I only hope picks up soon and if it doesn't, I really do hope that the developers allow this game to die peacefully and with the grace it has garnered by reputation alone over the glory years of its life.
I love DayZ, I love its survivors. I do not recommend DayZ.

Easily one of the most unique and enjoyable games I've ever played.
This displays one of the best relationships between gameplay and story I’ve ever seen in a video game. Given the choice between violence and non-violence, this game’s world has to be the most dynamic compared to other games I’ve played or seen; it really is a very malleable one. But you'll have to see for yourself for how so.
The story is excellent as well. It constantly keeps you on your toes and is definitely one of the most memorable I've experienced. The humor incorporated in its writing never feels forced; it feels rather natural and makes its wonderful characters (and enemies) much more relatable and thus easy to grow attached with. Of course, the downside to this is how much the game relies on the story for maximum player enjoyment. It's heavily advised to steer clear of anything Undertale from external sites or sources until after playing this game through, but really the choice is yours. (But seriously, try to go into this without any prior knowledge.)
The soundtrack is easily one of the best parts of Undertale for me personally. The vast majority of the tracks are rather memorable because it both captures the associated character/setting/mood very well and boasts melodies that get stuck in your brain upon first or second listen. It sounds very focused and on-point despite the vast musical breadth displayed ranging upbeat and happy backgrounds to downright terrifying pieces of cacophony. Also, the use of motifs not only undoubtably contribute to the cohesion but also accentuate some of the game's most unexpected and emotional moments. Did I mention that it has some of the most badass boss theme songs ever concieved by man? Long story short: one of my personal best video game soundtracks ever.
The best way to experience this game is to not watch any one play it and go in head first. I watched others play through most of their first run and even though I played through the rest of it on my own, I truly believe the real magic comes from not knowing what twist, enemy, or joke that comes around the corner. Regardless, the quality this game brings is top-notch and is delivered so on-point and cleverly it feels almost on another level. Undertale is absolutely wonderful and a must-play.

It's almost impossible to even try and start to put how amazing this game is into words.
Gonna be honest here, at first, I was an ignorant pleb and had no idea what this game's deal was, so naturally, I just began to talk down on it as if it was a terrible game or something. One day I saw a family member playing it and I was fascinated for some reason.
So I immediately went to my room, bought the game, and sat down for a session.
What entailed next was quite possibly the best experience I've ever had with gaming in my entire life.
At first I wasn't into it, and I was honestly thinking about a refund, but as I kept pushing, I found myself even more captivated minute by minute.
For starters, just the concept of the game is amazing, and it's one of the most unique I've seen in a long time. The fact that you can literally play through an entire game without having to hurt a single soul and progress? Amazing. The fact that each enemy you fight has its own attack styles and problems for you to solve? Amazing.
The soundtrack is so good that I find myself at any given point in the day just humming any song that pops in my head from the game, and I mean any. Each song is so catchy and unique that there is no way that you would be able to forget any of them.
The CHARACTERS. This is where the game shines. Ranging from Goatmom to your best friend Flowey the Flower, you meet a cast of the most lovable and relatable characters I've seen in gaming, and I'm not lying; why do you think there's such a massive fanbase backing this game?
And finally the story. At first, you're just given basic exposition about why the monsters and humans are in a clash, and why you've fallen into Mt. Ebott, but as you progress through the game, you're thrown into a massive arc which involves more characters and feels than you'd think, all the while dealing small-scale with meeting new characters and learning what they're all about, which involves you in a more personal aspect of the game.
I know I didn't go into really any detail at all about what I brought up, but that's for good reason. Seriously, this is a game you have to experience on your own, and I'd rather not spoil someone's time by going into specifics about why the story is good or about why the characters are amazing. You simply just need to play it to see it in its full glory.
BUY THIS GAME.

First and foremost, this is a review from someone that really didn't put much time into this game (as I asked for a refund on the first day of playing it), please do take this in consideration when reading this.
So, this is how it went:
-After buying and downloading the game I entered a random server, a pretty well-populated one (I believe it was London 1 or soemthing like that) and, after some loading, managed to appear in a beach, sleeping.
-Wild "Fps issues" appeared! So, I turn everything on minimal (so that you know, my Pc is a capable enough machine, running Gta V on almost max setting without any issues), which doesn't help, I get killed a couple of times before even managing to get up.
-I log out, change setting again, enter a empty server to test it, still problems, I try to change it from there which causes a game crash, okay, no problem: it's unity, I get it, no biggie, I'm sure I'll find a solution on the internet later. But on the meantime a resolution change seems to fix my problem.
-Cool, time to play. I enter a less populated server (55 people, the least populated official one at that time). I start collecting wood: A guy kills me with a rock, didn't say a thing just killed me for no apparent reason. Ok, I try again, I found a naked guy on the beach and try to approach him. Nope, rock to the face, manage to run away to get killed by a guy with a bow. Ok, nice. Then got shot and finally got stabbed with a spear.
I died uttering with my last breath "CONGRATS M8 YOU GOT A ROCK".
So, is this game nice? Sure, I guess,  if you have enough people to play with and don't mind having to deal with players that, instead of trying to survive together and kill better equipped players for their loot, kill every fu***ng one that they see just because.
So yeah, this might be an issue solved with the magical words "git gud" but as far as I'm concerned, I'm outta here.
Pd: If the community ever gets better I'm gladly coming back, it's a truly unique game with enormous potential and which I regret having to run away from due to the experience I had on it.
Pd2: If there was an intermediate term between recommending it and not I'd likely click that button, but, and this is just my opinion which I don't intend to force on anyone, I don't recommend this game, as per right now.

I wake up on the beach,with no memory of how I got onto the Island. No memory of my life. No knowledge of who I am. The only thing I knew was that, I needed to build a campfire somehow. Somewhere.
I found a rock along the beach, as well as a torch a bit inland. After coming across a tree I begun to swing madly at it with the small, fist sized rock in my hands. Smack after smack. Thwack after thwack. I slowly began to degrade the bark and the wood underneath as my onslaught continued onto the plant. Eventually, I had weakened the wood enough, and tore out a chunk of bark and inner wood. Using some of the vines on the tree, I tied my rock to the jagged shaft of wood and created a makeshift hatchet.
Noticing that I was stark naked with no protection from anyone or anything that this mysterious land could have in store for me, I began my work collected plants, wood, and pebbles, until eventually I had been able to make myself some garments and wraps for my feet. I then was able to make a bow, as well as some arrows with a bag that served as my quiver. With my goal of making a campfire next in mind, I set out to hunt something worth cooking over my soon-to-be campfire.
After treaking through rocky terrain and frozen tundra, I continue to not see any wildlife to collect. Starting to grow hungry, I look around and notice mushrooms growing between the rocks. Not seeing any alternative, I began to feast on the unsuspecting shrooms until my belly was full and I felt satisfied. After finishing my feast, I hear branches snapping in the underbrush. As I look up to see what the cause of the noise was, I see it:
A boar.
The hunt was short lived, as I chased the wild creature, shooting arrows into it as it ran from me. Eventually, the wounds from my arrows caused it to slow down and I was able to catch up with it. As it collapsed, gasping for air, I put the creature out of its missery with a swift blow of my hatchet to its skull. It twitched, and continue to do so for a few moments, but eventually, as all dead things do, it lay completely motionless. With a meal ready, I began to prep a campfire.
It did not take long, as I only needed some logs and something to spark it and set it ablaze using the tree sap as makeshift lighter-fuel. With the flame ablaze, I began to skin and prepare my meal. With the pike in place and the boar rotating above the flaming inferno. I sat next to it, staring into its firey depths, until, without warning, I hear a small explosion and feel myself get hit in the chest. As I crumble to the ground, I see a figure walk out from the woods, with a rifle in his hands and a grin on his face upon seeing the boar I had prepared. As he neared me, I held up my hand. A voiceless plea.
He looked at me for a few moments, before grinning and pointed his rifle at me.
"Don'tcha worry you sorry sod. I'll make it quick and painless."
With the pull of the trigger and a small pain to my head, I crumbled down. As I lay there, with the darkness taking over, I stare at my little fire. The way the flames liked the boar meat held over it by a pike. The light cackle of the logs as they slowly turned into embers. With that, the darkness took over, and I was no more.
10/10 Would get killed by a random again.

It is now April 5th, 2016. It has been exactly one year since I posted this review. So far, literally nothing has changed from the day that I wrote this review. It doesn't surprise me that all the fanboys in denial who went as far as spamming on my Steam profile have now come to a realization about this trashy game and shut their mouths.
April 23rd, 2017. Two years have past since I've originally posted this review. I'm pretty speechless to be honest. Yeah... don't buy this game.
DayZ is probably the biggest example of a cashgrab I've ever seen on Steam Early Access. As the game has now been in development since its release date back in December 2013, the developers have made tens of  millions of dollars off the 3 million copies sold (since January 2015). Many people have asked what happened to all this money: Only rumors remain... (I could go on a rant about how Dean Rocket stole all the money for himself and is now living in a cozy mansion but I digress).
What infuriates me, however, is the fact that this game has so much potential but was all squandered with the lack of updates, fixes and news from the surprisingly large development team. In the time that I'm writing this review (April 2015), it has been just under two years since the game's release (excluding the many months of development beforehand as well as the Closed Alpha stages - dating all the way back to May 2013 and even earlier) and very little improvements have been made; thus, the game remains in Alpha despite the many deadlines in which the game would move into Beta and even release, only to be delayed every quarter of the year.
My personal experience with the game has been an ever-worsening nightmare. With some history playing the DayZ mod and the many variants of it (Epoch, Overpoch, the whole lot) on ArmA 2, I simply just had to purchase the game only a few months after release with the mindset that it would be a great game by the end of the year, especially with the videos being posted left and right showcasing the new features and potential that it would be superior to the mod in every single way. Boy, was I wrong.
The main issue that was supposed to be fixed many months ago but has been pushed back was the
of the game. I cannot account for anyone else when I say that you require a NASA supercomputer to run this game. This is the main area where DayZ shows its potential: The game has gorgeous visuals on maximum graphic settings. The reality of this is that the majority of people that play the game have to run it on the lowest settings due to poor optimization and use of an outdated engine that fully renders the entire map all at once for some reason.
The game struggles even with the most basic functions such as moving, vaulting, equipping weapons and such. Often times, I would die because of how glitchy the ladders and staircases in the game are. Inventory management is a drag and does not add any realism or immersion. Also, it is important to mention that the game presents a very poor
: Apart from the few piles of debris (I'm talking about the infamous tossed-out laundry machine) and the building with the plane crash located at Cherno, all the major cities in the game look like they were built yesterday. The developers could have easily made vast improvements rather than just ripping the map off of the mod and just modifying the spawn points and adding a few cities. Other than the major cities, many of the small villages in the map are recycled and reused many times. It's easy to get lost in the map because of this. The use of an online map would deter this but, at the same time, remove what little immersion remains.
One large factor which was lacking in the standalone game but had a strong presence in the mod was
. At this time, there are only two vehicles in the game which are very similar: Both are military transport and they look visually similar, the only difference is the number of seats they provide. Due to the size of Chernaurus+, it would be less of a hassle to travel by vehicle rather than spending hours sprinting to a location. A bicycle at the very least could have been added.
I had high hopes for this game after its release. Unfortunately, the game does not deliver what it promised. The developers know this but yet continue to release very small updates every now and then to give us players the illusion that changes are being made in the game. In all honesty, there is no hope for the game. With all major fixes being constantly delayed, it is doubtful that this game will exit Alpha. Please save your money and play the mod if you want a good experience. Thank you.

Have any zombie survival fantasys? WIsh to live in a post apocalytic world and watch humanity fall apart and resort to desperate measures! Then this is the game for you, with a robust crafting system and loot aplenty, this game is a survivalist dream sim.

Over a year after it was first 'pre-released' and this thing is still missing major features that the original mod had for years, not the least of which is freakin' ZOMBIES. Almost nothing has been improved upon to any substantial degree. I'm left here wondering why they thought it was a good idea to break everything, remove half of it, stitch the remaining pieces back together wrong, and then charge money for it.
It's a buggy unoptimized mess. I had to go out of my way editing .ini files and launch parameters to get a framerate higher than thirty out of this steaming pile even on a i7 4770 and GTX 780. Even then, my hardware is only at ~30% load. Bug-wise it's not uncommon for your character to be teleported outside of a two story building and fall to his death, nor is it unlikely that one of the two zombies in town will phase through a wall (or simply spawn in front of you) and one-shot you through your body armor.
Speaking of bugs, they're about the only thing resembling a 'survival' mechanic in this game. Given the lack of zombies it's simple enough to just sprint through a town collecting and consuming canned food and soda. Because players face nearly zero threat from the environment the game essentially becomes the most horribly paced version of Deathmatch ever created. Spend hours finding weapons and the clothing required to carry said weapons, spend another few hours wandering around, and if you're lucky you'll spot the other guy first. Otherwise you'll likely be dead before you hear the rifle report. Due to the 'realism' of the games damage model the first person to land a shot is almost always the victor. This basically boils down to you dropping dead out of nowhere most of the time.
Maybe you're into that kind of combat. That's fine. The problem still stands that there's barely any threat from the environment itself, something I'd consider a major necessity in a survival game.
The controls, while they've been tightened up a bit from standard ArmA 2, still leave a lot to be desired. Fairly often when switching stances or holstering weapons the character will decide he should be running instead of standing still or vice versa. This often leads to a leap of faith from the top of a building, or a dead stop during a full sprint. That's assuming the commands are even executed. I've spent a fair bit of time mashing the hotkey wondering when my man's going to grab his damned fire axe. "Oh, no rush or anything chap. Don't worry about the completely silent teleporting 'zombie' mauling you."
I bought this crap expecting that within a reasonable amount of time I'd be looking at a more polished version of the mod. Instead I got a big fat steaming pile of buyers remorse.
TL;DR: It's been nearly a year and a half and this junk is still horrifically buggy, unoptimized, and not even remotely close to being feature-complete. This is supposed to be a proper game, but it's in worse condition than a mod slapped together by hobbyists who didn't get paid.

This recommendation goes for all the originality this game has. You fell into a cave that leads to an interesting world filled with monsters. When you encounter them you can choose between sparing them or fighting with them. Both options have consequences and a surprising depth to it. Sparing monsters is not just "ok, i'll run away from this battle" and fighting doesn't make you necessarily stronger (or does it?). The choices you do matter, some dialogues and actions of certain characters depend on them. There are multiple endings based on those actions. My recommendation goes for all of this. It's a unique experience that you must try for yourself.
Now, the bugbears. The game has some puzzles that i think don't really fit the world. Even though they are not very hard and usually have humor associated with them, i found those parts to be the weakest part of the game. I feel like there could be other ways to tell the story. Also some bosses were frustrating to get trough. That affected negatively my experience of the game, even though later i found it was partially due to my decisions (again, choices matter).
While i personally don't join the club of people that are giving a huge praise to this game and saying that it is the best game of 2015, i have to admit this game is very original and you should try it. Even if you end up not liking it, the experience is worthwhile certainly.

I have to say, I was a complete skeptic of this game when I first heard about it. Even when I first heard the name "Undertale" I thought it was spelled "undertail" so I thought it was like some sort of war game where you fly planes. Anyway, with my anticipation of the game being where you fly planes, I was quite underwhelmed to find out that the game I thought of was not real, and instead, it was a retro RPG game, where you do not have to kill. I thought to myself, "I'm not sure why this game is so good. It looks so boring," and so I left my attention off the game for a while.
I was still curious however, and so I looked up a walkthrough of the game on YouTube. I managed to see the first minute of the game, the introduction before gameplay. The guy who was playing it had this dull voice and seemed less enthusiastic than other YouTubers, so as a result I was bored again with the game.
Then came Christmas. I managed to get a Steam gift card from my sister with 20 dollars on it. You could guess that immediately I went to redeem it, and so my spending began. After buying many games on sale, I had about 9 dollars left. I didn;t know what to buy next, and so I asked my brother, who happens to be a pro gamer. I asked him, and he almost shouted at me, "BUY UNDERTALE!" He kept shouting at me to buy this game that looked so underwhelming, and through his eagerness, I bought the game, becoming a little excited of what to expect, but still skeptical.
After playing the game, I had come to a conclusion... that Undertale was the best buy out of any game I have ever bought.
To me, Undertale is more than a game. It's also an experience. Games today are all there just to entertain and keep kids and teens satisfied, and creates a massive payload to coorperations. Games like COD, WoW, the Halo series, are all the same once you think about. When you play them, you think nothing else but beating the game and getting the all the achievements. After that, what then? They become boring after a long period of time, and eventually you don't play them anymore.
The reason why that is, is because they lack emotion. The don't make you dive into a pool of Romanticism. Instead, they make you frustrated, they put you on tilt, and they make you addidicted. These feelings are found in games like COD, and other cashgrab games.
This is where Undertale succeeds. Undertale made me feel so many emotions; happy, sad, afraid, bittersweet, full of laughter, etc. So much content, coming from such a small game, unlike games like  Fallout 4, GTAV, and Skyrim. It has an enriching story that could light up anyone's day. Speaking from a musician's point of view, it also has an undeniabley great soundtrack, as I cannot tell you how many times I had a them or two stuck in my head for the entire day.
In short, Undertale is truely a fantastic little game, a diamond in the rough. I recommend it to anyone who is in for a surprise, as well as a great experience.

Undertale is an amazing game that can easily be overlooked. Mostly because of the hype around it and the way it looks.
Even if you are into retro-looking games, this game doesn't look very good. Even for an indie game, it's not at all an art statement such as Ori or Braid. Graphics usually stand fairly low in my own priorities of what I look for in games.
Yet my first impression of how undertale looks was "Wow. This is ugly". The character you control is yellow and looks bored / stoned. The environment looks worse than an RPG Maker game.
However, it doesn't. The whole game was made mostly by a single person. That's not an excuse for this game to look bad (Look at Dust). I'm saying that everything was drawn by hand and unlike the generic RPG Maker tileset, it has an incredible amount of charm. It will grow on you. You will end up loving how ugly it is. Every single character is very unique, everything is very imaginative.
For a story and choice driven game, the gameplay is actually very engaging. Combats look like generic old-school RPGs (mostly EarthBound, which seems to be this game's biggest inspiration). However, they're played much like a hellshooter. It might seem easy at first but DOES become quite challenging after some time.
Of course, gameplay alone is not what makes this game so great. In fact, I would not be inclined to say that any aspect of the game in particular makes it great. This game is just so incredibly charming as a whole.
The story is not overly complex and fairly lighthearted. It's not as much the plot in itself than each step of its journey and the way it develops that's interesting. Your choices as well as the way you play and the order in which you do things will affect how the story unfold, the game will often react to what you do and how you do it.
The greatest strength of this game and something I'm quite a fan of, is its tendency to think outside of the box and break the fourth wall. The game will interact with you in less conventional ways. The game will often be designed in a way that puts an idea in your head only to tell you exactly what you were thinking. It likes commenting on some of your decisions. It will be very amusing at time and even sometimes annoying on purpose. Annoying, but the good kind, kind of like a stupid joke you already expect but the fact that you do, is exactly what makes it so funny.
The game spends quite some time trying to tell you that it's a puzzle game. Which is funny because there are actually very few puzzles in the game and they're never particularly hard. This game is more ABOUT puzzles than necessarily having many of them. Combats are where you will need to think. Because, as the game mainly advertises, you do not need to kill a single enemy in this game, and this can be quite challenging on its own.
The game is not very long. You can expect 6-8 hours of playtime. However, it does have some pretty good replay value. The story will be quite different depending on how you play the game and it is very interesting to do it each way. It's not just a different ending cutscene. There are 3 different ways to play the game and they affect most of the game. And those 6-8 hours of playtime are not filled with tedious grinding or fetch quests. In fact, you never have to grind at all, the combats are well spaced out and don't feel overly repetitive or annoying. Furthermore, the game is loaded to the brim with little details that complement each other. You should definitely take your time looking around and interacting with everything in this game. I personnally found each dialogue and each interaction to be amusing or interesting. There are tons of things you will think of and wonder if you can do it. And you can. It does not necessarily affect anything but it's always nice to see that the possibility that you would do it was considered.
I think the hype for this game is justified and Toby Fox, the creator of this game, deserve all the praise he is getting. Undertale is a simple but very clever game that did not leave me disappointed in the (true) end.

Enjoyable but very overrated.  The well-written characters in the ensemble cast are clearly the stars of this show.  In an age of one-dimensional personalities, it's refreshing to see glimpses of the second dimension; if each character wasn't relegated to a single act out of the three in the game, we might have seen a third dimension come through.  It's normally difficult to make someone laugh out loud using only text, but Undertale's Earthbound-like, off-the-wall sense of humor when talking to people or checking out the environment managed to make me do so repeatedly.
The comparisons with Earthbound end there, though.  The environments and puzzles in Undertale are extremely bland and forgettable, giving me the impression that I was always being railroaded toward the next event.  Secrets are relatively sparse, but they do usually manage to subvert your expectations when they appear.
It's true that the combat system is clearly inspired by Earthbound's, but in practice, the similarities are purely superficial.  In each turn of an encounter, you have the option of either fighting the opponent using timed button presses or trying to perform a more tame action (such as talking, petting, cheering, etc.) in an attempt to make the enemy lose their will to fight.  During the enemy's turns, you are tasked with dodging various patterns of projectiles for a certain amount of time (luckily, these patterns are so unique to each opponent that this never grows stale).  I recommend sparing at least the bosses, both for story purposes and because each enemy's sparing setup is novel (it's also often a longer process, and this dodging minigame is some of the only real gameplay you'll find in Undertale).  One thing I appreciated is that in most games, characterization will halt when combat begins.  Not so in this one!
If you enjoy replaying through games, you'll be pleased to learn that Undertale offers enough of an incentive to play through it a second or even third time, if you really want to experience everything.  Some of this, though, manifests itself as sections being artificially blocked off during the first playthrough, which I think is bad design.
I see the word "charming" thrown around a lot when talking about Undertale.  It is indeed charming, but how much is charm worth to you?  Wait to buy it until it's 50% off.

Undertale is an amazing game that can easily be overlooked. Mostly because of the hype around it and the way it looks.
Even if you are into retro-looking games, this game doesn't look very good. Even for an indie game, it's not at all an art statement such as Ori or Braid. Graphics usually stand fairly low in my own priorities of what I look for in games.
Yet my first impression of how undertale looks was "Wow. This is ugly". The character you control is yellow and looks bored / stoned. The environment looks worse than an RPG Maker game.
However, it doesn't. The whole game was made mostly by a single person. That's not an excuse for this game to look bad (Look at Dust). I'm saying that everything was drawn by hand and unlike the generic RPG Maker tileset, it has an incredible amount of charm. It will grow on you. You will end up loving how ugly it is. Every single character is very unique, everything is very imaginative.
For a story and choice driven game, the gameplay is actually very engaging. Combats look like generic old-school RPGs (mostly EarthBound, which seems to be this game's biggest inspiration). However, they're played much like a hellshooter. It might seem easy at first but DOES become quite challenging after some time.
Of course, gameplay alone is not what makes this game so great. In fact, I would not be inclined to say that any aspect of the game in particular makes it great. This game is just so incredibly charming as a whole.
The story is not overly complex and fairly lighthearted. It's not as much the plot in itself than each step of its journey and the way it develops that's interesting. Your choices as well as the way you play and the order in which you do things will affect how the story unfold, the game will often react to what you do and how you do it.
The greatest strength of this game and something I'm quite a fan of, is its tendency to think outside of the box and break the fourth wall. The game will interact with you in less conventional ways. The game will often be designed in a way that puts an idea in your head only to tell you exactly what you were thinking. It likes commenting on some of your decisions. It will be very amusing at time and even sometimes annoying on purpose. Annoying, but the good kind, kind of like a stupid joke you already expect but the fact that you do, is exactly what makes it so funny.
The game spends quite some time trying to tell you that it's a puzzle game. Which is funny because there are actually very few puzzles in the game and they're never particularly hard. This game is more ABOUT puzzles than necessarily having many of them. Combats are where you will need to think. Because, as the game mainly advertises, you do not need to kill a single enemy in this game, and this can be quite challenging on its own.
The game is not very long. You can expect 6-8 hours of playtime. However, it does have some pretty good replay value. The story will be quite different depending on how you play the game and it is very interesting to do it each way. It's not just a different ending cutscene. There are 3 different ways to play the game and they affect most of the game. And those 6-8 hours of playtime are not filled with tedious grinding or fetch quests. In fact, you never have to grind at all, the combats are well spaced out and don't feel overly repetitive or annoying. Furthermore, the game is loaded to the brim with little details that complement each other. You should definitely take your time looking around and interacting with everything in this game. I personnally found each dialogue and each interaction to be amusing or interesting. There are tons of things you will think of and wonder if you can do it. And you can. It does not necessarily affect anything but it's always nice to see that the possibility that you would do it was considered.
I think the hype for this game is justified and Toby Fox, the creator of this game, deserve all the praise he is getting. Undertale is a simple but very clever game that did not leave me disappointed in the (true) end.

I have played both the Mod, and this Title. It seemed like it would be worth the price and payment. However this game has a string of broken promises in regards to deadlines following it. Elements which were broken in the original mod, such as the interface lag, the constant desync, zombies, items bugging out, animation lag, and poor optimization still plague Bohemia.
Promises of these things to be fixed have been on going since the Standalone was released. In addition, this game although it provides a lot of potential for growth - you cant help but get the feeling the developers are implementing new features to the game without even fixing the past broken ones.
Also, this game has an image crisis. On one hand it shows off the fact that its a Zombie-Survival, on the other it shows that it is a Survival Game with the inclusion of Zombies. This makes it difficult to cater for their audience as some just want a Survival game, and others want a 'The Walking Dead' experience of zombie survival - where the zombies and humans are the biggest threat in the game.
Instead this game feels like a Free For All Deathmatch, with loot mechanics, and some zombies thrown in.
Do not buy until another 3-4 years of development have past, hopefully by then these things will be fixed.

After reading, seeing, and listening to a veritable mountain of fan art, music remixes, etc., I finally decided to take the plunge and dive into this game. Underneath the simplistic layout is a challenging and unique combat system where you fight for your soul by dodging a wide variety of mechanics.  Tying it all together is a masterful music score that fits each scenario with fun and epic sounding boss battle themes.
This game is a definite 'must play'

I have played both the Mod, and this Title. It seemed like it would be worth the price and payment. However this game has a string of broken promises in regards to deadlines following it. Elements which were broken in the original mod, such as the interface lag, the constant desync, zombies, items bugging out, animation lag, and poor optimization still plague Bohemia.
Promises of these things to be fixed have been on going since the Standalone was released. In addition, this game although it provides a lot of potential for growth - you cant help but get the feeling the developers are implementing new features to the game without even fixing the past broken ones.
Also, this game has an image crisis. On one hand it shows off the fact that its a Zombie-Survival, on the other it shows that it is a Survival Game with the inclusion of Zombies. This makes it difficult to cater for their audience as some just want a Survival game, and others want a 'The Walking Dead' experience of zombie survival - where the zombies and humans are the biggest threat in the game.
Instead this game feels like a Free For All Deathmatch, with loot mechanics, and some zombies thrown in.
Do not buy until another 3-4 years of development have past, hopefully by then these things will be fixed.

Enjoyable but very overrated.  The well-written characters in the ensemble cast are clearly the stars of this show.  In an age of one-dimensional personalities, it's refreshing to see glimpses of the second dimension; if each character wasn't relegated to a single act out of the three in the game, we might have seen a third dimension come through.  It's normally difficult to make someone laugh out loud using only text, but Undertale's Earthbound-like, off-the-wall sense of humor when talking to people or checking out the environment managed to make me do so repeatedly.
The comparisons with Earthbound end there, though.  The environments and puzzles in Undertale are extremely bland and forgettable, giving me the impression that I was always being railroaded toward the next event.  Secrets are relatively sparse, but they do usually manage to subvert your expectations when they appear.
It's true that the combat system is clearly inspired by Earthbound's, but in practice, the similarities are purely superficial.  In each turn of an encounter, you have the option of either fighting the opponent using timed button presses or trying to perform a more tame action (such as talking, petting, cheering, etc.) in an attempt to make the enemy lose their will to fight.  During the enemy's turns, you are tasked with dodging various patterns of projectiles for a certain amount of time (luckily, these patterns are so unique to each opponent that this never grows stale).  I recommend sparing at least the bosses, both for story purposes and because each enemy's sparing setup is novel (it's also often a longer process, and this dodging minigame is some of the only real gameplay you'll find in Undertale).  One thing I appreciated is that in most games, characterization will halt when combat begins.  Not so in this one!
If you enjoy replaying through games, you'll be pleased to learn that Undertale offers enough of an incentive to play through it a second or even third time, if you really want to experience everything.  Some of this, though, manifests itself as sections being artificially blocked off during the first playthrough, which I think is bad design.
I see the word "charming" thrown around a lot when talking about Undertale.  It is indeed charming, but how much is charm worth to you?  Wait to buy it until it's 50% off.
8/10

initially avoided this game because of how its been blowing up the internet, but after LittleV did a cover of one of the songs and TB did a sort of review i decided to get it. I've only had it for about a week, but its already my 2nd favorite game of the year (the 1st being the Witcher 3, obviously). The possibilities are a breath of fresh air from most games today where their ideas of choice are a handful of vague/empty dialogue that all reach the same conclusion (looking at you fallout 4) and the multiple difficulties are a great way to keep you coming back to it, in fact coming back to it is a vital part of the game itself. Don't think you can get away with murdering everyone and then reloading, the game knows and it won't put up with your♥♥♥♥♥♥
Basic monsters can get a little repetitive after awhile but besides that the "combat" is rather interesting, essentially it's turn based bullet-hell. Most characters are really in-depth and have lots of backstory, although I may be one of the few who didn't get attached to Toriel that much, only after going through the True Pacifist ending did I actually start to like her. I did get attached to many of the other characters though, and I still don't think I'm capable of going back for a Genocide run, maybe after a few months or so.The game can get really serious, sometimes downright disturbing, but overall its a comedy game. Humor is a hard thing to interpret, so really it depends on what you find funny. Not liking the style of humor can possibly kill the game for you, so just bear that in mind. Game also gets a plus for the ♥♥♥♥ing amazing soundtrack, possibly my favorite alongside Metal Gear Rising.
So if you want a story rich rpg-lite type game, then Undertale is a great choice, its also rather cheap and will give you more than your money's worth in terms of enjoyment (or in a genocide run, a very bad time)

What can I say, I have over 500 hours on this game, and I have had a hell of a lot of fun moments playing this game with friends, but it is slowly, and i mean VERY slowly, being developed, and it seems that every new patch adds a lot to the game, which is good, but at the same time causes more problems then it solves. Right now .55 came out and now they apparently made persistance required, which is great, if it worked. Also, they claim that the loot econonmy has been fixed, I have been playing a lot since this .55 update came out, and I've been on one server that actually had loot. Persitance like i said before is broken, and there is no loot. Hackers are still an issue, but they have been appearing less and less, which is a good thing, or its just showing the loss of players since the alpha release 2 years ago. The optimisation is getting better as well, I can tell, mainly because I have a pretty lame gaming rig, but can run the game, and its becoming smoother every so often. But Ill break it down If you do not feel like reading.
Persistance:
Persistance is what the devs put in to allow players to make bases, and by bases i mean maybe find a tent. But it also makes the items in the server or instance fixed, meaning once its taken, its gone. The devs have tried to fix this with "Respawning Loot" but nothing of the type has ever actually been implemented. And right now the persistance is causing servers to not have loot at all.
Development:
This game was released in 2013 as an alpha, and is still in alpha in 2015, without much improvement. Sure they have added things to the map, as well as weapons, items, and features such as temperature control, and heath issues, sickness, hunger, etc. But the core of it all, of actually making a stable, finished game is nowhere in sight. The timelines they post are BS to say the least, sure they pump out the vehicles everyone wanted, but other then adding items, they really havent changed much. And what they do add is usually broken until 2 updates after the one it was implemented in.
Community:
The community is great all together, banding together to make fun servers like DayZRP's roleplaying servers. but there are still those who would rather shoot people on sight (KOS) or hack there way to a undeserved victory. but if you dont run into those types of people, you run into people that will talk to you, become friends with you, and you end up having a nice time playing a game with total strangers. HACKING:::!!!  the hacking problem has been getting better, as a person who feels inevitably in bad luck, i always find hackers that kill me, i have seen a decline in hacking, whether it be the devs fixing it, or the drop in players, i do not know. But it has been getting better.
TL;DR
All in all, i feel the game is fun in moderation. It has flaws, and a lot of them, but once the loot comes back, it will be playable as it has been, I'd give it a 5/10 for playability and gameplay, but it seems lacking in content, and development decisions. Feel free to pick it up, its fun to play with friends, but be aware that it is an alpha game, and probably will stay an alpha, so it has numerous problems, and will keeps having those problems.

Undertale, without a doubt is the best Indie game to come out this year, trumping even triple "A" titles, and on par with Fallout 4. It's RPG elements differ from most, because the characters are alive, and have emotions, even simple thugs have quirks to them. Therefore it brings you to the good and evil aspect, being good is essentially letting these very scared individuals know you are nice, and "Sparing" them allows you to win without killing them, thus making everyone around you more accepting of you and changing their opinion on the human race as a whole.
Then, there's being "Evil". Being evil indeed has the pro's and cons of being a villain, and finding your adversaries nobally defending their towns from you, and overall killing in this game fuffills nothing, and will indeed make you feel like a monster as you go from level to level finding people have been evacuated, and notes begging you not to hurt them or their families.
Undertale has ups and downs, seeing as it's a puzzle game (Depending on which moral route you take) it'd turn people off instantly, but I really do wish you make an exception in this case, as this game does indeed grasp the hearts of almost everyone who plays it, it can make you happy, sad, and even scared and disturbed at a lot of points in the game. I cannot reccomend this game enough.
Fall down into the land of monsters, and let the journey of these loveable characters guide you back up to the surface, weather it be showing them kindness, or by destroying everything in your path, and ripping your freedom from the cold, dead hands of the king; whatever choice you make, you won't regret getting this emotional roller coaster.

Adolf Hitler (20 April 1889 – 30 April 1945) was an Austrian-born German politician who was the leader of the Nazi Party (NSDAP), Chancellor of Germany from 1933 to 1945, and Führer ("leader") of Nazi Germany from 1934 to 1945. He was effectively dictator of Nazi Germany, and was at the centre of World War II in Europe and the Holocaust.
Hitler was a decorated veteran of World War I. He joined the precursor of the NSDAP, the German Workers' Party, in 1919 and became leader of the NSDAP in 1921. In 1923 he attempted a coup in Munich to seize power. The failed coup resulted in Hitler's imprisonment, during which time he dictated his autobiography and political manifesto Mein Kampf ("My Struggle"). After his release in 1924, Hitler gained popular support by attacking the Treaty of Versailles and promoting Pan-Germanism, anti-Semitism, and anti-communism with charismatic oratory and Nazi propaganda. Hitler frequently denounced international capitalism and communism as being part of a Jewish conspiracy.
Hitler's Nazi Party became the largest elected party in the German Reichstag, leading to his appointment as chancellor in 1933. Following fresh elections won by his coalition, the Reichstag passed the Enabling Act, which began the process of transforming the Weimar Republic into Nazi Germany, a single-party dictatorship based on the totalitarian and autocratic ideology of National Socialism. Hitler aimed to eliminate Jews from Germany and establish a New Order to counter what he saw as the injustice of the post-World War I international order dominated by Britain and France. His first six years in power resulted in rapid economic recovery from the Great Depression, the denunciation of restrictions imposed on Germany after World War I, and the annexation of territories that were home to millions of ethnic Germans—actions which gave him significant popular support.
Hitler sought Lebensraum ("living space") for the German people. His aggressive foreign policy is considered to be the primary cause of the outbreak of World War II in Europe. He directed large-scale rearmament and on 1 September 1939 invaded Poland, resulting in British and French declarations of war on Germany. In June 1941, Hitler ordered an invasion of the Soviet Union. By the end of 1941 German forces and the European Axis powers occupied most of Europe and North Africa. Failure to defeat the Soviets and the entry of the United States into the war forced Germany onto the defensive and it suffered a series of escalating defeats. In the final days of the war, during the Battle of Berlin in 1945, Hitler married his long-time lover, Eva Braun. On 30 April 1945, less than two days later, the two committed suicide to avoid capture by the Red Army, and their corpses were burned.
Under Hitler's leadership and racially motivated ideology, the Nazi regime was responsible for the genocide of at least 5.5 million Jews and millions of other victims whom he and his followers deemed Untermenschen ("sub-humans") and socially undesirable. Hitler and the Nazi regime were also responsible for the killing of an estimated 19.3 million civilians and prisoners of war. In addition, 29 million soldiers and civilians died as a result of military action in the European Theatre of World War II. The number of civilians killed during the Second World War was unprecedented in warfare, and constitutes the deadliest conflict in human history.

I have a personal vendetta against CRPGs because (traditionally) the plot is crap and there's a bunch of level grinding and boring gameplay elements and they don't have very many plot-relevant choices and a bunch of other problems.
...Suddenly, Undertale happened.
Literally every single issue I had with CRPGs was subverted, inverted, twisted, played with, and broken. Then, these "bad ingredients" were glued back together seamlessly with some dog-pattern duct tape, mixed with half a cup of humor and a gallon of genuinely player-driven plot, and topped with a few bits of plaster taken from the recently-demolished fourth wall.
Prior to playing Undertale, I had heard nothing but overwhelmingly positive reviews from literally every person I know that played it. Now, after playing through part of it, it easily surpasses Half-Life in my rating of "best game I've ever played," and I haven't even finished it yet.
If you haven't picked up this game by now, then clearly you're not convinced of how gloriously brilliant every aspect of it is.
I highly doubt I can convince you myself, though.
But, I mean, if you're refusing to play this for any reason...
...you're honestly missing out.

I have a personal vendetta against CRPGs because (traditionally) the plot is crap and there's a bunch of level grinding and boring gameplay elements and they don't have very many plot-relevant choices and a bunch of other problems.
...Suddenly, Undertale happened.
Literally every single issue I had with CRPGs was subverted, inverted, twisted, played with, and broken. Then, these "bad ingredients" were glued back together seamlessly with some dog-pattern duct tape, mixed with half a cup of humor and a gallon of genuinely player-driven plot, and topped with a few bits of plaster taken from the recently-demolished fourth wall.
Prior to playing Undertale, I had heard nothing but overwhelmingly positive reviews from literally every person I know that played it. Now, after playing through part of it, it easily surpasses Half-Life in my rating of "best game I've ever played," and I haven't even finished it yet.
If you haven't picked up this game by now, then clearly you're not convinced of how gloriously brilliant every aspect of it is.
I highly doubt I can convince you myself, though.
But, I mean, if you're refusing to play this for any reason...
...you're honestly missing out.

With all the hype surrounding this game it was impossible not to hear how amazing Undertale is and how it has received "Overwhelming Reviews". But of course you can't believe in the hype until you actual play the game right? I finally decided to buy the game when it went on sale during the recent Christmas sale and I can safely that it lives up to its expectations. Keep in mind that I haven't completed the game yet so I may not know every single detail about Undertale but I at least know the important points to tell if it's a good game or not. Undertale is a story heavy RPG inspired by classic RPGs such as Earthbound, but unlike other RPGs this one has a unique combat and dodge system (or in this specific game's case non-combat). The story is slowly revealed to you has you progress through the game and while doing so you will encounter a cast of interesting characters. I will say that this game and it's humor can be quirky, for lack of a better term, and does make a few references to anime in general. It's not a big issue at all for me, but to be honest I'm not really into "quirky and le random XDD" humor, or anime either, and I know that this can be a deal breaker for some. Other than that Undertale is one of those rare gems that you don't really see gaming nowadays and is worth the $10 pricing (or in my case $8 huehuehuehuehue).
