**EARLY ACCESS REVIEW**
I first purchased this game when it was very first released sometime back in 2013. At the time, I got a little lost, and it seemed laggy, so I quit playing.
Something kept knawing away at the back of my head, though. I had to get back into the game and find my way to another town, to find other players. I saw how many copies of the game had sold, so I knew I would run into someone eventually.
After a few hours of running around in the middle of Chernarus, I found myself in an airbase (now that I understand is Balota airbase). I ran into survivors that didn't KoS me (great first impression, yes.)
We befriended each other, and locked down the airstrip and waited for more survivors to show up. We recruited a new survivor here and there, and arrested the occasional soul and fed him alcohol tincture and disinfectant spray in a scientific attempt to understand what these items properties and affects really were.
From time to time my motley crew of men would have to pop a cap in a bandit on sight. I swear he was reaching for a knife.
After a few weeks, and having no luck finding a server during the early alpha that had regular server population, we decided to brand our group, and we called ourselves the Band of Hawk. I petitioned for donations, and within 2 days had over $300 worth of donations from only about the 10 of our community members at the time. I set up a 100 slot mumble server, and yes, a 50 slot DayZ Standalone server.
The Band of Hawk server, after lots of advertising, community recruiting and a promise to keep hackers (to the best of our ability) off our property, we skyrocketed to the top 10 servers worldwide on
.
Our community has since dispersed, but I want to attest that this game is one of the single best MMOFPS masterpieces ever created... and this review is based off of an experience starting from the first day of early access alpha in 2013.
DayZ Standalone is like a fine wine. You will acquire a taste for it. Give it a chance. It's worth more than whatever price tag they can put on it.
You will make many everlasting friendships, and some of the most brooding rivals of any game you will ever play.
99/100.
The Band of Hawk will be locking down Balota once more in late 2015.
See you in Chernarus.
Yours truly,
Kaplan

Clearly 11/10 GOTY, nothing else to add. There is no way you won't like this game.
There are 3 main paths through the game:
1. True pacifist path - you don't kill any single creature. I very much advice you to follow this path at your first playthrough.
2. Neutral path - you killed some, but not everyone. Even if it's called "path" basically it means that you failed both other paths, so try again.
3. Genocide path - you killed everyone, not a creature left alive. Everyone will run away from you in fear, they won't recognize you as human. You are the angel of death and you will go to hell for it, have fun.
This game might not look the best, but everything else (music, gameplay, writing) easilly makes up for its visuals. You won't regret buying this game, I promise.

Undertale is at first an unassuming game that appears to be of the RPGMaker variety, but the overwhelming level of buzz about this game is not in the least incorrect: there's a lot more to this game than the first location might suggest.
The number of innovations to RPG mechanics, as well as callbacks to both the cliches and narrative structures of typical games of the past is just wonderful, and it is a credit to the author's writing that the characters encountered in this game are at once familiar, but not at all tired; a difficult balance to achieve.
To anyone considering playing this game but hasn't yet done so:
Do it, explore it as much as you can, and you may be surprised just how long it sticks with you.

You control a heart, and you have to evade from falling objects with a few variables here and there. The real differing thing here is the way you deal with them. You can attack them and kill them, yes. And you get EXP from this, but there's a different alternative that might actually be better. You can spare enemies after acting a certain way to them. This doesn't get you EXP, but I honestly recommend this route. It's alright, and it's nice.
GRAPHICS AND PERFORMANCE: 30fps lock, but I WILL ♥♥♥♥ING MURDER YOU WITH A PENCIL IF THAT MAKES YOU NOT WANT IT. It runs fine, I don't notice anything, this type of game can get away with it easily. CHARACTERS: I could talk all day about the characters, but spoilers, so I'll pass, sadly. They're all phenominal, though. My favorite was Sans, personally.
EXTRAS: I really need to start talking about soundtracts, because this one was phenominal. I need to buy it. Nao. Wow.
FINAL THOUGHTS:  I feel as if I should give this an 11/10, but nah, that's just cheating. This game does easily earn a 10/10, however. It's ten bucks. Witcher 3 was better IMO, but hey, opinions are like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s. We all have them. I do say you should pick this up. Nao.

Hackers came and ruined the game as we expected, and nothing was done that actually stopped the hackers. Thats not to say they did nothing, but nothing they did stopped hackers, period.
After a few months of supposed hacker improvements, I returned. Most bugs were still there, and this is the period I/we realised that the engine and the core of this game, is not viable for a MMO style game. The bugs, glitches and clunkiness will not and cannot be fixed. Hackers had adapted and new stupid ways of dying was added to the already list of ladder bugs, stair glitches etc.
A lengthy time between then and now, the map has been updated, spawns heavily changed, many new guns and items, and now the story of why this game will never ever improve, and simply dwindle in player base from here on,
I log on with my rediculus gaming computer, usual low fps, clunkiness in controls. I ask myself why there is no populated first person only severs, I remember going back to before standalone release and seeing the overwhelming majority of people (in my communities) stress the importance of realism and first person only over 3rd person wall abusing. I don't understand why ever since, 3rd person is the disguisting majority of servers, and first person is not populated ever. Going into game, within 1 minute my head hurts form the low FPS, jarriness and general clunkiness of the game. I go into third person and finally realize how this game is so appallingly unplayable in first person.
Whilst looting and seeing generally nothing new to the game, same clunky controls and game, general dissapointment, I still kinda have fun looting and progressing my character. I see a few people, all of which try or succeed in killing me with NO communication or interesting gameplay, and I remember the days where people would♥♥♥♥♥♥talk or roleplay, any communication or life in the game, now, 100% mindless laggy killing. I get instantly bled through a wall, then the zombie emerges through the wall and it takes my melee weapon a very long time to kill the zombie, I shred my t-shirt, for the rags to simply dissapear.
My character starts looking pretty cool, I had a hokey stick and sweat pants, then more normal clothes and a welding mask. I look pretty badass. I find sufficient ammunition in a kiosk looking shop, then as I leave the building, my entire inventory vanishes. I continue out of the building looking for a place to relog, when I see my character, pulling out my sledgehammer to kill me. This game is, and forever will be an unplayable piece of spaghetti code, unfit for multiplayer online, and beyond a joke from its improvement since release. This game without the mention of hackers is a dissapointing mess, a pretty arguable moneygrab, and a shame to PC gamers. It's hard to write a review for something that you have a strong urge to kill anyone who doesn't own it. I have never really felt this way towards anything, really. It took me 30 straight minutes to even figure out what to even type here, for ♥♥♥♥s sake. This is the indie darling of the year, a title, which used to be held by Westerado: Doubled Barrelled, and still might be, and what do I think of it.
STORY: The year is 201X. You are a young child who climbs up a mountain, but trips and falls into a cave. It turns out that this cave is the domain of the Monsters, a race that previously lived side by side with humans before a war broke out between the two, the humans forcing the monsters into the cave and forcing them to stay with a barrier. The human finds herself in trouble, when it turns out... well, I'll have to stop there because you need to experience this for yourself. The story is goddamn amazing. It's simple, yes. But it is heartwarming at time, it is funny, it makes you feel so many things. I was actually shaking in fear at parts, that's how good it is.
GAMEPLAY: Simple, except for one aspect I go into a bit later. It's a turn based battle kind of like the Final Fantasy games, except for combat takes place in a box. You control a heart, and you have to evade from falling objects with a few variables here and there. The real differing thing here is the way you deal with them. You can attack them and kill them, yes. And you get EXP from this, but there's a different alternative that might actually be better. You can spare enemies after acting a certain way to them. This doesn't get you EXP, but I honestly recommend this route. It's alright, and it's nice.
GRAPHICS AND PERFORMANCE: 30fps lock, but I WILL ♥♥♥♥ING MURDER YOU WITH A PENCIL IF THAT MAKES YOU NOT WANT IT. It runs fine, I don't notice anything, this type of game can get away with it easily. The game looks pretty good, it has that 8-bit style to it that looks nice. If it isn't your style, alright, but still pick the game up anyway.
CHARACTERS: I could talk all day about the characters, but spoilers, so I'll pass, sadly. They're all phenominal, though. My favorite was Sans, personally.
EXTRAS: I really need to start talking about soundtracts, because this one was phenominal. I need to buy it. Nao. Wow.
FINAL THOUGHTS:  I feel as if I should give this an 11/10, but nah, that's just cheating. This game does easily earn a 10/10, however. It's ten bucks. I don't care if you have to sell your family into slavery, pick this game up. It is easily one of the best games I have played in my life. GOTY? I wouldn't call it that. Witcher 3 was better IMO, but hey, opinions are like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s. We all have them. I do say you should pick this up. Nao.

I bought this game the day of release. It was very fun, there was a lot of bugs but we assumed they could be fixed somewhat easily and quickly, simple quality of life and clunkiness stuff.
Hackers came and ruined the game as we expected, and nothing was done that actually stopped the hackers. Thats not to say they did nothing, but nothing they did stopped hackers, period.
After a few months of supposed hacker improvements, I returned. Most bugs were still there, and this is the period I/we realised that the engine and the core of this game, is not viable for a MMO style game. The bugs, glitches and clunkiness will not and cannot be fixed. Hackers had adapted and new stupid ways of dying was added to the already list of ladder bugs, stair glitches etc.
A lengthy time between then and now, the map has been updated, spawns heavily changed, many new guns and items, and now the story of why this game will never ever improve, and simply dwindle in player base from here on,
I log on with my rediculus gaming computer, usual low fps, clunkiness in controls. I ask myself why there is no populated first person only severs, I remember going back to before standalone release and seeing the overwhelming majority of people (in my communities) stress the importance of realism and first person only over 3rd person wall abusing. I don't understand why ever since, 3rd person is the disguisting majority of servers, and first person is not populated ever. Going into game, within 1 minute my head hurts form the low FPS, jarriness and general clunkiness of the game. I go into third person and finally realize how this game is so appallingly unplayable in first person.
Whilst looting and seeing generally nothing new to the game, same clunky controls and game, general dissapointment, I still kinda have fun looting and progressing my character. I see a few people, all of which try or succeed in killing me with NO communication or interesting gameplay, and I remember the days where people would♥♥♥♥♥♥talk or roleplay, any communication or life in the game, now, 100% mindless laggy killing. I get instantly bled through a wall, then the zombie emerges through the wall and it takes my melee weapon a very long time to kill the zombie, I shred my t-shirt, for the rags to simply dissapear.
My character starts looking pretty cool, I had a hokey stick and sweat pants, then more normal clothes and a welding mask. I look pretty badass. I find sufficient ammunition in a kiosk looking shop, then as I leave the building, my entire inventory vanishes. I continue out of the building looking for a place to relog, when I see my character, pulling out my sledgehammer to kill me. So apparently now there is a hack to completely and instantaneously steal my inventory. This game is, and forever will be an unplayable piece of spaghetti code, unfit for multiplayer online, and beyond a joke from its improvement since release. This game without the mention of hackers is a dissapointing mess, a pretty arguable moneygrab, and a shame to PC gamers. The hackers and the attempts to combat them are the cherry on this disgrace of a game. I wholeheartidly DO NOT recommend this game to anyone, ever. 100 hours of utter and constant dissapointment.

Since the game throws so many terrible puns at the player, it would be easy to conclude that this game is a joke. An empty appeal to the nostalgia of Chrono Trigger, Earthbound and the Final Fantasy series, with less than 5 hours of play time.
That would be unfair.
The puzzles may be simple and the story childish, but the world has so much character that you're bound to have a few smiles, a few laughs and a few shivers along the way. It may even make you appreciate two of the most hated fonts in word processing history.
What the game may lack in visuals, it compensate by an incredible soundtrack, mixing acoustic, orchestral and chiptune. However cringe-inducing some dialogues are, there is a real sense of remorse to be had for your decisions.
The puns may be stupid, but the way Undertale deconstructs RPGs (EXP, LV, SAVES) with regard to what happened on previous playthroughs is extremely clever. The amount of work that has gone through the endings tree and easter eggs is staggering.

A testimony to what can be accomplished by a small team of people when they have a great idea, and passion within them.
This title is a classic earthbound style Role-Playing Game but with an added twist - every single enemy in the game (including bosses) can be spared. No monster has to die. This is done with an extra menu available i combat where you may speak to the enemies and convince them to not kill you. This creates a warm, hilarious atmosphere, although it is not afraid to give you powerful, emotional sequences as well. One of the endings spooked me for sure, showing how masterfully crafted the narrative of the game is, as it delves into many genres.
From the first seconds of this title, the player is thrust into an unknown world. They are greeted with charm, and that charm stays with them the whole way through. Toby Fox has written dialogue of such calibre never before seen in video game format. Every character has a distinct style when they speak, every character has a different comedic device they use, even if it is just a simple minion. From the bumbling baddie, the kind caring mother, or even a wiggling pile of gelatin, the different people you encounter ooze charisma.
I went into the game expecting a short, but fun, experience and boy was I surprised when I found that there was more content than I originally thought. With three different endings (neutral, genocide, and true pacifist), there is some unexpected replay value, that takes every single battle of the game into account. In fact, some bosses will not be fought in every playthrough, showing just how much choice the player truly has. This is something that has been tried again and again in RPG's, but in my opinion hasn't been done as skillfully since Chrono Trigger.
Although the writing and combat is the true drawing factor of Undertale, the score and scenery are no slouch either. The art style for all adversaries is distinct, and jaw-dropping. The game takes pixelated graphics to a level I had yet to see, and when it diverts from the pixel look at a certain part of the finale it is done in such a manner that it leaves you feeling exactly how it should. The soundtrack of this game pulls you into all of the emotional scenes, and I am not ashamed to admit that the culmination of sound and writing brought tears to my eyes in the final minutes of the game. A particular favourite of mine was Undyne's theme which is filled with the urgency, power, and duty of the character.
Overall, Undertale was a quick but entirely satisfying game that I implore all to play. This is what the Steam platform has helped create, wonderful indie developements that get the game out there for all to play. Do not miss out on this exquisite experience. Undertale is an instant classic that should be held up as a triumph of comedic Role-Playing Games.

Do you hate yourself? Do you want to sink a sickening number of hours into a game that has skeletons you can date (and also kill... if that's what floats your boat), dogs you can pet, Moms you can flirt with, and tears you can cry? If so, Undertale is the game for you. If not, Undertale is still the game for you. It is a game for everyone.
Undertale will destroy your life. It will make you reconsider everything you have known. If you are a graphic designer, be warned, comic sans and papyrus are still awful font choices in any kind of product, no matter what this game may lead you to believe. Don't even think about it.
Most reviews of this game are spoiler free, for good reason! If you are thinking, even for a second, that you might want this game, stop right now and buy it.
For those who need a little more convincing, I'll try to narrow this game to my favourite of its features.
-The Endings. There are three distinct endings (that I currently know of, who knows, there are probably more.). One for each extreme of 'kindness', and the neutral ending. However, every little choice you make is reflected in the ending, even if it's a single line of dialogue. All the different endings make the game have massive replay value, and although I'd put the game as being around 5 hrs long on a neutral route, you can put so much longer in.
- The Soundtrack. It absolutely makes the game. I can't really talk technical terms; to me its nice tunes and sweet bloopy beepy stuff that reminds me of the Shovel Knight theme, but it's so good! Also there are secrets within the music that speeding up and slowing down the tracks can reveal. That's pretty cool guys.
-The Choice Mechanic. I didn't really know what to call this, but without really knowing it, all the choices you make are having an effect on your game, and on subsequent games. I was very shocked to see that characters remembered some choices I made, even after restarting the game. Without spoiling anything, the game seems cute and simple, until you replay it and realise you are the worst person in the world.
-The Characters. Every single character is lovable and rememberable. Even if you play through once and don't really like someone, play through again and you'll see a totally new aspect to them that you had missed before. Bitterness at being beaten by them aside, I can't think of a single character that I didn't like. Also, the 'mobs' are adorable. I love them all. The fighting style differs for each mob, and so half the fun of fighting, or sparing, is working out how to avoid their attacks, or reach a point at which you can spare them. It's fun to work out, and makes the game a lot more challenging than a standard attack/defense mechanic.
-Representation! So, to many this may not be important, but to me it made my game just that more enjoyable and unique. One of my favourite things is how the game does not ask you if you are a boy or a girl. You are 'The Human'. You have your name, but your character looks the same no matter who you choose to be called. The character is referred to as 'they'. This, for me, takes away the stress of 'how will my gender impact the gameplay?' 'am I supposed to be a male character?', that most games face me with. The human simpily is, and their gender plays absolutely no effect on the game. You can date anyone and everyone, the only concern really being that the character is a child so really they shouldn't be dating anyone. There are also (to my memory) two same sex relationships, and two opposite sex relationships portrayed in game, which may be nice for some people to hear. There are many other aspects that make this game LGBTQA* friendly, but I'm trying to not spoil too much of it (and keep this review a relatively decent length). This is a really neat aspect for a game that is so highly rated, for it to apporach gender and sexuality casually, but without the 'token gay' characters a lot of games seem to include. I like this a lot.
It's very difficult to think of negative aspects of this game. I would say that the 'Genocide' route is frustratingly difficult, which has led me to rage quit on numerous occasions. This detracts from my experience a small amount, because I have seen so many spoilers for what happens at the end of the route, and feel so close, yet so far. Seriously, Toby Fox. You're a sadist. Absolute sadist.

As my hours state, I put a lot of effort, time and hope into this game. Here is my overall educated opinion and thought process based from my experience of DayZ. I truly want this game to work, I see its concept and it's fascinating, engaging and fun. I even had a positive review up from a few years back, encouraging patience and persistence.
Two years later, an update.
Also, I'm aware devs are trying to remove bad reviews as "spam" "trolling". I'm hoping such childishness won't happen here. Reviews exist for a reason.
Back in 2013-2015, the developers gave us some status reports as the weeks went by, revealing to us their plans of what they'd like to do with the game, and where they'd like it to be. They even released a "Q1 - Q4" chart, claiming cars, planes, loot system and zombies would be in an impressive state by the end of 2014/2015. It was even claimed that BETA would be released in 2015, even console release.
None of this ever came. The failure to meet these plans were never addressed. Status reports just continued like NOTHING was said in the first place. Immese complaint from thousands were catagorised as mindless spam instead of feedback, as if the development team were sticking their hands over their ears and ignoring the blatent mess they had on their shoulders.
As each patch was implemented, it felt like a piece of the game was being built upon, as the developers intended, yet another part would crumble. An example being, Zombie AI was updated to involve stealth, but your weapons would glitch out of existence commonly. The guns would then be fixed, but you could die from walking into a shed. The shed would then be put on "a list of things to be fixed" and 3 years later, it would persist, along with many other issues that were never solved, despite being *PROMISED* (key word) to be fixed.
When 0.61 / 0.62 was announced recently, I came back after a year of not playing to see how things have changed. Mostly because, deep down, I truly want this game to work.
The new trees and sounds were impressive. The zombies were EVERYWHERE, and relentless. A massive improvement. I liked it a lot.
However... the loot system is still difficult to handle. I starved to death to lack of finding any food at all. The only way I could survive the next life was spamming apple trees for 10 minutes, which, when you take into account the purpose of a video game, doesn't feel like fun at all for the average gaming experience.
Being forced to exploit a mechanic, additionally knowing there are specific "loot routes" that if you do not follow, puts you at a disadvantage to try anything else... all to remain alive? It doesn't provide immersion, it provides the feeling of systematic thinking, which is a constant reminder you're playing a game of method, as opposed to travelling with your character's story.
Strangely the trees had a small chance of yeilding apples per *search* which makes little sense.
However I continued on playing, trying to give this game as much as a chance as possible.
I got to NW airfield, I found a few bits and bobs, a gun, some military gear; things were going smoothly.
I was then attacked on sight by a random bandit in the tents. He died. "Finally, I remember why I played this game!" I thought to myself. I cleared the area, absolutley NO ONE or ANY ZOMBIES were around me.
My game then crashed. This wasn't the first time this session... I loaded my character back up. I was bleeding heavily and being attacked by zombies that had respawned instantly. I killed them and went to bandage yet I fell unconcious. I woke up again, to then be killed on sight by someone who had logged into the tents in front of me.
Had it have been a fair fight, I'd understand, but it was the faulty game mechanics and unstable crashing that had me killed, with odd robotic movement controls that made evading and firing back a chore.
"I remember why I stopped playing." I thought to myself.
This game is a chore to play, to progress to a point where you can engage in your surrounding enviroment is painful. There is no feeling of immersion in an apolalypse. It's a methodical, illogical grind that throws you into a world of 70% kill-on-sight bandits, 25% glitches and bugs that disrupt your experience, and only 5% respectable, talkative, interactive players.
I want this game to work, so very desperately. The concept is incredible.
But when a development team makes such a poor choice to attempt merging the "enfusion" engine to replace the older one, complicating every update they've made for the past 4 years...
I have one thing to say to it.
The game is in the wrong hands.

Since the game throws so many terrible puns at the player, it would be easy to conclude that this game is a joke. An empty appeal to the nostalgia of Chrono Trigger, Earthbound and the Final Fantasy series, with less than 5 hours of play time.
That would be unfair.
The puzzles may be simple and the story childish, but the world has so much character that you're bound to have a few smiles, a few laughs and a few shivers along the way. It may even make you appreciate two of the most hated fonts in word processing history.
What the game may lack in visuals, it compensate by an incredible soundtrack, mixing acoustic, orchestral and chiptune. However cringe-inducing some dialogues are, there is a real sense of remorse to be had for your decisions.
The puns may be stupid, but the way Undertale deconstructs RPGs (EXP, LV, SAVES) with regard to what happened on previous playthroughs is extremely clever. The amount of work that has gone through the endings tree and easter eggs is staggering.

What is there to be said that hasn't been already?
You know what this game is. Bar and none. You have seen it. Everywhere. E v e r y w h e r e. You have seen everyone rave about it and sing it's praises. No one will shut up about this game!
And that is for good reason. Undertale isn't just a game to me. It is an experience. It has an absolutely fantastic (and hilarious) memorable cast of characters who, when they aren't giving me stitches in laughter, are making me cry sweet, pure puppy dog tears. The story is absolutely incredible, in which you play as a fallen human who fell into a monster world, after a war between the 2 species which lead to the monsters being banished underground, and saying anything else will spoil your experience. I'll just say that this game plays like a choose your own adventure book, making the path you choose really stick with you no matter what. I have pure faith every ending will leave you happy. And there isn't just the main 3 endings either (Neutral ending, where you choose who lives and dies, Genocide, where you kill everything you see and kill every enemy in each area until none remain, and Pacifist, the complete opposite)! Any person you kill and let live WILL affect the story. Every. Single. One. And if you are like me, you always felt SOME remorse for killing SOMEONE, due to how well developed every character is. There is no hero or villan in Undertale. Everyone has their good side, and their bad side. Even the FINAL BOSS of the neutral run can have his goodness inside of him! The only true heroes or villans are the players, and the game definetly lets you know this. And the only way to truly experience this game is to do the main 3 endings, to BECOME THE HERO, BECOME THE VILLIAN, AND BECOME THE VICTOR! You do this with the most unique combat system I have EVER seen in years. You have 2 options, 1. Use the FIGHT option, and with some well timed button presses, kill the enemy, or 2. I bought this when it was first released for early access.
During that time I have committed to the game and can confidently say I am familiar with the experience it currently provides. Keep in mind the experience may change as more patches are released, but this is my thoughts, and feelings, towards the game presently, I will update the review if they change. I will not talk about the specific mechanics of the game during this review, just a general tackling of the game's holistic experience.
This game brings out the worst in people. Fact. You will be thinking "oOoO, that sounds interesting.." well, it is not. You will be on the recieving end, like the rest of us.
It is a Clan game, and not a solo survival game with other people around you. You lose, often, if you havnt joined a clan of about 10 people, this game cannot be mastered by you and your mate laboring hard for 100 hours. Trust me, we've tried. "Losing", in this case, refers to being dirt poor almost all the time because your base only lasts about 4 game evenings (about 8-10 hours of peak time) before it is annaihilated by a clan. Worse still, and bringing me back to the first point, people tend be intentionaly hurtful to your experience of the game. Raiding and stealing is fine and expected because that it part of the game. BUT to destroy your base and then build a container around you decorated with signs marked with insults so you read them all before having to console 'kill' yourself just to respawn is sadistic. Keep in mind immediately after coping with that you have to start all over again. Starting all over again means giving up those 8-10 hours of, for the most part, hitting rocks and chopping trees, before you are inevitably raided again.
Why do people lock up others? or build spikes around where you sleep? or plant sign posts with rude pictures and offensive words on them for you to wake up to alongside the ashes of your former base? SImple, because every other player has had this happen to them. So in order to stick at the game like the brave soldiers we are we embrace that way of life, and as soon as you can raid another person you feel the urge to take revenge and laugh at the sadness that the victim will feel when then come back online. Even though the person you're raiding often isnt the person who f***** you.
Dont buy the game if you value your time and sense of wellbeing. Pick a different one. Care about yourself, You and your mate should play a better coop to pass time. But if you do play rust, remember it is a CLAN game, find a clan quick.
Alternatively, if you are one such potential bad guy then this game needs you! come join the clusterf*** of genuinely unpleasant people.

Rust has had its ups and downs like every alpha, but unlike mosy devs facepunch have a strong realationship with the communuity. We cried for rocket launchers, we got em. We wanted skins, we got em. Rust is a game which sells itself and you get your moneys worth.
The game play is great and brutal at the same time, solo players have no chance of surviving on a high population server. If you do you can almost 100% guarantee your base will be raided and you will wake up on the beach. This game isnt for casuals, unless you play on a heavily modded server which i dont recommend.
The community isnt the best but what do you expect for a post apocalyptic survival game? Thing are ment to be rough, theres no easy mode which brings out the inner savage of people. Try to be friendly and make buddies and you will go no where fast. This is Rust not the Sims.

When this game first came out, I found it in my queue and read the description. It sounded...mediocre, and the graphics deterred me. Something about the lack of emotion in the chara(cter)'s face was unsettling. So I ignored it. But for some reason, it still left some interest in me.
I love YouTube and watch it every day, so when I saw Steam Train play this, I thought "Maybe they'll be a good way to see if it's a good game."
I got hooked.
The first thing the tell you is "He bought too many games." But later, they say NOT to watch before you play the game, and I, unlike most of the audience, didn't.
I spoiled everything for myself.
But it still came to be my second favorite game of all time. Right behind Ocarina of Time. Nostalgia is an uncomparable emotion. (Edit: This has now become my favorite game of all time.)
But anyways, I've yet to complete a single run, but believe me, I'll have upwards of 20 by the time I finally quit.
So do yourself a favor, and buy this game before you spoil it for yourself. Don't even look up walkthroughs where you get stuck, it might spoil something amazing.
But if you want a rating on each individual segment, here you go.
Music 10/10 - The music is amazing, catchy, and a major part of the story. Yeah. How many games use songs to tie loose ends? 1. Undertale. Pay attention to the music, and the story will reveal itself. Which brings us to the next point.
Story 15/10 - This story is better and more complex than the entire Legend of Zelda FRANCHISE. Everything has a meaning, and what doesn't have any meaning, there are theories for. Play it for the story if nothing else. You'll cry, laugh, get angry OH so angry, and realize that this game has given you a new perspective on the world.
Graphics 8/10 - Compared to what it could have been A.K.A. 3D with mouth syncs and everything, it's crap. But how it's used, that makes it good. Sprites have so much detail, showing emotions and thoughts. What N64 game could do that as well as this game does? Not one I've played. And if you're an Earthbound fan, this was heavily influenced by those games.
Comedy 3/10 to 10/10 - The reason I say this is because most of the comedy is random and just funny because it's stupid. Not everyone likes that. But for those who do, this is on point, making me laugh more than any game before.
Overall 11/10
AND I CAN ONLY COUNT TO 3.
But seriously, one of, if not the, best game ever made.
And just a tip or two, go for pascifist before you do genocide, and try to make connections. Leave no rock unturned, because it's probably a key item in the story's plot.

Time to revise this review, because I made the original one under a period of intense emotional stress.
Let me get the cons out of the way before I gush about this being one of the better gaming experiences of 2015 for me.
Well, the game's too damn short (made by one guy, so I understand) and for what it is has very little replay value (since the game begs you NOT to replay it after you get the best ending). The puzzles stutter erratically in difficulty from "childishly easy" to "I had to look up 5 walkthroughs to figure it out", and the characters, though lovable, are archetypal as hell. Also, the best healing items are at the beginning, so you need to do some intense backtracking to buy more of them for most of the late-game boss fights.
Now the goods? The battle system is amazingly unique, all the characters are enjoyable (even the ♥♥♥♥ing flower) and the story is one of the better ones I've ever played through this century (pay attention, Life is Strange). Creativity really isn't dead within the gaming industry, and contrary to the traumatizing experience most people seem to have had with it, I've come out a better person because of this game.
The real gameplay isn't much to look at beyond the unique blend of Earthbound and Touhou, so if you like a story-heavy game that's still fun to play (which seems to be really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hard these days), play it.
Play it for the mind-♥♥♥♥ing meta-game fight with a power-hungry flower.
Play it for the Bad Ending boss, which is a combination of technically the easiest paired with the absolute hardest encounter in the game.
Play it for the quaint sense of humor, and lovely mix of gravity and levity.
Play it for a wonderfully written (if badly expositioned) lore.
Play it to read the negative reviews, which are a combination of good points and enough salt to properly season every plate of french fries in North America.
Play it.

What is there to say about Undertale that hasn't already been said?
A lot of people have been talking badly about this game lately because of its persistent and somewhat annoying fanbase, especially due to the recent GameFAQS Best Game Ever poll.
Do NOT skip this game or talk bad about it because of its fanbase, it has a loving and dedicated fanbase for a reason.
Undertale is one of the most creative, charming, hilarious, and heartwarming games that I've ever played.  Its soundtrack is phenomenal, and you quickly fall in love with each and every character that this game throws at you.  The dialogue is easily quotable and some of the best I've seen in a game.  Perhaps the most impressive quality of this game its unique gimmick.  I'm not going to spoil it here if you don't know it, but just know that it's unlike anything ever seen in a game before.
So yeah, I would reccomend this game to anybody.  As a fan of the Mother/Earthbound series, I adore when a game can mix fun, emotion, and laughs flawlessly, and Undertale does this just as well (if not better in some situations).  Is Undertale the greatest game ever made?  ...  Probably not.  But Undertale IS one of the most satisfying and unforgettable experiences that gaming has to offer.  Buy this game, pronto.

Man, i so wanted this game to be a better version of the mod, and i come on to check every once in awhile to see the progress, but the sad truth is this...
It's alpha.  its been alpha. and it seems it will continue to be in alpha stage for a long time. I paid the money to support the development team, and was very hopeful, but this game is practically unplayable at this stage.
If you want to enjoy the real DAYZ, i would recommend getting the ARMA II set and play the original mod. I've had a hell of a lot more fun playing the modded version of arma, than this developing standalone. don't be duped by the "very positive" standing in the user reviews.
PROS: biggest one is people are friendlier here. this game is still under development. they warn you that it clearly is in alpha, so maybe some day this game will live up to the name of what DAYZ can be. There are a lot of new features/actions that are not in the mod, and it could lead to a interesting adventure with new things to worry about, or new things to try. thats about all i see for pros.
CONS: its really hard to stick with it at the moment. if you played the original mod, you know what i mean. you spawn with practically nothing. more importantly, no weapon but your fists. and you can't even harm zombies with your punches so its useless. zombies chase you endlessly and even go through walls so buildings don't help. in the mod, they have to walk indoors, giving you a chance, but here... you're screwed. everything is scarce which is part of the "survive" thing, but it takes hours to run to a town and scavenge for breadcrumbs and garbage you can't use. most modded servers have bicycles or prebuilt cars. people are generally more friendly and trusting here, but i think its because its so impossible to survive on your own.
BOTTOM LINE:
its way too "early" for this to really be an enjoyable experience. i quote early because its been in alpha for such a long time i wonder if the developers have lost their drive to complete it. seriously, download DayZ commander, get the arma 2 necessities to play the game, and have way more fun. i've had some hilarious moments there. like finally meeting a friend who helped me raid and loot a ton of food and guns from another group, only to try and escape via chopper, which i crashed and perma-killed both of us because i didn't know how to fly well enough. I would crash it again for those laughs.

Undertale's gameplay is simplistic and minimally interactive. The bullet hell minigame is something you would only have to play for 5 seconds in a WarioWare game, but here it is the center piece of the combat. It is a really dumb mechanic, and one of the most abstract and asinine ways to contextualize the player's input I've ever seen.
There are very few additional systems in the game for the player to interact with, things that might be taken for granted in other RPGs. No skills, no stats, there are only 2 inventory slots, there's no overworld, it's completely linear for the most part and so on.
Furthermore, the breaking of the fourth wall is a particularly lazy and pretentious story telling method for anything that isn't pure comedy. Is it still 1998 here, and everyone's impressed that Pycho Mantis knows you played Castlevania? Hidden save files and commenting on the player's meta gaming is not clever. Any game that has good storytelling and engaging, properly contextualized mechanics has no need to break simulation and rib the player for playing the videogame like it's a videogame. A more impressive game would be able to tell this story using its characters, and give the player something engaging to do while it was doing that.

What's the goal?
There isn't really any underlying goal to the game, no environmental factor to overcome or point to reach. The game play comes from the interaction with other players and environment.
How are the player interactions?
Poor. Most players will aim to kill you, or simply destroy your shelter(s) while you're offline.
Are shelters safe?
No. Any shelter you build can be easily destroyed for relatively low cost. Additionally, it can be destroyed while you're offline and 9/10 times will be. Shelters should absoloutely be raidable, but rust takes it a step too far by making it a simple task to completely demolish even large structures in little to no time, so that it can be done in the span of an hour.
What items are there?
A lot of great survival items, building items and tools. It gets weird however, since players can also accumulated military grade items such as C4, Rocket launchers, AK47's and Machine guns.
Is it balanced?
No. Knowledge is created via blue prints, which persist between server resets. This means, players who have been on a server longer will be able to build AK's and all the aforementioned items, while you'll start with a rock.
How is development?
The developers maintain a development blog which is a great layer of transparancy. However, updates seem to be generally quite slow, and the direction the game takes is constantly changing, and seems to favour militarization and new weapons (which seems to conflict with the core values of the game).
Conclusion.
I wouldn't recommend this game, it's made a lot of progress, but it's still about a year or two away from being a complete game. Additionally, it doesn't really capture the "survival" aspect that it campaigns on, and it's too far gone in the wrong direction. It would be great if your weapons maxed out at a much lower level to keep player interactions tense and to give more meaning to building a shelter.

So as a player since the legacy version of rust here is my review. The legacy version was horrible, gameplay was too simple and too easy. Hackers everywhere and no way to stop them. Thankfully Garry noticed all of the flaws in the unity version that was used in the legacy version and decided to remake rust on a more up to date unity engine.
I loved the new rust as it came out. Everything ran great, the gameplay was flawless, and it gave me hundreds of hours of gameplay with my friends and community to make giant bases and wage war on other groups. Recently however (last 4-5 months) it has become impossible to play. The performance has got so bad that i get an average of 8 FPS. And i got a computer that can max out everything on ultra settings and get over 100+ fps. Yes i have older hardware but 2 GTX 680's getting 10 FPS on a sandbox shooter is just wrong.
Garry and the team have countlessly noted that their performance sucked. And it would be fixed this week, next week, next month, in 2 months, in 3 more weeks, etc. As i continued to wait, and wait. It was months that i could not play the game with my friends. Months i could not play something i paid for.
The more stuff they update and the more content they add it seems to only make the game worse. Every single update they have done my FPS has got worse and worse. I am a pretty patient person but when i got to wait more than 6 months for a optimization fix that still has not been released. Nope.
The game is great, addictive, and the weekly updates is nice. However the players are toxic, finding friends to game with on here is nearly impossible as everyone just shoots you in the face and insults you or stands outside your home and threaten to kill you in real life and "hack/ddos" your computer unless you give them your stuff. I am one of those players that tried very hard to be friendly, not shoot people on sight, help new people with gear and show them how to play, only for them to use the very bow and arrow i gave them to kill me.
Garry/Facepunch/Rust Team need to realize that 80%+ of their players have older hardware. And a lot of them have nVidia. I have tried playing this on my AMD computer and the FPS difference is sickening. It seems like they are providing performance support for their own choice of hardware and the rest of them can go shove it.

I came in as a casual gamer related a hard core player. I'm not usually a fan of gaming and play very sparingly, but I love this game. I enjoy games with great stories. Those are amazing games for me, and I don't like games with overly complicated mechanics.
That is Undertale.
Here is the twist though.
This isn't just a story. It is an experience that changes with every choice the player makes. I did a neutral run (and felt terrible for killing a character) first followed by a pacifist route I'm not ready to leave. (I'm avoiding the genocide run right now. I'm too emotionally invested in these characterst to kill them.) As many other reviews will tell you, this game and the characters in it don't let you forget things you did in your last run just because you clicked reset. They make it obvious that there is no true reset. Its like "forgive and forget" except there is no forget. If certain characters are killed, they may not show up in other runs. You can't befriend certain characters because killed others. You show kindness to some characters, and they show up later to help you. All of your actions reflect back on you even if you try to reset.
I don't get this invested in games. Every details matters in this game, and the humor and heartbreak stay with you. That makes this game the exception.
So, you should play it if you feel inclined.
Overall, its a pretty weird departure from the first Cave Story, but it was nice seeing grown up Toroko. Still a good game though.

It's good but at the same time, I think that's what's killing it for a lot of people. People are overhyping it to fantastical points and it really ruins the experience for others.
However, that's the biggest complaint, honestly. All my bad experiences with the game have just come from my expectations being really high for this game thanks to the interwebs. For 10 dollars (possibly cheaper when it goes on sale), this game is definitely an experience that's worth it.
The combat is a fun bullet-hell turn based system that is accompanied by a well done soundtrack that I still listen to often. I don't really like turn based systems because it always felt kind of slow but with the dodging of enemy attacks and the possibility to always spare enemies, the combat was still fun and refreshing compared to other turn based games I had played before. Especially if you play the Pacifist route, where you have to keep dodging and try to do the correct actions in the right order to get the enemy to like you.
Soundtrack, as I stated before, is really good. Each important moment has it's own song to go along with it and now when I listen to the songs on Youtube or on my phone, it just brings me back to the moments where the song starts playing.
Now for the big part, the story. I'm trying to keep this spoiler free so all I will really say is that....
It's pretty good.
The humor and likability of the characters are honestly the best part of my experience with Undertale. The closest example I can think of to describe the humor is the Internet.
Like, seriously.
If you are a dank Internet kid, I think you would enjoy the humor and presentation of this game a lot. It's quirky and very enjoyable for those who browse reddit, tumblr, etc.
I did expect something alot more emotional because of all the hype I was reading (This goes into my point at the beginning). Towards the end of my True Pacifist run, it really felt started to feel like something out of a Shounen manga like Naruto or One Piece. It just felt REALLY cheesy rather than the "emotional moments that made me cry" (-Some person in this review section) that people have been praising like crazy. There have been no points where I felt the need to cry where as other people have apparantly broken down in tears even when I watched the Genocide Run.
Maybe I'm a heartless ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of a flower.
Nonetheless, still a very enjoyable experience with nice twists and turns. I would definitely recommend this game to others as it has a lot of inside jokes that can be made between you and your friends (Your real life friends). In addition, if you do end up liking it, there's always a humongous fanbase and fandom with extras just waiting for you at the end. Someone even made a mod that adds a new boss battle called "Undertale Red" (and the mod runs at 60 fps, god bless).
Overall,
Temmie / 10

I came in as a casual gamer related a hard core player. I'm not usually a fan of gaming and play very sparingly, but I love this game. I enjoy games with great stories. Those are amazing games for me, and I don't like games with overly complicated mechanics.
That is Undertale.
Here is the twist though.
This isn't just a story. It is an experience that changes with every choice the player makes. I did a neutral run (and felt terrible for killing a character) first followed by a pacifist route I'm not ready to leave. (I'm avoiding the genocide run right now. I'm too emotionally invested in these characterst to kill them.) As many other reviews will tell you, this game and the characters in it don't let you forget things you did in your last run just because you clicked reset. They make it obvious that there is no true reset. Its like "forgive and forget" except there is no forget. If certain characters are killed, they may not show up in other runs. You can't befriend certain characters because killed others. You show kindness to some characters, and they show up later to help you. All of your actions reflect back on you even if you try to reset.
I don't get this invested in games. Every details matters in this game, and the humor and heartbreak stay with you. That makes this game the exception.
So, you should play it if you feel inclined.
Overall, its a pretty weird departure from the first Cave Story, but it was nice seeing grown up Toroko. Still a good game though.

Is it sad? At some moments, yes.
Is it funny? Yes.
Does it have good music? HELL yes.
Does it have an interesting gameplay? Quite. At least the combination of classic JRPG with danmaku and point 'n click adventure elements is quite new.
Is it the best RPG ever done? IMHO, not close to that. It surely is a good game, but a rather small one and with under average graphics (don't tell that's because it's indie or meant to be minimalist, just look at other games in the same category and you'll know what I'm talking about).
I admit I fail to understand all the hype around this game; as an old JRPG fan (and a deep fan of Mother series) I found it OK and entertaining as long that it lasts, but not deserving this much attention. I believe the trend will fade out in some months when people will be back to normal games, 'cause you really can't squeeze out that much from a game you finish in 3-4 hours - yes, even if you're supposed to finish it at least three times to really understand the whole point of it.
I would still recommend it, even if not for its full price.

Rust is a survival game created by Facepunch Studios. Inspired by games like DayZ, Minecraft and Stalker – Rust aims to create a hostile environment in which emergent gameplay can flourish. The aim of the game is to survive. To do this the player should gather resources. Hitting a tree with a rock will give you wood, hitting a rock with a rock will give you rock and ore. You can then craft a hatchet from the wood and rock, allowing you to gather faster. You can go out and hunt a variety of wildlife such as boars, chickens, rabbits, bears, wolves and deer. Once you have killed an animal you can butcher it to gather its meat and skin. You can craft a fire using wood and cook the meat inside the fire. Then you can eat. You face two major dangers in game. Rust is a multiplayer game, so there will be other players trying to survive in the same way that you are. Unfortunately for you they can find you, kill you and take your stuff. Fortunately for you – you can kill them and take their stuff. Or maybe you can make friends and help each other survive. Rust’s world is harsh – so you might need to make friends to survive. The environment is not kind. Bears and wolves will chase and kill you. Falling from a height will kill you. Being exposed to radiation for an extended period will kill you. Starving will kill you. Being cold will kill you.

Dont know what to write, so I will write a recipie for pancakes.
ingredients
100g plain flour
2 eggs
300ml semi-skimmed milk
1 tbsp sunflower oil or vegetable, plus extra for frying
pinch salt
Method
Blending in the flour: Put the flour and a pinch of salt into a large mixing bowl and make a well in the centre. Crack the eggs into the middle, then pour in about 50ml milk and 1 tbsp oil. Start whisking from the centre, gradually drawing the flour into the eggs, milk and oil. Once all the flour is incorporated, beat until you have a smooth, thick paste. Add a little more milk if it is too stiff to beat.
Finishing the batter: Add a good splash of milk and whisk to loosen the thick batter. While still whisking, pour in a steady stream of the remaining milk. Continue pouring and whisking until you have a batter that is the consistency of slightly thick single cream. Traditionally, people would say to now leave the batter for 30 mins, to allow the starch in the flour to swell, but there’s no need.
Getting the right thickness: Heat the pan over a moderate heat, then wipe it with oiled kitchen paper. Ladle some batter into the pan, tilting the pan to move the mixture around for a thin and even layer. Quickly pour any excess batter into a jug, return the pan to the heat, then leave to cook, undisturbed, for about 30 secs. Pour the excess batter from the jug back into the mixing bowl. If the pan is the right temperature, the pancake should turn golden underneath after about 30 secs and will be ready to turn.
Flipping pancakes: Hold the pan handle, ease a fish slice under the pancake, then quickly lift and flip it over. Make sure the pancake is lying flat against base of the pan with no folds, then cook for another 30 secs before turning out onto a warm plate. Continue with the rest of the batter, serving them as you cook or stack onto a plate. You can freeze the pancakes for 1 month, wrapped in cling film or make them up to a day ahead.

What a game, what a lovely game!
A lot of people recommended Undertale, so I decided to give it a shot even though I was never a huge fan of old school rpg's. What I got was something quite more than that. This game takes you for a real rollercoaster ride of emotions. This game had multiple hilarious moments, but then there were also points in the game that got me all tear-eyed, which is something that doesn't happen very often.
The cast of characters in this game is brilliant, and all of them have their own unique personalities and backstories. The music is superb, and it can set the mood very well. There is also a suprising amount of variety in it. This game even managed to do something totally unique with it's combat system, and I gotta give the devs credit for doing something totally new. The way you play the game will effect the story, and there are multiple unique and satisfying(each in their own way) endings that you might get and certain things change the game completely so there is plenty of replay value here. I don't wanna spoil any story details here, because it really is truly brilliant, and something you should experience yourself. There are so many clever little details sprinkled throughout the game, and some of those are the most basic video game features possible that end up being important narrative elements. There was not a single point in Undertale where I wasn't invested in what was happening.
However, Undertale does have some minor issues. I wish the game would give you more dialogue options, usually you get to choose from 2 or 3, and one of those often ends up being the obvious wrong choise. Also, there are times when the illusion of choise is quite apparent. Visually the game is not exactly too appealing,1 might even say that it looks quite terrible at times. Quality consistency would have been nice. Last but not least, I do think the genocide run could have been handled a bit better. I wish you wouldn't have to do hours of grinding to do it, and yes, I know the game is actively trying to make you have a Bad time so you'd stop but grinding is not the best way to handle that.
But even with it's (minor) flaws, it's still 1 of the best games I've played in years, and it is possibly my favourite indie game of all time. It is quite rare to play a game that totally blows all your expectations right out the window like this game did for me. Do yourself a favor and go play it!

Well then!
I went into this game with some healthy scepticism, as I always do whenever a game receives as much acclaim as it does. Did this game meet those expectations? I... I actually think it might have.
My style as a gamer is to go against the grain. If the game instructs me to go right, my first instinct is to go left. By the same token, if a game world presents killing as the explicitly Wrong Thing To Do, then I'm going to go ahead and kill everything I meet. Literally all conflicts in the game can be resolved peacefully, but I obviously had no intention of doing any such thing.
Much to my surprise, the game then made a great effort to make me feel bad about this. Some of the ways it does this are more effective than others, but it still is a testament to the game's writing and presentation that I actually felt something for a world that I determined very early on that I was going to run roughshod over.
Nevertheless, they all fell down.
That left me with an ending that was genuinely surprising and disturbing.
I thus can say that Undertale is a worthy investment. It's cheap and short. Go give it a try and see how it treats you.
Edit:
Now that I've played the Pacifist run... hmmm. Yeah. Game of the Year, I think.

SUMMARY: A witty, subversive, heartfelt and clever game that uses old JRPG displays and ideas to give you a clever and complex game with lots of memorable characters.  Not a game for those unfamiliar with RPG games of the past, but one for people looking for something smart and different.
Summarizing Undetale is a bit difficult because there's really two parts to it:
* Classic old-school JRPG mechanics . . .
* . . . and what it does with them.
So we know the formula.  Walk around, talk to people, get into menu-driven fights, beat enemies, solve some puzzles, continue.  Undertale does that, only it throws in new mechanics, plenty of surprises, and replayability because of said surprises.
The story sounds simple - Monsters and Humans warred, and the Monsters were driven beneath the earth.  As a youngster who suddenly finds themselves in the Monster Realm due to a fall into a deep caver, you instantly face . . . a motherly goat-woman.  She wants to protect you, but eventually you want to venture further . . . and it begins.
And twists, turns, gets weird, gets surprising, gets disturbing.
In Undertale you get to make various decisions, mostly related to combat - which will affect what happens in the game.  See, you can go and whack monsters via some simple arcadey elements.  Or you can interact with them nonviolently.  Or both depending on what you do.  Between simple arcade-like puzzles to deciding what interactions work, there's lots of choices, strategy, and tricks to get further into the game.
As you get further you unlock the story of the world, meet more characters, and as you may guess, not all is as it seems.  There's always something new around the corner, and even when it's frustrating, you can eventually figure out a puzzle or an enemy to get to the next section - where something new awaits you.
Your decisions in all of this matter and will affect what happens down the line.  Undertale also doesn't hold your had on the result of your actions, a nice deviation from its roots.
Is it worth it?  Yes - if you want something different and surprising and are familiar with some genre conventions.  It's a game for people that know their games and want to be surprised - and does it ever deliver surprises.  If you are at all curious it IS worth purchasing as it is not only good, it represents a historic point in game development, repurposing many mechanics and ideas into something new and challenging.

Undertale is a game where you play as a human child who falls through Mount Ebott into the ruins of what used to be a place where "monsters" were exiled after a war between them and humans. From there you beging an adventure like no-other, filled with memorable characters, witty humour and honest, sad, tearful moments. I'm not going into details here, I'm just going to say the game has a great story, lovely characters you will instantly fall in love with and a great story. The best thing is you don't have to kill anyone. Infact it's much preferred you didn't kill any of the various creatures you encounter while traveling through the ruins since this will inpact how your story will turn out.
The gameplay is very much like any JRPG you might be familiar with. The visuals are simplified and have this nostalgic gameboyish feel to it. The gameplay is fun and keeps you as an active participant at all times and the music is absolutely fantastic, probably the best I've heard in a very long time. True dat.
Undertale is a game you absolutely don't want to spoil yourself by going through gameplay videos and plot twists on youtube before trying it out. It's best enjoyed while going in blind. Even the start of the game already has a big twist to it and you will probably soon start giving the game some credit for being extremely crafty with its setting.
Go give this game a go, I can almost guarantee you will enjoy it. I know I did and I was hesitant to buy the game. Something about it was really putting me off, but once I started playing I gradually fell in love with this masterpiece.

Okay, to all the ragers and folks contemplating buying this game....
You HAVE to know what you're getting yourself into.
Trust Nobody, this game and many others like it are FILLED with hostile players who are just itching to shoot someone, and they will not hesitate to shoot an unarmed fresh-spawn.
The game is extremely frustrating when trying to find your friends, as the map is ENORMOUS and you have to run for upwards of 45 minutes just to find a friend, and 65-70% of the time, you'll die before you get there, whether that be from zombies, hostile snipers, or hunger/thirst.
In a large group, this game is intense, realistic, and nerve wracking beyond anything you'll ever play (excluding real life)
The heartrate increase is real, and the tensions are real. Getting shot at in this game is one of the scariest things i've ever experienced, because you really want to save your character.
If in fact you do come across a friendly, it is completely your choice to trust them, but most "friendlies" will kill you as soon as they see something on your character that they want. (IE: Rare gear, better gun, etc) So be careful who you choose to roll with.
There are A LOT of bugs/glitches that will kill you, whether it be walking on stairs, or zombies appearing out of nowhere, the game WILL frustrate you until they can work out the issues, so don't complain about how unfairly you died because i'm telling you right now you will die unfairly a few times, because the game is still in Alpha.
Stealth is KEY, running down the road in the middle of a city looking for food is a TERRIBLE idea, it's basically asking to be shot. Don't do it.
Food can be very hard to find (and isn't very filling) so you'll need to stop quite a few times on your way to your destination to get food/water or you'll die of starvation/dehydration, which is very annoying.
There you go, everything you'll need to know if you plan on buying the game, just know that this game is extremely frustrating at times, and you WILL rage quit at least once. That aside, have fun and we'll see you in the game!

Okay, to all the ragers and folks contemplating buying this game....
You HAVE to know what you're getting yourself into.
Trust Nobody, this game and many others like it are FILLED with hostile players who are just itching to shoot someone, and they will not hesitate to shoot an unarmed fresh-spawn.
The game is extremely frustrating when trying to find your friends, as the map is ENORMOUS and you have to run for upwards of 45 minutes just to find a friend, and 65-70% of the time, you'll die before you get there, whether that be from zombies, hostile snipers, or hunger/thirst.
In a large group, this game is intense, realistic, and nerve wracking beyond anything you'll ever play (excluding real life)
The heartrate increase is real, and the tensions are real. Getting shot at in this game is one of the scariest things i've ever experienced, because you really want to save your character.
If in fact you do come across a friendly, it is completely your choice to trust them, but most "friendlies" will kill you as soon as they see something on your character that they want. (IE: Rare gear, better gun, etc) So be careful who you choose to roll with.
There are A LOT of bugs/glitches that will kill you, whether it be walking on stairs, or zombies appearing out of nowhere, the game WILL frustrate you until they can work out the issues, so don't complain about how unfairly you died because i'm telling you right now you will die unfairly a few times, because the game is still in Alpha.
Stealth is KEY, running down the road in the middle of a city looking for food is a TERRIBLE idea, it's basically asking to be shot. Don't do it.
Food can be very hard to find (and isn't very filling) so you'll need to stop quite a few times on your way to your destination to get food/water or you'll die of starvation/dehydration, which is very annoying.
There you go, everything you'll need to know if you plan on buying the game, just know that this game is extremely frustrating at times, and you WILL rage quit at least once. That aside, have fun and we'll see you in the game!

TL;DR
Rust is a great game, it is worth the money. But it falls short on speed, stability, and is very laggy. 7/10.
If you dont know, Rust is an Early Alpha Survival game. Like much SURVIVAL games, you SURVIVE. But this is almost half a crafting game. You need to build a base, big or small, to survive.
PROS ARE HERE, CONS ARE BELOW!
With my experience of both legacy (the old, abandoned alpha of the game) and the current alpha, I have quite some backround. There are a range of tools, weapons, guns, and a guitar.
The map is big, and unlike DayZ, it's hard to recall any familiar places (You deicde if this is good or bad). There are 3 biomes to live in; Forest, Desert, and Arctic. Each place needs different type of clothing. For the Desert, you have to walk around in almost nothing to not burn to death, and the opposite with the Arctic. There are also Radtowns, abandoned areas with barrels to open, crates to search, and a bunch of other phat lootz. With the word RAD in it, the places sometimes have radiation. Fortunately, there are a lot on this big map, unlike Legacy, so there are many without building around it.
You can be a friendly person who takes anyone in their team, scavanging and searching radtowns. You can be a gang of builders, just building GIANT skyscrapers. You can be a lone wolf, killing anyone who walks near you. You can be a group of raiders, blowing up doors with C4 annd rockets! Or naked men. You can be any group you want.
PvE (Player vs Environment) is where there is not people killing each other, only the world.
PvP (Player vs Player) is where players are fight other players.
This game is both. You can use guns, bows, crossbows, rocks, spears, axes, and more to kill people or animals with.
The game has many prey, such as horses, pigs, deer, chicken, and other people. It also has predators, such as bears, wolves, and other people. You also have to fight cold, heat, and hunger.
PROS
CONS

Man, I don't know how many minutes, or hours, I have wasted crying about the story of this game.
Before the review, here's a small fact:
When I first seen the game I was "oh, it's look interesting" but I didn't feel at all in it charm, after about 4 - 5 days ago a friend that played this game (Unfortunatelly not from Steam) told me the game is deserve to be played.
Since I didn't want to make as him (You know, go any site and just download it) I rather decide to sell some of my dream-wished skins of CS:GO just to buy the game, tho not many of them were so valuable (Sold a few cases under $0.10, and a Nova Antique MW).
At last I did got the game, and to be honest, I felt that... Maybe I don't deserve it at all? Well at that moment I felt like that, my friend was so hype and love the game so much, plus, things over here were I live are really harsh (Venezuela), and since he created his Steam account he haven't got any official game, so well, you might know what come now, yeah, I gifted it to him!
So welp, there goes the game he wants me to play, but at last I decide to make him happy rather that wantint it for me, and left him without nothing.
To be honest I was thinking to gift him something for christmas, so why not the game you most love official?
If I don't have the game, how I'm posting this review? Well because he shared it with me! So at last I was going to be able to play it!
So well, here goes what I think about the game, and don't worry, don't expect spoilers of any kind:
At first impression, it like any other game, you move, you have actions, items, LV, EXP, and all stuff, and as the trailer say, you decide their fate, you can kill them, or spare and be friends of everyone, it's all up to you what to do! But here's one thing, once you kill someone, it's dead for good, so it's up to you what to do with everyone!
The battle style is way unique in it way, at least for a RPG, but if you have played those bullet-hell games the game is kinda a cliche, but that's what doesn't stand about the game to be honest.
I believe what makes this game great is it story, the way how every single character has their personality and the way they act, it's really something. And the fact that you can be a pacifist and spare them all, or just make a genocide and kill them all, or just being in the middle, just killing which one you dislike and which not, it's all up to the player!
Soundtracks of this game are AWESOME, I think that's another thing that Undertale has to offer, no matter what, there is one I just can't get out of my mind just like that, but well! That's something I won't tell.
If you are the kind that want to make every single thing of a game, see every side of it, every single monster and secrets, it give a lot of time for that.
Even tho the game doesn't have nowadays graphics, I bet this game beats most of the games that has come out this year, and it's a simple indie game mostly made by a single person, what do you think about it?
Oddly, I don't know if it just me, but sometimes the controls feel kinda clumsy, or slow, but that didn't stop me to make it out of a boss fight or a monster.
Personally I'll give this game a 9.5/10, it deserve the attention is getting, the features are pretty unique for a RPG game, and it make me see RPGs in a different way now.
Hope anyone that is reading this give a chance to the game!

; another changes depending on who you do and don't kill.

I liked this game so much... That as soon as I beat it and started up being told the power I held. I didn't have the heart to ruin the lives that everyone now lives. As soon as I quit the game I then spent about an hour looking at and downloading fan art. For those who don't know me well... That means quite a lot. You can tell I'm really passionate about something when I start downloading fanart. Not even joking. I honestly don't know whether I loved the story so much that I can't see the game's faults. Or Whether the game just didn't have any. Good mix of humor and serious. Beautiful story telling that really tugs at your heart. Like a dog runs up to you bites out your heart and starts flinging it around whilst covering you in slobber and blood. All the while you can't decide whether to smile or cry at how sweet/painful the situation is. That's the kind of ride this game takes you on. I honestly would give this game a 10 out of 10. The whole while I was interested and fully engaged. (Aside from grinding for Temmy Armor) I seriously reccomend this to anyone who likes a good hearted adventure/story. I wasn't expecting a WHOLE lot from this game untill I saw a bit of gameplay. I was flabberghasted at just how charming this game was. And how right off the bat you are thrust into a tough decision. You meet this lovely Mother figure. I didn't want to leave her. I just wanted to stay and end the game there... But alas I had to break poor Toriel's heart. Then to brighten the mood you meet Sans a happy go lucky skeleton with a "Cool" brother. I'll let you figure out the rest for yourself. I wasn't ready for the amazing ride I was taken on. This genuinely happy game had a surprising and quite scary darkside as well. I'll spare the details, but I will say that I just wasn't prepared. Don't even get me started on the soundtrack every song has it's own charm and is genuinely pleasant to hear. The music is both beautiful and powerful. Sometimes downright awesome. Level designs were nice no complaints there and usually very colorful. I loved every moment of this game... Every Character... Every song  This game makes you feel loved as if these characters really were there.  Really talking to YOU. Somewhere inside your computer and at times; You really wish they were. Do I really have the heart to go back through, and kill it all? I have too... I must because the curse of curiousity.  I must. Or I will go mad.
Verdict
Undertale 10/10

*Spoiler Free review*
When I first began finding out about Undertale it was already early October and I was debating whether I wanted to buy it or not. One day I was feeling particularly depressed and was going on buying spree based purely on impulse and great rating recent games had recieved.
A friend of mine had managed to get this game via torrent and told me about all the quirks and turns the story could take and spoiled many important elements for me but seeing as I had no clue what he was talking about, they didn't stick with me (much like Star Wars spoliers for The Force Awakens).
On another day I was feeling deeply depressed I decided to play this game and I finished it without stopping.
I was glad I did because a lot of themes present here serve to encourage and remind you that a lot of current hardships are temporary.
As mentioned here by countless reviews you have choices to make:
You can either spare everyone or... you can kill everyone.
You can choose a middle path but it's not very satisfying to stick with it.
The fact that this game can be hilarious at times quickly build the tension and go back down to a silly ambient is astounding. There will be moments where you will find yourself laughing out loud, squealing in the more cute moments, crying in the heartwrenching ones.
Also keep in mind, this game is actually VERY dark and I think that's why it plies you with so much humor early on.
It gets dark to the point of it being mentally disturbing without the need of gore or lewd language. Which, in my opinion, is quite a feat and the mark of excellent storytelling.
The combat system is quirky, unique and funny, I would hum the battle tune even while I was taking a shower or helping my mom cook some food. Being merciful is as difficult as you'd expect, you WILL have to find ways to bargain with these creatures in order to meaintain a clean slate. Or... kill them if that's what you want. Keep in mind that once dead, they won't respawn making the game change the way the characters interact with you and judge you.
This game has some very deep and real themes we see that happen to us, and people we love, and addresses them with the right kind of tact. It even pokes fun at things we deem important and life altering such as romantic rejections.
The characters are very likeable and even sympathetic. You will find yourself falling in love with the different little monsters that live in this wonderful underground world.
The fact that the story can go from whimsical adventure to FNAF levels of suspense and tension (even horror) is what makes this game stand out among all other RPG's I've played this year.
And personally? It helped me feel better about myself in a period when my life is not exactly pleasant. In a way, this game made me cry not only because of the story, it was also because I felt understood.
And it keeps reminding us that every choice we make has a consequence.
My choice? I give this game a 10/10 and a very shining recommendation. Will most likely play again as many times as needed.
