I would like to point out that DayZ should be treated with alot more than what people have been saying it has been. First off. This review is a basis of what Ive encountered in the game, and saying what I think should be some justice for DayZ.
1. The Zombies can be a big buggy. However, Coding a completely different AI from the mod DayZ, with the AI hearing and seeing you from a good field of vision is easy enough for a novice programmer. However, Noding the entire world of Chenarus so that the AI is pitch perfect to every square inch, has to take a toll on the way the game and the AI coordinate with eachother. Do I give Bohemia slack for not improving the game? no. Its been 2 years, there should have been alot more improvements to the zombie AI.
2. The game has a poor optimization, you need a beefy computer to run it and enjoy it, which I am lucky to have, however many of the gaming world has either an average or below average computer to run said game,(I have only experienced one really bad lagspike in my 120 hours of gameplay) Which in turn, developers these days should recognise and tweak their games to the other majority of the PC gaming world.
3. The talk of zombies clipping through walls and what not. I have yet to see any zombie clip through walls or natural things (Tree's, Rocks, Etc) Since the early days of DayZ (About a year and a half ago). So the pathfinding and barriers have seen improvement, If you have these issues and have 200+ ping constantly, really think about what you are saying, And I constantly have 120 ping, which is mediocre to say the least to some people.
4. There is truth where the developers should be releasing alot more updates then they are, With that much money they have earned, they have little to no excuse to be feeding the fanbase and game with constant updates. Final Verdict: I have played DayZ since the mod itself, For about 5 years, I believe there will be no game like DayZ for a very long time, and people have set the bar to high for a developer that has created a one of a kind game. Do they deserve slack for a game they have had 5+ years to work on?. No. Do they however give updates and not completely drop the game? Yes.  Its only a matter of time before they really truly consider what they have in their hands.

If you are a person who believes a good solid game that does not need updates every so often for it to be enjoyable. ( AKA, Update every 2-3 months) I would recommend this game.

Pros :
1. Set your own goals
2. Work with/against other people
3. Neat Building system and collectable/craftable iteams.
4. It makes me think how I might play this scenario out in real life.
5. Unless working with a team, it takes more than a couple of hours to get situated (which is a pro and con).

6. The map is huge and they vary in layout (unless playing directx 9 version), with a number of places to go with cool items present.  You can play quietly by yourself or dive right into the madness.
7.  Most of my console gamer friends enjoy the graphics.  I think they're decent as well.
8.  Early Access! They are constantly adding new elements/items to the game
9. I'm sure there are other pros..  this all I can think of at the moment.
Cons :
1.  A compass would be really cool.. as to not make it too easy to find your way.  Although, you can use the Sun/Moon.
2. The map is huge.. so sometimes getting places can be a pain

5. The countless hours spent playing with little to show for it, haha. (I'm flirting with 30.. so I have a few responsibilities)
6. Some people KOS (Kill on sight).  Which is pretty lame, since I'd probably just hand the stuff over if I didn't have a weapon to protect oneself.
Conclusion :
The game is pretty dope. I'm addicted! I never expected this when I picked it up.  Early access is neat, since you can have a small say in how the game is put together.  I'd recommend this to really anyone.  Although, you might want to set some time aside. 9/10?

* The combat feels really intense and realistic.
All in all over all other titles i would choose Rust, I heavily recommend you to do the same.

I can't really say whether or not this game is going in the right direction.  But I can, and have the right, to express dissapointment.  Feels like the BI can't get in the groove with making this game.  I've played plenty of Early Access games, and they've had their ups and downs but never like DayZ SA.  The progression is dissapointingly slow.  Often the updates take the game backwards in development.  Probably going to catch some flack, but I changed this review to NOT recommend this game.
But, on that note, I don't regret getting the game.  I was very good at it, met a lot of people which with whom I still play other games with, and had a lot of fun.  Dollars for hours, I feel I got my moneys worth.  However, as Early Access, this game isn't really playable (for me).
-Many different ways to interact with players and the world.
-Persistance allows for players to store gear and supplies.
-Graphics are great if you have everything way up.
-Always an adventure.
-More afraid of other players than of zombies.
-Frames are a little bit better now.
-Customizable settings in the DayZ folder under Documents for low end computers.
-Stealth is now implemented.
-Exploding fireplaces.
-.59 Building vehicles!
- FIXED looking through walls in 3rd person, loot explosions, zombie pathing.
-Added sedan, offroad, and buss
-NewUI
-V3S can't make it up a hill to save your life.
-A bug where your vehicle is stuck, trying to drive it will just cause your screen to shake but goes nowhere (told to change the tires, doesn't work).
-Not focusing on fixing core development.  This is not an accurate measurment, but it seems they put more emphasis on putting aesthetic items in the game rather than getting the gameplay right.  Plenty of new items but nothing in the gameplay has been substancially fixed.  Framerates are marginally fixed, changed some cities and roads.  Removed some gun attachments, and added guns.
-Updates seem to take two steps forward, one step back. (example: Guns, which are your greatest defense, randomly dissapear, don't allow you to equip them, etc)  Big con.
-Hit boxes on trees are much larger than the tree in some areas.  Vehicle damage is on; drive with care, especially on roads with deciduous trees nearby. (Fixed?)
-Needs a lot more optimization.  But also this game renders a long distance, so not so much of a con, but a con nonetheless.
-Zombie attacks are a bit wonky.
-New UI
**Not sure about this one, if it's bugged or not, a correction would be helpful**
-Landmines detonate immediately after activation, supposed to be a three second count to get away from the mine.
Having issues with framerates?  -Upgrade your processor.  This game is very processor heavy due to the large areas of render.  I was playing at 10-35  FPS depending on the area with an AMD-6800K processor.  Bought a newer motherboard with intel chipset (i7-4790K) 45-90 FPS.  Both were 4.0+GHz processors, but my sampling is over twice that on my Intel than of my AMD.
Buyer beware - Bohemia itself recommends you not to buy the game, but naturally, we're not listening.

This game is pretty decent. You basically start with absolutely nothing and build up from there.
Pros:
-Survival mechanics are perfect. You aren't forced to look for food and water nonstop like in DayZ
-Just the right amount of NPC threat i.e. the deadly helicopter, bears and wolves (although I heard there were zombies and I'd love to see them return)
-Base building is fun, and if you don't chat and make friends with people (turst no one) you have decent chance of actually getting somewhere
-Daytime lasts longer than night time (I can't stand playing in pitch black settings)
-Games is optimized quite well (My machine is by far not anywhere near new)
-Guns are hella fun once you can make them, especially when someone thinks they can attack you
Cons:
-Your body gets left behind when you log off
-Absolutely zero character customization and this is my biggest complaint. They're calling it a definitive realism feature but it totally isn't and here's why: I am a woman, if I wanted to be forced to play a male character I could play literally any other game on the market. That's not definitive, that's just the way it's always been. The people happy with this feature are the dudes that heavily populate the game, so of course they wouldn't complain about being forced into a male character. Besides, character customization adds fun to a game, and there's a point where realism is just too much realism.
-Once you've discovered everything (the crafting list is rather small at the moment) and you've got a giant fortified base that's pretty much it, which is fine if you're on a populated server but boring as hell if you're own a new/empty server.
Overall I would recommend this game, but only if you can stomach the total/complete lack of character freedom. The best way way to play is to not care about anything, otherwise you'll likely end up hating it. And bashing people's heads in with a rock is quite fun.

I waited three years for this game to come out.  I replayed the demo off and on the whole while with eager anticipation.  I was excited to see if Toriel would leave the Ruins with me, to met those strange skeletons at the end of the "best" run, to kick Flowey in the face and prove it wrong.
Naturally the internet spoiled practically everything within a week of release.
Even loaded up on spoilers, the game tugged at my heart and I felt things for all the characters, from the NPCs to the Boss Monsters.  I made friends with them all even though some made me nervous at first blush.  I forgot at for a while that the game was judging me as I played it, but all it found was a friend.  A friend who *flirts at times, but someone who earned their happy ending by being determined to stay nice.
If they remembered the tragedies the demo wrought, I would had been likely screwed.
I know the internet at large has raved about this.  That there are people who will be put off by the part of the fanbase that ships and lusts.  But please.  Don't let that stop you.
This game isn't completely perfect but the work and thought gone into its creation makes it solid.

When I first discovered Rust about a year ago, it was broken, with bad combat mechanics, laggy, and extremely poorly optimized, but overall a very fun experience. A year later it's broken, with bad combat mechanics, laggy, still poorly optimized AND it's almost unplayable for solo players or even small teams. So the only positive point for me (fun experience) went down the drain.
In other words, with the new features added these last couple of months that can only be built and maintained if you're part of a 5-6 men group or more, Rust became almost unplayable for casual solo players, including myself. I can't really be bothered nor do I have the time to commit to this game to such an extent. Organized teams get most airdrops (which contain op gear), helicopter drops as well (which will soon contain exclusive parts for turrets according to the devblog), build large bases with space for all the high capacity furnaces and other processing facilities, quarries etc.
edit: Smaller servers are now available.
As a solo player, you can't get online and just gather some resources, build a small house, put a couple of furnaces and start collecting stuff - no, you'll get raided as soon as some team's scout spots your house and decides to tear it down with a couple of C4 charges (that you, as a solo player, don't have access to).
One last point: the community. Russians, children, hackers, sociopaths, you name it - Rust has it.

This is probably my favorite post apocalypse survival game to date [ And there are so many to choose from on steam] I have played a good amount of them and Rust always sticks with me, it has an addictive feel to the game. On most servers you will find yourself nervously attempting to make yourself civilised enough in terms of tools and weaponry to stay alive long enough to build a base and make it strong enough to withstand a raid. Other servers are purely for building and community pleasure and you meet a lot of great people in game eager to help you [which cannot be said about the PvP servers] even if someone is friendly on a PvP server you have a strong instict not to trust them and leave you for dead once they have robbed you blind. Here are a decent list of reasons why i choose Rust over so many survival titles:
*Dev team are solid on bringing new cool stuff with every update, whist working on bugs from previous builds.
* You actually feel threatened even in the safty of your base, keeping you on guard.
* The look, feel and atmosphere of Rust all way down the the maps and sound fx keeps you hooked
* The many many options you have while building
* Being able to customize your character to great lengths
* The combat feels really intense and realistic.
All in all over all other titles i would choose Rust, I heavily recommend you to do the same.

Negatives:

The twig update for example, should have been put in the experimental branch and used as a means to test and see if the general player base liked it. I can understand from their viewpoint that the best way to reach the majority of their audience is to put it right into the main branch but I cannot understand why the experimental branch is not used sometimes, this game has a massive amount of work put in and is still in development. So why not have the community help develop the game and test updates before they go into effect.

I'm guessing you are like me. You just now find out about this game and you have my issue.
"Ohhhh..another indie game everyone cheers about....that has only happened 50 times this year..."
Well, many indie games, many AAA games have not hit me in the core like this game did.
And not in that boring "Walking Simulator" or "Deep story that is no different than a good movie way"
This game is for long term gamers only because the emotions this will bring across you will only touch those gamers who have messed with game world and not cared one bit.
We have all had good and bad stories in all the types of games, but this game is one of the few that makes you learn to make true friendships and learn about every enemy. I will not say in what way this happens because I feel the gameplay is actually the best if not spoiled.
But what had me touched was the darker story. The game pushes you to do your best to do good your first playthrough, but then uses the accomplishment of finishing all the game to push you into playing the game like any old RPG where you kill all that stands before you.
But I've done many evil stories, where you act bad "Ohhh no you killed them, ohhh you bad person" Where the characters just act shocked, and then die. This game does the shock, but then as you travel, they do their best to console you in their own way....really making you feel horrid rather than making the dark path cool or epic. "This game pushed you into caring about these people and through that, when you deside to do evil, they console you like a real friend would.
And that is what is so magical about this game. It knows us gamers better than we know ourselves. It knows how we play and why we play and uses that to spark emotions you haven't felt in a videogame but all too familiar in real life.
-Story- 10-10
Fantastic story telling. Plays on how the game works, plays on the fourth wall. Every choice matters and has very real reactions and changes in the story. Multible endings. Great Characters that are so popular their art is flooding the internet.
-Gameplay-  ??-10   (For myself 8-10)
I had to be a little strange with this because for me, I love this take on oldschool rpgs where it stopped being boring work selection. This game works on more of skill. But it does this by forcing you to always go through what is called bullet hell. Where you guide a sprite through tiny bullets trying not to get hit. It sounds strange and I don't want to ruin how this makes the most epic boss battles and also adds story telling as characters bullets react to rage or sorrow.... But this also in my eyes makes the game unbalenced to casual players. After all, if your reactions are slow or you are disabled, where other rpgs are easy for you to play, this game can be next to impossible for players who can't react quickly for what ever reason.
-Sound and Music- 9-10
The music to this game has already had many already cover it. It is and will be a classic in gaming. From making you excited and happy, to creepy music and background sounds that will chill you to the bone.......though I wish I could say the same for the effect noises. Where the music goes from 8-bit to midi, the sound effects are very oldschool. They don't sound bad at all, but with such work done on the music, it does make the sound effects and few voice clips sound strange and off. Not bad in the least, but enough I was thinking about it and longing for crisper tones.
-Graphics- 5-10
Remember art is in the eye of the beholder, so you could feel differently. You can always look at the gameplay clips to make your mind up.  I love 8-bit style, many games look so good in the old 8-bit style. But this art style is like a fan wanted to be inspired Earthbound /Mother in Japan/ yet never knew why Earthbound looked great. From what I studied about how this game was made. The art style I love in this game was made by Fox and the art I don't like was drawn by others. Fox did great and love his art, but you can tell what he didn't draw was not as carefully made. But all the art and design is stuck in my head and makes great memes, so I think I'm one of the few that felt this way.
Overall for gamers 10-10 and for casual 8-10
This is a must have game for any gamer all based on experence you have with the story and character. Enough said about that when gameplay, story and characters all melt into a wonderful story about choice and life.
For casual gamers....this game will touch you, but simple strange graphics and bullet hell gameplay that jerks up and down in difficulty can and will break your spirit down and might make the whole game unbeatable for you.

Fantastic game; it happens so quickly.
I remember one play through where I was down with my roommate on the beach path between Cherno and the old factory in full combat gear. We were handing out water bottles and can openers to bambis, protected with fully auto rifles, helmets, riot vests, army boots, gas masks, everything.
Two guys run from up the road - at this point I'm alone as my mate has left to show a fresh bambi the game's water well refill system. They're clothed only in underwear, nothing but flashlights in their hands. I lifted my rifle, and told them to slow down. I was confident then, strong, and ready; I'd scrounged for hours for this gear, and walked half the entirety of the map to secure my survival safety. I truly thought I was invincible on the spawn beaches. T'was not so, and I learned a very powerful lesson that day.
My rifle aimed high, I spoke - nay, I commanded the two to cease movement, and had them kneel. I explained to them my mission, and asked if they had played before - they had. The one gent seemed overjoyed by my gifts, and I dropped them in front of him. The other, however, did not meet my sincerity; instead, he stood, challenging my devine authority, and told me to "go f*** my mother's bunghole."
I was enraged! it was obvious that I needed to kull the beast in front of me before he grew to any real power. My pristine acog scope aimed to his body, I squeezed the damn trigger and bled a full 35 round mag dry into his chest. It was glorious. I was truly alive. Unfortunately, the dead beast's partner did not share in my enthusiasm - he jumped up, and shouted jargon along the lines of "you♥♥♥♥♥♥ I'll have your♥♥♥♥♥♥stained anal ring as my prize." He started running around, swinging his fist wildly into the air. While I once thought there was no way he'd come close to me, I hadn't anticipated his charge - I tried to reload with a fresh mag, but lo, I was too late! He brought his fist down upon my crown, and alas: I was slain. My fibreglass helmet was but seran wrap to his knuckles, my re-enforced armour a useless crust against the wrath of his uppercut. I saw blackness, and in the blackness, my jaw-dropped reflection. I screamed a useless cry of help to my roommate, but he was too far and too slow to assist my recovery. By the time he found my naked, used, and bloodied body, my assailant was long gone.
Until my final hour I had only feared the powerful and patient - those who travelled in marauding caravans armed to the teeth hunting their prey. I learned that day that it was not the powerful in DayZ you must fear. It is the weak. The new spawn who has not spent the time hoarding, hiking and sneaking. The defeated gladiator, risen again, hoping to regain his glory. The lost and damned, hungry to resume the carnage again. The man with nothing to lose.
"memoirs of King - March 8, 2015"

Though Rust is a game in early access, it is a very good game amoung it's genre.
If you've played ARK before, then I can tell you that Rust has much better graphic optimization. (I've played ARK for over 800 hours, so you don't need to ask me about how I made the comparison.)
Rust is an open-world multiplayer game with servers hosted by both the official and players from the Rust community. Which means that there are griefers, new-player unfriendly as*holes, scavengers, raiders and PVP enthusiasts here in some servers. And these people are the main reason to define Rust as a survival game.
So, if you prefer soloing multiplayer games like ARK, avoid Rust. That's because Rust is mainly a PVP game, and a pvp game like this usually means that you have to group with others. Otherwise you may learn the definition of the word "heartbreaker". What may break your heart is not the game itself, but people.
However if you
going to group up with some friends and play together, then the situation won't be too hash for you guys. Just build your stronghold (though I doubt that you can find somewhere large enough for a stronghold in a heavily populated server) and raid those poor solo players and enjoy the feeling of dominating.
The building mechanics in this game is similar to ARK's  (snapping of course), but more flexible and realistic than ARK. Though both Rust and ARK are flawed. Guess that's what a game in EA phase should be.

CHOOSE YOUR OWN REVIEW ADVENTURE:
-If you're wondering whether Undertale is worth your ten bucks, scroll to answer #1.
-If you're browsing reviews out of desperation because you already finished the game, looked at every single piece of fan art, and reread your copy of "Bone-Based Puns and Other Humerus Material" for the fifth time, try #2.

(2) The only comfort I can offer you is that the pain of loss will ease a little with time, and you'll always have your memories. However, your suffering will flare up whenever you try another game and realize that you want more than it can offer. As a player coming in who's never played any of the Mother games, this was something new. I was swayed by the amount of hype and attention this piece got so quickly after release, I figured it was just a lot of nostalgia and over exaggeration.
But I finally played it and I have to say; while it might be over blown, it's not done so by a lot.
A game like this comes along once in a generation. One with enough soul that it demands you love it. (Even if you suck at it, like me) Few games ever have any kind of morality system. Even fewer question the morality of the very basis of their own mechanics. (Spec Ops comes to mind) But Undertale asks the questions; is it right to kill an enemy in a video game? Could you talk it out instead? If so, why not?
The amount of meta this game digs into might not be 'original' but it's certainly a refreshing change of pace. Not every choice you make is completely clear as to what it will do and the actual gameplay segments can feel a bit clunky, mainly due in large part to the slow amount of movement you're allowed during your dodge phases. The only real issue this game suffers from is that it's simply not enough. Too short and too lacking in all the amazing characterization it has, it's asking for an expansion or a sequel or something. One playthrough isn't enough to sate most people's taste for the amazing world laid out in Undertale, and playing through it has lead me to understand why. There's too much to drink in and not enough game to hold it. (Not enough hours in the day as they say)
Other than that though -- I have 0 complaints about this game. It's simply incredible. It will make you laugh, it will make you cry, you'll get mad in frustration and cheer in victory as you finally win against that boss you've been stuck on for 3 hours. The music is amazing, the overall feel pulls you into the world and makes you a part of it and it's all done with sprites and pixel art, and sometimes literally, through the meta games.
I really had to think it over since I didn't even give Far Cry 3 a full 10 due to it simply falling short in terms of gameplay stability. And I feel I should do the same for Undertale, but I don't think I will.
So for the first time ever in a *serious* review, I have to give Undertale a full 10/10 for its story and writing alone.
Hats off to you Toby.

Before buying the game, you must realize it is an alpha. Most of the negativity surrounding this game comes from the fact that people, for what ever reason, can't understand what it means to be in alpha phase. The game has its bugs, yes. There are some that are very annoying, such as zombies clipping through walls. There are also hackers who manage to find a way through the anti-cheat systems, although as of late those are encounters are few and far between. Optimization for the game is also a work in progress, although I personally don't too much of an issue.
To me, the issues mentioned above are the primary downfalls. If you can look past the fact the game is a work in progress and you will run into those issues, this game is for you.
On the upside, the game offers ever changing player interactions.  The best times I've had while playing the game are running into other players. Some are friendly, most are hostile. But to me, thats what keeps the game interesting. Never knowing when you're being stalked by another player combined with the constant need to be aware of your surroundings and looking over your shoulder. If you're looking for a purely PvE game, this is game is not for you.
The developers of the game are also consistently making changes to the game, the vast majority of them in the right direction. Hackers were a pretty big issue in the game until the last major patch. That was give or take a month ago and I've yet to see one in the game since then. I guess what I am trying to say here is the game has made leaps and bounds in the right direction since i first played it. And, if they continue on this trend, this game is going to be epic.

I'm guessing you are like me. You just now find out about this game and you have my issue.
"Ohhhh..another indie game everyone cheers about....that has only happened 50 times this year..."
Well, many indie games, many AAA games have not hit me in the core like this game did.
And not in that boring "Walking Simulator" or "Deep story that is no different than a good movie way"
This game is for long term gamers only because the emotions this will bring across you will only touch those gamers who have messed with game world and not cared one bit.
We have all had good and bad stories in all the types of games, but this game is one of the few that makes you learn to make true friendships and learn about every enemy. I will not say in what way this happens because I feel the gameplay is actually the best if not spoiled.
But what had me touched was the darker story. The game pushes you to do your best to do good your first playthrough, but then uses the accomplishment of finishing all the game to push you into playing the game like any old RPG where you kill all that stands before you.
But I've done many evil stories, where you act bad "Ohhh no you killed them, ohhh you bad person" Where the characters just act shocked, and then die. This game does the shock, but then as you travel, they do their best to console you in their own way....really making you feel horrid rather than making the dark path cool or epic. "This game pushed you into caring about these people and through that, when you deside to do evil, they console you like a real friend would.
And that is what is so magical about this game. It knows us gamers better than we know ourselves. It knows how we play and why we play and uses that to spark emotions you haven't felt in a videogame but all too familiar in real life.
-Story- 10-10
Fantastic story telling. Plays on how the game works, plays on the fourth wall. Every choice matters and has very real reactions and changes in the story. Multible endings. Great Characters that are so popular their art is flooding the internet.
-Gameplay-  ??-10   (For myself 8-10)
I had to be a little strange with this because for me, I love this take on oldschool rpgs where it stopped being boring work selection. This game works on more of skill. But it does this by forcing you to always go through what is called bullet hell. Where you guide a sprite through tiny bullets trying not to get hit. It sounds strange and I don't want to ruin how this makes the most epic boss battles and also adds story telling as characters bullets react to rage or sorrow.... But this also in my eyes makes the game unbalenced to casual players. After all, if your reactions are slow or you are disabled, where other rpgs are easy for you to play, this game can be next to impossible for players who can't react quickly for what ever reason.
-Sound and Music- 9-10
The music to this game has already had many already cover it. It is and will be a classic in gaming. From making you excited and happy, to creepy music and background sounds that will chill you to the bone.......though I wish I could say the same for the effect noises. Where the music goes from 8-bit to midi, the sound effects are very oldschool. They don't sound bad at all, but with such work done on the music, it does make the sound effects and few voice clips sound strange and off. Not bad in the least, but enough I was thinking about it and longing for crisper tones.
-Graphics- 5-10
Remember art is in the eye of the beholder, so you could feel differently. You can always look at the gameplay clips to make your mind up.  I love 8-bit style, many games look so good in the old 8-bit style. But this art style is like a fan wanted to be inspired Earthbound /Mother in Japan/ yet never knew why Earthbound looked great. From what I studied about how this game was made. The art style I love in this game was made by Fox and the art I don't like was drawn by others. Fox did great and love his art, but you can tell what he didn't draw was not as carefully made. But all the art and design is stuck in my head and makes great memes, so I think I'm one of the few that felt this way.
Overall for gamers 10-10 and for casual 8-10
This is a must have game for any gamer all based on experence you have with the story and character. Enough said about that when gameplay, story and characters all melt into a wonderful story about choice and life.
For casual gamers....this game will touch you, but simple strange graphics and bullet hell gameplay that jerks up and down in difficulty can and will break your spirit down and might make the whole game unbeatable for you.
A grand game I'm glad I played on my friends pc and now have my own copy and will clock many hours on my copy.

After sixth playthrough:
"Undertale is a good game." - Zero Punctuation
Undertale makes me want to say smart things.
Like how it becomes greater than the sum of its parts because of the music alone.
Or how its incredibly nieve story still somehow makes me feel more than any other game.
Or that the greatest problem with the game is that it is built primarily on surprising the player, so it is difficult to convince someone why they should buy it without giving away the whole point.
Undertale makes me want to recommend it. It is endearing and simultaneously maniacal. It is funny and meaningful. It is alive, and it is self aware. I replayed this game six times within the first month of me getting it, having never replayed any other game more than once.
I have thought more about this game than any other piece of art in any other form, and will probably continue to do so for months, ever asking the question - What makes it good?
Undertale makes me want to write a very short review, so as to give away as little as possible.
After 3 months not playing:
And I'm back. Again. Even if only one person reads this, it is still worth writing, for my own sake.
Many people have, myself included, hailed this game as amazing beyond all belief, and for some people it is. It pains me in every way to know that some people will never experience the joy that this game can bring, simply because it has not been made with them in mind. From what I have observed, this game is for those with a quirky sense of humour (especially bad puns), an interest in philosophy and politics, and a state of mind in sync with the 'this is fine' dog meme. And yes, people who like memes. Undertale is silly with serious undertones, allowing itself into your heart with its wit and charm, only to reveal a strict set of consequences, a law of cause and effect that can send the unwitting reeling with fear, because you realise who's holding all of the cards, and it's definitely not you.
This realisation has sent a part of my brain into a state of constant flux, and as my opinions of the game part change, I have begun to realise that this game is in some way more alive and real than any other, despite all its fatal flaws and sterotypes and repetitions and laziness. Because when it comes down to it, no amount of graphx or gamplys or dank memes can possibly surpass an inch of knowledge this universal.
I don't doubt that I'll be back.

10/10 ... Although not for the faint of heart, Rust is a game unlike most others--if you let it.
You're able to role play if you're into that, there are battlefield servers where you spawn in with armour and gun kits and can just shoot people and get rekt, there are battle royale servers where you spawn in with a torch and have to find loot and try to win first place while being pushed towards the inner circle by radiation and bombs, and there's regular servers where you just try to survive and build. There's a game experience for everyone.
There ARE nice people in Rust, but they're difficult to find. Trust is hard to come by on this game. Backstabbing is a regular thing. People will kill you mercilessly even when you have nothing in your inventory except your rock and torch. Rust is a hardcore survival game. It's not a friendly game where we run through fields of flowers, galloping and riding into the sunset.. Realize that and you'll be peachy.
As it is early access, there are bugs and exploits that sometimes make the game experience less than desirable. But if you look past the eternity it takes to load the game, the hackers that are far less rampant than legacy days (but still exist), and the KOS mindset of the players, you'll get 100s of hours of playability for a cheap price.
The developers of this game are putting their heart and soul into it and you can tell. Not only will you get an amazing game experience of heart pumping survival, you can also make lifelong friendships from people you interact with. I met so many people that have become some of my closest friends through Rust. So be open to interactions and friendships. There's honestly nothing like this game. The fear of losing your loot and getting killed really gets your adrenaline going.
My recommendations though -- 1. Make sure your PC is able to handle it before you buy the game, because you will not be able to play it if your PC can't handle it (obviously). Don't blame the game for your crappy PC. xD 2. You will get raided, you will die with an inventory full of loot, don't let this ruin your experience. It's a game. You can get it back. It's okay to grieve and be salty for a moment but don't let it ruin the game for you. It's going to happen. Deal with it. 3. Definitely get a mic. It doesn't have to be a top of the line $200 mic. But a decent mic that will let you interact with players is a must! Because the human interaction is really where a lot of the magic is in this game. 4. If you're new, don't join an offical server straight away. Join a lower populated (but not empty) noob friendly community server. Ask questions, learn the game, join up with someone who will teach you the ways of Rust. 5. Don't be annoying. You'll make a lot of enemies if you're annoying.

As a player coming in who's never played any of the Mother games, this was something new. I was swayed by the amount of hype and attention this piece got so quickly after release, I figured it was just a lot of nostalgia and over exaggeration.
But I finally played it and I have to say; while it might be over blown, it's not done so by a lot.
A game like this comes along once in a generation. One with enough soul that it demands you love it. (Even if you suck at it, like me) Few games ever have any kind of morality system. Even fewer question the morality of the very basis of their own mechanics. (Spec Ops comes to mind) But Undertale asks the questions; is it right to kill an enemy in a video game? Could you talk it out instead? If so, why not?
The amount of meta this game digs into might not be 'original' but it's certainly a refreshing change of pace. Not every choice you make is completely clear as to what it will do and the actual gameplay segments can feel a bit clunky, mainly due in large part to the slow amount of movement you're allowed during your dodge phases. The only real issue this game suffers from is that it's simply not enough. Too short and too lacking in all the amazing characterization it has, it's asking for an expansion or a sequel or something. One playthrough isn't enough to sate most people's taste for the amazing world laid out in Undertale, and playing through it has lead me to understand why. There's too much to drink in and not enough game to hold it. (Not enough hours in the day as they say)
Other than that though -- I have 0 complaints about this game. It's simply incredible. It will make you laugh, it will make you cry, you'll get mad in frustration and cheer in victory as you finally win against that boss you've been stuck on for 3 hours. The music is amazing, the overall feel pulls you into the world and makes you a part of it and it's all done with sprites and pixel art, and sometimes literally, through the meta games.
I really had to think it over since I didn't even give Far Cry 3 a full 10 due to it simply falling short in terms of gameplay stability. And I feel I should do the same for Undertale, but I don't think I will.
So for the first time ever in a *serious* review, I have to give Undertale a full 10/10 for its story and writing alone.
Hats off to you Toby.

You're able to role play if you're into that, there are battlefield servers where you spawn in with armour and gun kits and can just shoot people and get rekt, there are battle royale servers where you spawn in with a torch and have to find loot and try to win first place while being pushed towards the inner circle by radiation and bombs, and there's regular servers where you just try to survive and build. There's a game experience for everyone.
There ARE nice people in Rust, but they're difficult to find. Trust is hard to come by on this game. Backstabbing is a regular thing. People will kill you mercilessly even when you have nothing in your inventory except your rock and torch. Rust is a hardcore survival game. It's not a friendly game where we run through fields of flowers, galloping and riding into the sunset.. Realize that and you'll be peachy.
As it is early access, there are bugs and exploits that sometimes make the game experience less than desirable. But if you look past the eternity it takes to load the game, the hackers that are far less rampant than legacy days (but still exist), and the KOS mindset of the players, you'll get 100s of hours of playability for a cheap price.
The developers of this game are putting their heart and soul into it and you can tell. Not only will you get an amazing game experience of heart pumping survival, you can also make lifelong friendships from people you interact with. I met so many people that have become some of my closest friends through Rust. So be open to interactions and friendships. There's honestly nothing like this game. The fear of losing your loot and getting killed really gets your adrenaline going.
My recommendations though -- 1. Make sure your PC is able to handle it before you buy the game, because you will not be able to play it if your PC can't handle it (obviously). Don't blame the game for your crappy PC. xD 2. You will get raided, you will die with an inventory full of loot, don't let this ruin your experience. It's a game. You can get it back. It's okay to grieve and be salty for a moment but don't let it ruin the game for you. It's going to happen. Deal with it. 3. Definitely get a mic. It doesn't have to be a top of the line $200 mic. But a decent mic that will let you interact with players is a must! Because the human interaction is really where a lot of the magic is in this game. 4. If you're new, don't join an offical server straight away. Join a lower populated (but not empty) noob friendly community server. Ask questions, learn the game, join up with someone who will teach you the ways of Rust. 5. Don't be annoying. You'll make a lot of enemies if you're annoying.

What can I say about this game... It's like nothing you've ever played before, I can assure you that much.
Gameplay-wise, it's pretty innovative. It combines standard RPG elements like turn-based combot with a unique enemy-attack evasion system not unlike bullet-hell shooters like Touhou. Charming pixelated graphics accompanied by a fantastic soundtrack make this a treat to look at and listen to, much less play.
Now, for what I think is the most important part: the story.
Basically, you are a child that has fallen into an underground ruin, which is where monsters, a second race besides humans, have been trapped after a large war. The greatest thing about this game is that it makes you think. It makes you reflect on your actions. Should you just run through and kill anything that you come across? Do all of these "enemies" really need to die just because you have a weapon and an attack option? Depending on how you choose to play this game, you'll have an experience that reflects your play style.
And the writing, oh boy the writing. These characters, these encounters, everything is so lovable and memorable, the cast just gets more and more interesting the further you play the game. I can't go into further detail without spoiling these moments for you, but I assure you this game is worth every dollar.

tl;dr:

-Wonderful soundtrack
-Fantastic writing

Ok, I've put enough time into this game now, and seen it develop enough to be able to make a few points about it. Hoplefully it'll help would-be players know what they're getting in to/
It should go wiithout saying that since this game is in alpha, bugs are common. This review will not be considering issues that are blatntly just a factor of the game not being done yet. That being said, you will likely see some clipping issues, occasional bugs with loot and pickups, occasional bugs with health (i had a character drink about five gallons of gasoline and just shrug it off at one point.)
A few months ago I would not have recommended this game, it was just a litle too unpolished to be playable. However, in the last few weeks and months the devs have been fevrishly updating, and adding content, which now makes the game enjoyable to play.
OK, so first we must consider something crucial; what sets DayZ apart from the multitude of other sandbox survival mmo zombie games? Well, it's not really a game so much as a simulation. The fictional eastern Ukrainian region of Chernarus is brutal and unforgiving (and not due to bugs). DayZ will punish you every step of the way for not knowing what to do. It's extraordinarily difficult to get into initially, but once you do you'll find a rich and complex system with more potentilal than any of it's competitors.

Let me give an exmaple; Let's compare Dayz to say...Unturned, H1Z1, and seven days to die. Arguably, all these games are the same thing, and that is zombie survival sandbox mmo. While the aforementioned games rely heavily on gaming cliches such as ridiculous weapons and proficiencies, or ignorance of things like cold, wetness, hunger, condition equipment, etc. That doesn't make any of those games bad, far from it, if you want a real game with solid objectives and recognizable hard mechanics, play those games. (in particular unturned is free and pretty fun) but that;s not DayZ.
DayZ is like you literally woke up one day into a world that was lost to zombies weeks ago. You have no idea what or who is left, or what you might do to survive. Oh no! a zombie! But wait, you have no weapons. How long would it realistically take to punch a zombie to death? or beat it down with a broom or rock? Forever. If something seems like it would be that way in real life, it's probably accounted for in DayZ. You'll even break your legs by falling more than 15 feet, causing you to exclusively be able to crawl around in slow, agonizing ways.
So with all that being said, If you're going to play it alone, don't bother. The game shines the most when you play with friends or brave a highy populated server. Humans are terrible people when the chips are down, and in DayZ the chips were eaten a long time ago. Every single person you meet online is a heart-pounding threat.
One last thing, an anecdote about the last time I played the game.
My friends and I were meeting up in <Elektro> so we could loot more safely. Before we knew it, the server we were in was full. I sat in Elektro, waiting for my friends to arrive, since they had found a cargo truck, and searched for food and supplies. After a while, i heard the roar of a truck engine approaching Elektro, followed by my buddy yelling "HOLY♥♥♥♥♥♥WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥ IS HAPPENING" I looked up to the windows to see outside on the hill above Elektro, what i can only describe as a truck wrestling. Three semis were in a veritable death race,  shunting and ramming to destroy the others.
Soon gunfire could be heard echoin all the town, not only from the trucks and their passengers, but from other people hiding in other parts of Elektro. Unfortunately my friends were both shot or run over, leaving me alone to face the murderous truck gang. What happened next i can only describe in my friends words. "They're just circlling you, like a bunch of sharks" and that was accurate. I stayed inside my relatively safe cabin and watched and listened as the roar of the trucks confirmed they were indeed just circling the house waiting for me to come out. The next half hour was spent by me fleeing through the back alleys of Elektro, trying to elude my pursuers as well as the other survivors that were in Elektro at the time.
That didn't go so great, they followed me to the hospital where i hid, axe on high, ready to strike. But axes don't do so graet against revolvers and i was shot dead by my pursuers.
TL;DR
its not a game, its a simulation. Don't buy it if you want a game to enjoy alone, this game shines because of its open interaction, and gritty, harsh world. Active devs mean this game is only going to keep getting better. I Predict eventually it will kill it's competitors.

Undertale is a very interesting combination of ideas and genres. Sometimes, seemingly conflicting ones, even. For example - it's a jRPG (of Earthbound-like variety) at the first glance, but focuses more on things more associated with adventure and visual novel games in both overworld and battle mode, bullet hell dodging, Resident Evil: Gaiden-like fighting and even platforming. It goes very meta about RPG mechanics, yet usually doesn't leave it's own fiction to be fourth wall breaking to the point of losing immersion. And most surprisingly of all - it manages to be much more of an actual "roleplaying game" than a lot of RPGs. You can be an adventurer, you can be a hero or you can be an actual proper world threatening villain. And game goes to incredible lengths to acknowledge what you do and how you do it.
This game will make you laugh and smile every few moments. And it will make you worry for it's characters. And it can make you sad. And it can make you care about what you do in the game. It treats it's own fiction with enormous care, using tricks more associated with romhacks and "haunted game"-like games to make world of Undertale, the game itself, seem like a real window to some other world, and does it well. At least, most of the time.
It's not without issues, yeah. Sometimes the writing or the tone goes a bit too off, going very black and white or just of quality more associated with fanfics and amateurish work. Sometimes jokes are not let go earlier than they should be. Sometimes the battle-associated mechanics are insanely frustrating, especially if you're actually trying to not hurt anyone on your first go only to be forced to use "Fight" command in the very late game, something you probably don't even know how to do, for a fight that lasts longer than it should. In fact, sometimes game just feels to try and be "challenging" just for the sake of the idea that "all games should be challenging", despite all other parts of Undertale making the game fantastic without any need for "challenge".
But these issues are noticeable just because how contrasting they are to everything else. Just because they unexpectedly hit you in the middle of you having a blast in a great game. Maybe, those little things will be tweaked later on and the game will become even better. But even now it's a game that I can highly recommend for, well, anyone. Great game, great soundtrack, it's an unforgettable and fun experience.

Ok, I've put enough time into this game now, and seen it develop enough to be able to make a few points about it. Hoplefully it'll help would-be players know what they're getting in to/
It should go wiithout saying that since this game is in alpha, bugs are common. This review will not be considering issues that are blatntly just a factor of the game not being done yet. That being said, you will likely see some clipping issues, occasional bugs with loot and pickups, occasional bugs with health (i had a character drink about five gallons of gasoline and just shrug it off at one point.)
A few months ago I would not have recommended this game, it was just a litle too unpolished to be playable. However, in the last few weeks and months the devs have been fevrishly updating, and adding content, which now makes the game enjoyable to play.
OK, so first we must consider something crucial; what sets DayZ apart from the multitude of other sandbox survival mmo zombie games? Well, it's not really a game so much as a simulation. The fictional eastern Ukrainian region of Chernarus is brutal and unforgiving (and not due to bugs). DayZ will punish you every step of the way for not knowing what to do. It's extraordinarily difficult to get into initially, but once you do you'll find a rich and complex system with more potentilal than any of it's competitors.

Let me give an exmaple; Let's compare Dayz to say...Unturned, H1Z1, and seven days to die. Arguably, all these games are the same thing, and that is zombie survival sandbox mmo. While the aforementioned games rely heavily on gaming cliches such as ridiculous weapons and proficiencies, or ignorance of things like cold, wetness, hunger, condition equipment, etc. That doesn't make any of those games bad, far from it, if you want a real game with solid objectives and recognizable hard mechanics, play those games. (in particular unturned is free and pretty fun) but that;s not DayZ.
DayZ is like you literally woke up one day into a world that was lost to zombies weeks ago. You have no idea what or who is left, or what you might do to survive. Oh no! a zombie! But wait, you have no weapons. How long would it realistically take to punch a zombie to death? or beat it down with a broom or rock? Forever. If something seems like it would be that way in real life, it's probably accounted for in DayZ. You'll even break your legs by falling more than 15 feet, causing you to exclusively be able to crawl around in slow, agonizing ways.
So with all that being said, If you're going to play it alone, don't bother. The game shines the most when you play with friends or brave a highy populated server. Humans are terrible people when the chips are down, and in DayZ the chips were eaten a long time ago. Every single person you meet online is a heart-pounding threat.
One last thing, an anecdote about the last time I played the game.
My friends and I were meeting up in <Elektro> so we could loot more safely. Before we knew it, the server we were in was full. I sat in Elektro, waiting for my friends to arrive, since they had found a cargo truck, and searched for food and supplies. After a while, i heard the roar of a truck engine approaching Elektro, followed by my buddy yelling "HOLY♥♥♥♥♥♥WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥ IS HAPPENING" I looked up to the windows to see outside on the hill above Elektro, what i can only describe as a truck wrestling. Three semis were in a veritable death race,  shunting and ramming to destroy the others.
Soon gunfire could be heard echoin all the town, not only from the trucks and their passengers, but from other people hiding in other parts of Elektro. Unfortunately my friends were both shot or run over, leaving me alone to face the murderous truck gang. What happened next i can only describe in my friends words. "They're just circlling you, like a bunch of sharks" and that was accurate. I stayed inside my relatively safe cabin and watched and listened as the roar of the trucks confirmed they were indeed just circling the house waiting for me to come out. The next half hour was spent by me fleeing through the back alleys of Elektro, trying to elude my pursuers as well as the other survivors that were in Elektro at the time.
That didn't go so great, they followed me to the hospital where i hid, axe on high, ready to strike. But axes don't do so graet against revolvers and i was shot dead by my pursuers.
TL;DR
its not a game, its a simulation. Don't buy it if you want a game to enjoy alone, this game shines because of its open interaction, and gritty, harsh world. Active devs mean this game is only going to keep getting better. I Predict eventually it will kill it's competitors.

No. They play it as smart and as cheap as they can get away with. This prevented relying on game mechanics alone and forced people to think smarter not just thicker to properly defend themselves. Human intelligence should be apart of this game, instead it appears to be going in the opposite direction. Our beloved caveman simulator is becoming an AI simulator. (quarries, pumps, drones, auto-turrets, vehicles) Goodbye "Rust", hello "Technology" or "Garry's Whim". I say the buy depends on what the current iteration is like and what the updates are geared towards at the time.Or buy when they make concrete decisions on mechanics or the general idea of what end game is supposed to become. For an early access survival game that drops you into the game as a fully naked (censoring available) man geared with a rock and a torch, it's pretty epic.
The hunger/thirst starts out low and some take that into too much consideration when they start out but the main concern is making sure you don't get killed by someone else.
The objective is to "survive" and the gameplay as a noob is exactly that on the Official servers. Those who have been gathering the Blueprints for better gear don't mind the monthly wipes of items and bases, but those who are just joining in? Well, it's a "dog eat dog world" out here in Rust.
If Official is too tough, the awesome selection of Community Servers is always available. These modded servers can be interesting though. Some wipe items and bases at random... some every 2 weeks! Currently the one I'm on wipes even the Blueprints (that can take a long time to obtain) every 4 weeks(monthly) to keep it interesting and noob friendly.
Biggest Con I find right now is that an attacking animal (wolf/bear) can hit you and deal damage while at a considerable distance.
Biggest Pro I find right now is the epic replayability.
10 for 10 will play again.

I use to have no life playing rust. Then explosives started to become weaker (in both good and bad ways) then ladders became useless and the direction of the game seemed to change. Now you can spend all week to get ready for a raid and the server wiped before you could, because you arent playing with an active 5 man crew. Sure bases might be more secure but that was half the fun. Let me ask you this does a bank robber blow through the banks front door or wall? No. They play it as smart and as cheap as they can get away with. This prevented relying on game mechanics alone and forced people to think smarter not just thicker to properly defend themselves. Human intelligence should be apart of this game, instead it appears to be going in the opposite direction. Our beloved caveman simulator is becoming an AI simulator. (quarries, pumps, drones, auto-turrets, vehicles) Goodbye "Rust", hello "Technology" or "Garry's Whim". I say the buy depends on what the current iteration is like and what the updates are geared towards at the time.Or buy when they make concrete decisions on mechanics or the general idea of what end game is supposed to become. I will miss the Rust I Fell so in love with, I hope in the end you come back to your roots.

Undertale is a beautifully crafted game with intense gameplay, inspiring music, and clever humor. This text-based game is filled with decisions, which will all result with different endings. The diverse characters and items add to your journey, but the humor sets Undertale apart from other games. About 50% of all NPC's dialogue includes some kind of pun and/or joke. Many Easter Eggs are hidden through-out the world. By far, the funniest characters are Temmies.
In this game, players are able to 'personalize' who their character becomes. Players can choose how violent they act to how much they explore the land.
Undertale is very similar to the Nintendo 64 game, Paper Mario. They are both played the same way- turn-based fights and a branching story line, however Undertale outranks all other games of this type. Even though much shorter in gameplay, Undertale can be enjoyed multiple times because of choice making.
Overall Rating for Undertale- 9/10

I have over 100 hours on this game. So i'm going to tell you how people are in this game.
If you are looking forward into buying this game., Make sure you know what you will be getting into when you play this game.
1, Looters. It's a cool feature to be able to live in houses in this game. And i really like the fact that every level you play will not be the same. The thing is with looters. Some of them get really cocky and they get a group of 5 or 6 people with guns and smash your walls down and steal everything you worked hard for. I have no problem with that. It's just depressing havng to start over from what you found. I wish there would be away to set up this one post to be able to remove the looters gun untill they leave the base area. They have clip boreds in this game so that you can block people from building into your area. But it really doesn't help if people are over powerd and break down your walls with out even trying. And i'm talking about the people that just start out. If you get to the point that you have made a really big base and you spent hours working on it, It gets a little upsetting when they raid a huge base that you spent hours on. Something you should know about before buying Rust.
2, The coummunity. Their are some really nice people on this game. But most of the time, You are dealing with people that shoot you on the spot and take all your stuff even though you told them you was a friendly. But that's nothing compaired to the things you see in the chat room. There are people that are so gross in the chat room, It just makes you sick to know them kind of people live in this world.
3, Server wipes. Something you should know right off the bat befor buying this game is that they do server wipes. Witch means they remove everything from the level, Houses bases, You name it. I have been hearing about blue print wipes to. But i heard they are rare. But just keep that in mind that they might take away all of your blue prints even thought you worked your♥♥♥♥♥off trying to find quarries and all that.
4, Server lag. I have noticed when playing this game. My PC lags like hell well playing in a server for a few hours. Once this happens. You need to reset Rust. And it does become a pain after awhile. But maybe it's something they will fix in the futrue.
5, The Graphics. What you see in the videos on steam that was posted here on this page is nothing like the real thing. (And mind you. I have a really good gaming PC. )The game does not run at 60 FPS. It runs at like maybe 40 or 50. Or even lower if the game is lagging.So keep that in mind as well.
6, Looks can be deceiving. This game from the videos looks like a happy game. And i thought that when i got the game. I was all ready to get to see all the nice people helpping one another out and all that. But i was wrong. 90% of the people that play this game don't give a♥♥♥♥♥♥about you no matter who you are. Don't get me wrong. I have met some really nice people along the way of playing this game. You can still find friends that could become your best friend. But people get into groups and they will make fun of new people that just started the game. And it's sad. Vary sad. I see in the chat room sometimes people say that they kill naked people for no reason even if they are friendly. One thing you got to know is people don't have morals anymore in this time of the world. So you will see it play out here on rust.
7, Serviving. If you want to make it in this game. You need to have friends who play this game and that they are willing to get you on your feet. If not. It could be really hard for someone like myself to start out in this game.
After all that being said. Here are the things i really like about Rust.
1, Building on this game is really good. You can go as far as making a town and making stores and sell items in the stores to other players. ( Just make sure you have a friend with a gun to protect you if things get nasty. )
2, Collecting things. Barals are like finding gold. They have goodies inside of them and sometimes contains guns and blue prints.
3, Building things with my friends on here. I really enjoy playing this game with friends. One friend is cooking metal ore, And you are out cutting down trees and looking for ore rocks to bring back to base. Something i realy enjoy doing in this game.
4, The fact that i can hind my really valuble stuff underground in a box is really cool. I can hide guns underground and get raided and have nobody see the box that i put underground. Really a nice feature to have for this game.
5, I like the fact that every map is huge and has something new in it rather than a game like dead island. This game is open world and it really sets a nice theme to the game.
6, Being able to go around and see new houses and old houses that have been sitting for a long time, You never know what you will find from just walking down the road or hill.
7, The fact that servers can hold up to 150 people at a time. So meeting you people is endless on here. ( But like i said, 90% of them are♥♥♥♥♥holes. )
With all said. I really enjoy playing this game. I just wish some things could be better and the community could be a lot nicer. But that's something you can't get rid of in a online community. It's everywhere you go. And it's only getting worse. But i rate this game 8 out of 10. I am lookng forward to the updates in this game. I hope the developers see my post and understand what is happining in this game. If you get♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off easy. Then this game is not for you. Till then. Hope this post was helpful to anyone wanting to buy this game. Take care.

After nearly 500 hours spent in-game, I now feel confident in giving this a fair review. I have played this game enough to see it go through many stages of it's development. I spent nearly twice as many hours in the mod version for Arma 2 outside of steam, so I already knew what I was getting into when I bought it. Here is what I have to say about DayZ Standalone:
If games have ever felt too unrealistic for you, you might like DayZ. With emphasis on realism, simulation, and authenticity, DayZ strives to give the player an accurate prediction of what living in a post-cataclysm world where mankind has reverted from civilization into survival of the fittest. Any purveyor of a George Romero zombie flick knows that the true danger lies not in the environment, nor even in the undead/infected horrors, but instead in humanity itself. Keeping your grip on sanity and civilization is much more challenging than simply surviving.
That leads to the games most interesting mechanic: player interactions. With a myriad of game mechanics to facilitate a variety of interactions, it is always a tense moment when you happen across another player in the game world. Is he armed? Does he have friends? Are they armed? Do they have good intentions, or do they plan to kill me and dine on my corpse? Do I have enough ammo to kill them all efficiently?
Being entirely multiplayer, this mechanic is always present. You can never safely loot a military camp without looking over your shoulder. You can never just survive. You have to make hard choices and tough calls. Death is more than just inconvenient in this game, and players actively seek to preserve their lives at great lengths.
The actual game mechanics may feel slow and clunky, but as a simulation game it is pretty believable. Bullet physics are nearly the best in the genre, with realistic bullet drop and material penetration. Damage is more than HP on a bar, it is realistic. Get shot in the leg with a high-calibre rifle? You are probably going to have a broken leg. Headshots are often fatal no matter what firearm was used to inflict it. A broken arm makes it nearly impossible to aim accurately.
Mechanics aside, the graphics are very good so far. Realistic environments, high resolution textures, and impressive lighting effects all add to the atmosphere. The animations are pretty good, although some could use improvement. Training yourself to pick out players from the environment is a challenging experience, ultimately I find it the most realistic game environment I have seen in a game. You are going to want a decent gaming rig to play this game because, despite being able to be played on lower-quality machines, it is much more immersive when the graphics can be set on higher settings.
My review has been positive so far, but this game is not without its flaws. Being in alpha for over a year, it's riddled with bugs. Each patch as they introduce new features, new bugs get introduced as well. They fix some of them, but since alpha is the feature-development stage, they are not usually a priority unless they are completely game breaking. Performance is definitely under par, and it is very difficult for even high-end rigs to get consistent frame rates.
Aside from bugs and performance, there is also the problems of hackers exploiting security flaws, slow game development, and the flaws inherent to a simulation sandbox game (such as long amounts of time spent running from place to place, the difficulty of learning the game without tutorials, etc). There previously had been flaws with the game persistence and the spawning of loot, but each patch brings us a bit closer to a satisfactory solution.
Final Verdict (tl;dr): At 35 dollars for early access, I highly reccommend adding this title to your library if you enjoy sandbox games, survival or tactical simulations, and direct player interactions. Although flawed in its present state, this game has the potential to become highly polished. It is well worth the price. Immersive gameplay, high quality graphics, and an immense player base will keep this game from going dead for quite some time. It is my go-to game, and I expect it will remain so for another 500+ hours.
Final Score: 9/10

Undertale - Maybe Games can be Art
Instead of being like most people on the internet and saying things like "13/10 2gr8" or "had a bad time. 10/10" or "best game ever. if you disagree you are the worst scum out there and i will proceed tell you, in detail, why", I have decided to write an actual reveiw for this game, praising its strengths, and pointing out its weaknesses.
---REVEIW START---
So if you've been living under a rock, you might have no idea what Undertale is. And that’s pretty sad. But that is also a great thing. THE LESS YOU KNOW ABOUT THIS GAME, THE BETTER IT IS! Sorry, for yelling there, but that is extremely important. But gameplay-wise, the game acts like a traditional JRPG, where you traverse a world from a top-down view, solve puzzles, and most importantly, engage in random enemy encounters. Except, the game will take all the expectations you have for the genre, and flip them on their head.
GAMEPLAY:
Unlike a traditional RPG, you do not have to kill anybody. You can discover a series of actions that will allow you to give your attackers mercy, and "spare" them. But if you do, you will never gain any XP, and won't ever level up, making the game much harder. Even if you chose not to attack your foes, they will still attack you. And this is another way Undertale denies the genre it comes from. When enemies attack, you aren't forced to take damage like in a normal RPG, but instead, you enter a kind of minigame-esque window. Here, enemies will launch lots of harmful projectiles, which deal damage to you if they hit you. So you must try to dodge all of the incoming enemy projectiles. This really mixes up the gameplay, as every enemy has multiple attacks, and can even do combo attacks when working with other enemies. The gameplay, even still, is Undertale's weakest link. I, personally, enjoyed it very much, and it never got too stale to me, but there are some that disagree. For starters, if you aren't good at these dodging minigames, you are going to have a very bad time in some of these fights. Also, the bosses, although they mix things up often, they are long, occasionally tedious, and one can often get stuck on them. However, none of these issues are big enough to detract from the game's value. Case in point: a friend of mine who didn't like the combat, and got stuck on multiple bosses constantly, considers the game to be the best he's played all year.
---Gameplay: 8/10 (Unique, Occasionally Repetitive)
STORY:
This game has a great story. It is deep, complex, and emotional. It may not seem like much at first, but as you go deeper into the game, you will find yourself enthralled and engaged. Unfortunately, there are some times in which you will be very confused, and the game does little to remedy that, which can lead to confusion blocking some of the most emotional experiences of the game. Besides that, the game has some of the most humorous and instantly likable characters I've ever seen. You will be laughing, or at least smiling, for the majority of the encounters you have with these great characters. The other times, you will probably be tearing up, or in deep contemplation. However, some of these characters fall into some predictable tropes, and don't do much outside of them. The writing is still top-notch. As a side-note, this game's creator thought of just about everything, and the game has dialogue for just about every action you can take, in and out of the game itself. But overall, the story is engaging, heartfelt, emotional, AND SHOULD NOT BE SPOILED (sorry, I did it again)
---Story: 9/10 (Emotional, Heartfelt, Beautiful)
GRAPHICS:
Ok, let’s be real. This game has some pretty garbage graphics. I didn't mind them, but I know some people (not personally, thank goodness), that have turned the game off simply because it looks like trash. This is true, but it is the dumbest excuse I have ever heard to not enjoy this wondrous game. And also, the game will slightly ramp up its graphics as you progress, so don't be turned off by the first area
---Graphics: 4-6/10 (Tolerable. Depends on your opinions on artstyle)
MUSIC:
This game has incredible music. It has invaded my music playlists, and been in my head for about a month as of this review. I'm listening to it while typing this, and more likely than not, I'm listening to it right now, while you are reading this. It’s that good. It’s catchy, emotional, and extremely well written. This game's music is incredible. My friends while playing, would be right before a boss, and would ask "is this boss hard?", and all I would say in response would be "It has good music", and they wouldn't care about the difficulty of the boss anymore. There is an incredible use of motifs, and the soundtrack is all-around superb
---Music: 10/10 (Memorable, Exciting, Emotional)
SOMETHING ELSE (?):
This review so far has not done this game justice. Looking at the individual parts makes this game seem so much less than it is. I made my almost all of my friends that didn't have it already buy this game, because I wanted to share the experience so badly. I watched almost all of their playthroughs, and I saw them love it all the way. This game got into my head. I've binge watched youtubers playing this game. I've seen so many people laugh and love and cry all because of this game. There is something indescribable about this game, it is truly heartfelt, and it deserves to be played by you, and all of your friends. In the end, Undertale isn't a perfect game, but it’s a unique one, and one that you won't forget, or put down in the near future
---Magic: 10/10 (Heartfelt, Moving, and Witty all at once. This is a powerful game)
FINAL SCORE:
9.8/10 (One of the best games the year, maybe more, as long as you can put up with some minor annoyances)
It was a truly life changing experience.

Undertale has been called one of the best games ever. But is it?
Plot: You're a human child who feel into a hole directly to the subterranean world where monsters live, isolated from the human world. Your character's goal is pretty much to GTFO of there before you're killed. That's all that I'm going to spoil, as this game has a good story with some surprises that are better left to be uncovered by the players themselves. Enough to say, it'll definitely need to be played more than once to see all of them.
Aesthetics: The game's graphics have an Earthbound-like feel in it: simple 16-bits graphics, backgrounds with basic textures and weird character design. The battles are way less attractive to the eyesight, the enemy models are more detailed, but they are usually monochromatic. Even with all this, the game is still appealing to eyes and ears. The game has a running meta theme that's reflected perfectly on screen, in battles and in the dialogue itself. The support NPCs can be somewhat predictable, but rarely boring. And the music is exquisite, making boss battles memorable events.
Gameplay: Retro bullet hell-JRPG. That's the real gameplay in this game. Attacking is a mini-game of timing, and each turn you can avoid damage in a mini-game of evading the enemies' attacks.  If you wish, you can spare the enemy, but it requires special conditions for different monsters (but you get no EXP, and you'll still have to evade attacks). Whichever method you decide to use, you'll pass most of the battle evading enemy projectiles; which isn't a bad thing, as the patterns are varied (even from the same monster) and short, and some battles can be a breeze while others feel like you're playing Ikaruga. Outside battle is just walking, talking with NPCs and solving puzzles. Most are simple, but some are a little more ingenious.
Likes: This game feels like an amalgam of light-heartedness and deepness. The game slowly becomes meta; specially if you die in boss battles (sometimes letting you skip monologues in your next-attempt) and in subsequent replays. Even the battles go meta, with projectiles no limiting themselves to the mini-game area and having an effect somewhere else. When it happens it's chaos and it's entertaining.
Dislikes: As minor complains, I think the game takes the meta road a little to far by the end (like crashing the game on purpose if you lose). And the final boss looks is an LSD-induced nightmare; with visuals way out of place from the rest of the game (imagine Mario using a Kamehameha in the final battle with Bowser).
Conclusion: This game does a lot of things right, and has lots of original (or rare but well implemented) features. IMO not the best game ever. But it's still 100% a MUST play.

A game created by Toby Fox, creator of music for the webcomic Homestuck. Honestly, this game is really good. It features the main types of endings, and variations thereupon. It defies regular conventions of games, such as saving, levels, exp, and battles.
Now, being that this game was created by a composer, one wonders: how is the music? Answer? Very good. Seriously, there isn't one track in this game that I can't listen to and enjoy. Not only that, but there is a fantastic use of motifs in the music. If you like music in video games, getting the soundtrack is worth it.
The gameplay is, for the most part, nothing new. Well, there is one thing: it is possible to play through any given battle without killing anything, with the handy dandy "Mercy" option. It opens up plenty of possibilities for the game, and how you play it.
The characters are all rather well fleshed out, even the ones that don't actually have flesh. Yes, that's right, there are skeletons in this game. And robots. And ghosts. And more! They're all unique characters, and you'll likely find yourself growing attached to them at some point in the game.
So, TL;DR, if you like RPGs, pleasant music, and interesting, changable storylines, this is a game for you.
