I really wanted to hate this game. I didn't wanna get sucked into the hype like it seemed everyone else had. But I just couldn't, the game's too goddamn good to hate.
My first run was a neutral run, I killed a few enemies at the start, skipped any optional objectives(such as the dates with Papyrus and Undyne) and went full pacifist later on(killed Muffet though, ♥♥♥♥ spiders) and my impression of the game was decidedly "meh". Then I replayed it with the intention of getting the true ending, and absolutely fell in love with it. I noticed little things in the plot that I didn't know about on my first playthrough, I did all the dates and thoroughly enjoyed every second of them, and once I got to the true final boss and ending, my opinion of the game went from "meh" to "I ♥♥♥♥ing love this game".
I don't know if I could really say the writing and plot were the best I've ever experienced, but it's definitely up there. Undertale is simultaneously the happiest, funniest, saddest and scariest game I've ever played. The gameplay is leagues above any RPG I've played, completely abandoning traditional RPG gameplay and making every bit of the fights entirely skill-based, with the sparing mechanic adding a bit of a puzzle to every enemy.
And the music. Dear god the music. I've never bought a game's soundtrack before, but I bought this one as soon as I had the funds in my Steam wallet. The music was honestly the only reason I continued playing despite not having much of an interest in the game at first, I can't describe exactly WHY I enjoyed it so much but it's easily the best soundtrack out of any game I've played
Don't be stupid like me and let the batshit crazy fanbase turn you away from the game, it's truly a great experience despite each run only taking roughly 6 hours. The longer you wait to play it, the less you'll enjoy it as you'll inevitably have some things spoiled for you

A game created by Toby Fox, creator of music for the webcomic Homestuck. Honestly, this game is really good. It features the main types of endings, and variations thereupon. It defies regular conventions of games, such as saving, levels, exp, and battles.
Now, being that this game was created by a composer, one wonders: how is the music? Answer? Very good. Seriously, there isn't one track in this game that I can't listen to and enjoy. Not only that, but there is a fantastic use of motifs in the music. If you like music in video games, getting the soundtrack is worth it.
The gameplay is, for the most part, nothing new. Well, there is one thing: it is possible to play through any given battle without killing anything, with the handy dandy "Mercy" option. It opens up plenty of possibilities for the game, and how you play it.
The characters are all rather well fleshed out, even the ones that don't actually have flesh. Yes, that's right, there are skeletons in this game. And robots. And ghosts. And more! They're all unique characters, and you'll likely find yourself growing attached to them at some point in the game.
So, TL;DR, if you like RPGs, pleasant music, and interesting, changable storylines, this is a game for you.

This is truly an amazing game, amazing enough that I'm actually leaving a review for it, I don't usually do this. I got this game merely because my friend told me about the Netural Ending and how freaky deaky it was, and surprisingly, it was enough to convince me to buy this game. And let me tell you, it was the best decision of my life. While it's a somewhat short game, roughly 10+ hours of gameplay, those hours will either be amazing, or awful. The characters introduced throughout the short but memorable story will probably be better friends then some of your real friends. But of course, you can't make these friends unless you choose to. In most games now a days, it's just kill everything that exists because reasons, and nothing changes. In this game, each time you choose to take a life, it will only come back to bite you in the bum.
And if you regret killing one monster, and restart the game to make up for it, the game will remind you of your wrong doing. But if you spare everyone you meet, and form friendships along the way, you will certainly receive a critical hit in the feels. I think it's truly unique that there are actually multiple endings based on your actions, and even though it's just a game, you will remember everything you do in this game, from enjoying some spaghetti with your friends, to saving an entire race from imprisonment and becoming a hero, or the opposite, and becoming the harbringer of destruction possessed by a demon hellbent on killing everyone. The choice is yours. But seriously, why even bother reading the reviews? Buy the game and try it out for yourself. It's gotten enough hype from the interwebs, join the party.

This is truly an amazing game, amazing enough that I'm actually leaving a review for it, I don't usually do this. I got this game merely because my friend told me about the Netural Ending and how freaky deaky it was, and surprisingly, it was enough to convince me to buy this game. And let me tell you, it was the best decision of my life. While it's a somewhat short game, roughly 10+ hours of gameplay, those hours will either be amazing, or awful. The characters introduced throughout the short but memorable story will probably be better friends then some of your real friends. But of course, you can't make these friends unless you choose to. In most games now a days, it's just kill everything that exists because reasons, and nothing changes. In this game, each time you choose to take a life, it will only come back to bite you in the bum.
And if you regret killing one monster, and restart the game to make up for it, the game will remind you of your wrong doing. But if you spare everyone you meet, and form friendships along the way, you will certainly receive a critical hit in the feels. I think it's truly unique that there are actually multiple endings based on your actions, and even though it's just a game, you will remember everything you do in this game, from enjoying some spaghetti with your friends, to saving an entire race from imprisonment and becoming a hero, or the opposite, and becoming the harbringer of destruction possessed by a demon hellbent on killing everyone. The choice is yours. But seriously, why even bother reading the reviews? Buy the game and try it out for yourself. It's gotten enough hype from the interwebs, join the party.

I had a friend recommend this game to me, and quite honestly, I wasn't sure what I was going to think of it. It's was my usual "I'll give it a shot". And so I did.
I was already a fan of the pixelated style, and RPGs have also been a personal favorite of mine. Now I've played many a pixelated RPG in my days, from simple brower-based to console, but Undertale sets the bar at a whole new level.
Here's why: this game breaks what I like to call the "player's wall". Most games have you playing as a character/inanimate object in which you must automatically assume you inhibit the characteristics of within the game. Along with this, you expect everything in your game to remain within the boundaries of a traditional game.
Undertale breaks the "player's wall" by making your choices not only seem to personally and gravely affect every file you may create, but goes beyond standard games with its quirks that often make the game feel as though it has a mind of its own. The well-placed implements of humor, as well as sudden, unexpected twists in graphic style, dialogue, and above all, story progression makes this game seem well out of its element.
It's the unpredictable nature of Undertale that ultimately breaks the player's wall, and makes me feel like I'm doing more than just playing a game. I'm experiencing something made personally for
. The characters are talking to
, not the small bundle of pixels I control.
Amazing character development. Fantastic story arch with a roundabout finish. Very entertaining and humorous, and hard to stop once you've started. Short and sweet, and ran smoothly.
Each battle sequence featured different enemies with unique abilities, so much that despite the layout of the battles being the same, they never felt redundant.
I highly recommend! Fun, touching, with a high replay value! ^.^

Sit down ladies and gentlemen, let me tell you a story.
Once upon a time a lonley noob logged onto his first server, the great London III Test server to be precise. I never left this world but instead began my time mingling with the local flora and fauna, once mauled by a bear in the dead of night as I was escaping from angry Russians with Assualt rifles and another gunned down by an angry helicopter as I inspected by loot, stolen from the corpse of an unsuspecting man.
I started with my small 2 x 2 hut which lasted the staggering time of 27 minutes before I was beaten to death by angry men with rocks - Note to self, I really must get a lock for that door. They took my Wilson, torch, stone hatchet, blueprints and hammer, then disappeared into the night.
Lurking around on chat I found an active community whom deemed me friendly, I joined them only to discover they were actively at war with another "clan" - the lonely noob was cast into a great battle and was soon geared and ready for combat!
It ended in a hail of gunshots and looked like a scene from Mafia as my body was thrown against a stone wall from the sheer quantity of Thompson bullets hitting my frail body. I respawned in my bed, aptly named "Liquids S**g sack" and collected my meagre belongings - they team assisted me in taking a small and poorly guarded home on the airfield for myself. I joined with a few other solo'ers as we crafted and reinforced our little part in the world, we sent out supply runners and traded with the larger clans, all whilst maintaining good relations with the other server dwellers.
The day before the wipe, everything changed. Darkness fell that night as usual, I sat atop my tower with a team of three - we waited for the sunrise but little did we know we would be cast into a recreation of the purge. It started small, a few skirmishes here and there, the odd burst of gunfire or stray arrow but soon out outer wall was slowly chipping away. The Russians had found us and they were determined to get in, I moved around silently on our upper tower and peaked around, only to be met by the sound of my skull crushing under the weight of a finely timed rifle shot. I respawned quickly at the tower sleeping bag and retrieved my equipment, shaking I moved around to the lower firing platform and thats where I saw them, several members scatted on the rocks - I look aim - FIRE! I direct hit, his wails could be heard and my position was met by a barrage of fire. Wood splinted and the stone clanged as the air was filled with lead, we had lost the base, the encampment that has stood the test of time but in the end we were undermanned and out gunned.
My allies fell and with no local sleeping bags made were banished to the unknown of the darkness.
A messaged appeared in the chat - "We are coming." - Our saviours had arrived, the local smaller groups had combined into a roving kill party to assist us. As I sit under my stone stairs bandaging my wounds, the cackles of fire eminated from outside, the rumbles of F1 granades, the sound of whizzling lead and the thrum of arrows was all around. Dirty, bloody and glorious.
The fire fight died down outside, I crept towards the sniping perch and peered out. It was done, we were victorious. We lost some brothers in arms but the day was won, I ran down stairs to greet my new brothers, opening my airlocks and reaching the front door. The door flew open as the electronic lock pinged, the team had assembled outside I walked to towards them and  ... BANG. BANG. I fell to the floor, screaming and bleeding. The voice chat icon appeared "We are sorry", they stepped over my body and began looting my gatehouse.
So ended my Rust adventure.
The treacherous "allies" will fall, I swear this. The first light dawned on a fresh server wipe, I look out upon my new grassy home. I smile. "Soon."

Undertale is an rpg with graphics and an art style of snes rpgs and has hummor similiar to Earthbound. Despite this, the game does not ever rely on nostalgia to be a good game. Instead, its a one of the most creative games I have ever played in my entire life. The main difference between this game and traditional turn-based rpgs is that you dont have to kill any enemies. You heard that right... NOBODY HAS TO DIE, not even the final boss. Although if you want to be a cold blooded killer then you can. But if you dont, you can be a pacifist and "act" (that will make more sense when you play the game) and spare your enemies without killing them. Being a pacifist actually has perks though. For one, if you are a pacifist then the game is much more light-hearted and happy. Also, if you dont kill boss characters you can go on dates with them and hear lots of funny dialogue. When you play the pacifist run though you only have 20 HP for the ENTIRE GAME. Did I forget to mension that on enemies turns (since it is turn-based) you basically play a bullet hell minigame to avoid their attacks, and you have to do something entirely different to spare each different enemy. But if you play the Genocide run (which I highly reccommend you dont play first), its dark, sad, depressing, and makes you feel like a jerk. This is because in a genocide run ABSOLUTELY EVERYONE HAS TO DIE. You arent allowed to spare anything or else you mess up the run. Combine this creative way to play with a wonderful cast of characters and you got your self one amazing game.

"Would you smooch a ghost?"
Yes, yes I would. I'll be honest. I was turned off by Undertale. I was never really a fan of classic RPG style games and when I saw this one gaining popularity I gave a sigh. But, one day I ended up buying it. Let me tell you. I do not regret buying this. I do not regret a single second of this entire game. Undertale is literally so well designed and well made that it drives me nuts. So much love and care was put into this game. So much vast detail in such a simple looking package. Undertale is so much more than what it seems. There's literally A bunch of different stories packed into here. I'm not going to get into spoilers with it but. I highly suggest giving this game a try. It's cheap. It's my game of the year. And most of all, it fills you with a sense of accomplishment. A sense that you did something good. Not many games can give you that actual feeling. And the soundtrack!!! The soundtrack is amazing and just. I love every single track. I have never loved every single track in any game ever before, but I love all of these.
All in all, Undertale is a literal masterpiece of game design and I cannot praise it enough. I can only hope that this review can convince more people to buy it and experience the game for themselves.
Stay Determined.

*Sobbing profusely* Oh Undertale I love you so much, why must you be so perfect? Putting aside all the hype and fanboyism, It's honestly up there with some of my favorite games of all time. Don't let this one slip by simply because you either think A) It's an indie game fad. B) The fanbase is ♥♥♥♥ and Tumblr is cancer. C) It's so popular it has to be garbage. D) It won an arbitrary "best game ever" poll on gamefaqs, Oh Undertale has killed my childhood!
There is no point in looking up reasons to play Undertale, because it is simply an experience everyone needs to try.

It is impossible for me to do justice to my feelings towards this game through the words of this review, but I feel like it is only right for me to write about my experience with it. I think this is the most
game I've ever played in my entire life since I started my gaming life with the Nintendo 64 when I was only 3. Never has a game left me so emotionally stricken as this one. I don't even know where to start.
Started playing this after a dear friend gifted it to me about a week before I completed my first run. Before that, my little brother would tell me how much I needed to play this game, how much I'd love it, and so on. I however, not having been truly interested in any video game that came out after 2010 due to being filled with disappointments in the past and simply growing out of games, wasn't very interested in this one either.
With time, when I had finally gotten my hands on
I began my journey with my little bro's company throughout its entirety. All I was told by him was to not kill anyone. I made that a promise to him and myself. What if I met a ruthless murderer I wondered, though? What would I do? What if I couldn't run away? Would I
to kill? I didn't want to. I couldn't break the promise.
No expectations whatsoever were had by me when I first played this. I went in as unbiased as I possibly could. Sure, I knew something was there from all the positive reviews, and with my little bro wanting me to play this so much... but I had no idea it was
good. I was utterly blown away. From the beginning, merely in the
such a powerful introduction, the attachment sparked and was incredibly strong already. The best part about this attachment is that it only grew stronger as the game went on and didn't drop at all at any moment.
The world within
is massive and astounding. The characters are fun, interesting, and charismatic. The dialogue is what I believe to be one of the most praiseworthy aspects of the game, since it's due to that, that the characters
so real, so human, and thus so easy to like. Toby is an outstanding writer, and I'm not just saying that because of his stunning story, but also because of his versatility. Going from character speech that seems to come from a 12 year old on the internet, to excellent poetry.
Something that won't go unnoticed unless for some unholy reason you have your sound disabled, is how marvelous and stellar the soundtrack is. I can't listen to a few songs in it after completing the game because they ache my chest and make me want to cry, reminiscing the moments when they were played. That is how memorable and gorgeous the music of this game really is. The music is very diverse while being shared too, I should add. It's genuinely smart and makes it even more gloriously memorable.
It's often hilarious and clever how the game comments on things you wouldn't think it'd comment on. Mere and obscure details matter. Sometimes you'll be doing a choice without even knowing it is a choice. It's so hard to describe this gem's beauty without spoiling the story, especially because the different paths one can take and the different choices one can do is one of the biggest reasons it is so magnificent.
is a deconstruction of the JRPG genre and the general idea of choice and black/white morality in video games. It manages to be simultaneously cute and humorous while being eerily dark in its own way.
It's extremely well written and designed for a one-man indie project, which is super impressive in my eyes. I cried like a little ♥♥♥♥♥ twice in my playthrough.
It only left me wanting more of its world. It left me yearning for more character interaction and development. This isn't something to be put in a negative way though, because the game doesn't need more than what it offers. It's not lacking. It's just so delightful and extraordinary that I can't help but desire more of it. The game is wonderful and fantastic, thank you so much Toby.

Let me start off by making a few key points.
- Is DayZ Standalone a finished game?
No. DayZ is far from finished, and it will most likely still be in development for quite a while. This game is far from perfect, due to sometimes game-breaking bugs, and glitches. There are currently features that still need working on, and features that still need to be implemented in the first place. Things such as getting eternal shake glitch, or being killed by stairs are common experiences in the game, and can be quite frustrating when they happen. More often than not, players will find tht they get killed by glitches more often than they get killed by other players or zombies.
Although this long process of development can be frustrating (I personally hae been upset at times), I choose to remain patient with the development team, and I choose to appreciate all the work they've clearly put into this game, even if it may be taking them longer than they promised in the past.
All too often, I see people giving the game a disike, along with a "♥♥♥♥ you, devs", or "This game is♥♥♥♥♥♥and will never be finished". Although people are entitled to their opinions, I would suggest that people considering buying DayZ just ignore these reviews, as they honestly are not costructive, and don't look at the the big picture. Instead of just looking at the status of the game's development, please consider my next point;
- Is DayZ Standalone a FUN game?
In my opinion (and 600+ hours), I can safely say that DayZ has been very fun to play. Looking past the bugs, glitches, and unfinished features, I have had hundreds of awesome experiences, with awesome people. The things that make DayZ what it is, is the player interaction, and this is something I have never had an issue with.
Gunfights, tense moments, sudden, unexpected battles, hostage situations, meeting friends and making enemies. Even just dicking around, throwing zuchinnis at passers bym or starting bambi fight club. These are, in my experience, the core features of the game. Very seldom have I ever had a boring experience on a fifty-player server. There is always somebody to meet, greet, fight, kill, etc. It really all comes down to who you meet, and how you play your cards.
If DayZ was a single player survival game, I honestly would be much more upset with the status, and speed of development, but since it is a multiplayer game, I can really back up and realize that as a player, I don't have it too bad. Although some features are broken, the game is still enjoyable to play, alone, or with friends.
So in conclusion; Yes, DayZ is buggy and is evidently ot finished as of yet, but to everybody out there being turned off by this, and reacting with anger and "♥♥♥♥ yous", you aren't doing the game any justice, when it does in fact deserve at least a little.

Sit down ladies and gentlemen, let me tell you a story.
Once upon a time a lonley noob logged onto his first server, the great London III Test server to be precise. I never left this world but instead began my time mingling with the local flora and fauna, once mauled by a bear in the dead of night as I was escaping from angry Russians with Assualt rifles and another gunned down by an angry helicopter as I inspected by loot, stolen from the corpse of an unsuspecting man.
I started with my small 2 x 2 hut which lasted the staggering time of 27 minutes before I was beaten to death by angry men with rocks - Note to self, I really must get a lock for that door. They took my Wilson, torch, stone hatchet, blueprints and hammer, then disappeared into the night.
Lurking around on chat I found an active community whom deemed me friendly, I joined them only to discover they were actively at war with another "clan" - the lonely noob was cast into a great battle and was soon geared and ready for combat!
It ended in a hail of gunshots and looked like a scene from Mafia as my body was thrown against a stone wall from the sheer quantity of Thompson bullets hitting my frail body. I respawned in my bed, aptly named "Liquids S**g sack" and collected my meagre belongings - they team assisted me in taking a small and poorly guarded home on the airfield for myself. I joined with a few other solo'ers as we crafted and reinforced our little part in the world, we sent out supply runners and traded with the larger clans, all whilst maintaining good relations with the other server dwellers.
The day before the wipe, everything changed. Darkness fell that night as usual, I sat atop my tower with a team of three - we waited for the sunrise but little did we know we would be cast into a recreation of the purge. It started small, a few skirmishes here and there, the odd burst of gunfire or stray arrow but soon out outer wall was slowly chipping away. The Russians had found us and they were determined to get in, I moved around silently on our upper tower and peaked around, only to be met by the sound of my skull crushing under the weight of a finely timed rifle shot. I respawned quickly at the tower sleeping bag and retrieved my equipment, shaking I moved around to the lower firing platform and thats where I saw them, several members scatted on the rocks - I look aim - FIRE! I direct hit, his wails could be heard and my position was met by a barrage of fire. Wood splinted and the stone clanged as the air was filled with lead, we had lost the base, the encampment that has stood the test of time but in the end we were undermanned and out gunned.
My allies fell and with no local sleeping bags made were banished to the unknown of the darkness.
A messaged appeared in the chat - "We are coming." - Our saviours had arrived, the local smaller groups had combined into a roving kill party to assist us. As I sit under my stone stairs bandaging my wounds, the cackles of fire eminated from outside, the rumbles of F1 granades, the sound of whizzling lead and the thrum of arrows was all around. Dirty, bloody and glorious.
The fire fight died down outside, I crept towards the sniping perch and peered out. It was done, we were victorious. We lost some brothers in arms but the day was won, I ran down stairs to greet my new brothers, opening my airlocks and reaching the front door. The door flew open as the electronic lock pinged, the team had assembled outside I walked to towards them and  ... BANG. BANG. I fell to the floor, screaming and bleeding. The voice chat icon appeared "We are sorry", they stepped over my body and began looting my gatehouse.
So ended my Rust adventure.
The treacherous "allies" will fall, I swear this. The first light dawned on a fresh server wipe, I look out upon my new grassy home. I smile. "Soon."

"WARNING: THIS GAME IS EARLY ACCESS ALPHA. PLEASE DO NOT PURCHASE IT UNLESS YOU WANT TO ACTIVELY SUPPORT DEVELOPMENT OF THE GAME AND ARE PREPARED TO HANDLE WITH SERIOUS ISSUES AND POSSIBLE INTERRUPTIONS OF GAME" is the message they display on the main page of DayZ. Take that into account.
Although this game is a buggy, hard to run early access alpha it already has a booming community and almost 3 million players (2,991,282 at the time I wrote this review) I think that shows how even though this game isn't even complete yet it stands up against AAA titles which are also available on the steam marketplace.
DayZ is a zombie survival game and unless you are an especially calm level headed person it will make you rage and get annoyed, either at some♥♥♥♥♥♥killing you in the street or from dying to some stupid ladder bug. But the beauty of DayZ is that you can rage quit and a day or two later you'll feel the want to play it again. I understand that this may not be a good game for some people but if you get into it to start with you wont want to stop playing.
One feature that makes DayZ the game for me is the extremely tactical play you can have with friends. You'll really need to know the map of DayZ if you want to have fun with your friends or you'll have to research a lot but once you know the map you could literally play forever.
Additionally, with the constant updates coming out every month or so new game changing features are introduced contantly. It's not too long ago that DayZ standalone was a Balota deathmatch. Would recommend.

The massive drop in players on the game RUST isn't for nothing. There's no words to describe how infuriated and disappointed I am with this game in its current state.
Rust started out as one of the most amazing, innovative, and engaging survival-based multiplayer game that I had the privilege of playing. The game had a sense of tension, and doubled as a fascinating social experiment in an anarchist enviornment.
The question you're probably asking is "you're saying good stuff about it. Why are you not recommending this game?"
Simple answer: The component system.
Any sense of character progression and character development is completely destroyed, making it impossible for people new to servers to obtain any fighting chance against other players because the zones that drop essential end-game components is monopolized and controled by clans.
The first crafting system, the blueprint system, was simple and effective. Not the best, but certainly not the worst. The second crafting system, the Experience system, was tedious, but still gave players a reason to keep playing. With the component system, there's no point in playing, you don't have any recipe knowlege that will make you stand out among your group/clan, the game is 100% spoiled now. It's like having a cheat code in an old game that gave you all special weapons from the start of the game. Why play?
Worst of all, as stated before, the places that have important components are controlled by clans. This means that a new player or someone new to the server is forced to visit high-risk areas to have a fighting chance. If you lose your base, and all of your stuff, there's absolutely nothing to fall back on. There's no "Well, at least I know how to make ____ with minimal materials." Not anymore.
This game is NOT worth your money, the player base is dying QUICKLY (and has been since the component system was released) and the devs don't respond to steam forum complaints at all.
If you want a survival game that's better, play Hurt World, Age of Kings, even Miscreated is better than this garbage now. The only reason people still play it is the same reason people still play WoW. It's for nostalgic purposes, wanting to maintain loyal to a once-great game.

I don't write reviews usually. But let me explain. Im a very competative gamer. The last game i felt any real life adrenaline pumping hardcore action was Halo3. Down the long journey to becoming a General. Recently i got DayZ. But don't let that fool you, ive followed this game since the mod and have spent countless hours watching a friend play both the mod and SA. However, I didnt expect much when i got it. Was i wrong. I was absolutely blown away by how competative and immersive and ruthless the game can be.  The rush that you get when you enter a firefight,  with everything on the line, is beyond words. This game may be by far, the greatest game concept ive ever seen. How it is implemented, is another story...
-Garbage optimization (No, being in Alpha isn't an excuse). This game has been in Alpha FOREVER and just the bare minimum of a decent rendering system is LONG overdue. The current rendering system renders every single object in the player FOV. So when looking at a huge city, you are actually rendering all the furniture, rugs, walls... pretty much anything you cant see.  Normal renderers wouldnt render objects like this, it literally kills FPS.  Expect random FPS drops and zombies running through the floor and wall.
-Bad Dev Team: The Dev team made 12 million dollars in the first week. 60 million dollars total... And RAN. Most are toxic towards people who bring this point up, they are foolish.Some of that money should've been recirced back into the game.Period. Instead, its years later and the game is unplayable for most people, is riddled with glitches and bugs, and the dev team claims they have a small team that will get to optimizing a decent renderer soon (just read their patch log). That was about a year ago. Plus the lead Dev left the team after making millions off the sales, with no intentions of finishing this game. Sadly, just another money pit.
With that out of the way, i have to say the game itself is like no other.  Adrenaline pumping . PVP. Survival. Humainty at it's finest. It is tough when you are a Bambi, and even tougher when you're geared. Trust no one.
All in All, It's well worth the money. But dont expect quality updates. Most will break the game further. And dont expect to be buying anything close to a finished game, or rather, dont expect it to be finished within the next 2 years.
EDIT:  If you can't run skyrim on Ultra, do not buy this game in its current state. You'll be getting around 8-10 fps. Decent computers will average around 20-30 fps. Top ends, have no issue.
Should you buy this game?  HECK YEAH

Absolutely. Amazing. Everything about this game. You wouldn't expect a game with simple graphics about monsters and talking flowers to be realistic, but in certain ways, it is. Everything you do, every person you kill or spare, has a profound effect, not just on one playthrough, but on all the rest afterwards. This game plays with your emotions in the most amazing way. It will make you feel bad about killing and even about RESETTING.
It is incredibly well done, and well worth the $10 (or less on sale) you have to pay to get it.
And the music- if you listen to it outside the game, it sounds like video game music. Well done, but not earth-shattering. The great thing about the music isn't how it sounds outside, but how it flows with the game itself. Each soundtrack is perfectly tailored to the character and scene. And I'm not even going to TALK about the easter eggs. (So... Many... In the music... In the game...).
At first, I was hesitant to get it, but I'm glad I did. Just looking at the game, it looks cutesy, but not that interesting. However, after playing for a few minutes, I was hooked. Each playthrough only lasts about 9 hours or so, but there are so many ways to end it (Pacifist, True Pacifist, Genocide, all of the Neutral pathways, and those are just the single-playthrough ends).
I have no idea how Toby Fox fit this much awesome into such a small file, but he did. This game is also incredibly intelligent. Now, that may sound strange, but what I mean by that is that it knows. If you kill a certain character, feel bad and exit to a previous save file and spare them, one of that characters KNOWS. And this same character can mess with your save files. And exit the game without your permission. And view previous playthroughs. Creepy as heck, am I right?
All of the characters, even the random encounter monsters, have so much character. They're all adorable, and sad, and amazing. Alright, I'm done rambling. Sorry this took so long. If you took the time to read this review, then thanks, and if this game isn't worth 10 measly dollars, I don't know what is. <3

Holy hell where do I start with this game?
And yes, I got caught up riding the Undertale hype train, but hear me out. I'm not the type to get caught up in hype, so that alone says something. I also don't normally do reviews, so bare with me a bit. Alright, the whole pro's and con's thing, right?
ONE THING! Before anything else, I need to stress that if you want to expreience this game in its fullest, you HAVE TO DO A PACIFIST RUN FIRST. Wanna be a homocidal maniac later? That's fine. More power to you. But for the sake of what this game's trying to accomplish on an emotional level, be a good kid on your first walk through the Underground. You can thank me later.
PRO's (a lot of them)
1. One of the best ways I've seen of presenting a "Karma system" in a video game.
Yes, there are only three real endings, but that's not the important part. All three ending types (because doing certian things can cause different events during the endings to happen, depending on what order you did them in, what you did during your run, etc.) are actually really well thought out. It's not your standard "middle ending is♥♥♥♥♥♥so either be an angel or a devil" kind of affair. This is the kind of game that makes you want to play through it over and over again in different ways, which in my opinion anyway, is really kind of a rare thing for RPG's to pull off. Most are really drawn out one off's. You have a great time playing a traditional RPG, and maybe it was a fantastic game, but no way am I sitting through 100's hours of pounding attack commands and using healing items to be told the exact same story twice. No other RPG I've played in my decade and a half of being a dedicated fan of the genre has told me, "play through me again" quite like this one does. And maybe it's because it's a shorter RPG, but I digress.
2. This is a game that you MUST PLAY THROUGH MORE THAN ONCE TO REALLY APPRECIATE
Every ending is worth seeing. But how the world of Undertale reacts to YOU while you walk through the Underground is what makes this a must. Are you a pacifist? Great! You're going to make some new friends, and find that every encounter is a clever dialogue puzzle. The world you interact with is as sweet as you are. Decided that other main characters are worth keeping around, but you're just gonna kill whatever random monster gets in your way to save time? Alright. Certian characters will interact with you differently. Certian events won't happen. Others will. Some will play out differently. The world will be colder, but not unbearably so. Remorseless sociopath? Wanna murder everyone that gets in your way? Are you the type that keeps killing until there's literally nothing left to kill? OK... But I have to warn you... You're gonna have a bad time..... Once again, the world reflects you. Different atmosphere, diferent diolouge, and more difficult enemies more determined to stop your murderous rampage will help the Underground reflect the emptiness you're showing through your actions, assuming you have the heart to complete a Genocide run at all (I've seen a good few people that couldn't take how wrong it makes everything and stop).
3. Absolutely insane level of character and storyline depth
There are games with 1000X times the budget that don't even come close to scratching what this game does in terms of storyline and character development. I wasn't kidding when I said you'd make new friends. This is the kind of writing that makes you CARE about these little 8 bit sprites. It's what makes doing a genocide run so hard for some people. You WON'T WANT to hurt these characters (assuming you're not a complete monster). Throw in a bunch of easter eggs that only show up during certian runs, and you have an overall great story driven experience that you won't want to put down.
4. The Soundtrack
Holy freaking Hell the soundtrack on this game. Buy the soundtrack. Seriously. Stop reading this and go buy it. I don't even care if you buy the game. If you like retro style bit tracks, you need to listen to the whole album. Maybe I'm a little biased as a musician, but there are few things, to me anyway, that can make or break a game quite like the music. And this game nails it. The soundtrack alone holds up fine, but just wait until you're in the game and decide to start killing. You'll see what I mean.
5. The Community (Not really game related, but worth making the list)
The one good thing about hype trains is that they have this way of getting other creative minds to take what the subject matter has to offer, and expand on it. This part of what makes Dark Souls such a great game and Undertale has the makings for the same kind of community. Now, I love comics. I love comics more than I love cartoons. There's just something about looking at panelled pictures with text bubbles, and having your imagination run with it that makes comics one of my favorite story telling mediums. This game has generated enough hype to get people drawing a LOT of comics, and posting them online. And since this game basically plays with multiverse theory, they all hold up really well. If you finish the game, and want to see a bit of an expanded Undertale universe, hop online and look some up.
Alright. Still with me? Great!
Now, the CON's...
1. Combat
This game is all about interaction though the ACT button. Leveling is generally seen as a bad thing. As a consequence, this makes the traditional random spawn type enemies a bit too easy to topple. This makes actually fighting in this game pretty easy. Now the bosses are still great, and combat isn't really even the focus of the game. I'm not even saying this game's particularly easy to steamroll through. But it's generally pretty easy to kill your enemy.
2. It IS a shorter RPG
The game has rediculous depth. As for length... Well... I'm 9 hours in on my pacifist run, I've been taking my time looking for easter eggs and whatnot, and I'm basically at the end of the game. I have 3 or 4 more bosses I know about and I'm done. Now I know this game was made by, what, one guy? And there's plenty of replay value to be had, so I personally don't have a problem with the game's runtime. It's just something to note. As much as there is to explore and do, I just WANT MORE.
3. The FREAKING SNAIL RACE
When you get there, you'll know.
ALRIGHT! That pretty much wraps it all up. I can't think of anything else to write. I'll update if I do think of anything else though...
Catch ya later, kid. I'm going to Grillby's.

The massive drop in players on the game RUST isn't for nothing. There's no words to describe how infuriated and disappointed I am with this game in its current state.
Rust started out as one of the most amazing, innovative, and engaging survival-based multiplayer game that I had the privilege of playing. The game had a sense of tension, and doubled as a fascinating social experiment in an anarchist enviornment.
The question you're probably asking is "you're saying good stuff about it. Why are you not recommending this game?"
Simple answer: The component system.
Any sense of character progression and character development is completely destroyed, making it impossible for people new to servers to obtain any fighting chance against other players because the zones that drop essential end-game components is monopolized and controled by clans.
The first crafting system, the blueprint system, was simple and effective. Not the best, but certainly not the worst. The second crafting system, the Experience system, was tedious, but still gave players a reason to keep playing. With the component system, there's no point in playing, you don't have any recipe knowlege that will make you stand out among your group/clan, the game is 100% spoiled now. It's like having a cheat code in an old game that gave you all special weapons from the start of the game. Why play?
Worst of all, as stated before, the places that have important components are controlled by clans. This means that a new player or someone new to the server is forced to visit high-risk areas to have a fighting chance. If you lose your base, and all of your stuff, there's absolutely nothing to fall back on. There's no "Well, at least I know how to make ____ with minimal materials." Not anymore.
This game is NOT worth your money, the player base is dying QUICKLY (and has been since the component system was released) and the devs don't respond to steam forum complaints at all.
If you want a survival game that's better, play Hurt World, Age of Kings, even Miscreated is better than this garbage now. The only reason people still play it is the same reason people still play WoW. It's for nostalgic purposes, wanting to maintain loyal to a once-great game.

Undertale is a game where every aspect feels thought out. Saving has repercussions, and loading can destroy worlds. It's an RPG with great music, great character, and nothing has to die. It's Undertale, and I think it's a better successor to Fallout than Bethesda's.
This game is low budget, sharply focused. It's elevator pitch is 'the friendly RPG where nobody has to die.' The music is catchy, the art is simple, highly functional, and well done. The plot is generally simple, buoyed up by great characters and brilliant execution. Everything in Undertale matters in some way. The game is tightly coded to keep track of your choices, and it will happily tell you that. There are liars, and they're revealed, but the game never lies. It tricks you, but it doesn't lie. This means the game has to be clever, control your information, and be super sneaky about how it reveals things. It also means that the guy who made the game had to be insanely detailed about responses, because it really does remember everything.
If you're reading this, you're either looking for information on if you should play or have already done it and are seeing how much ohers agree with your assessment.
For the first, I'm sorry... but this is the game that spoiler warnings are made for. Try the demo; it hits the gameplay and shows off the early story. If what you see is worth a tenspot, I think you'll like it. If not, Toby definately won't be starving.
For the second, yes, I bought the soundtrack. I blame this one for proving that Fallout 4 is less than awesome. Also, got two endings, can't ever play again, have to watch youtubes for the others.

Disclaimer: I have had RUST before it came out on steam more than two years ago in Closed Alpha. I was heavily into base raiding and PVP. If you plan on playing in carebear PVE servers, skip this review. But here are my two cents about its current status otherwise. Take it with a grain of salt if you will...
----------------------------------
Yes: The developers are more active now than ever.
Yes: The Developers add pointless content.
Yes: It gets frequent content updates.
Yes: Game's a blast when playing with a group.
Yes: Graphics are looking more spectacular now than ever.
No: The game has good performace.
No: The Developers are fixing issues that need fixing.
No: Glitching/hacking still exists. (It's just the nature of this type of game, more on that later)
No: Game feels like a clunky mess after being rebuilt numerous times. (It was very responsive originally.)
No: Janky new mechanics are a hindrance in a situation where you need to be responsive against other players.
No: The game is STILL in Alpha Early access after two years. (Not unusual if you look at DayZ, but still.)
No: Updates are slowly transitioning towards content only updates, with less and less technical updates from Garry. (Which is what this game needs in my opinion; more on that below.)
----------------------------------
With that being said, the two biggest issues is that the game has been rebuilt from the ground up constantly, and the hacking/glitching issues.
----------------------------------
1. The updates seem to get worse. At the begening the updates seemed to fix bugs add cool content and help performace. Yet now it seems that every update breaks the game for a few days until another patch comes out to fix the last patch. The developers just got lazy; They used to update on a weekly bases and have the same issues so they did a poll and despite people wanting them to stay on a weekly bases they decided that they will go on a bi-weekly bases. They said this would stop the annoying hot fixes and enabe them to add more content in each patch. Yet take last weeks update as an example (Dev patch 80) they added almost nothing to the game, said the performace would increase (Yet most people didn'y experience any change), and managed to make the game unplayable for many (crashes) and not fun for many more. They broke much of the game with bugs and when a hotfix came out it broke a core feature of the game. They made a bug which made spawning inside your base (aka sleeping bags in your base) impossiable, which in a game like this is big. That would be like if a COD patch came out that made you unable to reload. There bi-weekly updates have not done anything to help and if anything made things worse as it game the team more time to slack. Aswell if you look at the dev vlogs it seems that every week there is at least one member taking a week off and with a dev team of like 15 people that takes a toll.
----------------------------------
2. The game used to be responsive, though with the introduction of each rebuild it turned into a more and more unresponsive mess. Movement and responsiveness are huge factors in a game where aiming and positioning are the two most important things when PVP comes into play. This leads to unsatisfying deaths feeling like your character should be moving one way but turned out to be kind of glued into a certain spot. More often than not the game looks like a testing ground for Garry to practice his coding, the game worked as is initially, and now too much time was spent redoing the entire thing just for it to look nicer and feel smoother.
----------------------------------
3. The developers are starting to slack on the things that matter. Despite 70% of the community complaining about slow performance the developers seem to be focused to much on adding useless content to the game. I personally am able to run Battlefield 4 on high setting and get a descent 39-49 fps usually stick around 45 and run Skyrim with ultra settings, lots of visual improvement mods, and 2k textures with 60fps. Yet in this game I have every setting turned all the way down to the point where the game looks like an ugly blurry mess of a game, that would have been released in the 90's and only able to achieve a horrible 16-24 fps. With a game like this fps is important and yet when the developers say they are doing a performance update personally I have not seen a change in fps. in order to run this you need a beast of a PC that should run Battlefield 4 on ultra settings at a fps of 60+.
----------------------------------
4. With hacking and glitching overall: It's hard to blame Facepunch Studios on this one, as they have taken a lot of measures to prevent hacking and glitching, but it's such a huge issue in these types of games. You can't stop someone who constantly works against you in coming out with paid/private hacks when they have a price incentive for customers who are willing to skip the games week grind if it means killing a top tier base and being at the 'end game' instantly, along with having the edge and never dying. Dying and losing your stuff is a huge net loss, both morally and game wise.
Find a hacker in CS:GO? Report him and move on, you only wasted 30 minutes of your time, and you most likely never see him again. Hackers in DayZ/RUST? Your entire weeks worth of work is down the drain. With all the anti cheat improvements, RUST is the type of game where even one hacker/glitcher getting through can ruin the game for an entire server. Though with the type of game its hard to even identify one, granted if you're offline and your stuff is just gone with the doors/walls still up, you'll have no person to point at. Even with wallers/aimbotters, it's hard to tell with no spectate option, unless you get shot in the head 5 times instantly. But a game such as this can't be expected to have a spectate option. Like I said its just the nature of this type of game.
----------------------------------
I expect this to be in Alpha for another two year honestly, if it ever leaves Early Access is another question entirely. I honestly can't recommend a purchase at this point knowing that the formula is said and done, and if you're looking for a game like RUST, then there are others way ahead of the curve. I feel like a games experience shouldn't come down to an admin trying to police a server, which is what happens here. The game itself should be designed with preventative features like that in mind. Games like these apply a human band-aid in the form of admins, who can be more often than not, biased, and given/give special treatment, though its hard to argue when you own the server. Still the thought of an in-game admin is archaic and should be left in the past along with the games that lacked proper mechanics that required a person to log in and manage a game.
----------------------------------
All in all, I feel like the game just isn't worth it. The current direction its headed reminds me of ARK:SE, which isn't a bad thing, but ARK:SE already got there first. Even worse is that Facepunch Studios is working on the next Garry's Mod, which means Garry will focus his time on the next project and leave this one up to his community managers and content staff to finish up the main bits, while he adds a shiny new effect here and there.
----------------------------------
----------------------------------
----------------------------------

This game is kinda of a conundrum to review. On one hand, it CAN be fun to play, but on the other hand, it can be outright MISERABLE! And STRESS INDUCING as well. So here are my issues with the game thus far. The first problem, and probably the most obvious, are the GLITCHES
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This is a conundrum too. Imagine spending 3 hours, REAL WORLD time, gathering supplies, slowly, carefully and meticulously building a house. The game crashes, or something happens, and when you re-spawn your house and everything you had is GONE. Now your between a rock and a hard place, cause if you complain, well, people will just make YOU feel bad, saying that you should know and not complain it's in early Alpha. Unfortunately, this is where I tend to remind people that the whole purpose of even having"Playable Games in Early Alpha", are for us to act as testers. In fact, we are expected and ENCOURAGED to give input with regard to what works, what happens, and the things that DONT WORK. But hey. Whatever right.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The next issue I have with this game is that if you make friends or allies, as rarely as that may happen, it can be a good thing. BUT, if you make enemies, you REALLY MAKE ENEMIES. What I mean when I say that, is this; if say for instance, I kill a guy, and he does not like that I killed him, well, now HIM, and everyone he knows, which can in some instances be up to 10-12 different people, will now all kill me on sight the moment they see me, and or ruin everything I've built and worked hard to construct. If I say anything in the social chat, people will say and I quote; “seems to me like you need to play the sims” or “someone is salty” or “u mad bro”. Basically, if you get upset that you were wrongfully killed, or pretty much anything at all, you are immediately attacked socially.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Which brings me to the last few reasons I would never recommend this game unless you were a glutton for punishment. The first of them being the Social aspect. As I stated earlier, socially it can be a disaster. If you get upset that you were wrongfully killed, it's somehow twisted around and made to be your fault. If you are actually NICE to other players, and do not kill them the moment you see them, and GET KILLED as a result, it's YOUR FAULT, you shouldn't be so trusting. And if you KILL THEM the moment you see them, now everyone is angry at you. As previously stated, no matter what you do or say, except to a very select few, it's YOUR FAULT, and YOUR MADE to feel bad, or wrong. This is something I absolutely despise.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
.This brings me to my last and final issue with this game. If people killing you on sight, is not enough. If people killing you despite you're being naked and completely unequipped is not enough. If bears, wolves, and animals glitching their way through and into your house and killing you is not enough. If randomly and inexplicably loosing EVERYTHING you built or made for no reason at the drop of a dime, is not enough. And if a horrible social network of; Whiny, Spoiled, Stupid, Internet Tough guys, or Tough-guy Wannabe's is not enough. You also have THE MONTHLY WIPE TO LOOK FORWARD TO!!!! Please allow me to explain the lovely monthly wipe. Basically, in a game that encourages and essentially requires YOU the PLAYER, to both look for items, and construct dwellings and fortifications, it somehow for some reason simultaneouly WIPES IT ALL OUT once every month. Now I know people will give dumb and stupid explanations for why this has to, or must be done, but I say BS to that person. The idea, of taking a game, where people are required and encourgaed to both forage for items, build homes, make weapons, and tools, then every month TAKE IT ALL AWAY, makes playing this game “all in vein”. Seriously, what is the point in even starting to build or make anything at all, if at the end of the month, it's all gonna be gone and reset anyway?? Some of you may like that, or not care, I DO. That's like me making you work for money all month, after you PAID ME to work for money, then towards the end of the month when you're expecting to get paid, I say “eh, nah, come back next month and I'll think about it”. It's insane, and considering all the downfalls of the game, I'm sorry, but it's hardly worth it.
Oh, and the HACKERS.. They're fun too. Another play I know had 8 different 4 digit coded locks, all with different numbers. Do you know the possible combinations of digits that can be had with 0000 4 digit places, it's a lot. A lot more than people think. And magically and mysteriously this guy figured them all out, ransacked the house, destroyed everything, and stole everything. But ah, remember, I can't complain, otherwise that means that I'm salty. So when I get shot by someone flying overhead with an Automatic Bow and Arrow, I still can't complain.
Give it a go if ya want, but don't say I didn't warn you.

Alright. Grabbed the demo of the game, liked it, and finally bought this one for the full experience.
Undertale may have a fair share of flaws (in which I suck at explaining so I'm not going to say anything about 'em to save my hide), but it is unique in its own right. Now, I might spoil you a little bit of backstory (or maybe a lot of backstory, but I'll try to keep it vague), but you play as the eighth (and last, depending on how you play the game) human who fell into the underground portion of a mountain (thus the game's namesake). You find out what's going on down there AND depending on your actions, you either save an entire civilization of monsters or doom them along with yourself.
This game has a fresh take on role-playing game experience as it offers options other than outright killing anyone who stands in your way. You can choose to attack monsters in a battle OR spare them (Many monsters need to be interacted with before you can let them go, and sometimes this can be hard), or in-between. You will meet some important characters along the way, and whether they live through or die trying is up to you. Entirely. Undertale's system files REMEMBERS your actions throughout the game, and if you make the right choices, you will be lead to an ending that is satisfying (even if it's not for you, it certainly is for the characters). One wrong step though gives you a "Pandora's Box" effect. Remember the tale of Pandora and a box in her possession? This game basically applies the rules, "Virtue brings fortune" and "Many will die for the sins of one".
If you haven't played this game yet, this may definitely be worth a try for you. That is, if RPGs are your thing. I don't know about you, but I have played this game and it gave me a mind-blowing experience.
So what are you waiting for? If this game is your cup of tea, grab it. It's worth every US Dollar or whatever your native country's currency is (In my case, it's Malaysian Ringgit).

Undertale is a game where every aspect feels thought out. Saving has repercussions, and loading can destroy worlds. It's an RPG with great music, great character, and nothing has to die. It's Undertale, and I think it's a better successor to Fallout than Bethesda's.
This game is low budget, sharply focused. It's elevator pitch is 'the friendly RPG where nobody has to die.' The music is catchy, the art is simple, highly functional, and well done. The plot is generally simple, buoyed up by great characters and brilliant execution. Everything in Undertale matters in some way. The game is tightly coded to keep track of your choices, and it will happily tell you that. There are liars, and they're revealed, but the game never lies. It tricks you, but it doesn't lie. This means the game has to be clever, control your information, and be super sneaky about how it reveals things. It also means that the guy who made the game had to be insanely detailed about responses, because it really does remember everything.
If you're reading this, you're either looking for information on if you should play or have already done it and are seeing how much ohers agree with your assessment.
For the first, I'm sorry... but this is the game that spoiler warnings are made for. Try the demo; it hits the gameplay and shows off the early story. If what you see is worth a tenspot, I think you'll like it. If not, Toby definately won't be starving.
For the second, yes, I bought the soundtrack. I blame this one for proving that Fallout 4 is less than awesome. Also, got two endings, can't ever play again, have to watch youtubes for the others.

This player behavior is encouraged by the fact that the resources are somewhat scarce and it is actually more lucrative to just kill someone and take their stuff,it is somewhat balanced because even as a fully geared  player with an AK-47 and body armor you can be taken out by a Naked Born Player with a simple bow and a couple well placed headshots.
Once you get over the fact that the ruthless player behavior is  actually part of the game it opens up and becomes more fun. And you begin to treat the other players as nameless faceless NPC's just shoot anyone that is not part of your group on sight. Before they do it to you.

At least if you play through the game as a pacifist, there is really not much gameplay. You basically just repetitively select from a small number of options that let you interact with the monster over and over. None of the "fights" have much challenge and the side quests mostly involve hanging out with deeply annoying characters. It's as though a game tried to capture the awkward time you had as a kid when your mom made you hang out with the weird kid down the street to make them feel better. The music is grating and played on 8-bit instruments making it even more irritating. I played most of the game with the sound off. There are also "puzzles" to solve, but they are so easy, they don't even slow you down, let alone challenge you, and seem to have been almost an afterthought (which is bizarre since the NPCs keep telling you how the world is covered in puzzles). Like a lot of indie games, it tries to make up for the simplistic artwork and game mechanics with what the designers must have imagined was emotionally moving scenes; in general, though, they come across as cheap or even maudlin. Having played through to the "best" ending after being told it got more interesting as you played, I was very disappointed.

1. Just about everyone who is raving about the quality of the game has (generally) under 30 hours ( this obviously includes myself)

2: the gameplay/experience is great. Don't expect graphics. Expect surprisingly three dimensional characters and amazing music (assuming you're into more electronic type music). I wouldn't classify it as some great art piece of a game, however I will say that the dev, Toby Fox, put some real care into the game and it truly shows.
3: that's the fan base and they're fantastic. I think I've spent about as much time jamming to the sound track while surfing
reading the comics and whatever other thing someone who's more creative than I made.

Forget RPGS, this is undoubtedly one of the most compelling and provocative
I've played in a long long time. Period.
To say too much about the game would be to ruin it, as it's best to go into this blind, but the gist is that you're a child who's fallen into the underground, a place where monsters were sealed after the great war between humans and monsters. You'll face random encounters with these monsters as you explore, just like in a tradition RPG. The catch is, you don't have to kill any of them. Through the game's "ACT" and "MERCY" commands, you can find a non-violent solution to these battles, and resolve them by SPARing the enemies. Whether you choose to kill or spare will have an effect on the whole story. The game never forgets what you do, and there are real, story-related consequences for your actions.
The fighting is a twist on the traditional RPG turn-based system too. When you are attacked, instead of a computer calculating your odds to get hit and how much damage is done, you have a little box where projectiles fly at you (kind of like a bullet hell), and you can move your heart shaped cursor to dodge these attacks. Get good enough and you could actually take no damage throughout the whole game, even if you're only level 1.
The gameplay, writing and art direction (which both feel reminicsent of Earthbound), as well as the excellent music and sound design make this one of my favorite games this year. This game is a unique experience, and saying more wouldn't do justice to how truly awesome this game is. If you haven't played it, I highly, highly recommend that you do. It is phenomenal.

It keeps on getting worse.
It used to be so fun 1.5 years ago, it wasn't grindy, gunplay was pretty good, the game itself looked good and felt snappy, and It had pretty good performance.
Then the lead dev changed.
The game now requires more grind than ever before, barrels have almost no loot in them, you only get components that you can't use anyway because you have no BPs. The workbenches cost a lot to get all 3 of them you need 1800 scrap, gettings scrap for them requires a ton of looting/recycling. Just smashing barrels insn't an option since barrels only give a single scrap.
Finding AKs is harder than ever before, in the old BP system you used to be able to find them everywhere even in barrels. You didn't have to build near a radtown to get stuff, now you pretty much have to build near launchsite/mil tunnels since these are the only radtowns where you can find AKs and other high level equipment.
Rockets can only be obtained by the heli, you have to kill a heli, otherwise you can't rocketraid, this is really hard for small groups on big servers. Rockets used to drop from every other barrel. Rocketlaunchers can be looted from bradley (requires c4 tho) chopper and from elite crates. Elite crates spawn every 2 hours on 2 different radtowns, I haven't seen a rocketlauncher since the new system was implemented.
Items/bps that were standard/common in oldschool BP are now rare, getting BPs in general require you to camp launch/mil tunnels. Some of the radtown that used to be good are now trash. Sattelite has the same loot as 20 metres of road, it used to spawn military crates.
Servers still die within 2 days, they used to live a minimum of 3 days up to 4 weeks. Official/Rustafied servers eat up all the population, these are the only servers that are alive for more than a week. On wipedays they usually get a queue of about 300 people.
Over the past year gunplay worsened a lot, you used to have a lot of recoil and a high accuracy, you had to tap at mid ranges with the AK. Some people complained about gunplay being RNG reliant, so the dev who's name shall not be mentioned thought  it was a genius idea to rework the gunplay. He lowered the recoil and decreased to overall accuracy. ♥♥♥♥in great, now everyone can "control" the recoil and hitting somebody on range is pretty much pure luck.
Tons of player including PvP streamers complained about it decreasing the skill ceiling of the game.
The dev just brushed it off as "vocal minority" as he does it with every problem he doesn't want to touch any further.
Some months of♥♥♥♥♥♥gunplay have passed and he finally decided to rework the gunplay once more, it got better but it still is way too easy to control. Triple headshotting people with an AK over 100 metres is. The AK has less recoil than the semi auto pistol. The MP5 has 5 times the horizontal recoil of the AK, even though it is a mid range SMG.
The implementation of the stance "recoil" was a letdown as well, it was intended to stop players from standing and strafing while full autoing an AK. What it essentially did was make shots inaccurate while tapping and strafing, which is essential since you don't want to stand still while shooting.
When complaining about gunplay in this game, the dev who's name shall not be mentioned keeps comparing it to other games like call of duty or battlefield, even though you can't compare any of these games. In none of these game you lose literal hours of  of farming when dying, RNG shouldn't be such a big factor in gunplay. RNG recoil was ok because you were able to control it just fine, it took a lot of practice but it was okay.
Performance used to be pretty good, getting over 100 fps on a server that is several days old wasn't uncommon. The game had little to no inputlag. When comparing 144 fps on july2016 to 144 fps today you can see a big difference, july 2016 looks way smoother and feels way snappier.
This weeks patch ♥♥♥♥ed my performance a lot, I lost over 40 fps this patch and my game keeps freezing.
Nights currently are a big mess, you can't see anything inside your base at night and you can barely see anything when going out, a lot of people use a third party program to see better at night, it is somehow acceptable to use a cheat now to actually see something. This has been a big problem for a long time and the devs refuse to comment on the subject.
The game has gotten worse and worse over the past year, I forced myself to play this game in the last 2 months but I just can't play it and be happy, I want to enjoy this game like I used to.

What I would like to say though is that Undertale, while certainly playing like a game, felt like more of a philosophy lesson in its message. Should you play it?  I cannot suggest it enough, but again, just take your time with it.

Buy DayZ in early access alpha only if you genuinely have an interest in helping to shape the direction of a game's development. There's plenty of fun to be had, great potential for unscripted events and player interactions, a really good atmosphere and plenty of tension. But until it reaches beta (or full release), it will be buggy and fraught with usability issues.
If you want to play a high quality, complete and polished game, DO NOT BUY IT. Check back in when DayZ is in Early Access Beta or full release.
To all the people complaining about it "taking forever", being in "permanent alpha" or that alpha is being used as an excuse:
- As of this review, DayZ has been in open alpha for just over 1 year. Most games are in alpha for 3-4 years.
- Very few games are available to the public in alpha. If Left 4 Dead or Arma III were in open alpha at all, no doubt people would have had the same complaints about progress or bugs being left unfixed
- Alphas are all about adding functionality and content to the game. Do not expect significant bug fixes until the beta. This is the nature of game development
- You should have read all the early access warnings before paying for an alpha

I judge early access games based on the attitude of the developers, as this is less likely to change than core features. Here is what you can expect from Facepunch, this is from the project lead quoted from the latest patch notes:
"You know how you’re all ♥♥♥♥♥ing about optimization? ‘When are we gonna optimize the game? I wish the game was optimized. You should take a week off and optimize the game.’ Well that’s what we’ve been doing, so don’t ♥♥♥♥♥ and moan that you don’t have anything new to play with."
You are going to be punished for criticizing this game. Stop hiding behind 'Early Access'. Negative feedback is the most beneficial. So if a huge majority of your customers are saying this game runs poorly, don't berate them; take it as valuable feedback and fix the problem.
The game itself can be a lot of fun, but those moments where it shines are due to player interaction, and the developers credit themselves far too much. Create a sandbox, throw players in with very little limitations, and suddenly you are an innovative genius?
There is no discernible end-goal here; half implemented features create the illusion of a full experience, but isolated from each other each mechanic is clearly feeble. Survival aspects are non-existent (I will pay you if you can manage to starve to death in this game). Building/crafting features are a fraction of what is offered from similar titles. Gunplay needs a lot of work.
To top it all off, your playtime is completely redundant because you *will* be cheated by script-kiddies.
Let's not forget the intention of Early Access is stable, full release (no homo). There is no indication that Rust will ever meet that milestone, and as time progresses there are more and more indications that it will not. Which is a shame, because like many Early Access titles, "this game has so much potential".

Survival games... Why do people like them? I'd like to believe it gives someone the oppurtunity to do things that in real life that would be morally wrong or good.
KOS (kill on sight) is a real problem in this game. Mind you, not everyone shoots on sight.
Are you a benevolent protector? Do you feel like being a medic? Do you want to roleplay as a blood thirsty bandit?
Maybe something in between? Player interaction is one of the highlights of this game, just approaching someone you don't know is a risk. Be cautious because once you die you lose all of your gear and have to start again as a fresh spawn.
Hunger and thirst are your major concerns, thirst being the most important. Scavenging is the primary way to find what you need, but the devs are adding in things like farming vegetables, hunting wild game, and fishing.
These activities require alot of gear space, should they add in ways to store your gear, you'll find it a bit easier to survive if you know what you're doing.

I made a Steam account just so I could play Undertale, and I'll never regret that decision for as long as I live! I couldn't go three clicks without coming across any Undertale related stuff, and that made avoiding spoilers a challenge, so I finally gave in and saw this through for myself. Sometimes peer pressure is worth it. While it masterfully provides a wonderful cast of characters like so many other great RPG's, this goes one step further by giving even the enemies interesting personalities which really gives the main mercy mechanic it's purpose! Every piece in the soundtrack comes together perfectly in their places in the game to really leave an impact, so much that multiple songs are stuck in my head at once and I love it (and by multiple, I mean all of them)! I many have peeked at a few spoilers along the line, but I always kept myself from going too far down the rabbit hole, and I still had an absolutely spectacular and unforgettable experience.
Of course, with all this praise I'm giving for the best parts of this game, reason would have it that the events that came in my wake left me in a pleasantly satisfied mood, so I obviously did a Pacifist Run first, and like everyone else before me, I'm having an internal dilemma about going back in for a Genocide Run. I like to experience as much as I can in game that I truly hold close to my heart, and knowing that there's still more for me to see, I still want to keep things spoiler free. But if the only way to do that is to destroy everything I've come to love, I just don't know if it'll be worth it (it probably won't be).
For now, I should just enjoy all the hopes and dreams that I'll always hold close to my soul while I take a good long rest so I can contemplate before.............I decide to have a bad time.
You feel your Sans crawling on your back, it made you have a bad time, you firmly tell Sans to stop crawling, but he refused.

Undertale is the perfect representation of why good writing in a game will create the world and immerse the player greatly. Not to say that the game is perfect, because there are frustrating times, and times that the dialogue seems to drag on, but for the majority of the time, Undertale will bring in the player by use of humor. Once the player is immersed, the writing brings an emotional end that rivals similar games of Earthbound and Mother 3, which are hard to compete with.
The visuals and music really stand out here as well. The game goes for a pseudo-NES/DOS style of sprite work, which really emphasizes how much it was inspired by games of those eras. The music, mixing some classic chiptune stylings with amazing melodies is the standout of the game.
This game feels like a love letter to RPGs similar to those, and that fills me with determination.

At first, I wasn't all that sold on the "game of the year" talks surrounding this.  Yes, it was a cute game.  Had some funny jokes, cute characters, and some plot that could hit close to home at times. (I felt that date scene right in the feels).
But, once I got to the end of my first playthrough (Neutral), MY GOD was I sold on this game.  Every caveat was thought of.  Every little thing is very intricately designed, and I love it.  I'm eventually going to do a pacifist run and a genocide run, but I was let on to EVEN MORE things than just that.  I would have to completely uninstall and reinstall undertale again and do some of the runs AGAIN to get to see EVEN MORE of the game.
It's REALLY worth the $10 price being asked.  If you do not have this game yet, you're doing yourself a disservice.  Seriously, it's THAT enjoyable.
Pros:
Very enjoyable humor (I love puns)
The plot was fairly good.
Every little detail was carefully thought out.
There are so many possibilities to the game, with the whole mercy system.
The "combat" system varies, and keeps you interested rather than being repetitive.
The music is well-made (the soundtrack is worth it)
Some of the sprites are really well made and cute
There are a lot of enjoyable characters in the game.
Did I mention the mercy system is realllly well done?
Cons:
It's severely lacking in a travel system.  You have to do some backtracking.
The puzzles are honestly (for the most part) a little TOO easy.
Some of the in-game sprites dont seem that great (I'm not fond of the main character's sprite)
Other than that, I'd say 10/10 GET THIS GAME NOW.... bOI!!

The suvival aspect is monotonous and even time consuming thus the background noise. Word of advice always have your background noise be it youtube or teamspeak easy to turn off or on. You never know when you will need to determine the direction of incoming shots and the last thing you want to do is to TAB out to shut something down. Personaly I never kill on sight aka KOS, Its anit social and the real skill of the game is to make friends with strangers while working together to accomplish a common goal. The hardest part is to build "dat trust" you cant really tell what another players intent is unless you've been around them for more then an hour or you get their steam info, thats a good way to build trust. Once you get a REAL friend or two to help you "survive" in DayZ you can then move on to the more fun aspect which is to take over a town or open a market or any number of roll play ideas you may have.  All in all its fun with friends and with DayZ constantly being updated and content being added all the time there is always something to explore.
Have fun out there and remember never KOS

An RPG of the finest caliber. The characters are wonderful to interact with, so great in fact that you wish they were real.
