Undertale has redefined my expectations, and rekindled my love for video games.
The gameplay is practically revolutionary. Take your favorite turn-based, random encounter RPG. Now double the character depth and erase the repetitive and unimpactful encounter elements. The soundtrack and combat mechanics will keep you awake, which will be critical, as every decision will sway your saga differently. Destiny is in your hands.
The writing is so compelling. Between the dialogue and narrative texts, you feel fully immersed in this world. Through capricious and casual exploration and adventure, you uncover the secrets veiled within this dark underground realm. But in the face of darkness you summon from the depths of your unwavering soul boundless DETERMINATION - the will to survive, and to change fate!
You will not regret this game.
Story-
Plot: 9/10
Dialogue: 10/10
Narrative: 10/10
World Depth (History, etc.): 9/10
Side Stories (exploration, side quests, etc): 9/10
Time: 5-7 hours for first playthrough.
Post Game/Epilogue Content: High. 8/10
Choice Impact: 9/10*
*(You expect choice to impact nothing more than which final boss you battle, or which end credits art you get. Expect more. Much more.)
Gameplay-
Combat Difficulty: 7/10 (It's not THAT hard. Git gud.)
Creativity: 10/10
Soundtrack: 11/10
(I would leave the game open to listen to the soundtrack. It pained me to close so that I could show it to my friends.)
My single complaint is a lack of multiple save files. This, however, is also an integral element to the game's plot and central theme.

Many games go backwards to deliver an experience likened to another game or series. Shovel knight influenced by ducktales, megaman and so on. Axiom Verge being a big throwback to the original metroid and metroidvanias as a whole.
These games; while fun at the very end of it all; don't deliver anything truly new to the table.
And while Undertale on appearance is certainly a throwback to titles like EarthBound, it most certainly brings many new things to the table.
The morality choices are not perfect but they are most certainly effective.
The combat; or given your choice the lack of; is a perfect blend of bullet hell alongside the RPG Elements.
Add a narrative that has so many moments of happiness and humour, but also has many dark, horrific, and tragic moments;
Undertale is not a "perfect" game. But it is one of the greatest games I have ever had the pleasure to play.

I bought this game with a hefty nerd scoff. Fully believing it to sit in a dark corner of my steam game library never to see the light of day as I played other titles that would hold my interest.
All those social media kids were just getting excited over another game with some cute characters and internet savvy humor. Still it had some appeal...
I launched the game. Looked harmless enough, started playing, started grinding and eventually killed an important NPC, quite by accident mind you. I tried to reload to undo a seemingly simple undesirable mistake any gamer might make… Surely everyone has at some point accidentally harmed an NPC and had to reload… such as setting a guard or townspeople on fire accidentally via a missed keystroke.
As I went to reload my save, suddenly there was consequence. My saves no longer mattered, actions done could not be undone, not truly! While I get a second chance it seems my previous attempt or decisions would haunt me through each choice or decision therein regardless if I reload a save or not. “What the hell” This was not just the cutesy RPG it appeared to be.
Still I reluctantly gave some more effort then quit, mildly frustrated that it didn't really follow the typical intuitive game play I had come to anticipate in similar games. Scolded for my choices, told to reload a save or try all over again; actions weight upon other actions. It was crazy. I didn't last long and quickly picked it up again resolved to find out more.
As I played I dreamed of the perfect ending to this game, what I really wanted (and expected) to see after this journey concluded. Each time I got close to what I could only assume to be the typical feel good ending, all was not what it seemed. I will say, I was not initially aware of the multiple gameplay paths that are common knowledge now (I just jumped right it). Still the game practically spits in your face and says “you IDIOT, you didn't think it would be this easy?” And by easy they mean straightforward or even intuitive! I lamented the weird ending I received only to find out I hadn't even scratched the surface of the game, there was more to do, much much more, hell it wasn't even the ending at all!
I will not lie ladies and gentlemen, this cute little RPG brought me to tears more than once. There has NEVER been a video game that has made my eyes water. But I digress.
This game is better than the hype, it's legitimately a good game. It takes you out of your comfort zone, makes you think, throws goofy comedy at you all while drowning you in darkness and despair. I highly recommend this game. It's highly deserving of it's praises.

Rust (Раст) - это детище Facepunch Studios. Основной идеей игры является выживание. Как DayZ, Minecraft или Сталкер - события в RUST будут происходить в крайне враждебной среде, в которой вам предстоит выживать или может процветать.
Я буду жить!
Основная цель игры состоит в том, чтобы начиная только с камнем в руках выбить себе место под солнцем. Для вам потребуется собирать разнообразные ресурсы. Например, дрова можно добывать с деревьев или вязанок дров, породы и руду можно добыть с больших валунов. Затем можно попробовать создать себе более совершенные орудия труда, например, из древесины и камня у вас получится топор , что позволит собирать материалы гораздо быстрее.
Вам потребуется еда. Вы можете охотиться на разнообразных животных, представленных в игре. Медведи, волки могут представлять большую опасность для начинающих игроков. А кабаны, куры, кролики и олени будут просто убегать от вас. После того, как вы убьёте животное с его трупа можно будет собрать такие ресурсы, как мясо и кожу. Далее вы можете сделать костер из дров и приготовить мясо на огне. В итоге вы получите хорошую еду и больше шансов на выживание.

Like rocks? Rust has rocks!
Like PVP? Rust has player killing constantly :D
Like building a base just to lose it the next morning? Neither do I but it happens!
1. Constant death from other players
--Naked men will attack you on sight
--Players will shoot you for existing
2. Your base will be destroyed, raided, griefed, taken over, or have naughty signs made by other players on your stuff
3. You will die from bears, wolves, cold weather, etc.
4. People will mock you, knock you down and refuse to shoot you just to whisper sweet nothings in your ear before double tapping you.
1. You start out with basically nothing and must gather, find, or steal resources from the world and build or steal an awesome house.
2. The crafting in this game has an interesting system and you must find certain recipes to craft special items and said recipes are in pvp hot zones giving the game some battleground for fun. This also makes you work for the good stuff. (recipes stay on you even after death)
3. The game gives you choices to be lethal or not. You may ask another have them give things to you, if they don't you have some options:
--Shoot/melee them till they are on the ground and loot their body
--Shoot/melee them to the ground then double tap them, possibly after hearing them scream a little so they know you're twisted.
4. You can build almost anywhere in the game and build how you want except a few resricted spots and the stability system. If your house isn't stable then it won't stay up, if you build it by a pillar holding up half your house then once that pillar gets destroyed so does half your house when it collapses.
--You may upgrade the materials of your house to be more suited towards defense so it makes it REALLY hard for people to break in unless they have some massive fire power ( C4, Grenades, Rocket launcher)
--You may lose your house often in this game depending on how well you build it, how many friends you have with you, etc. but build wisely and you won't lose it so often and you can take over other players' bases which is fun and rewarding.
5. Killing other players in this game is very satisfying and is not some arcade shooter, you shoot someone and they will bleed and probably die very very quickly if you shot them in a good spot. You may also eat your Foe after cooking it of course. Unless you want to eat it raw... and get sick...

To start off the guide I would like to say that I would probably recommend this game to anyone, but if you are looking in or at negative reviews you are probably looking for good examples of the games shortcomings and what might make it deserve a negative review.
To drown out the "Why are you looking at negative reviews?!?!" reviews, I will make this review.
The game has a great story and many aspects that generate immersion, BUT a huge, specific, part of the game revolves around a literal grindfest making it very drawn out as well as carpal tunnel inducing.

Undertale is a really fantastic RPG in the style of Earthbound, but you don't need to have played Earthbound or anything similar to it to appreciate it. It offers incredible depth and immersion, while still managing to subvert and play with its medium. The characters are all incredibly lovable, but I won't say anything about the plot - this game is best when you go into it 100% blind. I'll only say two things about it: the tagline - "The RPG game where you don't have to destroy anyone" - is 100% true, if you're clever enough to make it happen, and that this game, despite being an incredibly enjoyable, awesome experience, is something I don't think I could ever bear to replay.

Undertale is arguably the only game I have ever played which, after I completed it, I wish I could acquire some sort of memory-erasure device (the Neuralyzer from Men in Black comes to mind) and wipe all the memories associated with this game...only to play it again and again and again with the mindset of a "blind" playthrough, just so I can appreciate how much of a mental and emotional rollercoaster ride this game had on me.
My god. All the happy times. All the sad times. All the INCREDIBLY scary times. All the impressively hilarious times. Every momentous occasion in Undertale has resonated with me in such a way that I have never experienced in ANY other game I have ever played that I just wish I could bring it up on Steam and play it as if I were playing it for the first time, every time.
Sadly, no such Neuralyzer exists, and I will always know what happens next after playing through the game 10 or so times. Still, the mental and emotional impact is a testament as to how much Undertale means to me, and I believe anyone who is reading this review and has not played this magnum opus will feel the same way after spending an incredibly reasonable amount of time and money on the future 2015 GOTY.
$10/$10 money well spent.

Admittedly, I did not play the genocide route (yet) so I am missing a chunk of storyline as of right now. However, I'd still like to lend my praise to Undertale.
I understand there's a bit of hype surrounding the game right now and there's a large fanbase. Personally I find myself staying away from fanbases like the plague because they'll sour me on anything I once loved. Yet I find that Undertale has really deserved all of the fanfare that has been drummed up since the game has gained popularity.
Undertale has been likened to Earthbound and Mother. While I have not personally played these games, I have watched friends play these games and enjoyed my time during these playthroughs. It's a very easy comparison to make and Undertale has that same charming feeling that is often missing from other RPG-type games. Undertale has characters you become emotionally attached to and you start to care about what happens in this story. You start to really feel for your main character and you worry about that journey onward and about what sort of cost it might take to bring you back to the home you once knew.
The fighting system is one that I enjoy. If you're taking Toriel's cue and you're trying to avoid confrontation, you're dodging unique attacks while trying to spare your adversary. If you're in battle and must fight for some reason (be it your choice or game mechanic), you are able to land a critical hit by timing your hit correctly. Items you find will help your stats, but you don't actually need them. It's possible to beat your game without leveling at all. The idea that I could choose my game play and not have to do an endless grind if I didn't want to was incredibly appealing for me. Undertale had become the answer to my prayers for just that alone. I can't begin to admit how many games I stopped playing for long periods just because the required grind took too long and there was little satisfaction I got out of it in return.
Another immediate draw is the soundtrack. While it's going to take you back to your early days of gaming (again, think of the time you first loaded up your first RPG), it's also a bit more complex. I found myself inspired at certain pieces of music and filled with (GROAN) determination to keep going when a boss fight seemed impossible. Then there were pieces of music that were so perfect and emotionally moving that I did become a bit teary eyed. Bittersweet text flying by on the screen certainly didn't help much, but without that music, I wouldn't have found the moment nearly as stirring.
The graphics for each character are unique. Truly, each character, even the unnamed ones, get a unique sprite and they are all bright and pleasing. Everything is beautiful, even if it is unappealing. It's a very pretty game with pretty music.
Of course, important in an RPG is the story. I can promise that it's entertaining and it does make use of a few popular memes that are relevant now and were relevant a few years ago. The characters have a very natural dialogue even for a fantasy setting and they mesh very well together. This feels like a group of friends you'd know, except the whole skeletons, fish-woman, dinosaur-thing, and minotaurs. Oh and the other assorted people you meet who help you, too. Really, there's a lot of people to name here. It works well. While some plot points feel predictable, there are major parts that are a huge twist that I was very impressed with. I don't usually see anyone looking to write something new while using techniques that have worked for years in a game. Undertale, for the most part, does this.
I didn't find this game to be completely without flaws, however. Dying constantly because you decided to take the peaceful approach versus having an easier time during the genocide route seems a little bit unbalanced. There's also the fact that, despite I clocked in fourteen hours due to mulitple deaths and needing breaks, I still found the game very short. This is all minor to me. To experience the game fully, you should be playing all three ways of playing. This would increase your game time, vary the level of difficulty, and show you all the game has to offer.
I do have some concerns for gamers with any handicaps. If you have nerve issues, please take frequent breaks. Using your arrow keys for prolonged attack dodging is going to hurt hands and cause severe pain if you have issues. As someone with this pain and speaking from the realm of "learn from my mistake, please", I suggest you take a break every 1-2 hours. There are also sequences with heavily flashing lights. If you are prone to seizures and migraines, please take warning. I was able to time them before they went off so I was shielding my eyes. Your worst issue will be during some of the final bosses. They become very difficult on the eyes and use quite a bit of flashing lights. Please be careful if you choose to play this game.

Admittedly, I did not play the genocide route (yet) so I am missing a chunk of storyline as of right now. However, I'd still like to lend my praise to Undertale.
I understand there's a bit of hype surrounding the game right now and there's a large fanbase. Personally I find myself staying away from fanbases like the plague because they'll sour me on anything I once loved. Yet I find that Undertale has really deserved all of the fanfare that has been drummed up since the game has gained popularity.
Undertale has been likened to Earthbound and Mother. While I have not personally played these games, I have watched friends play these games and enjoyed my time during these playthroughs. It's a very easy comparison to make and Undertale has that same charming feeling that is often missing from other RPG-type games. Undertale has characters you become emotionally attached to and you start to care about what happens in this story. You start to really feel for your main character and you worry about that journey onward and about what sort of cost it might take to bring you back to the home you once knew.
The fighting system is one that I enjoy. If you're taking Toriel's cue and you're trying to avoid confrontation, you're dodging unique attacks while trying to spare your adversary. If you're in battle and must fight for some reason (be it your choice or game mechanic), you are able to land a critical hit by timing your hit correctly. Items you find will help your stats, but you don't actually need them. It's possible to beat your game without leveling at all. The idea that I could choose my game play and not have to do an endless grind if I didn't want to was incredibly appealing for me. Undertale had become the answer to my prayers for just that alone. I can't begin to admit how many games I stopped playing for long periods just because the required grind took too long and there was little satisfaction I got out of it in return.
Another immediate draw is the soundtrack. While it's going to take you back to your early days of gaming (again, think of the time you first loaded up your first RPG), it's also a bit more complex. I found myself inspired at certain pieces of music and filled with (GROAN) determination to keep going when a boss fight seemed impossible. Then there were pieces of music that were so perfect and emotionally moving that I did become a bit teary eyed. Bittersweet text flying by on the screen certainly didn't help much, but without that music, I wouldn't have found the moment nearly as stirring.
The graphics for each character are unique. Truly, each character, even the unnamed ones, get a unique sprite and they are all bright and pleasing. Everything is beautiful, even if it is unappealing. It's a very pretty game with pretty music.
Of course, important in an RPG is the story. I can promise that it's entertaining and it does make use of a few popular memes that are relevant now and were relevant a few years ago. The characters have a very natural dialogue even for a fantasy setting and they mesh very well together. This feels like a group of friends you'd know, except the whole skeletons, fish-woman, dinosaur-thing, and minotaurs. Oh and the other assorted people you meet who help you, too. Really, there's a lot of people to name here. It works well. While some plot points feel predictable, there are major parts that are a huge twist that I was very impressed with. I don't usually see anyone looking to write something new while using techniques that have worked for years in a game. Undertale, for the most part, does this.
I didn't find this game to be completely without flaws, however. Dying constantly because you decided to take the peaceful approach versus having an easier time during the genocide route seems a little bit unbalanced. There's also the fact that, despite I clocked in fourteen hours due to mulitple deaths and needing breaks, I still found the game very short. This is all minor to me. To experience the game fully, you should be playing all three ways of playing. This would increase your game time, vary the level of difficulty, and show you all the game has to offer.
I do have some concerns for gamers with any handicaps. If you have nerve issues, please take frequent breaks. Using your arrow keys for prolonged attack dodging is going to hurt hands and cause severe pain if you have issues. As someone with this pain and speaking from the realm of "learn from my mistake, please", I suggest you take a break every 1-2 hours. There are also sequences with heavily flashing lights. If you are prone to seizures and migraines, please take warning. I was able to time them before they went off so I was shielding my eyes. Your worst issue will be during some of the final bosses. They become very difficult on the eyes and use quite a bit of flashing lights. Please be careful if you choose to play this game.
It's an outstanding game, truly. I haven't had this much fun in a long time and I haven't cared about video game characters since I was fourteen.
I mean, I went on a date with a skeleton, had a cooking lesson with a fish, and then got a fish and a dinosaur-thing to sorta-kinda fall in love. Then we ran laps. It was awesome. I had a good time.
Not looking forward to having a bad time, thank you.

I initially dismissed Rust as Youtuber-bait and ignored it for quite a while. But since the graphical/UI/gameplay overhauls, Rust has actually turned into a game worth purchasing. I'm not going to bother giving you a breakdown of gameplay mechanics as many others have already done, so I'll just provide some brief snippets of the encounters I've had in this game thus far:
-Convinced a new player to "tour" my sex dungeon in the woods, but decided to let him go after he displayed exceptional beatboxing skills
-Broke into a poorly defended home with my friend, found three naked dudes sleeping on the floor, briefly felt a tinge of empathy, but then took all of their ore and harvested their flesh with my machete
-Decided to introduced myself to my new neighbors...never doing that again
-Made the rookie mistake of going out for a night harvest fully strapped with weapons and armor, got wounded by a single wolf and bled out
-Took a handful of hours to build my first house, only to realize that I had placed all of my walls backwards...needless to say, that place didn't last long
-The first time I spawned into the game, I met some seemingly chill dudes who had a house on the beach, I ended up with about 6 arrows in my face because they wanted to "test out their new bows"
Anyway, Rust has come a really long way from launch, and truly is one of the most enjoyable survival simulators out there. It really gives the players the freedom to make their own stories, instead of having them sit through endless exposition. Really glad that I refunded H1Z1 to buy this.

When everyone was hyped for this game and telling me I should get it, I looked into it and thought it looked like another crappy indi dev trying to make his name or something, so I didn't care that much for it until someone got me the game, that's when I gave it a shot.
I first played a 'neutral' run and thought the game had an interesting twist at the end and an interesting story reguarding the monsters' and humans' history. When I learnt of a 'true pacafist' ending giving more to the game and its characters, I decided to give it a shot. I honestly didn't expect much more from it at all... Boy was I wrong!
It's true what they say, True Pacafist is the way the game should be played if you want the 'best' ending, it has the best twists, best backstory, best character development, best everything pretty much. The playthrough was full of laughs and shouting as it takes you on an an emotional rollercoaster that you would never expect from a game such as this. I would personally recommend this game to any that are looking into it.
This next part of the review may contain some spoilers, so read on at your own risk - I will try and minimalise them as much as possible though.
STORY/BACKSTORY:
At first, it looks like your typical 'Monsters vs Humans' approach where the humans have fought galiently against the evil, murderous monsters, sealing them underground for eternatly where only seven human souls can free them. However, we are then thrown off when the game reveals the true nature of the monsters, painting the humans as evil people that feared what they could not understand. As we progress many twists will leave you feeling happy, sad and angry in this excellent story. The only issue I see with this is that if a player wishes to have the full experience, then they must ensure that they explore and read everything they come across. 9/10
CHARACTERS:
I honestly can't seem to find a fault in the characters that Undertale presents the player with. First of all, we have you - the only human in this monster world, capable of making friends with the most fierce of monsters. Then we have our comic relief duo, sans and papyrus who provide us with the laughter we need during our exploration around the underground, with sans taking an interesting turn in attitude towards the end of the game. We also have our little helper Alyphys who guides and annoys us through Hotland towards the core. Then we come to the more serious characters that are Asgore and Toriel, at first they may not seem like much but explore their backstories and you'll see how heartwarming this game can be. 10/10
FIGHTING:
This game takes a rather unique approach (compared to other games I have played) to fighting enemies, in the sense of you have two ways of fighting. You can either take the 'Kill or be Killed' approach (not recommended) or try and resolve things peacefully. Either way you will have to use the arrow keys to try and dodge their attacks, or take some serious damage in some cases. I personally found that the death screen was INCREADABLY annoying in the sense that you saw it so many times in them harder fights and you COULDN'T SKIP IT, which annoyed me more than the deaths did themselves. I won't go into too much detail about the leveling system as it has a very unique approach to that in the form of LOVE and XP. 9/10
CONTROLS:
The controls to this game are pretty simple and easy to learn, only really requiring you to use the arrow keys and the ENTER, SHIFT and CTRL keys on your keyboard. The only issue I have with them is that after that first screen shows you, then you can't see the controls again which really sucks if you are rubbish at remembering things, particularly at the beginning of the game when you first start playing. 9/10

Undertale review
Disclaimer; There will be spoilers
Story; When you first begin the story of undertale, the game opens up with a nice musical piece and backstory telling you that once the world was inhabited by both humans and monsters, but one day war broke out and the monsters were banished underground and were never to return. The underground serves as the main setting of the game. You play a young child that you name and because of cartoon antics you trip on a root and fall into the underground, which to be perfectly honest kinda makes a plot hole. but I will get to that later. Anyways, after moving around, you meet a small little flower who goes by flowey. He shows you the basic game mechanics. You play as a little heart which represents your soul, and you go around picking up friendliness pellets... yeah. anyways its immediately revealed that those pellets are going to damage and flowey takes the opportunity and abuses your naivety and attempts to kill you, but a random fire ball comes out of no where and stops the demonic flower and saves your♥♥♥♥♥ Your saviors name is toriel. Upon bringing you through mystrerious ruins and to her home she attempts to block the door from her home, and the rest of the underground. You stop her because obviously you don't wanna be stuck in this♥♥♥♥♥♥whole where everything and there god damn dog wants to kill you so you enter a fight with toriel to win your freedom. This is where the game branches of into paths but for the sake of not wasting to much time I will only write about the nuetral ending. From here you can either kill or spare toriel effecting minor details... for now. anyways as soon as you leave you meet sans, and papyrus. these two are apart of the great cast of chatacters. sans serves as a sort of gaurdian for you. papyrus just wants to capture a human, and after the many puzzles and traps set up by papyrus, you make it to snowdin where you finally fight the delusional skeleton. after an easy boss fight, in which you can spare or kill him you progress to the waterfall area where you learn about the history of underground. The monsters just want out with out violence at first but that all changes as you find out in the story. This is where you meet Undyne, a hero of monsters ready to kill you and claims you to be the destroyer of everyones hopes and dreams. after a somewhat difficult fight you progress to hotlands and meet alphys, essentially a navi from Ocarina of time but less annoying. after meeting her human killing robot and escaping multiple traps laid out by this thing who by the way is named mettaton, you arive at the last few areas of the game, Core and new home. after talking to sans and learing that he is your gaurdian because he made a promise to toriel to protect anyone who comes out the door she attempted to block, you become more attatched to sans and not just because of this mans brilliant puns, er skeleton. after battling with the transfromed mettaton EX who reminds me of some 80s rocker, you learn from alphys that in order to break free from underground you must take the soul of asgor dreemur, the king of monsters. mind you thats the entire progression motive, getting home. After walking through new home you learn that the son of asgore was murdered by humans alond with a human child he befriended. Out of rage asgore wishes to kill the humans and break out of underground and needs 7 human souls to do it... the last being yours. after defeating this goat dude (asgore) you are interupted by flowey, yeah this♥♥♥♥♥♥isnt gone, and he gives you the bullet hell experience of the game. afrer beating him you are given a phone call from sans and told that there is more to do.
My thoughts on the story; Okay... I like this story. I really do. but the thing is. there are three. which makes it harder to review. I think this story has the perfect blend of charm and darkness in it, and it really shows that your decision can have a huge impact. over all I think the story is well written and only has the issue that you fell into underground when there is an implied barrier and it is never really explained.
Gameplay; using the heart you can dodge enemy attacks, and by timing your hits right you can dish out a lot of damage on your enemy. but here is the thing; This is an RPG where you don't HAVE to kill anything. This has a huge impact on gameplay and story. With in the gameplay, you can instead of killing, find the correct sequence of actions to end the battle and earn money, or attack them until the spare option is available. With the mix of different items it spices up the conbat very slightly, but I do have a problem here. There are many different weapons, but once you get a new one you don't go back because the new one is so much better and makes attacking slighty different, while I like progression I would also like options, not obligation unless it is the story. However the gameplay isn't always the same, each boss will force you to fight in different ways, papyrus turns you blue and turns the fight into a sort of platforming bullet hell. Undyne forces you to use a sheild to defend your soul, metton turns into a space shooter, and asgore is a normal fight... flowey is also "Normal". Over all I find the gameplay to be very solid, but slightly repetitive at times. But I am not done. Remember sparing and killing? Yeah that is what casuses the story to split. You have true pacifist which shows the true ending to the game and you kill nothing, and genocide where you kill everyone and the final boss is sans... my god he is a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ anyways. I have a huge problem with genocide. you have to kill everyone in an area... before progressing to far. Which is annoying considering this is random encounters and they can be few and far between. I wouldn't have such a problem with it if I could kill everything later but no, this screwed up my genocide run 3 times. forcing me to restart the game. over all I like the gameplay but I don't like some of the restrictions.
Music: The music in undertale is great. With it's nice mix of calming paino pieces to its techno, and 8 bit music styles, you will be boping your head the entire time and highly recommend buying the games soundtrack on steam, it is very worth your time and money. I really loved every track in this game, even the ominouse tracks with no beatm but help you become imersed in the games atmosphere.
Presentaion of Graphics; This game goes for an 8 bit style with color, and honestly... it looks really good and reminds me of the gameboy color a lot. I think the games sprite work and animation is extemely well done and each sprite was handled with care.
Final thoughts; Undertale in my opinion is worth your time, even though the gameplay gets repetitive, it still has 3 great stories and boss fights to show and tell. This game combined with its wonderful presentaion, music, intersting combat, and story is very much so worth your time and money, this game is only 10 dollars, I highly recommend it.
Personal rating; 8.5/10

Undertale is a game that, while not the most difficult, provides an experience unlike any other game I've ever played. Funny, touching, heartbreaking, jaw-dropping, but most importantly enjoyable and memorable. Every single character, be it enemy, friend, NPC, etc. have personality that goes so far above and beyond what a game needs to provide.
Undertale is a game meant to be played completely blind, without any knowledge of what the game holds, and for good reason. Everyone will have a different playthrough, and (I'm going to be intentionally vague) every choice you can make impacts the game.
Undertale is the best $10 I've spent on a game in a very long time. Do yourself a favor, don't watch videos of gameplay or someone else's Let's Play. You should play this game. If you don't like it, fine. But if you get drawn in, you may agree that this is one of the best games ever made. A lot of hype has been thrown around about Undertale, but IMO it's fully deserved.
Smart writing, a novel combat system, absolutely fantastic soundtrack, and even the weak parts of the game (and there are a couple) are easily cast aside because the experience of Undertale is a triumph. Buy it, play it, love it.

Did 3 neutral runs, 3 genocide runs, and one true pacifist.
TIME TO BE BRUTALLY HONEST WITH THE GAME!
It's great. No really, the game is great. Not an Ocarina of Time kind of great, or Star Control 2 kind of great, but still great. The game offers you a lot of freedom in how to play, and dozens of secrets and easter eggs that still are hidden away in the game. The greatest part about the game by far is that, for solving puzzles or in combat, there is no single way to beat an enemy. Take for example: All dog enemies can instantly be beaten by using the stick. There are tons of little secrets like that littered throughout the game, and I love it. Not to mention several different endings depending on which major characters you kill or spare, it adds in quite a bit of playtime if you're a completionist.
Or if you're like me, you did Genocide run 3 times just because it is the only fun run.
Now time to REALLY be brutally honest with the game
As I mentioned before, there are multiple endings, but two distinct paths which can only be achieved by following a specific path. There's pacifist run, where you kill nobody and date every major character (Yes, DATE every major charactar), or genocide run, where you literally kill everything. To fill you in on that, every area has a set limit to random encounters you can encounter, and you can actually clear out an area of every living thing. Everyone seems to love the True Pacifist run except for me, soley because of one factor: There is little to no challenge or reason for me to truly care for the major characters. There are only THREE characters who are above average, and that's Sans, Papyrus and Flowey. The rest are just bare-bones characters who I wouldn't give two and a half damns about. Toriel, in the beginning, comes off as insanely creepy, and you don't learn too much about who she really is or why she acts the way she does. Undyne's entire character can be summed up with a quotation from Ike: "I fight for my friends." Alphys is just a weaboo lesbian (I'll give credit where credit is due, she at least develops in ONE ending). Asgore is a king who wants your soul to destroy humanity. I'm well aware there are other parts to a few characters' pasts, but they still don't make too much of a difference. The ironic part about Sans and Flowey being the only good characters is that in order to find out how, you HAVE to do a genocide run. The only amount of challenge in the True Pacifist run is the final boss, but
SPOILER ALERT FOR GENOCIDE RUN
SPOILER OVER
I enjoyed the genocide run so much just because it offered challenge, while True pacifist was button mashing to get through boring dates and dialogue about characters I couldn't give a damn about.
What about it being a metagame?
Some of the meta aspects are either clever (how saves work, again, ironic how you only discover this through the genocide run) or pointless/♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. I honestly think that it's kind of clever how there is an in-game reason to how save points work, and it isn't just a one-off thing. But then comes the genocide run ending.
SPOILERS
The game is stupid in a lot of areas, but as a game, it works out really well. I still recommend it.

I woke up naked and alone on a beach only to be chased for five minutes by a naked man with a machete until he cut me down. My next attempt at survival went slightly more smoothly. I sucessfully made a shanty! Ensuring my little hovel was adequately protected, I logged off with a confident mind. I logged in the next day to play and, once again, awoke naked and alone on the beach. My beautiful home had been destroyed, and I had been murdered in my sleep. I began to detest the other players. I lived in fear. Cold and naked. I HATED the "raiders". I didn't understand why they wouldn't let me live my life.
Over the next couple of weeks I struggled to survive, living in the fringe of society. I studied the collapsed ruins of once-great bases and forts. I searched feverishly for blueprints. I stalked other players, learning to sneak around unnoticed. I watched.
The server performed it's monthly wipe, leaving me with the blueprints to success. Using the knoweldge I gained from exploring raided forts, I was able to build myself a fortress - ensuring that I did not make the same mistakes as the ill-fated survivalists of the past wipe. I farmed for what felt like days. I created weapons. I murderd anyone who DARED to settle within range of my sniper tower. I ruled my kingdom with an iron fist. I have become what I hated.

I'm not a terribly 'gamey' sort of person: I'm picky about controls and difficulty, I can't stick with the story if the characters are flat (and vice versa), and if I feel the need to mute the game to put on my own music then my interest overall is at risk.
Then I met Undertale and immediately fell in love.
The controls are simple, making it easy to navigate from the getgo without having to spend much time getting accustomed to them (I speak as someone who played using standard keyboard direction buttons, though I haven't heard any complaints about the controller compatibility). And it's a good thing the controls are easy to pick up on, because your focus needs to be primarily dedicated to the characters and the storyline.
The plot of the game seems pedestrian at first: you find yourself in an unknown land, navigate back home, voila you're done. The intuitiveness comes in the plot twists, and while some are more predictable than others, overall it leaves you feeling satisfied. I could rave about the characters for hours, they're so complex and interesting from the smallest of side characters to the mini bosses to the main cast.
The game is by no means the most difficult level grinder out there; if anything, level grinding is highly discouraged. The laughs are played up and - depending on the route you take - you likely won't be tearing your hair out in frustration too often trying to defeat a boss. Radiation focuses on the world building and creative problem solving rather than a simple Shoot Now Question Later approach. As the description says, you don't have to kill anyone!
The soundtrack is beautiful and fun to listen to inside the game and out. The comedy is witty and delightfully cynical, the concept of having to live with the consequences of your actions even after the game is done, and the novelty around the idea of truly choosing your own path and ending - of which there are much more than simply Good, Bad, and Neutral - all tie this game together in a lovely little package that is well worth the $10 you're shelling out for it (go for the game + soundtrack pack, you'll save yourself a couple of bucks when you inevitably decide to buy the soundtrack after your first playthrough). If you can overcome the guilt that the game makes you feel for resetting, this game's worth a thousand replays.
The first game in a long while I've wanted to see through to the very end and is definitely going to stay with me for a long while. Undertale gets a 10/10 from me.

I'll separate this by categories, Gameplay, Graphics, Story, Music. and Final Thoughts
Gameplay - 8

Graphics - 8
I feel this is the highest I can rate it since it is very old school looking and not the most impressive for old school looking games but the art direction is superb despite the old look. It looks more so 8 bit than 16 bit and even over that looks more like an old DOS-pc game over a console game. I can't just give a 9-10 here but the more you play it you realize just how creative they were. A nice thing they do is make it gradually more pretty as you play through it. It starts off very bleak and slowly becomes more pretty as it plays out. They use design to amplify the mood of story brilliantly.
Story - 9.5-10
This game is very surprising here. What starts very simple gradually like the graphics reveals it capable of more and more. You begin to think they can only tell the story in one direction and feels like its very simple and linear.  Then it throw some REALLY crazy♥♥♥♥♥♥to throw you off. There is shockers, there is twists, and there is moments I really gasped like watching GOT. Also worth mentioning is the humor of this game. It's absolutely hilarious. One of the funniest games I ever played. But over its humor is it's emotion you really care for these characters in the end and most of them are very love-able. And the gameplay ties into the story perfectly. How you play the game is the message of the game.
This story IS TOP NOTCH.
Music  - 10
I am so capable of writing a thousand page essay here so I'll keep this short.
The sound track is up there with the works of Nobuo Uematsu and Yasunori Mitsuda. I know that's a bold claim but that is how well  this music is sticking in my head. Except neither of them wrote the game as well.

Only until you play something that feels just as good.
Playing Undertale proved to me that this is not the case. All the bits of wonder I received playing games like Chrono Trigger and Final Fantasy VII, in my younger years came alive in me while playing Undertale. That sense of childhood wonder was burning bright as ever. It proved to me that a game can STILL be as amazing as those titles if done correctly and because of that I'm filled with new optimism for gaming in the future.
Toby Fox's Determination has filled me with Inspiration.

You know, when this year started, I was thinking that Witcher 3, or maybe Fallout 4, would be my favorite game of the year. Who would have thought it would be some ten-dollar JRPG/Bullet hell hybrid indie game?
Undertale is an absolutely phenomenal game that expertly blends all kinds of different emotions and styles into a coherent and, above all, satifying product. What seems like a cute little indie game slowly unravels into a fresh and exciting experience that spans multiple playthroughs with choices and consequences that, for once, ACTUALLY have some weight to them  (I'm looking at you, Fallout 4) and, ultimately, decide the outcome of not just that playthrough, but perhaps even the playthroughs to come. As far as the actual story, what you get is a fantastic experience filled to the brim with memorable characters, great dialogue, tons of choices, fun bullet hell gameplay and a unique visual style and world.
TL;DR Get it if you like a great story and extermely fun and varied gameplay.

Rust (Раст) - это детище Facepunch Studios. Основной идеей игры является выживание. Как DayZ, Minecraft или Сталкер - события в RUST будут происходить в крайне враждебной среде, в которой вам предстоит выживать или может процветать.
Я буду жить!
Основная цель игры состоит в том, чтобы начиная только с камнем в руках выбить себе место под солнцем. Для вам потребуется собирать разнообразные ресурсы. Например, дрова можно добывать с деревьев или вязанок дров, породы и руду можно добыть с больших валунов. Затем можно попробовать создать себе более совершенные орудия труда, например, из древесины и камня у вас получится топор , что позволит собирать материалы гораздо быстрее.
Вам потребуется еда. Вы можете охотиться на разнообразных животных, представленных в игре. Медведи, волки могут представлять большую опасность для начинающих игроков. А кабаны, куры, кролики и олени будут просто убегать от вас. После того, как вы убьёте животное с его трупа можно будет собрать такие ресурсы, как мясо и кожу. Далее вы можете сделать костер из дров и приготовить мясо на огне. В итоге вы получите хорошую еду и больше шансов на выживание.

Pros.
-It's fun
-Good co-op game
-Intense
-Makes you always stay on guard
-Challenging
-Pretty
Now, the negatives.
-Poorly Optimized
-Bad PC bindings (although can be re-bound)
-Zombies are way too OP
-Massive Glitches
-Broken Textures
-Terrible lag
-Hit detection is terrible.
Now there is more Negatives than Positives but I am not here to make up your mind for you but only to give you some help if you are "on the fence" about buying it. Disclaimer: I have had RUST before it came out on steam more than two years ago in Closed Alpha. I was heavily into base raiding and PVP. If you plan on playing in carebear PVE servers, skip this review. But here are my two cents about its current status otherwise. Take it with a grain of salt if you will...
----------------------------------
Yes: The developers are more active now than ever.
Yes: It gets frequent content updates.
Yes: Game's a blast when playing with a group.
Yes: Graphics are looking more spectacular now than ever.
No: Glitching/hacking still exists. (It's just the nature of this type of game, more on that later)
No: Game feels like a clunky mess after being rebuilt numerous times. (It was very responsive originally.)
No: Janky new mechanics are a hindrance in a situation where you need to be responsive against other players.
No: The game is STILL in Alpha Early access after two years. (Not unusual if you look at DayZ, but still.)
No: Updates are slowly transitioning towards content only updates, with less and less technical updates from Garry. (Which is what this game needs in my opinion; more on that below.)
----------------------------------
With that being said, the two biggest issues is that the game has been rebuilt from the ground up constantly, and the hacking/glitching issues.
----------------------------------
1. The game used to be responsive, though with the introduction of each rebuild it turned into a more and more unresponsive mess. Movement and responsiveness are huge factors in a game where aiming and positioning are the two most important things when PVP comes into play. This leads to unsatisfying deaths feeling like your character should be moving one way but turned out to be kind of glued into a certain spot. More often than not the game looks like a testing ground for Garry to practice his coding, the game worked as is initially, and now too much time was spent redoing the entire thing just for it to look nicer and feel smoother.
----------------------------------
2. With hacking and glitching overall: It's hard to blame Facepunch Studios on this one, as they have taken a lot of measures to prevent hacking and glitching, but it's such a huge issue in these types of games. You can't stop someone who constantly works against you in coming out with paid/private hacks when they have a price incentive for customers who are willing to skip the games week grind if it means killing a top tier base and being at the 'end game' instantly, along with having the edge and never dying. Dying and losing your stuff is a huge net loss, both morally and game wise.
Find a hacker in CS:GO? Report him and move on, you only wasted 30 minutes of your time, and you most likely never see him again. Hackers in DayZ/RUST? Your entire weeks worth of work is down the drain. With all the anti cheat improvements, RUST is the type of game where even one hacker/glitcher getting through can ruin the game for an entire server. Though with the type of game its hard to even identify one, granted if you're offline and your stuff is just gone with the doors/walls still up, you'll have no person to point at. Even with wallers/aimbotters, it's hard to tell with no spectate option, unless you get shot in the head 5 times instantly. But a game such as this can't be expected to have a spectate option. Like I said its just the nature of this type of game.
----------------------------------
I expect this to be in Alpha for another year honestly, if it ever leaves Early Access is another question entirely. I honestly can't recommend a purchase at this point knowing that the formula is said and done, and if you're looking for a game like RUST, then there are others way ahead of the curve. I feel like a games experience shouldn't come down to an admin trying to police a server, which is what happens here. The game itself should be designed with preventative features like that in mind. Games like these apply a human band-aid in the form of admins, who can be more often than not, biased, and given/give special treatment, though its hard to argue when you own the server. Still the thought of an in-game admin is archaic and should be left in the past along with the games that lacked proper mechanics that required a person to log in and manage a game.
----------------------------------
All in all, I feel like the game just isn't worth it. The current direction its headed reminds me of ARK:SE, which isn't a bad thing, but ARK:SE already got there first. Even worse is that Facepunch Studios is working on the next Garry's Mod, which means Garry will focus his time on the next project and leave this one up to his community managers and content staff to finish up the main bits, while he adds a shiny new effect here and there.
----------------------------------

I do recommend this game but I just wanted to give my own recent experience.
While playing on a low population server I made the wise choice of starting a shop, seeing as I was better off than others who were playing on the same server. In my five days on the server i saw some dramatic changes, the server as a whole became friendly and began helping one another out, they didnt raid each other, they hunted, gathered, and scavenged together. Eventually, my shop became too small for the amount or merchandise I had, and the amount of customers I got, so I had to build a new shop, others on the server decided to follow me on my move to a new shop, and decided to build a town around it, they even nominated me as mayor.
My shop was mainly an experiment into human nature, to see if when given the opportunity people band together and create a functioning society, the answer was yes, even in a video game people will band together, but it wasn't all sunshine and lollipops on the server, we had some people go rogue on the society. They would break into peoples houses while they were away, steal their things, and maybe their home, some would go so far as to frame others for their deeds. Eventually I left because of the degradation my society was facing, my dream had become a nightmare, all in the space of five days, and all because a handfull of people.
My time on that server was rather dramatic in its entirity, but through the bad times there were many people who made the game worth playing. Thank you for your time.

Have them all and for me this is currently the best zombie survival game on the market and it still has not reached its potential being still in alpha state.
Pros
+ Every time you play is different as you can never predict how other players will react

+ Plenty of active servers and player base

Cons

- Hackers (.52 was especially bad but now they have implemented new anti hack system)

- You meet some idiots
So yes i recommend this game although its best played with friends.

Let me preface this by saying this game is incredibly fun and completely worth the $20 bucks it's going for at the moment. Rust is the most infuriatingly fun game there is right now.
I'm not going to do a pros and cons for you like most would. I'm going to keep it short, sweet, and to the point.
Simply put, this is not a SURVIVAL game. This game is about 10% PVE and 90% PVP. Despite what the description says and what some players might say, this game is not centered on survival. Hunger, thirst, and fatigue are just a small fraction of what you have to be concerned with while playing. You can play for hours and not think about your hunger and thirst once. This game is all about:
- getting a base started
- keeping the furnaces burning
- crafting those weapons
- raiding other player's bases
- defending against other players trying to raid you
For what this game really is, it is a ton of fun. Going solo is simply not sustainable. You will die and you will lose your base if you go it alone. If you are in a group, this game is much more fun because then you have teammates who will have your back when the wolves come knocking.
If you want a game where you are fighting against the elements and mother nature to survive then this game isn’t for you. Try "The Long Dark" or something similar. (TLD is a really fun and addicting PVE survival game)
If you want an open world shooter game that makes you earn your weapons. If you want to fight other players. If you like gun battles. If you like explosives and destruction. If you want a game that can offer you fast paced action and the occasional lull to catch your breath. Then this game is probably for you.

I...I don't get this. I really don't. I should play more and try to get into the game deeper, but I just can't: I cannot play this game without having a utter sense of boredom on my shoulder. It's probably one of the most boring games I've ever played and I don't get this a single bit.
For starters I want to be fair: the game IS NOT BAD. You read that fanboiz? I said the game is good: it's detailed, has a lot of love and passion on it, the writing is good, the music is OUTSTANDING (it's one of the fewest things that I love about it: I occasionally listen to it on youtube) and overall its got a good old style graphics that retro fans will enjoy. On the surface, Undertale is gorgeous and I'm sure that anyone will agree on this.
In the core, Undertale is an RPG but also not: the game is all about your choices and the consequences of said choices. Do bad stuff, and the enviroment will show the inevitable results and, on paper, it's actually amazing! The game also follows a pretty interesting story and the characters are "funny" to interact with, so you end up either liking or disliking them. As I said, nothing is really wrong with the game itself: it's well done, and I'm very impressed by it.
But also, I don't get it: I just got extremely bored on playing it and that's because the "morality" in the game is completely and utterly flawed. Here's how I depict this game: it's like playing Skyrim and whenever I kill an entire village, the guards will come to me and say "what have you done" and try to arrest me and try to make me feel bad. And that's what this game is all about: did you kill someone? OH NO, you did a terrible thing, how could you? Have you no soul? Repeat this over and over, and that's essentially what you get. It does feel bad, no wonders, but the situations in this game aren't always fitting and that's why I disliked doing the genocide run. It's like the game slaps you for doing that choice, but it's a forced slap rather than a punishing one.
Then the other choice is Pacifist, which you literally don't kill anyone and basically behave like some sort of "goodie goodie" boy who does no evil. Now, I will admit that I like this way: I always like to have a different way to deal with things and being able to win everything without fighting, has all my admiration.
The problem is that now the game becomes utterly and incredibly BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOORRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIINGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGG.
Yes I had to do that.
Why is it boring? Well, you don't get any experience. "Duh" someone would say, but then what's the point of fighting? Money? Well yes but you want to buy armors and weapons with it, and you buy weapons for the genocide run. You're not doing the Genocide run? Then you want money for armors, since you'll be stuck with 20 hp for the entire game. Also, It's not always easy to understand how the fight works while in pacifist: some fights requires you do specific things before you can spare the enemy and it's not always completely understandable. It's a minor complain, but still one nevertheless.
In both cases however, the fights are also quite interesting: after each action you do, the enemy will try to hit you in a sort of Bullet-hell mini game that requires you to dodge all of the attacks. There will be lots of variations on the formula and I like that. It's just too bad that you can't just have it in a normal RPG: you either don't fight and make them all useless, or fight and have the worst possible ending you could get.
But maybe that's why I'm doing it all wrong? I probably should say that UT is not an RPG: it's an adventure game with RPG elements and lots of story choices. It's some sort of VN without being a VN: lots of stuff to choose and occasional fights in it to change the pace. I'm sure that if you've watched videos you have a better idea on it, but for me it just didn't click: I have played RPGs with better choices that didn't always end in being totally evil and angelicly good.
Do I recommend it? Of course: I don't see anything bad in it overall, just little flaws that are mostly subjective but that I felt the need to expose. You think I'm wrong? Go play it then: why did you have to read this review? Oh, because it's positive? Even positive reviews can tell flaws on them: doesn't have to be negative to pick on things. But I'm still being very positive about because it's good and I have nothing really against it.
It's just sad that I couldn't get into it as many others did.

There is a high possibility of running into someone and getting screwed over but thats kinda a part in every game. I look at rust like a post apocalyptic survival game. While looking like a classic/retro RPG game, it flips all the traditional gameplay completely upside down. Like the motto of the game says "The RPG where you don't have to destroy anyone." is completely true and is also frowned upon by the community.
It is a classic/retro game so the controls are very basic. Arrow keys to move, enter key to interact and shift key to cancel an action or skip through dialogue. It relies heavily on characters and dialogue so there is a lot of interactions with friendly and hostile NPCs. When getting into a battle the player is given a choice to
.
is self-explanitory.
Lets you use an item from your inventory to replenish health or activate other effects. However, instead of going through the game and fighting everyone and anyone you encounter, there is the option of a
and
. These two systems work with each other if you want to go through the game in a Pacifist playthrough.
lets you help the enemy solve its problems so that they won't want to fight anymore and then you can
them.
When it is the enemy's turn to fight, you are in control of a sprite that's in a box while the enemy is attacking. You'll have to dodge the attacks the enemy uses or else its game over.
On the topic of game overs, Undertale uses the traditional save mechanic of having save points occasionaly that save your progress and recover your HP.
I feel like this needs to be addressed on its own. You can go through the game multiple different ways but the main two ways are
and
This game, as most games like to boast about now, has a strong morality system. However, this is game shows what a morality system should be. Not just a certain companion disliking something you do, but fully affecting the world around you if you decide to go Genocide or Pacifist.
As I mentioned earlier this is a game in the style of classic/retro games such as Earthbound. Don't expect the graphics to be as good as something like Star Wars battlefront or Halo 5 or one of the more recent games. The graphics are very simple but they fit the game well.
This are where the game shines, each character you meet is fleshed out and has their own unique personality. Even some of the NPCs have this effect on them, which makes the game feel alive and really makes you immersed in this universe. There are many jokes that the characters make about themselves, modern culture or just tell bad puns because they can. I would write more on this section but I would be walking into spoiler territory.
We finally reach the end of the Undertale's aspects. This soundtrack is outstanding, easily the best I've ever heard in a game. I would like to say that this music rivals that of Martin O'Donnell and Micheal Salvatori (Halo soundtrack composers) and John Williams (Star Wars soundtrack composer). Each main character has their own theme tune that fits their personality perfectly. This includes the location's theme as well.
Overall Undertale is one of the best or maybe even the best game that I have played of all time. Whether you want to have a serious game or a joyful, happy game, it all depends on how you play it. Thank you for reading this review and I hope it has convinced you that this game is worth the price it is at.

I ABSOLUTELY recommend Undertale to anyone and everyone. There wasnt one thing i disliked about the game other thatn maybe its a nit on the short side for some, but being a $10 indie game, i went into it expecting that and it still wasn't too short.
I know from other sites and comments that there are some people who don't get it or find the story and the gameplay reptitive and boring. Thats fine, it their opinion, not a fact. The story felt very original too me and very heart warming, or very heartbreaking  depending on how you play and how you look at it. The jokes all made me laugh, some a lot, some a little, but still and even the bad ones, cause they are clearly meant to be bad, which in itself makes it silly funny. For me combat didn't have an overly repetitive feeling at all, but that could be cause i play pacifist route, which each characters pacifist methods are all different, but even if you fight, the dodging and attacks are almost always different for each character as well. As for too many random ecounters, I didn't get that many at all, and this is coming from a guy, whos played every single pokemon game for hundreds of hours and sometimes just wants to run through a cave or tall grass with out fighting a freaking pokemon EVERY 2-5 STEPS >:(............. I didn't get that feeling at all with Undertale.
As for the rest of the game, the music is, in opinion AMAZINGLY well done, i love the entire soundtrack. The pixelated style felt like it fit just fine with the type of game it was and even still looked beautiful at times, even if it isnt High res by anymeans. The characters are all lovable in one way or another, i dont know if I'll ever be able to do a genocide run becuase of it, and I loved the story all the way through. It felt original to me, and if it does have a cliche side, then I ask you, what doesnt any more, and is that even a bad thing? I don't think so.

I can safely say that I've had it easy in this game. One of my friends is hooked to Rust like it was heroin, so when I join the server, there's no need to start from scratch - I just teleport to him and he gives me everything I need before we go raiding.
Our raiding process has always been the same:
It's fun as hell, and as you can see, most of the fun in this game relies on coordinated teamwork, so
: Rust is as demanding as Crysis 3 in ultra settings, yet it doesn't look even half as good. I'll leave it at that.
: play while skyping or use the steam chat, as the in-game communication system is pretty much useless. Unlike most multiplayer games, in Rust you can't set up T for your team and Y for everyone - if you use the in-game voice chat, you'll be heard by everyone in the proximity, so it's heavily recommended not to use it.
: want to teleport to your friend? "/tpr <your friend's name". Want to establish your newly built base as a spawn point? "/sethome <name of your base>". Want to see if the server offers free clothing/weapons? "/kit". Intuitive, eh?
The description doesn't lie though. It's an early access game and if you buy this, you better be ready to play an unfinished, buggy alpha. One would expect that after 2 years it would at least be close to beta and the gunplay wouldn't suck SO BAD, but the reality is that Rust is being developed slowly. Very slowly.

I ABSOLUTELY recommend Undertale to anyone and everyone. There wasnt one thing i disliked about the game other thatn maybe its a nit on the short side for some, but being a $10 indie game, i went into it expecting that and it still wasn't too short.
I know from other sites and comments that there are some people who don't get it or find the story and the gameplay reptitive and boring. Thats fine, it their opinion, not a fact. The story felt very original too me and very heart warming, or very heartbreaking  depending on how you play and how you look at it. The jokes all made me laugh, some a lot, some a little, but still and even the bad ones, cause they are clearly meant to be bad, which in itself makes it silly funny. For me combat didn't have an overly repetitive feeling at all, but that could be cause i play pacifist route, which each characters pacifist methods are all different, but even if you fight, the dodging and attacks are almost always different for each character as well. As for too many random ecounters, I didn't get that many at all, and this is coming from a guy, whos played every single pokemon game for hundreds of hours and sometimes just wants to run through a cave or tall grass with out fighting a freaking pokemon EVERY 2-5 STEPS >:(............. I didn't get that feeling at all with Undertale.
As for the rest of the game, the music is, in opinion AMAZINGLY well done, i love the entire soundtrack. The pixelated style felt like it fit just fine with the type of game it was and even still looked beautiful at times, even if it isnt High res by anymeans. The characters are all lovable in one way or another, i dont know if I'll ever be able to do a genocide run becuase of it, and I loved the story all the way through. It felt original to me, and if it does have a cliche side, then I ask you, what doesnt any more, and is that even a bad thing? I don't think so.

This is Early Access done right!
Been playing since day 1, and it's been quite an adventure. First, the game is wildly addictive and fun. I play on my own low population server since most players are jerks. I'm hoping they add in some more environmental threats and NPCs to give people something to do other than kill and grief eachother.
Within the last few months the game has finally surpassed legacy in playability and fun. The choice Facepunch made to basically start over is paying off. We're starting to see new stuff added much more frequently and the Workshop is really cool if you're into cosmetic items.
The game is much more tedious if you're a solo player, but it's also rewarding to build a whole base by yourself.
Every time I play I'm struck by how beautiful the game has become. Just running across the island lets you see so many amazing landscapes.
Finally, I love the weekly dev blogs. I've learned so much about the development process from keeping up with this game. Facepunch does the best job of listening to the community while filtering out all the idiots that are constantly complaining. This game is definitely worth the price.

I always write reviews about the games I truly love and the ones I truly hate. Undertale was the only game so far that I WANTED to write a review but simply couldn't. I didn't knew where to start. I have so much to say, I have so many items to point out, there are so many spoilers I could make for the sake of expressing the many feelings I have for this game! There are so many good points and so much writing to do that I simply couldn't pull the energies to do it for fearing not making the game any justice. So I'll make just a tiny and generic portion of everything I have to spill out:
This game touches your feelings. It gives you options all game long and you will pay the price of your choices in the future. You can be the nicest guy ever or the biggest d*ck in the entire universe. This game has ways of reaching for the very depths of your mind and emotions and yank everything out to scrub against your face with a big "That's who you are, happy?".
My reccomendation is that if you have kids at home, let them play the game and do whatever they want. And if they take a mean route, make them play again and this time be by their side to guide them through the 'pacifist' route. This will surely teach them to be kind to people and that it pays to make the extra effort to be a better person. If you're an adult (and mature at mind, of course), go play the game through both 'bad' and 'good' ways and you'll see what I'm talking about.

-3 hours in...
I finally had the foundations down for my house. It was a little off the beaten path, but not too far from those precious resources. The new procedurally generated map offered a much better experience than my previous involvement in rust a year ago. More varied, less predictable establishments. Except for the big clan bases. Those guys plant right in the center of large fields. My home was a little out of view of the largest base. I was out collecting wood one day when some naked man came up behind me with a torch. He beat me with it. And stole all I had. Including the key to my lock. Luckily he didnt know where my place actually was. I had to build a second establishment close by. Unfortantly it was a little in view.
-5 hours in...
I never play with fire at night. Too dangerous. Too foolish. So I was chilling in my shack, avoiding the cold. i could only scrape enough cloth together for some pants to hide my shame. But it was enough. I had food, shelter, and clothing. The only thing I lacked was friends. In the pitch black of the night was the worst for raiders. They went to high ground looking for fires, and unsuspecting victims. Really thos people deserved it. Better them than me rigth? Unfortuitiously a man happened to come down the hill precisely where i had hid the shack. I heard the foot steps and shuddered. I could hear him traversing the remains of my previous base, where I had hid the entrance to the new one. It was a quick job but it had befuddled others. I figured he would assume it was empty and move on as there was no door in view at a glance. He decided to look further however. I didnt have time to shut my door. I huddled to the corner beside the door clutching my bone blade I had made not but an hour before. He came into view. Head to toe in full armor, and AK47 in hand. He didnt see me as my storage chest were directly across from the door. He went for it, and I went for him. Stab, Stab Stab i floundered in the dark. I heard a clunk as my blade bounced off his helmet. $#!t he turned to me with the AK and opened up. I tell you this! I did not expect the shoddiness of my construction to safe me. His bullets destroyed my base. I fell two floors down. I heard a scream of agony. "What the heck?" The sun was starting to come up. I could kindof see. I made my way back upstairs... Silence. My house was in shambles. Only two walls remained. One section of floor. Where did he go? Surely he wanted my loot. The it hit me. The cliff beside my home, the scream. I rushed down to inspect and sure enough. All his nights loot, armor, warm clothes, weapons. A gold mine. Six hours it would have taken for me to gain whart I had just won by chance. I grabbed all I could and ran. He would be back. ASAP
I scurried away, up the hill to start a new base. One the was secret. Another tricky cliff dive I think. And someplace far away from... him... and vengeance

Undertale is... something else. It harkens back to what made RPGs what they are: Role Play, and story! It's so simple on the outside, yet so complex and well-crafted on the inside. Don't get Undertale for one playthrough. There's no point in doing that. The true beauty of the game is when you try different ones, a different approach each time. Yes, the game changes, sometimes DRASTICALLY depending on the path you choose and sometimes not so much. A full playthrough's about 6-8 hours or less, so go nuts! In short: It looks like nothing, yet it's everything.

There's a lot of talk about DayZ being a buggy mess, filled with hackers. And it's right, sometimes. What you're getting from this early access is a cheaper, unfinished version of a game - you give the developers money now, for the full game later, and meanwhile you get to play what they've done up until this point. If this sounds like a negative review, it's not. I've logged 53hrs in DayZ, and I enjoyed all of it. But I think it's important to not get carried away by the hype.
DayZ is not finished, not even close. When it is, it should be one of the best survival games ever made. If it's not, a lot of people are going to be very disappointed. But if you buy DayZ now, expecting one of the best survival games ever made, you're going to be diappointed. If you buy it now understanding what an alpha is, are willing to laugh bugs, hacks and glitchy animations off, and are genuinely interested in competitive zombie hiking, you'll love DayZ.
Hours per $ (when I bought it) - 5 ($0.2 per hour)
Enjoyment - Unlimited with friends, rather tedious without
Recommend for hiking enthusiasts, people who like jump scares, bandits and Russians.

Probably the funnest game I've ever played. If you like Surviving, this game is for you. If you hate PvP then don't buy this game, because that is one is the elements to the game. You have to keep in mind that this is a sandbox PvP survival game. there is always a chance you could die and lose everything you've worked hard for over the past several days. Don't expect people to hold your hand while you play this game, Its community is brutal and often cut throat. The games main focus is starting with nothing and gaining resources in order to build bases and craft weapons. This process can go on indefinitely depending on the size of the group you play with (or if you play solo), how much you play, the server you play on, and how far you're willing to take your efforts. This game is high risk high reward most of the time. most players kill on sight(KOS) so be prepared to die often. Overall the game is very playable in it's "early access" state. There are a few bugs here and there, but nothing long term. The Dev Team "Facepunch studios" are great and do a tremondous amount of work on this game everyweek, so bugs get fixed often the same day. Oh Yeah, because the game is in early access, you can look forward to weekly content updates. It's awesome. It's been this way for a while now and I hope they continue to keep pushing content out like they have been.

I always write reviews about the games I truly love and the ones I truly hate. Undertale was the only game so far that I WANTED to write a review but simply couldn't. I didn't knew where to start. I have so much to say, I have so many items to point out, there are so many spoilers I could make for the sake of expressing the many feelings I have for this game! There are so many good points and so much writing to do that I simply couldn't pull the energies to do it for fearing not making the game any justice. So I'll make just a tiny and generic portion of everything I have to spill out:
This game touches your feelings. It gives you options all game long and you will pay the price of your choices in the future. You can be the nicest guy ever or the biggest d*ck in the entire universe. This game has ways of reaching for the very depths of your mind and emotions and yank everything out to scrub against your face with a big "That's who you are, happy?".
My reccomendation is that if you have kids at home, let them play the game and do whatever they want. And if they take a mean route, make them play again and this time be by their side to guide them through the 'pacifist' route. This will surely teach them to be kind to people and that it pays to make the extra effort to be a better person. If you're an adult (and mature at mind, of course), go play the game through both 'bad' and 'good' ways and you'll see what I'm talking about.

I found DayZ to be quite buggy, long winded, but still alright if you don't mind messing around with a friend. I'm not a fan anymore, especially with PUBG being a thing.
I think PUBG does everything better: Instead of playing scavenger hunt for items in order to survive just getting around, you play scavenger hunt for items you need to fight. There's no "You're cold" BS going on in PUBG which lets you concentrate on the things that actually matter. Along with that, the playzone doesn't stay still. DayZ was a stagnant game that you could run around for an hour in without seeing anyone; this was a really bad problem that led to boredem quite quickly for me. But the biggest diffence is updates. PUBG has a great update schedule that makes some noticeable differences to the game. DayZ.... yeah, no.
With both games nearly the same price, I can't recommend DayZ when PUBG is a way better game. In less time, I've racked up WAY more hours, had a greater experience, and keep coming back to it almost every day. I think this game is pretty dead.
