It's already got such a rush to it, and it can only get better from here. Hopefully.

Where to start...
First, take a second glance at the system requirements for Dayz.  This game Requires.
Second, understand that this game has been in Alpha for about two years and isn't looking like Beta is happening anytime soon.  The game is under constant development; just take a look thru the logs.  So no need to complain endlessly about the perpetual 'Alpha' status.  Either enjoy what you are given or go elsewhere.
Ok but lets get serious...
You will spawn into the game in a random location on the map with nothing useful.  You'll be lost, hungry, thirsty, cold, possibly wet, chased by zombies, and you can't trust any player you meet not to try to kill/rob you.  Sounding fun yet?  Your first steps playing will be to survive, and this is no easy task.
Now lets skip ahead, assuming you have now mastered the basic skills required to survive and kill the undead.  At this point you will understand many of the hidden dangers that lurk.
Dangers like..?  Walking down the stairs, getting out of your vehicle, hidden sinkholes, zombies phasing thru all walls, stepping off a one-foot drop, ... ect.   All of which can kill or cripple you.  Did I mention 'Alpha'?  The game has alot of bugs.  General gameplay is rigid.  It all takes some getting used to.
Even with all this, I love Dayz.  I have put a insane amount of time in back when it was only a mod of Arma II and will continue to play.  If you get hit in the leg with a bullet, you will feel it.  Bleeding with a broken leg... yes bullets do hurt.  If you get hit in the face with a bullet, your screen will go black, "You are dead"... and once again, you spawn in a random location with nothing useful.  So very satisfying to know you deal actual damage when you kill someone.
Dayz, keep up the good work.  No other game delivers the hardcore gaming experience that I desire.
That all being said, I will check back in another year.  There is alot of work to be done yet and the overall progress has been slow.

I will admit I was very sceptical about Undertale when I saw how much hype it was getting, as I usually steer clear from overhyped games (at least until the hype dies down and I haven't lost interest). Also, this review will be spoiler-free.
Then a friend bought it for me for an early Christmas present and I was immediately hooked.
It's just... it's beautiful. The graphics are a nod back to the retro gaming era and the battle system is a new and interesting one. Plus, unlike other RPGs, you don't have to kill everything to move on. In fact, the way that characters interact with your actions in the game thus far is fantastic. The music is suitably catchy with a retro feel to it.
Currently I'm doing two runs on two separate computers - one as a neutral/pacifist run and the other as a genocide run. And the course you take affects what happens later. I love it.
And also, the style is somewhat reminiscent of Earthbound, which I believe is one of Undertale's main inspirations, and I think that's one thing that made me like it since I enjoyed Earthbound.
Buy this game now. And...
Stay determined...

Let me preface by saying that I can see the appeal of this game and do praise the dev(s?) for their unique take on the RPG genre.  While the coombaya pacifist take and bullet hell defense are very much not my thing, I might still recomend it to others based on how unique that is.
However I have some huge gripes that made me give it the thumbs down.  These should be very much promoted to deter players like me from buying and not liking the game.
1. No controller support on MAC.  Bullet storm with arrow keys on a laptop is not fun
2. It is VERY short for an RPG.  Beat the game in 5 hours.  Might have taken longer if I was a pacifist.  I'm not
3. There is an internet realm of younger adults and teens that enjoy sayin "teh" and love cutesy anthropomorfic things.  I'm not one of them.  I found the humor and extreme "do the right thing" attitude childish.  As if in the real world being benevolent to everyone, even when their attacking you works.  Sorry kiddies it doesn't.  Most RPGs have a mix where you cannot help one without hurting another, which is more realistic.  Here you take your lumps until your attacker feels better.  Saccarine to say the least.
There's also no internal conflict in the underworld.  Humans forced them down there, humans are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s.  Every monster agrees.  But they're nice so they help you.  Unlike the other 6 kids they butched for their souls...
I really don't see how this plot is being hailed as revolutionary and genius.  With so many games that build layers and complex characters, Undertales biggest brag is the lesbian lizard scientist.  A gay person(monster) in 2015??? How edgy!

4. The game is incredibly linear.  Why would I want to save the underground if it consists of one village and a lab.  NO sidequests, secrets, hidden bosses etc.
5. You can find weapons, but you're not supposed to use them.  You can level up but you're not supposed to, because you'd need to kill tweedlefly or whatever quarky enemy they throw at you.  So throw those RPG elements out.  Besides, why attack a knight throwing spears at you when you can flirt with them(?!)
I loved Earthbound and Mother 3.  Both were long sweeping adventures, full of great humor, secrets, different settings etc.  They also allowed you to make decisions, but never forced them down your throat the way undertale does.

This game has been hyped up so much that I went against my sale-only purchase policy and spent the full $10. It was 100% worth it.
Undertale has good everything. Characters, character designs, story, gameplay, music, replayability, etc...
It will only take you about 6 hours to get through your first time. The amount of care and detail that goes into every hour you play is admirable to say the least. For instance, it was refreshing to see that each enemy (even non-bosses) got it's own unique attacks and ways to interact with them. Some battles even show how much the creators were really "thinking outside the box".
It should be noted that story outcomes can vary greatly based on your decisions.  I made the mistake of trying to look up a particular battle on YouTube and saw something drastically different than what I experienced in my own playthrough.
I am excited to revisit this game and I'll be hearing the music in my head for weeks.

It's barely optimized, and even you turn the game into a potato on low graphics you get drops to below 60 constantly. A game aimed in this direction seems like so many I have played before. First off: No Character Creation, which I can see why they don't have it, but the fact you spawn as one character, every time you play the game, no gender pick, no difference among person to person. Second: Gunplay in this game makes me cringe. My Final Verdict of this game is buy it when it's 1, updated to a playable point, 2, buy when the game is on sale. It's been a long time since a game made me experience actual emotion. Like, connection with characters, understanding their flaws and their dreams.
Undertale is a unique experience. One that I, personally, feel is best done on one's own, with as little knowledge going in as possible.
The game is a unique JRPG-styled game where your hits are timed and you have full ability to dodge any enemy attack if you learn their patterns. It's simplistic, but it's very involved. And it feels excellent.
The story is absolutely stellar. I won't go into detail, but I suggest doing a total pacifist run either your first or second time through. I feel it's the most satisfying.
The music definitely shines too. I recommend the soundtrack if you don't mind putting out a little extra for this game. It's totally worth it.
All-in-all, it's my GotY of 2015. Not flawless, but certainly a game that I felt was a unique and worthwhile experience.

I have never been so emotionally attached to a group of characters so much before. Never has a video game, an electronic video game, left me physically in tears that it was over. I literally cannot recommend this game enough. From the bottom of my heart I beg you to try this absolute magnum opus of entertainment. We pay far more for AAA titles and none of them have left me feeling nearly as satisfied with my purchase. And the soundtrack combo is well worth the money because the music in this game is so much more memorable than anything I have ever heard. It really harkons back to the days when games made up for their lack of graphics with a phenominal story, and that's not to say the graphics are bad. If anything, they're perfect for this game. It leaves the characters open to so much interpretation that you can envision them almost any way you would like. If this game does not win indie game of the year, then it will be a sincere disapointment. My only complaint, is that it could't go on forever. 10/10.

It took me less than 5 hours to beat this game the first time.  This game is perfect for the young teen daughter, or girl gamer that just learned how to read.
If you like the 8bit, flat rpg genre style of game; then this will be perfect for you.
If you are a girl gamer getting into RPG's, then this will be perfect for you.
If you like great graphics, animation and voiced text; then stay away from this dog pile.
I don't want to overhype this game, because that may lead you to some kind of disapointment.  However, if you have played games with a similar style, Zelda on Nintendo, Pokemon on Gameboy, etc...  Then this game will blow your mind away.  It takes that style in a new refreshing direction that wont dissapoint.  I hope you play this game without spoilers, because they can ruin the fun.
One last thing, I don't know any recent popular games with this 8bit flat style of gameplay.  It's very old school.  I think if you haven't been exposed to this old school style, then the game might turn out to be a dud for you.  Buyer beware, if you don't like the 8bit flat graphics, old school text convosations; then this game may fall very flat for you.
For me, this game was worth the $10 I paid for it.  I'm an old school guy that used to play Zelda when it first came out in 1987ish, FF7 in 1996ish, and many of those oooold games...

As I sit down to write this review (I know I'm sounding like a preppy douchace, but hold on one moment), I don't know exactly what to talk about. If you are reading this, you probably already know the basics of the game already. It's an rpg where you don't have to kill anyone. But what Undertale is...I can't even begin to qualify it as a game. That would simply be unfair.
Undertale is about spagetti, bad puns, friendships, laughs, tears...murder.
When people think of Undertale (at least the people who have played it), these are the things they think about. I'm in that category as well. In addition to...
Choice. Meaning. Existentialism.
These ideas may turn you away from the game, but let me ask you this. When is the last time you cared about video game charaters? For most, it would be a long time, but the reality is that once you turn off the game...it doesn't matter.
Not with Undertale. Through humerous dialouge, insights into who the characters truely are, learning more about the lore, and even them trying to kill you, you form a friendship. Or they die. Your choice. But no matter what your desicion, you can't help but like them. They are just amazing people...
...people...
When you turn the game off, they still exist. They are still there in your heart and in your mind. The game plays your emotions like a harp. And I wouldn't have it any other way.
Here's where you say "Who cares? Is it fun to play?". Yes it is. But I don't care about that. No one who has played Undertale cares about that. Going back to what I thought of Undertale, I said exestentialism. Your probably confused, even if you know what that word means. In Undertale you can FIGHT or ACT/MECRY. The game makes you question these descision, as well as your existance in the game itself. "Well obviously the game wants you to not kill right?". Well the game doesn't say that. You may do as you wish (you monster). So let's talk about the endings.
Undertale has 3 endings, which happen based on your actions. Your probably already guessed them. Neutral, Pacifist, and the dreaded GENOCIDE. I don't want to talk about them as to not ruin them, so I will go into very little detail surrounding the idea of them (NO SPOILERS). As I said before, the game does't judge you based on your actions. Because there really is no reward to choosing either one (besides XP...but that's an entire other thing I can't get into). It mearly let's you experiance your actions and how it affected the world around you. Which again, you will care about. You don't think so now, but you will. I did. EVERYONE DID (Yes everyone. I'm not exagerating in any sense. I swear). You won't even be able to see spagehtti without laughing and thinking of Undertale.
And through these actions you gain...something incredible. Actual insight. A game can shock. A game can amaze. But only Undertale can teach. No spoilers, but you will be profoundly effected by this game (again, preppy douchaery, but hold on).
I'm rambling. I would love to talk to more, but I couldn't do it without spoilers. This game is very spoiler heavy. On that note, I do want to say that even if you have seen playthoughs, nothing compares to actually playing it. Even if you know what descisions you will make...it doenst matter. You will laugh. You will cry. You will feel quilty. You will learn.
To wrap it up (holy♥♥♥♥♥♥this is long), Undertale isn't a game. Undertale is...so much more. Which people will say about a lot of games. But I mean it. I'm sure a lot of people who have played it will agree with me.
Now let's talk about the Undertale community. It ♥♥♥♥ing sucks. I get it, it can ruin games that you care about. But perservere. It's worth it. On that note, I don't think many people actually understand why the game is so great. No one has talked about what the game actually teaches or why its so important. All everyone talks about is the ♥♥♥♥ing battle system and not what important lessons it leads to. Which pisses me the ♥♥♥♥ off.  I've already described in general without specifics why it's so great, but I cant go into detail. Because spoilers. But again, you've probably seen the endings. But again (again), that won't matter.
Do I recomend Undertale. Well, I obviously do. But to WHOM to I recommend it to? Everyone. Gamers, non gamers, lieterally everyone. Anyone will enjoy Undertale...as long as they have a SOUL.

I never play with fire at night. Too dangerous. Too foolish. So I was chilling in my shack, avoiding the cold. i could only scrape enough cloth together for some pants to hide my shame. But it was enough. I had food, shelter, and clothing. The only thing I lacked was friends. In the pitch black of the night was the worst for raiders. They went to high ground looking for fires, and unsuspecting victims. Really thos people deserved it. Better them than me rigth? Unfortuitiously a man happened to come down the hill precisely where i had hid the shack. I heard the foot steps and shuddered. I could hear him traversing the remains of my previous base, where I had hid the entrance to the new one. It was a quick job but it had befuddled others. I figured he would assume it was empty and move on as there was no door in view at a glance. He decided to look further however. I didnt have time to shut my door. I huddled to the corner beside the door clutching my bone blade I had made not but an hour before. He came into view. Head to toe in full armor, and AK47 in hand. He didnt see me as my storage chest were directly across from the door. He went for it, and I went for him. Stab, Stab Stab i floundered in the dark. My house was in shambles. Only two walls remained. One section of floor. Where did he go? Surely he wanted my loot. The it hit me. The cliff beside my home, the scream. I rushed down to inspect and sure enough. All his nights loot, armor, warm clothes, weapons. A gold mine. Six hours it would have taken for me to gain whart I had just won by chance. I scurried away, up the hill to start a new base. One the was secret. Another tricky cliff dive I think. And someplace far away from... him... and vengeance

I have just recently bought Undertale because I have seen it across the internet and all my friends own it already. However, I have seen multiple playthroughs of multiple types of runs and multiple endings, and I am prepared to share my thoughts about this game.
To start off, if you are considering this game, completely disregard any reviews that go along the lines of "Why are you reading this review? Just buy the game!!!!" or "Its only 10 dollars why dont you own this game yet!" Yes, there is a large fanbase following this game and yes, they are prepared to defend Undertale's title of "best game ever" at all costs. Contrary to popular belief, like any other game, Undertale has good parts and bad parts, and you might like it or you might not.
My main problem with Undertale is that some of the puzzles and situations are immpossible to lose, which takes a lot of the exitment and genguine feeling out of them. Although some may be funny or deep, they just take up time and get old fast.
My other problem is that in a pacifist run, it can get really boring to have to figure out how to make monsters spare you. The fight button is oh-so tempting, but you're afraid that a tiny scratch will kill the enemy. In addition, the genocide run can have the same effect. Walking around for hours trying to find the last two enemies sucks, and finally getting to the boss and killing it in one hit is extremely unrewarding. I get it, a no-mercy run is supposed to make you feel bad, but if we're talking about a video game, it should be entertaining rather than completely un-rewarding. After all, isn't that the purpose of a videogame?
Another issue is that the graphics aren't the best, but Undertale was developed by a very small team running on kickstarter funds in Andrew Hussie's basement, so you can't really complain. In fact, if you are not buying this game because it looks bad, I urge you to reconsider.
Moving on to the whole game in general. A large amount of people say that Undertale shouldn't be praised as a masterpiece because the only good/emotional parts are the endings. This is almost true. The endings are very well crafted and send chills down your spine. They can be sad, exiting, tragic, epic, and can overwhelm you with emotions. Even so, I see how it would be a problem if the endings are the only good part, but in Undertale's case this isn't true. What makes the rest of the game enjoyable is the quirky and interesting characters, the snappy dialouge, the backstory that you have to unravel playthrough by playthrough, and the odd world that you are lost in. The whole game isn't an emotional rollercoaster, but you do somehow find yourself getting attached to the family of magic skeletons trying to kill you, and you don't find that in many videogames.
Another big upside to Undertale is that your choices do matter. In a lot of videogames that claim that the decisions you make decide your fate end up like this: You can talk to someone and say A or B, you can either go left or right, and it doesn't change anything but the final cutscene. In undertale, if you decide to disable yellow text, you'll find it later in a trashcan. If you kill a boss, other characters will wonder why they haven't showed up to their house yet. Something you say in battle can result in you going on a date with the very enemy you were fighting a couple minutes later. Remember that time you killed those random encounters? Now people are giving you suspicious looks.
Overall I do enjoy Undertale and I do reccomend it, but it isn't a perfect game like everyone says.
Did I also mention the soundtrack is AMAZING? Seriously, your ears will get aroused.
TL;DR
Undertale is a good game but it can be boring and unrewarding, and the graphics don't look good. Story and characters are wonderful and the game is very entertaining. It's also only 10 dollars holy♥♥♥♥♥♥

As I sit down to write this review (I know I'm sounding like a preppy douchace, but hold on one moment), I don't know exactly what to talk about. If you are reading this, you probably already know the basics of the game already. It's an rpg where you don't have to kill anyone. But what Undertale is...I can't even begin to qualify it as a game. That would simply be unfair.
Undertale is about spagetti, bad puns, friendships, laughs, tears...murder.
When people think of Undertale (at least the people who have played it), these are the things they think about. I'm in that category as well. In addition to...
Choice. Meaning. Existentialism.
These ideas may turn you away from the game, but let me ask you this. When is the last time you cared about video game charaters? For most, it would be a long time, but the reality is that once you turn off the game...it doesn't matter.
Not with Undertale. Through humerous dialouge, insights into who the characters truely are, learning more about the lore, and even them trying to kill you, you form a friendship. Or they die. Your choice. But no matter what your desicion, you can't help but like them. They are just amazing people...
...people...
When you turn the game off, they still exist. They are still there in your heart and in your mind. The game plays your emotions like a harp. And I wouldn't have it any other way.
Here's where you say "Who cares? Is it fun to play?". Yes it is. But I don't care about that. No one who has played Undertale cares about that. Going back to what I thought of Undertale, I said exestentialism. Your probably confused, even if you know what that word means. In Undertale you can FIGHT or ACT/MECRY. The game makes you question these descision, as well as your existance in the game itself. "Well obviously the game wants you to not kill right?". Well the game doesn't say that. You may do as you wish (you monster). So let's talk about the endings.
Undertale has 3 endings, which happen based on your actions. Your probably already guessed them. Neutral, Pacifist, and the dreaded GENOCIDE. I don't want to talk about them as to not ruin them, so I will go into very little detail surrounding the idea of them (NO SPOILERS). As I said before, the game does't judge you based on your actions. Because there really is no reward to choosing either one (besides XP...but that's an entire other thing I can't get into). It mearly let's you experiance your actions and how it affected the world around you. Which again, you will care about. You don't think so now, but you will. I did. EVERYONE DID (Yes everyone. I'm not exagerating in any sense. I swear). You won't even be able to see spagehtti without laughing and thinking of Undertale.
And through these actions you gain...something incredible. Actual insight. A game can shock. A game can amaze. But only Undertale can teach. No spoilers, but you will be profoundly effected by this game (again, preppy douchaery, but hold on).
I'm rambling. I would love to talk to more, but I couldn't do it without spoilers. This game is very spoiler heavy. On that note, I do want to say that even if you have seen playthoughs, nothing compares to actually playing it. Even if you know what descisions you will make...it doenst matter. You will laugh. You will cry. You will feel quilty. You will learn.
To wrap it up (holy♥♥♥♥♥♥this is long), Undertale isn't a game. Undertale is...so much more. Which people will say about a lot of games. But I mean it. I'm sure a lot of people who have played it will agree with me.
Now let's talk about the Undertale community. It ♥♥♥♥ing sucks. I get it, it can ruin games that you care about. But perservere. It's worth it. On that note, I don't think many people actually understand why the game is so great. No one has talked about what the game actually teaches or why its so important. All everyone talks about is the ♥♥♥♥ing battle system and not what important lessons it leads to. Which pisses me the ♥♥♥♥ off.  I've already described in general without specifics why it's so great, but I cant go into detail. Because spoilers. But again, you've probably seen the endings. But again (again), that won't matter.
Do I recomend Undertale. Well, I obviously do. But to WHOM to I recommend it to? Everyone. Gamers, non gamers, lieterally everyone. Anyone will enjoy Undertale...as long as they have a SOUL.
By the way...
If you are going to get the game, you need to read the following. Trust me.
If you seem stuck in the game (which is guarunteed), I want to let you know there is a true pacifist ending which...is kinda stupid to reach. This is my first review, and I know its a little late for this but if this review can convince even one more person to play this masterpiece of a game - It'll be worth it.
The gameplay very Earthboundish, with your character moving around on the overworld until you encounter an enemy in which case you have several choices in combat
- The dodging mechanic in this game does away with the randomness that usually plagues games in this genre but instead opts to make it more like Galaga, minus the shooting.
Each and every single boss has their own, unique twist on this formula so it never really gets stale and each one's patterns are really fun to learn - like a Mega Man game
- The main marketing around this game is centered on the mercy and act command which helps drive the plot and serves as a tool to add funny jokes more than add anything to actual combat sequences.
: This is not a bad thing as I will explain later.
-There is an attack command, but in order to fully enjoy the game I would advise against it as it does little to innovate from the typical formula and because the aforementioned "mercy" command is much more fun to mess with.
-The story may seem very bare bones at first but as it goes on it becomes increasingly complex.
Undertale's greatest strength lies in how it eases you into it slowly and how the mercy command is used to great effect to draw you emotionally into the lore.
- I cannot praise this soundtrack enough, Toby Fox is an avid gamer and it really shows in how almost each and every track in this game has some kind of callback to another.
Some of the more emotional tracks in the game are used to really set the tone and drive home some of the more profound messages this game trys to teach you, I can almost guarantee you will download at least one of them.
Undertale is a phenominal game that I can't recommend enough as it excels in all the areas it wants to, you may think from how I worded parts of this review that it copies a bunch of previously successful games in an attempt to be good but its really just celebrating what made those games great while retaining its own sense of identity
I absolutely recommend this game for anyone on the fence and because its Steam tradition to have at least one joke on a review...

Do not buy this game if you have no patience, a short fuse, anger issues, or have a genetic predisposition to heart problems.
Main problems that contribute to my dislike of the game in its current state:
- Low FPS in towns/cities
- Light penetrates through buildings and terrain
- Hit & miss melee system
- Zombies rubber-band and teleport
- "Please Wait..." screen at spawn take a while to disappear
(The only major thing I can recall them fixing is zombies running through walls and fences. They run around them now but can still walk through closed doors.)
Instead of fixing these problems, the developers have instead added a plethora of useless content and items and built new cities. While this is good of them, what's the point if underlying fundamental issues I mentioned prevent enjoyment of the game? Supposedly there is a "new renderer" around the corner which should address some performance issues. I would like to see more news from the developers on when and how they plan to fix these issues, or a reason of why they are adding features and content before fixing game breaking issues.
Of course, the game is also full of fresh spawn killers which will never change and just create an angry player base who will kill anyone for no reason.
There is also a large community of people who say cut it some slack because it's only in alpha stage. These are the same people who think that content is more important than performance, and that all bugs should be fixed at the end. I don't care whether the game is classified as a pre-alpha, alpha, beta or whatever, just fix the big issues! DayZ first came out as a mod in 2012. Think about that and whether it should still be classified as an alpha almost 3 years on.

This is my first review, and I know its a little late for this but if this review can convince even one more person to play this masterpiece of a game - It'll be worth it.
The gameplay very Earthboundish, with your character moving around on the overworld until you encounter an enemy in which case you have several choices in combat
- The dodging mechanic in this game does away with the randomness that usually plagues games in this genre but instead opts to make it more like Galaga, minus the shooting.
Each and every single boss has their own, unique twist on this formula so it never really gets stale and each one's patterns are really fun to learn - like a Mega Man game
- The main marketing around this game is centered on the mercy and act command which helps drive the plot and serves as a tool to add funny jokes more than add anything to actual combat sequences.
: This is not a bad thing as I will explain later.
-There is an attack command, but in order to fully enjoy the game I would advise against it as it does little to innovate from the typical formula and because the aforementioned "mercy" command is much more fun to mess with.
-The story may seem very bare bones at first but as it goes on it becomes increasingly complex.
Undertale's greatest strength lies in how it eases you into it slowly and how the mercy command is used to great effect to draw you emotionally into the lore.
- I cannot praise this soundtrack enough, Toby Fox is an avid gamer and it really shows in how almost each and every track in this game has some kind of callback to another.
Some of the more emotional tracks in the game are used to really set the tone and drive home some of the more profound messages this game trys to teach you, I can almost guarantee you will download at least one of them.
Undertale is a phenominal game that I can't recommend enough as it excels in all the areas it wants to, you may think from how I worded parts of this review that it copies a bunch of previously successful games in an attempt to be good but its really just celebrating what made those games great while retaining its own sense of identity
I absolutely recommend this game for anyone on the fence and because its Steam tradition to have at least one joke on a review...
This is my pick for game of the decade, almost good enough for me to call it the game of century.

Overall, I think Rust has great promise as an open world survival game, but it does have some problems.
Pros:
-Reliable developer
-Lots of content
-Very large world
Cons:
-A bit glitchy at times, but I guess it's still in alpha so that's to be expected
-Players will probably not be able to customize their character. A new feature is going to be added that makes your character's race, gender, and other attributes completely random, which I feel takes the choice away from players, though it has good intentions.
-If you don't play the game every day, your shelter will decay until it disappears, at which point other players will be able to easily steal everything you've worked for. The decay system is meant to get rid of unused structures to reduce the load on servers, but I think there is a better way to do that than by deleting things.
There is also the issue with other players. You can have peaceful relations with other players, but the majority of people couldn't care less about you if you're wearing a nice shirt. Starting out as a new player is very difficult because everyone shoots first and never asks questions. You can be a fresh spawn, running naked through the woods and people will still kill you. It is very difficult to get ahead in this game.

My Undertale Review:
Undertale Is Neither Under Nor Tale.
Its Trash. 0 stars

In recent years, we have gotten many games. Some were good, some were great, and others not so much. Amongst the greater ones lie the pinnacle of what games are truly capable of, delivering experiences only games can deliver, but it is unfortunate that such occurences are far and between.
There has been a drought, IS a drought, of a game that has truly enamoured us and captivated us in the medium's beauty, especially regarding 2014 and 2015. Some releases, eagerly anticipated with stories we want to see in its glorious revelation, only to fall short, crashing, burning. Where oh where can I quench this thirst for a great story from a game? I looked upon the calendar, 2015 is almost over and the releases we have waited are already in the wild and had either disappointed, or was good, but failed to capitalise on its potential.
I go to Facebook, I see friends reposting neat art of some characters and comics, which all ended with "tale". Intrugued, I read the comic, and I was already more engrossed in this sadly incomplete but ongoing comic, and I had not realised that this was not "original content" in that sense, but it was inspired by a game. A game which I had regrettably overlooked its release and its promotional banner across Steam's front page, merely because it was in pixelated 8-bit graphics.
I went back to the store. I gave Undertale a proper look, to not give prejudices, and instead look beyond the surface. I had initially intended to hold off till a sale, but, the recurring art flooding across multiple sites I frequent, the monolithic praise this game has been getting, the incessant persuasion of my friends to get me to buy the game, I eventually gave in. I bought it at full price.
...
...
...
I was not strong enough to prove I could survive.
Undertale. A game that stands higher amongst most other games.
Undertale. A game with the kind of story I had craved for so long.
Undertale. A game which brought new twists to things we had long thought to be "traditionally fixed" and its (IMO) highly fun combat mechianics, akin to bullet hell shooters.
Undertale, oh how I had Underestimated you. Its a game, that at first looks simple, but do not let it deceive. Scrape through the surface, and you'll discover layer upon layer upon layer of... content that is simply, brought together to become a composited masterpiece.
Enter this game with ZERO prior knowledge of its story. This is a game where spoilers will really, really ruin the experience for you.
Buy this game and give TobyFox and Papyrus their money.
TL;DR: Why are you reading this? Go add this to your cart. Now. Like, NOW.

You'll awaken naked on a beach, and immediately begin hitting things with rock to scrounge whatever meager tools you can quickly improvise.  It will feel familiar if you've played any other hi-res Minecraft clone.  You may start to make plans or mentally assess your surroundings, but really, none of that will matter.
Within a few minutes, a nine year old with auto-aim will tag you with a spear, giggle like a sociopath or clumsily insult you, and then you'll get to listen as he carves the meat from your still-twitching body.
This is the chief issue - your first five minutes of Rust and the subsequent hours are going to play almost the exact same way.
You can join others, if you are lucky, in whatever defensive structure they've managed to erect.  But this game does not incentivize teamwork, AT ALL - it incentivizes exploiting people to do your heavy lifting for you.  Ultimately, you'll be betrayed by one or more of your members - all they have to do is type your four digit password in Steam chat to a member of a raider clan, and that's the ballgame.
Because of this heightened tension you are as likely to be killed by your allies as you are by your enemies, due in no small part to everyone looking like everyone else.  You can also be easily overrun, or simply killed and farmed repeatedly by raiders while trying gathering resources outside the walls until your entire operation becomes anemic.
Clothes are tricky to build, because you either have to enter the killing-fields of the forest to gather hemp, or somehow spear the very few animals which spawn.  There is no farmable crop to produce cloth or wood.  And because you will be killed often, you (and virtually everyone you meet) spend most of this game with your pixelated dong flopping in the breeze.
People have logged over 800 hours in Rust, and there's a reason for that.  There's something to the appeal of a game where you have to struggle and suffer for every inch.  If you enjoy titles like The Forest and The Long Dark where you are actively hunted at all times, Rust will offer a superior experience.  Human players are infinitely more creative and brutal than AI regulated MOBs.
There are two core issues:
1) Rust is easy to hack, because of the Unity system.
I saw several players glitch through walls and a few flying through the air.  A persistent and authoritative moderator could mitigate this, but it would take an exhaustive amount of effort.  The Steam Anticheat protocols help, but they do not remedy every issue.  And any game can be ruined by hacking eventually, but when it's this simple, it becomes pervasive.
2) The Rust community is god-awful.
They often have severe personality issues, and tend to make the experience feel cheap.  Their schemes are largely transparent, their jokes are cringey, and the game mechanics bring out the worst in almost every single one of them.  If you're a functioning adult, the experience will likely be nauseating.  You can to an extent alleviate this by playing on a lower volume server, or running it on a password coded private server with a 7-10 friends.
A few elements could improve Rust - a greater level of terrain destruction, the ability to fabricate autoturrets, a larger animal population.  But at that point, you might as well play a game which already features those elements - H1Z1, Ark, DayZ, 7 Days to Die, or Life is Feudal, to name a few.
If you have a book report due on Lord of the Flies, and you're having difficulty getting the tone of the work, or if you really enjoyed the 1994 film No Escape, you should play Rust.  If you want to see measurable, semi-permanent progress in a game you into which you sink hundreds of hours, play almost any other survival/crafting title.

First of all, I haven't touched this game in a while, so some of this might have changed.
Overall, I think Rust has great promise as an open world survival game, but it does have some problems.
Pros:
-Reliable developer
-Lots of content
-Very large world
Cons:
-A bit glitchy at times, but I guess it's still in alpha so that's to be expected
-Players will probably not be able to customize their character. A new feature is going to be added that makes your character's race, gender, and other attributes completely random, which I feel takes the choice away from players, though it has good intentions.
-If you don't play the game every day, your shelter will decay until it disappears, at which point other players will be able to easily steal everything you've worked for. The decay system is meant to get rid of unused structures to reduce the load on servers, but I think there is a better way to do that than by deleting things.
There is also the issue with other players. You can have peaceful relations with other players, but the majority of people couldn't care less about you if you're wearing a nice shirt. Starting out as a new player is very difficult because everyone shoots first and never asks questions. You can be a fresh spawn, running naked through the woods and people will still kill you. It is very difficult to get ahead in this game.

I was planning to get this game in a few weeks and then a friend gifted it to me.  I went in expecting a good game.  I experienced a great game... and then found myself thinking about it days after last playing it.  Not many games make me want to play them again immediately after beating them.  It is impossible to say anything more about what impresses me with the story without massive spoilers, but I absolutely love the game.
It would be a huge mistake to see this as an Earthbound/Mother clone.  It has some similarlites when it comes to humor and tone but the differences are vast.
It would also be a mistake to think that just because you do not have to kill, that battles are uninvolved.  The game manages to be not long but not too short either.  It does an incredible amount of things right. Rather than ramble further, I'll just repeat that I adore this game. I see myself revisiting it now and then, and while I like replaying beloved games few make feel that way so strongly.
All of this said it is best to go into this game expecting a decent semi-oldschool RPG experience, because the ways in which it surprises are quite unique.  It may not be best game ever material for everyone, but I think it's definitely something very different and special.
The only criticism I have for Undertale is that I can never play Plants Vs Zombies the same way again.

"Only the fearless may proceed.
Brave ones, foolish ones.
Both walk not the middle road."
Ironic that this is the hint for the first "puzzle" in the game, considering Undertale walks the "middle road" for the gaming industry, as it has both quality gameplay and story. Difficulty is fairly low, as long as you get used to the earlier enemies before moving on to the next area. The bosses are definitely no pushover, but going into more detail would ruin the surprise. Still, if you stay determined, you'll get through. Music's also a strong point, considering the creator himself was and is a musician, and essentially composed the entire soundtrack himself. Story's a bit touchy - only in the sense that if you can't connect to the story at all, there's no point to playing the game. The other points of the game are fine, but this is not a game you play for the "game", it's a story - thus the name Undertale - and if that falls through, so does the rest of the game. And, if you care about graphics - what are you doing on an indie game's store page, anyway? Heck, why are you still reading this review after the 300 above it telling you to buy the game? Do it. It's good. Seriously.

It is, at it's heart, a love letter to the Earthbound/Mother series, and it subverts those expectations wonderfully through the gameplay. Your choices against the puzzles/opponents will matter throughout the game and make you rethink your decisions throughout. The cast of characters is nothing less than delightful; A dorky, obnoxious group of weirdos that I spent 15 hours battling, befriending, and ultimately caring about.
An incredibly simple battle system that is cleverly expanded throughout gameplay, and is masterfully leveraged against a host of memorable characters. This is the game that sums up the Indie golden age of gaming: subverting traditional gaming tropes to rethink your choices as a player and ultimately engage in the well-being of the world you're part of.
Loved the game, intend to continue to explore it throughout the years.

Now, I loved this game, so my review will be subjective. You have to keep in mind what thing with Undertale. It may not please you. It doesn't work for everyone; no game does. But as your best friend Flowey would say, those people really ARE idiots.
First and foremost, you will not like this game if you absolutely REQUIRE the greatest in graphics. It's a 2D RPG. Keep in mind whether or not that suits you before you buy the game.
One of the best parts about this game is that EVERY choice you make matters, and EVERY interaction with major and minor characters changes the ending just a little bit. You don't see that kind of choose-your-own-adventure mechanic in many games, let alone an indie. Not to mention how the game makes you, the gamer, feel fully responsible for an fictitious world that you only spend a limited time in.
And the characters themselves? They have some of best development and design I've seen in years. Is the attention to detail and complexity intended to make you take the Pacifist route? Maybe. I honestly don't have a problem with it.
And the plot, even though I personally have only seen one, did something I would've never expected. I tend to be a cheapskate when it comes to games I like. I usually watch Youtube series of them. With Undertale, I watched a playthrough up until
, and I decided to buy the game because I literally had to see the ending of the game on my own playthrough. It could've been a $60 game and it still would've been worth it.
So, in conclusion, bake up a Butterscotch Pie in your Burnt Pan and Stained Apron, pet your Lesser Dog betwen bites of a MTT brand Glamburger, and settle in for one of best experiences to ever come out of indie development.

While steam says I have around 34 hours or so, I have put easily another 20+ hours offline on my laptop. I have completed the Genocide, Neutral, and True Pacifist routes of this game, and each one holds a special place in my heart.
Undertale was the first videogame to make me cry just by hearing it's soundtrack.
The game is a primarily light-hearted adventure where the player guides the human, "Frisk" to try to make it back to their home. This can be achieved by killing monsters, gaining EXP and LV, or by finding a peacful alternative to your problems.
You meet a variety of characters in the game, each one with their own loveable personalities. (Except Alphys, god ♥♥♥♥ing damn I wish you could put your phone on silent mode).
The soundtrack is obviously one of the most popular parts of the game, and for good reason.
The Undertale OST is a very extensive selection of music by Toby Fox, and each one sounds like they are made with heart. I love this game.
While the stories within the game are very simple, the endings of each of the routes have made me feel many ranges of emotions, and I can say confidently that this game changed me as a person for the better. While some of the game may feel a bit like a grind, I can guarantee that the experience you receive from this game is well worth the price.

Ok, so here's the deal - Undertale was that one-in-a-million odds-breaking game born in an humble Kickstarter campaign, only to later become one of internet's most beloved gems.
Now, the big questions here that everybody's asking are "How?" and "Why??". Well, first off, believe me when I tell you the first answer you'll surely discover later, the second one I'll tell you here and now - because it's bloody brilliant!
To better explain myself, let me start from the beggining: when I first bought this game it had been released for over a week or so and there was already a "big woop" around it. Of corse I had some nice expectations (because everybody was already going freaking wild about it), but even so, inspired by previous experiences, I never got that hyped for it - I wasn't hoping for much more than some 6-8 hours of indie-styled conceptuality from this game... but I soon realised it was waaaaaaaaaaaaaaay more than that.
Undertale is, today, one of my, if not my all time favourite game (along with Portal 2 and Ocarina of Time). It's simply a masterpiece.
Now, I know I'm probably not the first person you found making this kind of statement, but believe me, this game is beautiful!
To avoid getting into more detail, the best way to describe Undertale would be as an incredible love letter to the rpg genre. It manages to be hilarious, quirky and even really emotionally touching. With a wide range of charming well-constructed characters, one of the most amazing soundtracks of modern gaming, an excelent writting, an overall perfect mood and a beautiful story, Undertale surely stands out has one of my best gaming-related experiences.
To finish off, it was really hard writting this "review", but I really don't want to spoil anything for you guys, so PLEASE do yourselves a favor and buy this game (believe me, it's worth it).
P.s. Forgot to mention that this game also managed to make me cry like a baby, so be warned if you're a sensible person or, overall, just don't like emotional games.
P.p.s. For your own sake, do the pacifist route first (you'll thank me later).

Ok, so here's the deal - Undertale was that one-in-a-million odds-breaking game born in an humble Kickstarter campaign, only to later become one of internet's most beloved gems.
Now, the big questions here that everybody's asking are "How?" and "Why??". Well, first off, believe me when I tell you the first answer you'll surely discover later, the second one I'll tell you here and now - because it's bloody brilliant!
To better explain myself, let me start from the beggining: when I first bought this game it had been released for over a week or so and there was already a "big woop" around it. Of corse I had some nice expectations (because everybody was already going freaking wild about it), but even so, inspired by previous experiences, I never got that hyped for it - I wasn't hoping for much more than some 6-8 hours of indie-styled conceptuality from this game... but I soon realised it was waaaaaaaaaaaaaaay more than that.
Undertale is, today, one of my, if not my all time favourite game (along with Portal 2 and Ocarina of Time). It's simply a masterpiece.
Now, I know I'm probably not the first person you found making this kind of statement, but believe me, this game is beautiful!
To avoid getting into more detail, the best way to describe Undertale would be as an incredible love letter to the rpg genre. It manages to be hilarious, quirky and even really emotionally touching. With a wide range of charming well-constructed characters, one of the most amazing soundtracks of modern gaming, an excelent writting, an overall perfect mood and a beautiful story, Undertale surely stands out has one of my best gaming-related experiences.
To finish off, it was really hard writting this "review", but I really don't want to spoil anything for you guys, so PLEASE do yourselves a favor and buy this game (believe me, it's worth it).
P.s. Forgot to mention that this game also managed to make me cry like a baby, so be warned if you're a sensible person or, overall, just don't like emotional games.
P.p.s. For your own sake, do the pacifist route first (you'll thank me later).

This is a very good game!
It's wonderful to have an RPG where you don't have to kill anyone or anything, and it's not necessary to build up your level to get through. (During my playthrough, I only needed to 'grind' for a little bit once, right at the end of the game, and that was just to get in a few fights so I could get enough gold to buy more healing items.)
The combat system is creative and fun. It's very nice and refreshing to see a combat system that is aesthetic and visual, and which you get through not by making move after move after move, like I do with most other RPGs that I've played, but by avoiding the white 'obstacles' as they fly towards me. It's a combat system that rewards reflexes and co-ordination, so it feels more like you're in an actual battle, where you have to have your wits about you! Plus, some of the patterns that the obstacles fly in are very creative and actually fun to look at, which makes it all the better!
Also, the puzzles (and 'action scenes') elsewhere in the game are fun too. They're creative, well-thought-out and varied, so the game keeps feeling fresh. They, along with the fights, are challenging enough to keep me on my toes but not so hard that they become frustrating.
Admittedly, I did need a few tries to get past some of the 'bosses', but I managed them all with a bit of practice.
The game's story is engaging and interesting. It's also excellent that there are several different ways that the story can change, based on the choices that players make. That means that there is a lot of replay value for the game - I'm certainly going to play it again and see if I can do things differently.
Plus, the story is well-told, well-paced, and skillfully moves between atmospheres - sometimes gentle and happy-go-lucky, sometimes sinister and tense.
The music is very good, too. Sometimes grim and creepy, sometimes bouncy and joyful, sometimes soft, gentle and soothing. It does a good job at setting the atmosphere - especially in its use of silence! That's right, this game also knows just how to use silence to make an impact!
I like how funny the game is. I don't want to give away anything that happens, but there are a lot of funny parts.
Some people might think that this game is too short, but I don't think so. The game's story has a nice length, where it doesn't outstay its welcome, and doesn't feel like it's padded or like it drags. Plus, like I said, there are several different ways in which the story can progress and end depending on what choices the player makes, so it's good that you don't have to play through a really long game to see these different endings.
The only real crticisms I have to make of this game are quite small ones.
Firstly, I think that the backgrounds sometimes look a bit bland and uninteresting, with flat colours or undetailed pathways. That might be deliberate - maybe that style was done deliberately as a homage to old RPGs? I don't know, since I haven't played many old RPGs like the Earthbound series, Final Fantasy Series or Chrono Trigger or things like that. Anyway, other times the backgrounds look okay.
Also, I don't think the game has quite enough imagination or vision. Don't get me wrong, this is quite an imaginative game, and there are lots of interesting, creative moments in it, but... well, the game's world just seems to be a bit too similar to our own, with not quite enough fantastical flair.
Hopefully I don't give too much away here, but, Undertale takes place in a world different from the human world, full of monsters. However, the world just seems a little too human. There are human-like houses, human-like jobs, human-like ways of communicating... I dunno, it just felt like it could've been a bit weirder and more creative - more DIFFERENT than what we're used to. But then again, maybe that's just me - I like weird, creative stuff. And, like I said, this game is still creative and fun.
All in all, this is a very nice, well-made, fun, and even uplifting game. Thank you to everyone who made it, and well done!
EDIT, WRITTEN ON 4th JANUARY 2016:
I've recently finished this game without killing anybody, and I had a wonderful experience!
So much more of the game opens up for you! You can explore whole other areas, you uncover more of the story, you learn more about the characters! It was very satisfying, and I loved the different ending. I actually had tears streaming down my face at the end of the final 'boss fight'. I admit that that was mainly because of the beautiful, moving music, but the themes and the events in the story were very beautiful and touching too.
I love stories that talk about peace, kindness and friendship, and how important all those things are, and Undertale does that well! This game not only deals with those themes with its story and its characters, but it actually makes kindness and friendship important parts of its actual GAMEPLAY, and I love that.
Thank you, thank you, thank you to everyone who helped make this game! You did a good job!

I'm not a fan of the 8-bit graphics but the music melds in with it to make it feel truly retro unlike most of the newer games that use the graphics.
All in all, I would give this game a 10/10. If this was in a poll for game of the year, I would vote for it. It's the best game i've played since Bioshock:Infinite came out. I would buy it for everyone if I could. Don't skip this game if you enjoy games at all.

Undertale as a whole seems to want to cash in on the "Retro" craze that's sweeping video games as of recent. Is it necessarily bad? No. But in this case, it really could have been done better. I'll try to be brief and mention what I've come up with through playing this game.
As I've mentioned above, Undertale utilizes graphics akin to RPG Maker and other various 8-bit-geared gamemakers. That being said, the game's look will obviously mirror the "Less-than-128-bit" look. While this can be done in some games to a good extent (OFF somewhat does this well, although probably Yume Nikki does it the best overall), Undertale really dropped the ball here. Does the UI overall look bad as a result? To a respectable degree, yes. Most of the layout is pretty basic: simple actions to be done by the player, and the obvious enemy in front of the player. Nothing much to praise here, but TobyFox (the one-man band who made Undertale) really could've at least made the actions box and combat environment look at least somewhat appealing. Being locked at (if not always around) 30fps definitely is a downside here. I would've like a little more work done on the overall look, but that's me.
Without spoiling too much of the game, you're a dude/girl (the game never mentions what gender you are specifically for no reason) who fell down a hole in a mountain. Turns out there's a whole civilization of monsters in the mountain who have mixed feelings for humans. From there, it's up to you how to treat them. However you act dictates treatment and the ending (there's a ton of endings, by the way) in the game, one of Undertale's more positive features. The game constantly belittles the player for his or her respective decisions, and seems to be keen on breaking the fourth wall often. While this isn't always bad, it's abused, and kinda makes the game seem heavily dependent on a player who REALLY cares about their decisions in a game. The writing regarding characters is good at best and corny at worst. The character Undyne is anime stereotype #1337, sans is the "lazy but seriously powerful" character you see in various forms of entertainment, and Flowey is the "deep through incessant pestering" character. The characters as a whole don't have much depth to them, and playing through all possible routes of the game more or less confirms this. While the characters at least have some flavor to them, they're not teriffically outstanding, which is kinda a must for an RPG.
Combat in this game is varied depending on the character the player is fighting. Different moves are dealt by different characters, creating a nicer sort of combat experience. Attacks can sometimes affect even the player (breaking the fourth wall again) in ways outside of dealing damadge. While this is a neat feature, it gets old (and at times annoying) after several playthroughs. The game's difficulty regarding combat is light to average, as many of the items the player acquires can heal a good portion of their healthbar. That being said, many battles often drag on due to♥♥♥♥♥♥poor damadge, dialogue needed to progress, or lack of items. On the topic of items, it seems obvious that Toby designed many of the items to fit in with the story and to aid the player on certain levels. Upgrades require storage in a limited space, but that problem's fixed through a certain gameplay element that's only available to
playthroughs. Combat becomes a mess at points due to this, and that really cripples the experience when playing a RPG.
It's an entry-level RPG and Bullet hell game. I suppose it's my fault for expecting any more from this, but I'm a sucker for SHMUPS. Undertale has some good elements that make it a somewhat good game (soundtrack is ok, but only two-three songs are really good), but the neutral to bad elements outweigh the good elements. That being said, Undertale is a good game for people wanting to get into the RPG/SHMUP genres. If you're really into immersion and care about graphics quality, this game isn't for you. For those wanting a really good to excellent RPG/SHMUP experience, look elsewhere.

This is a survival game. You will die. You will lose everything you worked for. The players in this game are not afraid to rub salt in the wound. Not only will they kill you on sight, they will laugh and taunt at you and tell you that you are worthless, and will make every effort to find your fresh-spawned butt so that they can just kill you on sight again. Expect all of these to happen within your first 10 hours of gameplay in Rust.
It doesn't matter if this game will come out of Early Access. It will still be a survival game in its core. You must be prepared to lose everything you worked for in a blink of an eye. If you get angry easily, or if you have a job or going to school, then this game is not for you because you need an hour or two of initial gameplay JUST to be situated, even with a friend.
Why do I have 500+ hours of gameplay and am still writing a negative review, you ask? Because I believe I am literally insane. Every week or so, I just wake up and say "Hey, maybe Rust will be fun today!" But no. It never is fun.
I've had groups hunt me down, with absolutely nothing on me, for sport. I've had 5-6 rude players pickaxe my measly stone-walled base with armored doors for fun. I've had "friends" who would betray me for resources after working together. And the worst part is that I'll launch this horrible game in the next 2-3 weeks so that I can re-live the pain, because I'll somehow convince myself in the most stupid way possible, "Maybe it will be different this time!".
If you REALLY want this game to become tolerable, grab at least 1 friend (in real life) to help you start out. The more, the merrier. Solo play is near impossible.
Nothing is sacred in this game. Buy at your own risk. Save yourself from the eternal hell that I keep bringing myself back to.

Undertale as a whole seems to want to cash in on the "Retro" craze that's sweeping video games as of recent. Is it necessarily bad? No. But in this case, it really could have been done better. I'll try to be brief and mention what I've come up with through playing this game.
As I've mentioned above, Undertale utilizes graphics akin to RPG Maker and other various 8-bit-geared gamemakers. That being said, the game's look will obviously mirror the "Less-than-128-bit" look. While this can be done in some games to a good extent (OFF somewhat does this well, although probably Yume Nikki does it the best overall), Undertale really dropped the ball here. Does the UI overall look bad as a result? To a respectable degree, yes. Most of the layout is pretty basic: simple actions to be done by the player, and the obvious enemy in front of the player. Nothing much to praise here, but TobyFox (the one-man band who made Undertale) really could've at least made the actions box and combat environment look at least somewhat appealing. Being locked at (if not always around) 30fps definitely is a downside here. I would've like a little more work done on the overall look, but that's me.
Without spoiling too much of the game, you're a dude/girl (the game never mentions what gender you are specifically for no reason) who fell down a hole in a mountain. Turns out there's a whole civilization of monsters in the mountain who have mixed feelings for humans. From there, it's up to you how to treat them. However you act dictates treatment and the ending (there's a ton of endings, by the way) in the game, one of Undertale's more positive features. The game constantly belittles the player for his or her respective decisions, and seems to be keen on breaking the fourth wall often. While this isn't always bad, it's abused, and kinda makes the game seem heavily dependent on a player who REALLY cares about their decisions in a game. The writing regarding characters is good at best and corny at worst. The character Undyne is anime stereotype #1337, sans is the "lazy but seriously powerful" character you see in various forms of entertainment, and Flowey is the "deep through incessant pestering" character. The characters as a whole don't have much depth to them, and playing through all possible routes of the game more or less confirms this. While the characters at least have some flavor to them, they're not teriffically outstanding, which is kinda a must for an RPG.
Combat in this game is varied depending on the character the player is fighting. Different moves are dealt by different characters, creating a nicer sort of combat experience. Attacks can sometimes affect even the player (breaking the fourth wall again) in ways outside of dealing damadge. While this is a neat feature, it gets old (and at times annoying) after several playthroughs. The game's difficulty regarding combat is light to average, as many of the items the player acquires can heal a good portion of their healthbar. That being said, many battles often drag on due to♥♥♥♥♥♥poor damadge, dialogue needed to progress, or lack of items. On the topic of items, it seems obvious that Toby designed many of the items to fit in with the story and to aid the player on certain levels. Upgrades require storage in a limited space, but that problem's fixed through a certain gameplay element that's only available to
playthroughs. Combat becomes a mess at points due to this, and that really cripples the experience when playing a RPG.
It's an entry-level RPG and Bullet hell game. I suppose it's my fault for expecting any more from this, but I'm a sucker for SHMUPS. Undertale has some good elements that make it a somewhat good game (soundtrack is ok, but only two-three songs are really good), but the neutral to bad elements outweigh the good elements. That being said, Undertale is a good game for people wanting to get into the RPG/SHMUP genres. If you're really into immersion and care about graphics quality, this game isn't for you. For those wanting a really good to excellent RPG/SHMUP experience, look elsewhere.

So... Undertale, does it meet the hype? Short answer, yes.
The game's graphics are frankly spartan, from the bygone NES era with modern effects layered over, but the graphics merely serve a means to an end. This is a game that takes your preconceptions of J-RPG/CRPGs and proceeds to beat you about the head with them. You see, this game knows you are coming into the experince expecting another RPGmaker project. The combat is where the game will start beating you with your own preconceptions. Combat comes in two parts. First is the enemy's turn, with you having to actively dodge in a sort of side scrolling shooter, with each attack mirroring the enemy's mood and personallity. The second part is in of itself two parts, depending on how you choose to play. you can choose to just attack them, wherein you are presented with a timing challenge to hit the enemy. Alternatively, you can befriend them via the use of "actions" one example is a starting monster called a moldsmal, which you can flirt with in order to "defeat" it.
The Story itself is the second way this game will beat you with your own expectations, it is difficult to explain the story or elements of it without ruining your experince. Simply put it'll leave you in tears (either of melancholy or of total sadness). The characters are memorable and enjoyable, making the plot twist in the game absolutly tear-jerking.

Memetale is by far the worst game to come out in the past decade, and thats saying something considering Fallout 4 came out not too long ago, and that was a tragedy.
Undertale is an RPG that dumped all of its resources on trying to be as funny as possible instead of anything worthwhile, like graphics, gameplay, music, or even a compelling story.
Right off the bat, the graphics are so bad you can almost count the pixels. All battle sprites come in two colors: black and white, and the game doesn't even run at 60fps. The main character looks like a potato came to life and grew hair, trust me when I say you could find better artistic talent in Shrek 2 on GBA.
The gameplay is a repetitive grind, like all RPGs, it's "stand in place and kill enemies till you level up". To make it worse, the higher level you are the longer it takes to get in encounters, so if you actually want to get any cash income in the game you're all outta luck without investing hours upon hours of monotonous walking. Most enemies and bosses die in one to two hits anyways, so it's not like there is any purpose to the leveling, it just takes away any idea of a fight being challenging or threatening. The developer stole the "unique" bullet-hell fighting mechanic straight from ZUN's Touhou series, blatantly ripping off the patterns with no new features added whatsoever. Whether you're a casual gamer, or hardcore bullet-hell or JRPG fan, Undertale has nothing for either audience.
Given that Toby Fox made the music for Homestuck, you can already tell the kind of uncreative music that fills the different boss fights of Undertale. Theres only about 10-12 unique song melodies in the game, with every other one being a highly distorted or remixed version of another song, god knows how many times he reused the generic enemy fight theme and rehashed it into other boss themes. Overall, the 8-bit music sounds very grating on the ears, and while they can sometimes be catchy, they rarely fit the theme or feeling of the situation they're used in.
The 'story' of Undertale can be summarized as follows (no spoilers):
A human falls into a cave full of spooky monsters, and has to befriend a bunch of wacky characters if they want to get back home!
Not too bad conceptually, until they start trying to stuff forced drama at every turn of the story, and every twist you can see coming from a mile away. Not to mention they interrupt any sense of 'atmosphere' the story gives off to spew some pop culture references to some kind of weeaboo anime trash or various other nerd fandoms. Most of the comedy devolves down into "lol so randum!!xD" gags, such as throwing the word 'spaghettii!' into sentences at random, or having the mascot character dog show up and do something wacky at any given time.
If you've ever seen the character 'Temmie' from somewhere on the internet, they exemplify all that Undertale offers when it comes to writing.
The game offers around ~6 hours of gameplay, which is grossly unacceptable by today's standards for a game worth $10. Undertale is incredibly easy by all means, offering very few challenges, clearly due to the game's emphasis on writing. If you're interested in Dank Memez, this game is an easy 10/10, but for anyone looking for something else I'd advise looking towards ANY other game.

As it stands, the current build of DayZ is a great foundation for an amazing zombie survival experience.  But people need to remember just that, that this is a foundation for the game to be built upon.  This game STILL IS early access.  It's no where near finished and it's no where near beta. PLEASE, keep that in mind if you plan on purchasing this game.
That being said, you need to be the right kind of "gamer" to want to play this game.  The world is huge, incredibly detailed and full of awesome places to discover.  It is also covered with grasslands and woods that you will spend A LOT of time walking through.  That is one of my biggest criticisms of this game, you will be walking around hoping to not starve to death for hours before even running into anyone.  That and everything is in Russian (or something) so I would recommend downloading an app for your phone that can help you translate what you're reading and help you navigate the map.
A lot of what makes DayZ so special is interacting with real players.  More often than not, people will just kill you before you even get the chance to say hello.  But when you meet up with someone and decided to adventure together, or even just trade, the story begins to unfold.  The crazy things that can happen in this game really make DayZ quite unique.
There are many things that DayZ needs to become an awesome game.  I have faith that it will get there, but as it stands this is a great survival game that I would recommend to my friends.  But, if you do get this game PLEASE be smart enough to realize and understand that you are purchasing a game that is not done.  I get so annoyed reading reviews and people acting like they deserve a perfect game just because they paid for it.  I mean, hell, I could pay money for a car that isn't finished being built.  It may work, but it wont work perfectly... and to that point, the only person I should be upset with if I don't like the unfinished car... is me.
This is the gaming standard all future Zombie Survival Games will be  compared to.

Pros:
large play area
good variety of items
PvP
realistic: bullet drop, attacks damage clothes and items, may find loot in odd places (I found a pen in a barn-twice!) etc.
Currently cheap pricing (probably will be $60 when it is released as a full version, so buying it now will save you 25 bucks)
Cons:
loot is stuck in an object or otherwise unreachable (example being that I couldn't pick up a gun right in front of me even though it was at arm's reach because I was too fat to wedge myself through the stairs it was under)
zombie spawning is a bit derpy (spent 6 seconds investigating the roof of a stand for loot only to discover a zombie had spawned right at the bottom of the ladder I was on. It then tore up my shirt)
Issues other people have:
Zombie density: Chernarus (the game's setting) used to be part of the USSR before becoming an independent power in 1991. Therefore, its population density (and zombie density) should be low, and since zombies will follow potential prey for thousands of miles, many zombies may have been led out of Chernarus by aircraft and such.
Hackers: I have never seen a hacker in this game. I don't know how common they actually are, but the developers have apparently released an update to combat hackers.
Fall damage: worse than Skyrim. The fact that you can fall about 5 feet and ruin your shoes AND hurt your leg until you inject some morphine is ridiculous. I think that the mechanic should have a severity level instead, like for instance you sprain an ankle and your shoes take minor damage from a two meter fall, or your shoes drop one quality level and your leg breaks from a five meter fall.
Zombie aggro radius: A zombie can see a glowing cigarette butt from two to three miles away in the dark. All their senses are gearing towards one thing: finding food and eating food. The fact that they don't react to footsteps or doors opening/closing actually sort of annoys me, but then again, my favorite type of zombies are the old-time Romero ones.
Bugs:
Zombies will phase through doors and such. Only a little annoying since their hitbox usually travels with them, so they can be easily killed.
A glitch I suffer from (but not others, apparently) is that text will be broken and almost unreadable. This makes it very hard to decipher chat messages and status effects and impossible to determine amounts in the inventory withou the "inspect" option. A similar glitch happens with inventory icons, so I sometimes mistake one item for another. I have no idea why this happens, especially since I use a gaming computer and should have excellent graphics.
Recently, I've noticed a bug where the character will move in a random and jerky manner, with a tendency to try to affix themself to one spot and look in a certain direction whilst twitching erratically. Only known fix is to wait a few minutes for it to stop, but it makes combat impossible.
Other notes:
Knowledge is power. A veteran of DayZ can help you become one too, or visit the wikipage (I'm pretty sure it exists. Practically every game has one). Of course, a zombie apocalypse survival manual (I personally recommend "The Zombie Survival Guide" by Max Brooks) can also be of assistance.
The 2015 roadmap for DayZ is centered mostly around gameplay expansion like vehicles and basic construction.
A lot of navigational signs in the game are written in Cyrillic (Russian). A map has names in English, so either try to crudely match the map text to the sign text or use something like Google Translate to figure it out.
Overall: 8 out of 10

The idea behind rust is to survive as long as possible in a world where, for the most part, everyone kills you on sight. You start off with a rock and make your way up the food chain, acquiring new weapons ranging from spears to crossbows and ultimately the highly saught after automatic rifles and rocket launchers. You'll then learn the proper way to build a hard to raid base, only to get raided while you're offline. You'll get frustrated, and come back and look to rebuild and learn from your mistakes. You'll learn that trust is hard to come by and that seemingly friendly person jumping up and down on the horizon will almost certainly pull out a gun and kill you when you get closer to them. The devs release new updates every Thursday, so the game is constantly changing which makes me wonder if it'll ever make it out of Alpha. All in all this game is great so far, but could use a little optimization, but that'll surely get worked out as the game approaches Beta.
