Pros:
large play area
good variety of items
PvP
realistic: bullet drop, attacks damage clothes and items, may find loot in odd places (I found a pen in a barn-twice!) etc.
Currently cheap pricing (probably will be $60 when it is released as a full version, so buying it now will save you 25 bucks)
Cons:
loot is stuck in an object or otherwise unreachable (example being that I couldn't pick up a gun right in front of me even though it was at arm's reach because I was too fat to wedge myself through the stairs it was under)
zombie spawning is a bit derpy (spent 6 seconds investigating the roof of a stand for loot only to discover a zombie had spawned right at the bottom of the ladder I was on. It then tore up my shirt)
Issues other people have:
Zombie density: Chernarus (the game's setting) used to be part of the USSR before becoming an independent power in 1991. Therefore, its population density (and zombie density) should be low, and since zombies will follow potential prey for thousands of miles, many zombies may have been led out of Chernarus by aircraft and such.
Hackers: I have never seen a hacker in this game. I don't know how common they actually are, but the developers have apparently released an update to combat hackers.
Fall damage: worse than Skyrim. The fact that you can fall about 5 feet and ruin your shoes AND hurt your leg until you inject some morphine is ridiculous. I think that the mechanic should have a severity level instead, like for instance you sprain an ankle and your shoes take minor damage from a two meter fall, or your shoes drop one quality level and your leg breaks from a five meter fall.
Zombie aggro radius: A zombie can see a glowing cigarette butt from two to three miles away in the dark. All their senses are gearing towards one thing: finding food and eating food. The fact that they don't react to footsteps or doors opening/closing actually sort of annoys me, but then again, my favorite type of zombies are the old-time Romero ones.
Bugs:
Zombies will phase through doors and such. Only a little annoying since their hitbox usually travels with them, so they can be easily killed.
A glitch I suffer from (but not others, apparently) is that text will be broken and almost unreadable. This makes it very hard to decipher chat messages and status effects and impossible to determine amounts in the inventory withou the "inspect" option. A similar glitch happens with inventory icons, so I sometimes mistake one item for another. I have no idea why this happens, especially since I use a gaming computer and should have excellent graphics.
Recently, I've noticed a bug where the character will move in a random and jerky manner, with a tendency to try to affix themself to one spot and look in a certain direction whilst twitching erratically. Only known fix is to wait a few minutes for it to stop, but it makes combat impossible.
Other notes:
Knowledge is power. A veteran of DayZ can help you become one too, or visit the wikipage (I'm pretty sure it exists. Practically every game has one). Of course, a zombie apocalypse survival manual (I personally recommend "The Zombie Survival Guide" by Max Brooks) can also be of assistance.
The 2015 roadmap for DayZ is centered mostly around gameplay expansion like vehicles and basic construction.
A lot of navigational signs in the game are written in Cyrillic (Russian). A map has names in English, so either try to crudely match the map text to the sign text or use something like Google Translate to figure it out.
Overall: 8 out of 10

firstly, i will say the things i didnt like about the game, because its like a couple sentences, then the rest will be everything i absolutly adore about this game
my only problem with this game was the map designs, not the background mind you, or the atmosphere, just, the level design was kinda confusing to travel through mostly in the HOTLAND and the room after the HOTEL, traveling through them confused me slightly and i would have to backtrack a little through it to make sure i didnt miss anything, kinda taking me out of the experience of the game.
ok NOW ON TO WHY THIS GAME IS PROBABLY THE BEST GAME OF THIS YEAR
Story: the story is SOoooooooooooo beautiful and deep, making me long to play this game over and over again, but leaving me with enough of it to only want to play it once. this game had me in tears multiple times, my heart felt heavy with each interaction i had with the characters with multiple emotions. Lets not forget about the MULTIPLE story paths you can take, with which will DRASTICALLY change what happens in the game, and actually gives you ligitimately different story endings.
Characters: the characters in this game are real, i cant describe it any more than that. its hard to do that, to make me believe characters are real in a game. NOT ONLY did this game do that, they got me to believe these characters were real from the FIRST FEW INTERACTIONS you have with them. i fell in love with all of them, and after i finished the game i had a deep longing in my chest, i realized that i missed the characters after i finished the games, i wanted to talk with them more, and i wish they were in our world irl.
Gameplay: This game blew my mind with its ability to not only take an old way of playing RPG games and making it interesting, but to also keep the experience fresh with EACH INTERACTION YOU HAVE with any enemy. not ONCE did i get bored "fighting" against my enemies, and every interaction had me feeling a certain way afterwards
Soundtrack/Atmosphere: this games music. is. THE. HOW I FELT FINISHING THE GAME: all the emotions...
i didnt want to leave, it hurt my heart puting the game down, and i sat in my chair and cried a little. it felt like i was leaving my close friends, but i was happy i was able to meet them, and experience their life together. i feel like i grew as a person after this game. gained a new perspective in life, and i think my life will forever be different now that i have played this game, different in a good way.
PLAY THIS GAME IF YOU HAVENT ALREADY

I read a review which said "if you have 10 bucks to spare, buy this game. You won't be disappointed." I had 10 bucks to spare, bought this game and wasn't disappointed.
Another great example that shows graphics aren't everything. If you're able to immerse yourself in an emotional story told via textboxes and pixelanimation, this could be right up your alley. Though lacking in difficulty, it pulls you right into its world by cleverly bringing the memorable characters and their world to life, while forcing you to reflect on some gameplay habits in general. Thus not only your protagonist, but also you, as the player, are part of the story. The unconventional fighting system is accompanied by some catchy soundtracks that might force you to drag out some fights just to keep listening.
To sum it up: you either like Undertale's style or you don't, but I'm glad I didn't miss out on the experience.

firstly, i will say the things i didnt like about the game, because its like a couple sentences, then the rest will be everything i absolutly adore about this game
my only problem with this game was the map designs, not the background mind you, or the atmosphere, just, the level design was kinda confusing to travel through mostly in the HOTLAND and the room after the HOTEL, traveling through them confused me slightly and i would have to backtrack a little through it to make sure i didnt miss anything, kinda taking me out of the experience of the game.
ok NOW ON TO WHY THIS GAME IS PROBABLY THE BEST GAME OF THIS YEAR
Story: the story is SOoooooooooooo beautiful and deep, making me long to play this game over and over again, but leaving me with enough of it to only want to play it once. this game had me in tears multiple times, my heart felt heavy with each interaction i had with the characters with multiple emotions. Lets not forget about the MULTIPLE story paths you can take, with which will DRASTICALLY change what happens in the game, and actually gives you ligitimately different story endings.
Characters: the characters in this game are real, i cant describe it any more than that. its hard to do that, to make me believe characters are real in a game. NOT ONLY did this game do that, they got me to believe these characters were real from the FIRST FEW INTERACTIONS you have with them. i fell in love with all of them, and after i finished the game i had a deep longing in my chest, i realized that i missed the characters after i finished the games, i wanted to talk with them more, and i wish they were in our world irl.
Gameplay: This game blew my mind with its ability to not only take an old way of playing RPG games and making it interesting, but to also keep the experience fresh with EACH INTERACTION YOU HAVE with any enemy. not ONCE did i get bored "fighting" against my enemies, and every interaction had me feeling a certain way afterwards
Soundtrack/Atmosphere: this games music. is. THE. BEST! just added to the story and interactions, and made the WORLD feel epic, regardless of what actions you take in the game. the Atmosphere that the music creates along with the art style that was chosen made the world seem surreal. together the world was a work of art, regardless of what you think about pixel art. even the designs of the characters were fantastic and fitting to the world around.
HOW I FELT FINISHING THE GAME: all the emotions...
i didnt want to leave, it hurt my heart puting the game down, and i sat in my chair and cried a little. it felt like i was leaving my close friends, but i was happy i was able to meet them, and experience their life together. i feel like i grew as a person after this game. gained a new perspective in life, and i think my life will forever be different now that i have played this game, different in a good way.
PLAY THIS GAME IF YOU HAVENT ALREADY

I honestly wanted to like this game and I still have high hopes for it. The biggest problem I have right now is that you can't really play with your friends very easily. I spent 2 hours trying to find my friends only to come across sparce zombies I could not hit, starvation, dehydration, and hats (I found 20 hats under a boat, loved it). I was dissappointed because in the description it says you can team up with friends, but I could never find my friends. I feel bad that the updates are focusing more on polishing, rather than playability. I feel this standalone has so much potiential and I am very excited to see what becomes of it. The upcoming updates to server issues and hacking is very exciting and they are handling it well.
Here's what I like about DayZ:
+The World is amazing and the map is Huge
+The graphics are awesome
+Their is a learning curve, like drying out your clothes or tearing your shirt to make a bandage
+Realism - Limited inventory, squishy (Yes, your not invulnerable), and you get damp from water
What I don't like:
-The map is too huge and no way to travel "Easily" or find friends
-You starve/dehydrate to easily
-There is not enough things to interact with
-The zombies are meh (Although they will be better later I'm sure)
Overall this game has great potiential and I hope it turns out. For $35, I can only hope things progress smoothly, even if it takes awhile. I am down-voting because the playablility has potiential, but right now I am not seeing the direction and the "catch" from the game that amazing games have. Once this game surpasses that of the Arma II mod, I will certainly be back to change my point of view.

The premise is good, the implementation is horrible. As the entire game is build on a old and bad engine, I feel it will never be fixed, it will always just leave you wanting it to be better.

1. The player must always be aware how close they are to being a terrible person
2. There must be many ways to approach one goal in the entire game
3. The controls must be tight and responsive enough for the player to have agency in the gameplay
Undertale does all three things very well: each guard has a homosexual relationship with the other, the levels are open-ended and full of pointless puzzles, and the player is of ambiguous gender/age and fun to control.

YES, IT IS AN ALPHA AND I AM AWARE OF THAT.
It's annoying enough to need to click "I understand" twice when starting the game.
I played the mod before this and I've been with the standalone for a few months now, I have a few problems with the design in general.
Firstly it's an open world game meant to be very realistic, like you yourself are the character. This is shown by having no global chat, a walkie-talkie if you look hard enough, and some servers restricting you to first person view.
My problem with this is that because the environment is a very competitive free for all, you as an individual are completely hopeless unless you spend hours looking for a trustworthy companion, and hope they don't stab you in the back. This could be solved by inserting a kind of "Looking for Group" tab before joining a server, along with public character stats to show you how many kills these characters have had so that you may decide for yourself whether or not they'll be trustworthy.
Sure you could argue that you could play with friends, or sign up for a forum somewhere. But that would be completely against the "very realistic" part wouldn't it? Taking someone out of the game in order to play the game to the best experience possible I'm absolutely against. This kind of thing is also seen in games that REQUIRE you to look up information online (mostly a wiki) in order to progress or gain specific knowledge that is UNAVAILABLE in the game.
Melee combat is ridiculous in DayZ. What do you expect going into combat with another player, hand to hand? You face each other, approach head on, and take a few steps back before rushing at them for another punch.
Melee combat works like two blobs orbiting each other and occasionally bashing in the middle before continuing to  circle. I'd suspect this is mostly because swinging a weapon in DayZ swings it the same every time: one arc that doesn't necessarily land where your cursor is pointing. This makes first person combat ridiculous, but that's a very tricky thing to pull off in general. Not only are you dealing with some arbitrary "my weapon is swinging, I'm going to try to bump into you and hope a swing hits" sort of issue, there's also the desync. Desync sucks. I haven't personally had any issues with ranged combat in regards to it, but with players circling around and bashing heads, I've been floored. Even when well prepared for combat, which brings me into this point...
Press a button to take out your hatchet and kill that zombie chasing you? Might work, might not. Want to eat that can of food in your inventory? Might take a few tries, few clicks, might need to walk around and do something else and come back to it. Oh you found a great gun? Try to pick it up for 3 minutes all the while hoping the server isn't restarting, but oh, now it works. Did you do something different the 30th time trying to pick it up? Nope. These issues happen in every action you try to make, I'm not sure if it's a server thing, but I've been on many many many different servers and the same issue persists. DayZ is about scouring a massive world, looking for loot and company to survive. It fails at it's main premise as of 2/6/15.
I don't think they'll ever salvage the melee combat issue, but I do think adding a method to make community would greatly improve the game for players like myself. It's a nice idea to think you can start a camp with a a few players, but even cooler to start a little community that "owns" a village, with people taking up certain responsibilities to provide for it. In DayZ's current state, your life is always a very short spark, either you get shot trying to communicate sanely with another person, or you spend hours looking for all the best loot, then quit in a rage because you're sick of this game not being really what you'd signed up for. I'll check in next year.
Disclaimer: I'm not saying I don't enjoy the state of free-for-all that is DayZ, I'm just saying how it's implemented encourages the worst kinds of people to play, making it impossible to enjoy any player interaction besides putting a bullet in their heads.

DayZ SA EARLY ACCESS.
I hear so many people slating this game, "To many hackers", "I get cold, I die", "To many bugs ", "It should be finished by now" etc. etc. etc.
Some of these things are true but nowhere near as bad as some people make out. I've played nearly 600hrs and only been aware of two hackers (1x Unlimited round mag. very early on and 1x guy teleporting etc).
Yes the game has its bugs and they can be annoying but bear in mind this is not a finished game, hell its not even a Beta yet, It is work in progress.
The trouble with most people is that they are impatient, they want the game finished yesterday. They also expect certain things to be "Fixed" in game fairly quickly. If this was a finished game and you was expecting a patch to fix game problems then that would be fair enough. But its NOT, the Dev's are not going to fix something that may or may not change at a later stage anyway. They have a road map of what's going to get done and when and from what I see they appear pretty much on schedule.
This game is getting better and better each month of development and there are not many games that can give you the rollercoaster of emotions that this one does from the "excitement of your first battle with another player (Usually ending up with someone dying). To having to go change your under wear due to a sudden crack of lightening putting the S#@t's up you.
This game has a LOT of potential, at the moment it still has a few problems (To be expected) but nothing that shouldn't stop you from having hours of fun and when it's finished it will be amazing.
*** UPDATE (30/03/2017)***
I currently see most people are putting negative reviews against DayZ, Mostly because they believe that the current "Development build" that everyone plays (0.61 at the moment) is the current state of DayZ, This is actually incorrect the Devs have actually created a whole lot of content internally that no one gets to see yet as it is waiting for new animation systems and other key game engine components etc to be updated.
This creates the false impression that the game is slow in development (Most games average 5 years) and that it is lacking a lot of content and that no progress has been made. The next couple of patches especially 0.63 (Beta) should see some major changes as the old Arma2 mod content is removed and replaced with the new core components allowing all the new content to be implemented.
Ok currently 0.61 can become a bit tiresome if you have been playing DayZ for a while, but I still believe that it is a game worth buying, Everything appears to be on track (If a little behind schedule) to be one amazing game, Especially once the new mod tools are released (Much more powerful than the ones in the Arma2 mod.)

This is hand-down one of the greatest games I've played in a number of years. I would strongly recommend it to just about anyone. Its not often you get a game that just consumes your mind, but this game did it for me. Please play this game.

The game may be an RPG, but it heavily deconstructs the RPG genre and you'll, at most, be mocked at for trying to treat the game like a typical RPG. Battles use "bullet hell"-esque segments to help you avoid attacks from enemies, but this sort of thing may not be for everyone and I wasn't a fan of it at first. Using certain acts in battle can give you all sorts of effects on enemies and some can help you even win a fight without needing to kill anyone! There is no "wrong" or "right" way to play this game, so you can easily play how you want to.
The story and characters are simple, yet deep at the same time and you get to learn so much about them whether you want to play nice or play nasty and the results go far beyond a simple dialogue change. Even repeated playthroughs can be a bit different based on what you did last time and the game WILL know of your shenanigans if you try to beat the system. The music, which has a good variety and blends, helps bring the story and characters to life and is something I think is worth listening to once you're done with the game.
Give the game a try. You won't regret it. The bullet hell mechanics may not be everyone's cup of tea and the simple story and characters is also left up to individual taste, so wait for a sale if those things are making you iffy on wanting to try the game.

6 hours in and I can already tell that this game was a good use of my money.
Right from the get-go, I liked it. I have a soft spot for good stealth games, and this game set off on the right foot by following my 3 basic rules for making a decent stealth game:
1. The player must always be aware how close they are to being a terrible person
2. There must be many ways to approach one goal in the entire game
3. The controls must be tight and responsive enough for the player to have agency in the gameplay
Undertale does all three things very well: each guard has a homosexual relationship with the other, the levels are open-ended and full of pointless puzzles, and the player is of ambiguous gender/age and fun to control.
A good buy, even when not on sale. When it does go on sale, buy four copies and have fun testing your sanity!

The servers used to die after a day, 2 at most; but now after the blueprint update I see servers lasting up to 5 days, which might not seem like a long time.. but it IS. Going back to the blueprint update; it really increased this games value for me. Before you'd see people with AK 47's 3 hours into wipe, now it takes a few days. The update doesn't make the game any easier or more fair to solo players, however I dont think there is a solution that would make solo players able to compete against zergs. Speaking about zergs; there are a TON of them. Zergs are groups of players that rely on numbers more than skill. AKA a group of 15 players. Seeing as this is one of the only downfalls of Rust, and it is something Devs can't control as of now at least, i'd say this game is amazing. Another negative of Rust is the grind; however after the node mini-game update, farming (Nodes) has gotten a lot more enjoyable. Sadly farming for wood is still extremely lackluster, I trust the devs are working on a solution. As with almost every game, Rust is way way way more fun with friends; and to get the full rust experience i'd highly suggest either getting some friends to play with or playing with your currently existing friends. After 1000+ hours of Rust I am STILL learning about new things. Whether its a cool way to build a base, a new base design, a cool thing you can do at a rad town, or new raiding tactics; Rust is FULL of content. Rust on the surface might seem repetative and dull, however with friends or sometimes even solo, every wipe is a new experience. I'd highly reccomend picking up this game!

It may be pessimistic, but the more this tragicomedy goes on the more DayZ looks like an abandoned ship slowly sinking to me. A ship on which one dude and one dude only is there to try and save it, but for some reason only cleans the floor instead of taking a bucket and splashing some water out. Metaphores apart, there are few, major reasons i do not recommend this game, and i'll express them here. As my usual, there goes a pros/cons list of what's good and what's not in this game.
PS
You know, i've tried to write my fully extended thoughts about this game, but i've reached space limits. So here's the extremely short pros/cons situation:
PROS
-The feelings survival gives you are awesome
-The game mechanics are generally well thought and immersive
-Nice atmosphere, as depressed as a post-apocalyptic world can be
-Playing with one or more friends is amazing
-The graphics do their dirty job in creating nice landscapes and a vast, desolate, decaying environment
CONS
-The developers are taking too damn long, being sinnable for lazyness, terrible priorities (lackluster content over game engine improvements and bugfixing) and possibly for having lost the momentum of this game (when is this going Gold again? 2050s? I doubt it will be interesting anymore)
-The bugs. This entry alone chew up so much space. There are just too many in the original version. They're just billions, and they're 100% game breaking most of the time. Mostly clipping, lagging, zombies ignoring gravity and solid materials, broken things and terrible collision/hitboxes (more on that later), and also terrible texture loading problems, which leads to...
-...optimization. There is none. Game doesn't even "run", it slowly crawls around. Situation in cities is extra abysmal, but even empty spaces are subject to lag spikes caused by broken texture loading.
-Hitboxes are broken. Players are already terrible in that sense, but zombies are astonishing, capable of hitting you from impossible angles and distance and not registering clearly direct hits from point blank.
-Controls are sluggish and more often than not take multiple button smashing to register.
-UI is a ♥♥♥♥ing mess, as little as there is.
-The players community is so rotten it's not even worth considering it a community. No matter how you play: 99% of chance of being killed on sight if you meet someone is guaranteed. If he hasn't a weapon, he will then proceed to run away like crazy and maybe ambush you with his axe or whatever, because obviously he thinks you are going to kill him. Farewell, teamwork between strangers, it's been nice knowing you. Now it's kill or be killed.
-The zombies, hitboxes apart, pose no threat. They are incredibly scarce in numbers, and can be easily taken care of. Where are the hordes roaming in the cities?! Where are their massive numbers that should freeze one's blood at the thought of being chased by them? Nowhere, that's where. Players are your only threat, because if you don't have anything to team up for (like, you guessed it, an actual zombie menace), you will most definately start shooting each other for the sake of doing it. Sigh...
-Moving around is painful on foot, but i wonder how much more unbalance could more vehicles bring to this atrocity.
So please, since this game isn't cheap at all, don't feed the developer with more money they will waste on not improving this train wreck, and spare yourself the experience of one emotion-filled moment every 3 hours of cursing caused by the amount of broken stuff this thing has.

This is a unique game, indeed. The tale begins when a human child falls into the monster world below the surface of the human world. The (genderless) human child is controlled by the player. As one finds out, most monsters are not evil. However, there is one that is truly disturbing, but will you defeat him or join him?
As the player, you can decide to achieve either the "neutral" ending, "good" ending, or "bad" ending.
For the neutral ending, it's easy to get. In fact, it's required to get before you get the good or bad ending.
For the good ending,  you must never kill anyone. Show mercy, be nice. More importantly, be kind. Make friends.
For the bad ending, you must show no mercy and kill every single monster you encounter. You must kill those who would have been your friends on a different path.
Warning: Go for the good ending before the bad ending. ... Also, if you do go for the bad ending, be prepared for some serious guilt-tripping. I, personally, couldn't go through with it due to a strong conscience, even though I know it's just a game.
If you have trouble getting through the game, especially with the final bosses of the neutral ending and bad ending, there's always the Cheat Engine.
"This was more difficult than Dark Souls," <<< Direct quote from someone who's played Dark Souls and Undertale, referring to some bosses. So, don't feel bad if you can't get through the bosses.
I recommend this game to anyone that likes interesting indie games ... and perhaps heart-warming stories that result from being a good person.

A surprisingly short game that packs in a lot of character and personality into it's narrative, and it's the only RPG game I know of that offers pacifism as a legitament route in the game.
The game doesn't have much in the way of gameplay. There isn't really any stats to increase (with the exception of two), spells to learn, or character customization to speak of, which is unusual for an RPG game. It's also incredibly linear, and at best, the puzzles are child's play. However, this doesn't seem to take away from the game very much. The story is fun, humourous, and at times, a little terrifying. The most important aspect of the game is that your choices do matter, and it shapes the story (in particular, the ending) quite a bit.
I'd say it's worth your 10 bucks.

Some things I really like about this game:
- The game mechanic, especially in fights, is actually used to inform about the characters and tell the story in really creative ways. More games should do this! It's the opposite of quick time events.
- The music.
- The characters and comedy. I actually laughed out loud when playing this - which I rarely ever do when playing something alone.
- The story. Some stuff happened that really surprised me, and I think I probably went through all base emotions at least once.
- Gameplay is really fun! For me it was also very hard. I especially liked the bosses.
- It had more replayability for me than I first guessed. You can play it in vey different play styles. And also: Do you know movies you liked so much that you went in cinema to see them twice? I actually replayed the same play style twice with like, a week pause between, and really enjoyed myself a second time. That's really rare for me. I think it's the comedy that did it for me.
I went into this game nearly unspoiled, only knowing from a review that it's supposed to be good, and I'm very grateful for that. You should try to avoid spoilers as much as possible.
As for what I didn't like: well, nothing really comes to mind. I think you need some basic knowledge about video games and internet popculture to get by no means all, but still some of the jokes (for example: for some jokes you would need to know what a "tsundere" is to get them). Also I'd really like to have a run button. And a reset button for my brain so I can play this for the first time again.

Story-centric RPGs became my favorite type of game ever since I played Chrono Trigger on the DS. In my mind, the perfect game is one with lots of character or style, and gameplay that does at least something new, and if it lacks in one it makes up for it in the other. Undertale balances both very, very well, making it perhaps the most progressive traditional RPG of this decade. It's not perfect, and it's relatively short, but I think you might be hard-pressed to find a modern RPG with this much going for it. Don't spoil yourself like I did.
A fair warning though, there are some homo-affectionate characters. Given my political background, I'm personally not bothered too much if they're written well and aren't too in-your-face about it, which is DEFINITELY true. It also gets touchy with references to generic spiritual topics and symbols, such as an enemy that attacks with crosses. If you aren't fond of those things then that's at minimum TWO things that're gonna leave a bad taste in your mouth. I think the rest of the game will make up for it for you.
If you like RPGs, play it! If you don't like RPGs, still play it! Definitely play with a controller or arcade stick, though.

To put it simply, I thought this was just another game that people overhyped. Another indie game that people took under their wing and made it bigger than it is. It wasn't until I decided to look up a playthrough on YouTube that I realized how wrong my assumptions were.
The game itself is a real treat, incorporating not only the basic fighting mechanics of any RPG, but also giving you the option to resolve most fights by not attcking the 'enemy' at all. This causes the choices you make in battle, who you kill and who you don't, matter. Towards the 'end' of the game, the game tells you about your previous actions. You could be guilt tripped into not killing the final boss if you went about the game like a normal RPG. You are treated like a monster, a true, homicidal monster, if you killed everyone(and I do mean everyone) in your path. You are treated with love if you spared everyone, and never hurt a soul.
You would think that as soon as you finish one playthrough, you can reset the game, and everything is dandy, and you can go on ahead and do the other routes. You'd be wrong.
The game remembers every single choice you make. If you chose to go through the Genocide Route first and then decide to take the Pacifist Route after you feel horrible for you actions, you can't get the true, good ending. It's impossible. The game remembers your actions, how you killed everyone, and does not let you be comforted in the end.
But, the game features more than just battle mechanics and keeping track of choices. The game also has the following(and much more):
I rarely get incredibly emotional over games, and can count the times that I have been brought to tears on one hand, but Undertale just... wraps you up, makes you care, makes you feel the consequences of your actions. And even if those actions were benevolent and 'right', you still feel emotional. You're rewarded with seeing how your hard work affected the characters in the true ending. Even before that, when you're facing the true final boss, you're playing with this amped up version of a song that played at the beginning of the game, and it makes you realize that,
, this is what you've been playing towards, so do your best. And frankly, towards the end of it, I was brought to tears. I felt
for the antagonist of the game. Not a lot of games can do that, but Undertale can.
If you want to play a unique game, or want to treat yourself to an incredible experience, I would recommend this game.

Story-centric RPGs became my favorite type of game ever since I played Chrono Trigger on the DS. In my mind, the perfect game is one with lots of character or style, and gameplay that does at least something new, and if it lacks in one it makes up for it in the other. Undertale balances both very, very well, making it perhaps the most progressive traditional RPG of this decade. It's not perfect, and it's relatively short, but I think you might be hard-pressed to find a modern RPG with this much going for it. Don't spoil yourself like I did.
A fair warning though, there are some homo-affectionate characters. Given my political background, I'm personally not bothered too much if they're written well and aren't too in-your-face about it, which is DEFINITELY true. It also gets touchy with references to generic spiritual topics and symbols, such as an enemy that attacks with crosses. If you aren't fond of those things then that's at minimum TWO things that're gonna leave a bad taste in your mouth. I think the rest of the game will make up for it for you.
If you like RPGs, play it! If you don't like RPGs, still play it! Definitely play with a controller or arcade stick, though.

Wow, my chance to write a DayZ review. I'm probably not worthy but here it goes.
If you haven't played, it's got a steep learning curve. Once you play for a while you will find where to get loot. To put it simply, I thought this was just another game that people overhyped. Another indie game that people took under their wing and made it bigger than it is. It wasn't until I decided to look up a playthrough on YouTube that I realized how wrong my assumptions were.
The game itself is a real treat, incorporating not only the basic fighting mechanics of any RPG, but also giving you the option to resolve most fights by not attcking the 'enemy' at all. This causes the choices you make in battle, who you kill and who you don't, matter. Towards the 'end' of the game, the game tells you about your previous actions. You could be guilt tripped into not killing the final boss if you went about the game like a normal RPG. You are treated like a monster, a true, homicidal monster, if you killed everyone(and I do mean everyone) in your path. You are treated with love if you spared everyone, and never hurt a soul.
You would think that as soon as you finish one playthrough, you can reset the game, and everything is dandy, and you can go on ahead and do the other routes. You'd be wrong.
The game remembers every single choice you make. If you chose to go through the Genocide Route first and then decide to take the Pacifist Route after you feel horrible for you actions, you can't get the true, good ending. It's impossible. The game remembers your actions, how you killed everyone, and does not let you be comforted in the end.
But, the game features more than just battle mechanics and keeping track of choices. The game also has the following(and much more):
I rarely get incredibly emotional over games, and can count the times that I have been brought to tears on one hand, but Undertale just... wraps you up, makes you care, makes you feel the consequences of your actions. And even if those actions were benevolent and 'right', you still feel emotional. You're rewarded with seeing how your hard work affected the characters in the true ending. Even before that, when you're facing the true final boss, you're playing with this amped up version of a song that played at the beginning of the game, and it makes you realize that,
, this is what you've been playing towards, so do your best. And frankly, towards the end of it, I was brought to tears. I felt
for the antagonist of the game. Not a lot of games can do that, but Undertale can.
If you want to play a unique game, or want to treat yourself to an incredible experience, I would recommend this game.

This game. THIS GAME. I thought I had lost my interest in games, but it turns out that there has actually been a steady decline in the quality of games over the years. Or rather that games fail to do anything new or interesting these days.
But this game. This game is different. Toby Fox has put and endless amount of love into Undertale, so much so that it brims with personality and charm. Everything that makes a game good is here in full force. Gameplay? Check. Story? Super check. Humour? Hell yes. Character development? Hell check! Great soundtrack? Check yes! Elements that challenge you emotionally and make you question everything you know about life and video games? Super hell check yes. Graphics? Well ... no, but that just means you get to use your imagination more, and it's not a super big deal because the graphics fit with the style of the game.
The game play of Undertale is pretty straight forward, with some twists. You move your character around like any other top down, 2D RPG. But when you battle enemies, you move your "soul" (a red heart) around a little box in order to avoid attacks, and you attack by pressing the attack button when a line gets to the middle of the screen. The official description of the battle system is that the combat is turn based, but it's really not.
You "take turns" in the sense that when you're attacking, the enemy is not attacking you, and when they attack, you can't attack. However, when you're being attacked, you can dodge any attack as long as you have enough skill to dodge the incoming projectiles. People have likened this defence phase to a bullet hell shooter, but that doesn't really do it justice. It also gets changed up a bit throughout the game, so it never gets repetitive.
But the story and characters is where this game shines the most. Each character has a personality that is brought to life with a combination of their font, quirks, speed of text, and Toby's excellent writing. The story is amazing, but I can't say anything much since it is very spoil-able. Just know that there are many laughs, cries, WTFs and adventures to be had.
All of the choices you make are remembered, whether you want them to be or not. I'll let that cryptic piece of information linger in your brain. It'll make sense when you experience it. Every single possible thing you could do is planned for and has dialogue or characters that make it very apparent of what you did. When you realize this, it will seem as if the game is some sort of entity that is watching you and judging your every move.
If you don't like RPGs you'll love this game. If you do like RPGs, you'll love this game. If you have any semblance of ever maybe liking a game, you'll love this game. Just buy it already.

What can I say about Rust that hasn't already been said? The game is fun, I can't stress that enough. It's the most fun Sandbox Survival game on the market (in my opinion) But the game has many flaws.

What's to say about Undertale that hasn't already been said? It's awesome. I was expecting it to be a kitschy Earthbound clone, and while it certainly takes a few pages out of Shigesato Itoi's book, what I ended up with was something far greater that completely blew away my expectations. The combat breathes new life into the tried-and-true turn-based formula by adding a dodging mechanic where you have to avoid your enemy's attacks, just like in a bullet hell shoot-'em-up. This makes Undertale more of a skill-based RPG than a stat-based one- you can have the strongest weapon in the whole game, but it's not gonna make a difference if you can't dodge bullets.
But that's not to say that you even have to use weapons to begin with- Undertale also allows you to talk to your enemies and befriend them. Doing so will let you spare them, because monsters are people too! While this isn't new for RPGs either- the Megami Tensei series has been doing it since 1987- Undertale takes it a step further by giving you the option to befriend and spare EVERY enemy in the game, even the bosses. The moral dichotomy between killing and pacifism plays into the story of the game, as the story will be influenced by your actions in battle. You can go the pacifist route and play through the whole game without killing anyone, or you can commit genocide against the entire underworld, and the difference in plot events between both of those routes is like night and day.
But this game and its characters are so saccharine-sweet that entertaining the thought of a genocide run almost seems inhumane. I won't say too much about the plot, because the less you know, the better, but it's great. It also has a sense of brevity that few RPGs have matched- it can be completed in about 6-7 hours, and while that might seem short, it makes it easy to replay the game over and over.
Undertale is one of the most bizarre, quirky and unique games you'll probably ever play, and at only $10, it's absolutely worth your time and money.

So, Undertale. Probably the biggest Indie surprise of 2015. Has a record high-score on Metacritic. And you know, it's not BAD or anything. The characters are interesting and delightful, the world is vibrant, the art is simple but lovely. The game tracks a surprising number of little things and comments on them later, which makes the world feel much more alive. (Example - If you buy and equip an armor upgrade before fighting the first real boss, he'll comment about it later.)
But the game gets VERY meta as you go along, with the mute-ness of your protagonist becoming increasingly chafing and with storyline getting lost in bringing in game mechanics as story elements near the end, in a very unsatisfying way. Which is unfortunate, because it means that an excellent game the whole way along left me with a REAL bad taste in my mouth. This is doubly true if you get anything except the best ending. (Which I didn't, Because I told a dinosaur lady I didn't want to watch anime with her.)
All in all, still glad I played it. It's worth playing. But... Maybe wait for a sale.

So, Undertale. Probably the biggest Indie surprise of 2015. Has a record high-score on Metacritic. And you know, it's not BAD or anything. The characters are interesting and delightful, the world is vibrant, the art is simple but lovely. The game tracks a surprising number of little things and comments on them later, which makes the world feel much more alive. (Example - If you buy and equip an armor upgrade before fighting the first real boss, he'll comment about it later.)
But the game gets VERY meta as you go along, with the mute-ness of your protagonist becoming increasingly chafing and with storyline getting lost in bringing in game mechanics as story elements near the end, in a very unsatisfying way. Which is unfortunate, because it means that an excellent game the whole way along left me with a REAL bad taste in my mouth. This is doubly true if you get anything except the best ending. (Which I didn't, Because I told a dinosaur lady I didn't want to watch anime with her.)
All in all, still glad I played it. It's worth playing. But... Maybe wait for a sale.

As in all those other survival game clones, you spawn with nothing, collect resources, build tools, a house and start raiding other players in the long run. There's a new content update every week that always renews the game and keeps it fresh. Game gets boring? Just come back in a month to discover a whole lot of new stuff!
Seriously this is one of the very few Early Access games I would recommend without a second thought. I believe it to be a save bet for the future of it's development.

Like most of you, I found out about this game through the Fandom, and was told this was the "Best game Ever". Ya know, like most games are touted to be by fans. But, with the large popularity, The fact it was an RPG, and Muffet's theme being Awesome, I decided to check it out, puting all hype out of my mind. and that's the best way to play this game, honestly, just push the Hype out of your mind, and Enjoy. Because that's what undertale is: an enjoyable and memberable Experience, in a Mysterious new world, where your choices matter, and you can Befreind all the colorful characters you meet along the way.
Alternitivly, you can Kill them all. All of them. Every last one.
If that's all you need, then Buy this game. I'll go a little more indepth below.
And by 'indepth", I mean fangirling and Hypeing the hell out of it. so, if you dont want more Hype, leave now, and just buy the damn game already.
1. Music.
It's the best Ive heard in a game Ever. No other game has gotten me to listen to over 30 of it's tracts Reguarly IRL.
Not to mention what we like to call "Toby's Mother ♥♥♥♥ing Motifs"
Why do we call it that?
because every song is connected to another song in one way or another. Even ones you would think had NO Connection what so ever
*Stares intently and "But nobody came"*
2. Gameplay
As you may have heard, Undertale is a Turn based RPG, so Gameplay is split up into two segments:
The Overworld
and
The Combatworld
Overworld: Undertale takes full advantage of it's Pixel art syle, and it's wide range of color to create Among the most beautiful enviroments Ive ever seen in a game, but other then a few nice tricks, it's the only part of the game that's Typical in an RPG.
Combatworld: Notice I said world, because, as you may have heard, it's not a typical RPG battle format, but insted, a semi-Bullethell/Platformer/Puzzle/QTE, If that makes any sense. Attacking is usually just Timing your button press right on a bar slider, but Dodging is where the other 3 parts come in. The game establishes certain rules for the combat box in the beguining. These rules are broken by the time you reach the first boss. Each enemy has a unique pattern of attack, each with their own ways to dodge, or take reduced damage from. Every boss completely changes the way that the battle plays out in one way or another. Even a few non-boss fights can do this.
3. Puzzles
the Puzzles are mostly there for a laugh, or to plesently extend game time, and they do succeed at that. There is only one puzzle, about 3/4 the way through the game, that will challenge you, and I will say no spoilers here about it.
4. Characters
I cant say much about the characters without spoiling the whole game, but I will say that even the lowley exposition NPCs get more personality then some Side, or even Main characters in other games. And the Alternate endings are to dies for, While not being tedius to get most of them.
5. Writing
It's Comedic Gold when it wants, and can switch on a dime to Bloody Heartbreaking.
3. Puzzles
Alternitivly, there is a way to not do the puzzles at all. But i'm Not gonna tell you.
6. Conclusion
This Is now my favorite game of all time. thank you Toby, Temme, and everyone else, for makeing such a wonderful experience.
7. Why havent you bought the game yet?
Seriously, if not, and you can afford it, WHY?

While this game appears to be at first a throwback to classic RPG games, it is in all actuality a vessel for great storytelling wrapped up in a unique RPG experience.  What makes this game special is that the more you play and discover in your first playthrough, you will come to grow and love (or hate) the fully fleshed-out NPCs.

Not only does Undertale let you choose whether or no you will test your resolve for compassion towards the characters or take the easy way out and simply kill them. Another fantastic addition to this game is its soundtrack.  Never before have I played a game where I didn't dislike a single song from the entire OST.  My personal favorites are "Bonetrousle" and "Undertale".
However, my single gripe with this game is that I wish the main storyline was LONGER.  On my first playthrough it took me about 5 hours to complete it and I didn't even get the best ending.  After that, my two other playthroughs took me significantly less time because I had seen all the puzzles and dialogue before.  But, this is only my opinion.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Case in point, I higly recommend Undertale due to its combination of extremely lovable characters, excellent story telling aspects, and being an all around wonderfully emotional gaming experience amidst the filth of the current industry.

This game hardly needs another review, but I need to say my piece: I tried. I really tried not to fall absolutely in love with this game. I saw the fandom begin to bloom, slowly becoming acquainted with the concept of Undertale. I turned away. I already had so much on my plate, and was too into my other games and "fandoms." But, as good as this game was, it would hardly stay at bay forever, and finally a friend played it. After playing the game and falling in love themselves, they bought me a copy, and urged me to play it. I was hesitant. What could this game really offer? What if all the hype fell short? However, as I slowly begin to play the game, I found myself playing for longer and longer periods of time, until I finally beat the game. And as hard as I tried, I could not help but fall in love. The pixel work is fantastic, each route has great and affecting atmosphere, and the "battle" system was an absolute joy. One of my other friends said the only thing she wished was in the game was the opportunity to go back and spar with previous bosses during the pacifist route. I heartily agree! The story does such a good job of drawing you in, making you care, and then the ending... Even going into this game trying not to get pulled in, it happened regardless. I'm so glad for this game, and can say for sure, it's one of my top games of all time.

Undertale is a superb game.
It's gameplay is engaging, and while not the first in existence, it's one of the few examples of bullet hell mechanics implemented in an RPG. Thanks to this all the encounters feel novel and each enemy type is unique.
The spare or kill dichotomy around which the game is built makes the game interesting, and the central character conflict personally gripping.
The story is, simply put, heartwrenching, built upon a foundation of very rich lore and colorful characters. It's gripping and emotional, and has made me, and several other people cry.
And you can go on a date with a skeleton <3
Also, if you go genocide, you are a terrible person.

I have changed my recommendation to positive after revisiting this game.
While there are still an abundance of bandits who will kill on sight for no reason as soon as they find a gun and some ammo as there is almost no reason not to, most of the game breaking glitches have been fixed (zombies don't walk through walls anymore, animations are mostly fixed, to name a few) and the new icons and town are great. I also like the new zombie AI and how once they fall once they are dead for good. Melee combat is still a bit inconsistent, but it is better than before.
There are quite a few guns in the world now, and they are much easier to acquire. I found a gun in a bus stop once (I don't exactly know how I feel about this). For the most part it seems to be fine as ammo is still reasonably rare, especially for the gun you have (at one point I have at least 50 rounds of all bullets apart from the ones that my gun used). And the sword is great. I like the sword.
Recent updates have implemented a much larger crafting system to make things like backpacks and bows. Hunting is pretty fun, and needing cooking meat with a fireplace is a nice feature.
Now for a story:
I had super high-tier weapons and clothing, but died of dehydration cos I used my water bottle to make an improvised suppressor after pairing it with duct tape, which lasted 5 shots on my mosin before breaking.
TL;DR
Lots of bandits, melee isn't great, more guns in the world, sword is good, no bullets, decent crafting and hunting, water saves lives

Recommend this game to your enemies. If you play it with your friends, they'll soon be your enemies too.

I lost a good friend in this game. His name was John. We were on an adventure together getting geared up and finding food, We survived many encounters and fought off many zombies throughout our journey. But then one day, everything went wrong. My friend and I were in search for some people who had tried to kill us before. So as we were running through this big city, a group on bandits approached us and there was no way of getting out of this situation if we stayed. We made a run for it, hoping we'd  get behind the building on time and jet it, but little did we know there was another bandit sitting there with a shotgun. He shot my friend in the leg and shot me in the arm. I continued to run into the nearby forest and I yelled " I'll come back for you, I PROMISE! ".  A few seconds later I heard a gunshot as I ran into the forest. I couldn't get myself to look back at the horror of what just happened. I knew my friend was dead. The next few days were a blur. I found myself just sitting near the shore most of the time reminiscing about all the good times we had. I couldn't take the pain anymore so I went crazy. I took all my gear going from city to city killing anyone I saw. Then I came across a man. He had a helmet on, and it was foggy. We stared at eachother from a distance. I raised my pistol up at him, ready to shoot this guy in the neck when soon after I hear someone on the rooftop. I look up for just a second and see the guy in front of me with the corner of my eye make movement, so I quickly fired 5 rounds at his chest and ran for cover from the sniper. I then heard the sniper yell " JAY!! JAY!!!! ARE YOU OKAY!? ". Without hesitation I ran up into the building that the sniper was on and shot him in the leg like the bandits did to my friend, and stripped him of everything he had. I soon pulled my shotgun out and aimed it right and his head, and asked. " Any last words? ", and he said. " He gave me the signal to not shoot you, you... son of a ♥♥♥♥♥ ". As I stared at him and slowly put the gun down. I got close to him and said. " I trust no one ". I grabbed him by the vest and threw him off the roof. I soon go back downstairs to loot off the guy I shot 5 times in the chest. As I approach his body, I get a strange feeling. As I kneeled down, I slowly removed his helmet and I collapsed on the floor, my palms were sweaty. I Couldn't breath... I couldn't believe me eyes... It was... It was John.. It was ♥♥♥♥ING JOHN!

I really wanted to like this game. I played the Arma II mod and loved it but the standalone is far from being done. I understand that this game is still in alpha testing and the community is going to say "it's still in alpha" to justify this their cause in playing this terrible game. It's  sad to see a game with great potential fail because the developers are more interested in adding useless items to the game instead of fixing their current issues.
Before I go any further into this detailed review of DayZ I would like to state that, I am not the only one who has had this happen to them. Several people I play with and others I've talked to have experienced or still are encountering these issues.
I Bought DayZ over a year ago, and the only thing that has been fixed thus far is the zombies don't run through the walls. The zombies STILL have major problems with their animations and registration in the server.
For example -
Zombie runs up to you, you pull out your melee weapon to kill it, zombie gets about 10 ft away from you and ends up hitting you repeatedly because of the lag time in the server. So what should have been an easy to kill zombie is now a super zombie because it can teleport around you, and kill you before you have a chance to even hit it once.
There is still problems that result in a players character dying when they have lost connection. If you lose connection in the middle of your game and you are still walking or running your character will continue to run and walk until you log back into your game. Thus resulting you running off cliffs, buildings, etc.
Items that are dropped on the ground or moved end up falling through the floor (inside homes and on the terrain). This has always been in the game and has yet to be resolved. In stead of fixing this bug they decided to add more items to pick up (food, weapons, gear, etc). So if you find an awesome vest or rifle you better not let go of it, the world will eat it.
Everyone is going to tell me that "its because the game is in alpha" and that I should wait til it's finished. At the rate the developers are going to fix DayZ I don't see this game being complete anytime soon. It's been over a year for me and there has been hardly any changes made to the actual game. I'm totally fine with playing games that are in alpha stage and I understand that games like this are not suppose to be perfect.
When the Evolve Alpha test came out in late 2013-2014 it was insanely buggy, but it was still enjoyable. They eventually fixed all the problems and concerns that people were talking about. Evolve is set to release in early 2015. Beta and alpha testing are over.  My point with comparing the development of DayZ with Evolve is because the guys at TurtleRock studios seem to have more of a desire in finishing their product as soon as they can and have it done in an efficient manor.  Where as DayZ was released almost the same time that they were doing the first alpha testing for Evolve. Yes they are two completely different games but I think you can see the lack of commitment this game is receiving when you compare it other games that were released in an alpha stage around the same time.
If they do continue to keep developing this game their current rate, the game will not likely be finished until 2017 or 2018. It's clear to see that their objectives are not on perfecting the game but adding more and more trash to an ever growing pile of garbage.

Basically in this game, you can choose to fight or befriend anything that you engage a battle with. Fighting will increase your level; which will increase your HP, ATK, and DEF making it easier to beat the game. And your other choice is sparing your foes. You do this by choosing the 'act' option in a battle. There are several 'act' options to choose from and they vary depending on your enemy. It's usually a very silly sequence of actions you must fulfill to befriend and spare your foes. Your enemies are so charming and cute that you would feel bad killing them! They don't just get knocked out. They die! So choose wisely!
There are plenty of puzzles in this game to keep the overworld interesting. And these are not tedious puzzles. I had fun with them.
The most enjoyable part for me was the humor. This game made me laugh and smile throughout my whole playthrough. And right after I finished it, I went for a second playthrough so I could get the true ending. This game only took me 8 or 9 hours to beat, but it is truly worth it. $10 is a really good price. I would have bought it for $30.
The story starts out all fun and silly, but you soon will realize how dark it really is. It's going to make you emotional.
Toby Fox wrote this game, designed it, and composed the music. He really is a genius. And I really look forward to what ever else he will create. Hopefully another video game!
10 out of 10!!!

Rust is a game about survival, and that means that you are constantly at risk. More so at risk than most other survival games. Players are hostile and animals attack on sight. Environments can be harsh, causing you to freeze to death or overheat and eventually die. You spawn with virtually nothing and are expected to get to something with that. This game is not for people who want a game to just sit and play to relax, it's a game for people who want about as true of a survival experience as it gets.
Overall, I'd give this game a 7/10. It's still got a few bugs to work out, seeing as it is in early access, but I have to say that even where it is at right now, it is a great game(s) worthy of it's $20 price tag.

Undertale's another RPG with a simple twist. You can try to avoid fighting in any encounter, or you can fight it like an old style Final Fantasy battle. When you're attacked monsters attacks appear as bullet hell dodging games that you have to evade to avoid losing HP, which is an interesting twist on RPG battle mechanics.
In a way battles play out as a sort of sandbox. At no point are you forced into one action or another. The first boss is a great example of this. You can beat the boss by fighting it or you can try to talk your way out of it, or you can do a combination of both.
You can even change your mind at the very last second.
Go ahead, change your mind. It's just a game and if you don't like what happens you can load a save.

Okay, so this game has been praised by a lot of people and you might be wondering why. The graphics look like they belong on the Super Nintendo and the protagonist's sprite just looks plain awful.
The thing is, this game only looks good when it needs to be, that is during boss battles and big story revelations. And even though I disliked the style at first it really grew on me in the first ten minutes. Its simple but still manages to have a lot of details. Plus, during fights the graphics change too so you wont get bored of the same stuff all the time.
Now onto the stuff that makes this game so great, story.
The games story is really really good, it has multiple endings, all your choices are reflected trough npc's speech (said or did *blank* in the beginning of the game? npc's in the beginning, middle and end of the game will change his/her speech accordingly). AND what i love most, THE GAME REMEMBERS! It doesn't matter if you reloaded your save, it doesn't matter if you REMOVE your old save file. The game will remember what you did. Someone might just vaguely remember your favorite color, old conversations and ... sins...
Even so, play like you would always play, I personally killed everything in my first playthrough because i like to get the bad end first. I didn't get it. You think you know how to get it but you don't, this game tries and mostly succeeds in not being stereotypical. My end wasn't good but it reflected my playstyle perfectly, I wasn't actually evil i was just a bad person and the ending showed me that in a non condescending way. At this point i liked the game but I wasn't hyped... yet. The second playthrough, that's where the magic happens! I'm not going to spoil anything else because you get the best experience knowing as little as possible, but, everything falls into place in an altogether great way.
Edit:
A year later and I still think this is a great game. I come back to it every now and then just to listen to the music.
Edit2:
2 years later and when I tihnk of a great game this one still the one that comes to mind

Honestly I would never have purchased this game if I hadn't seen all these other reviews...but I have to be fair about this as a video game there are major problems that caused my play time to be less than satisfactory and I feel like way too much has been overlooked by other players.
The game uses super low resolution which is a problem.  The fights use a bullet hell style system (like a shoot'em up game).  Even with full screen the battle areas are just too small and difficult to see things happening, particularly when the fights get intense.  You can't remap your buttons which if you play using a keyboard is a problem (another review pointed out that using a controlller is an option, I do have a controller but did not use it so that may be a solution for you if you plan on playing with a controller.  I know it's made in RPG Maker and that engine (VX Ace) has serious limitations, but frustration points aren't removed just because I know this.
The characters are interesting and by far the best part of the game.  The story is somewhat unique but not THAT unique compared to many other RPG style games given various twists and tropes.  There are multiple endings but without looking at a guide you'll be replaying the game multiple times to get the one you really want which is a slap in the face if you do 99% of what you need to get the ending you want.  Now, you could hack the save file or go watch the other endings on youtube or just give up of course - but any way you go about it, it's not a good experience.
The sound and music are sometimes good, and sometimes annoying with bleeps and old school blurps, this is left to taste but sometimes I felt it enhanced the experience, and othertimes it fell short.  There is no real voice work...even for modern indy games and considering the short length this is a feature that would have enhanced the already stated best part of the game, the characters - yet it is completely missing.
I've played many flash games that were better...they were free as well.  I've played lots of games that I paid for that were better too, but this feels much more comparable to a flash game to me.  Considering that, this being a pay for game, it did not meet my expectations considering the high reviews.
Finally, I feel that Undertale is merely an average indy RPG game that is vastly over rated by mass hystery due to a few jokes, interesting characters, memes, and a somewhat unique (but not necessarily fun) combat system and a community starved for RPG innovation, which I would agree is an issue but not enough to justify the level of commendations Undertale has received.  A few well implemented ideas do not always equal a good gaming experience.  In my case, it did not.

Undertale's another RPG with a simple twist. You can try to avoid fighting in any encounter, or you can fight it like an old style Final Fantasy battle. When you're attacked monsters attacks appear as bullet hell dodging games that you have to evade to avoid losing HP, which is an interesting twist on RPG battle mechanics.
In a way battles play out as a sort of sandbox. At no point are you forced into one action or another. The first boss is a great example of this. You can beat the boss by fighting it or you can try to talk your way out of it, or you can do a combination of both.
You can even change your mind at the very last second.
Go ahead, change your mind. It's just a game and if you don't like what happens you can load a save.

Okay, so this game has been praised by a lot of people and you might be wondering why. The graphics look like they belong on the Super Nintendo and the protagonist's sprite just looks plain awful.
The thing is, this game only looks good when it needs to be, that is during boss battles and big story revelations. And even though I disliked the style at first it really grew on me in the first ten minutes. Its simple but still manages to have a lot of details. Plus, during fights the graphics change too so you wont get bored of the same stuff all the time.
Now onto the stuff that makes this game so great, story.
The games story is really really good, it has multiple endings, all your choices are reflected trough npc's speech (said or did *blank* in the beginning of the game? npc's in the beginning, middle and end of the game will change his/her speech accordingly). AND what i love most, THE GAME REMEMBERS! It doesn't matter if you reloaded your save, it doesn't matter if you REMOVE your old save file. The game will remember what you did. Someone might just vaguely remember your favorite color, old conversations and ... sins...
Even so, play like you would always play, I personally killed everything in my first playthrough because i like to get the bad end first. I didn't get it. You think you know how to get it but you don't, this game tries and mostly succeeds in not being stereotypical. My end wasn't good but it reflected my playstyle perfectly, I wasn't actually evil i was just a bad person and the ending showed me that in a non condescending way. At this point i liked the game but I wasn't hyped... yet. The second playthrough, that's where the magic happens! I'm not going to spoil anything else because you get the best experience knowing as little as possible, but, everything falls into place in an altogether great way.
Edit:
A year later and I still think this is a great game. I come back to it every now and then just to listen to the music.
Edit2:
2 years later and when I tihnk of a great game this one still the one that comes to mind

Ok, I will expose a very middling opinion here: I really liked the game but I think it's way overrated.
Let me tell you why I think Undertale is overrated: Despite having one of the most original and new, unique storytelling, it has little else to support itself. Graphics? There is nothing here. Music? Is really good, but the loops are way too short. Gamplay? I'll expand on it:
The Gameplay consists of 3 different elements: Dodging bullets, finding out how to progress in the game and exploration. In more details: The bullet hell part of the game is hindered by the fact that the frame rate is capped at 30fps and that the action is happening in a small box, which makes it not that enjoyable. Exploration is not that fun either, you don't have a lot to explore out of the main path you will take in order to complete the game. But the small amount of optional content there is to find is rewarding enough, I have to admit, because you'll usually find some bits of lore or dialog that is interesting to discover.
Now, the third element that I evoked as "figuring out how to progress", to be more precise
, which is definitely what the game advertises as "puzzles", not what you do when you push rocks on buttons. I can't describe it properly without spoiling anything, but it consists of fumbling until you get it right. Is that enjoyable? No. Or at least, as much as hitting your face against a wall until you figure out it's not a wall but a door you can open. Because that's exactly what "puzzles" in this game are. People find it "innovating" because it is a new way to present puzzles in perspective of how other games did it until now, but with a more critical view, it is still annoying, because it is not fun to repeat the same thing over and over until, by luck, you find an actual solution.
Obviously I focused on points that are negative to the game, because I don't think Undertale needs more advocacy. As I said, I found the storytelling (the way the story is told) excellent and unique, which made it one of the best game experiences I've had this year. Yet, I don't think it is fair to compare it to other games and say it is better overall, because it's not: Undertale is a flawed game with one outstanding part (the storytelling) which makes it memorable. And I do think it is overrated because people give way too much importance to story in video games. Also because games in general have poor stories, which makes one average or good story in a video game look like a Pulitzer prize in comparison.
So here you go. An actual positive opinion piece on Undertale that is not full maymay or blind fanboyism, I hope I helped someone forge their own opinion on the mater.

Undertale is a wonderful game and is done right in so many ways it might be better than Papyrus' spaghetti [*WHAT DID YOU SAY?!].
You start off the game in a a cave alone on a bed of flowers. Though it the flowers might appear to be "insignificant", they really aren't. He teaches you the ins and outs of the Underground and shows you his LOVE with "friendliness pellets". Though your new mom (or mum) doesn't like this and stops the Flower from spreading LOVE over you like butter. She shows you around the RUINS and teaches you to talk to the monsters and not to hurt them. This is where you make your choice. Kill or be killed, or love and be loved.
Along your adventure to travel back above ground, you'll meet a lot of monsters as you progress through the Underground. Depending on what you do, they'll love you, or they resent you.
Undertale is a game that teaches you what friends really mean, and how it feels when you hurt others. The mechanic of the game is amazing and wonderful, much like the music and Mettaton EX's legs. Storyline is great. Your actions have far reaching consequences- killing someone is always a big deal as it should be. People react to the deaths of other people. There is a deconstruction of the aspects of the standard RPG. A large part of the story paints the fourth wall as a medium, where the rules of the game itself are explored as actual elements of the 'verse itself, subject to bending or exploitation by savvy characters.
Combat is great. Rythym game for those who want to fight the enemies, puzzles for those who want to spare the enemies. Bullet Hell for defense and sometimes the entire purpose of the combat. There were a few situations where I could not avoid damage but that is probably due to my lack of skill- attacks were always fair even if difficult.
Overall, I would give this game my recommendation for people to play- especially people who like thoughtful games like "To the Moon" but are okay with the game's engine being put to the background.

There are so many details that make this game so enjoyable. Not only is Toby and excellent designer and writer, you can tell he has a passion for music. Every OST in the soundtrack gives of waves of emotion, ehancing the atmosphere by the ten-fold. From "Bonetrousle" to "Death By Glamour", I highly recommend you buy the soundtrack. I'm not ashamed to say that  I cried. I'm honored to say that I laughed. Please, try this game. You won't have a bad time, at all.

This is one of those games where you really don't think it'll be good because of the style, the hype, or maybe even the community it's associated with. I doubted it as well for those reasons, but my doubts were misplaced. It's actually a joy to play, and there's quite a bit of content to this little pixel indie game.
To break it down bit by bit:
The gameplay is that of a normal RPG, but there's a little more to it. It's like a blend of Shin Megami Tensei and Barkley: Shut up and Jam Gaiden. You have to time normal attacks and the different weapons alter your timing as well as the damage, similar to B:SUaJG. You also have to talk to enemies to change the outcome of the battle or Spare them after using certain actions, similar to SMT.
The graphics are more or less what you expect of an 8bit/16bit/however many bits you can consider this so I won't say much about them.
The story is pretty good as well, there's a lot of layers and lore to find in the three different paths (Genocide, where you kill everyone and everything, Neutral, where you do some killing and fighting, and Pacifist, where you spare everything) to match up and tell you the backstory to the game. The characters are all unique and relatable, and I actually felt myself connected to them. It's tough to think of doing a Genocide run after getting the Pacifist run because I feel like the characters are, more or less, friends. I can't bring myself to think of killing them, even if the boss fights in that route are cool. It's normally suggested to do NPG (Neutral, Pacifist, Genocide) since there's no true reset after a Genocide run until after you do a Pacifist run, but I suggest going NGP, if you can, because you'll more than likely be too attached to the characters after P to think of killing them, but keep in mind I'm only suggesting N first because G is the hardest route to do and it's probably best for you to learn the game first.
The soundtrack is actually pretty cool for a pixel indie, and the final boss themes are pretty powerful. I don't normally cry or get emotional when it comes to games, but I had tingly feels all over in the final boss fights (not including the Neutral finale boss, that fight is the bane of my existence.) I'd say to look some of them up but the videos are pretty spoilerish, it's best if you just experience them with the boss.
tl;dr You should probably buy this. Don't even wait for a sale. It's worth it.

Undertale plays with many conventions of video games, especially old school RPGs, in mostly great ways. You play as a human child on an adventure to the underground, where monsters of various designs, combat style, and personalities flourish.
Pros:
*Very endearing characters with few obnoxious ones.
*Different gameplay styles can be used, including one where you can avoid killing anything.
*Unique combat system that involves bullet-hell playing for spans of around 5 seconds per turn.
*Music is varied, catchy, and usually full of 16 bit charm.
*Skill curve is usually well-paced.
*Humorous and silly, but can provide meaningful conflict and emotional moments.
Cons:
*Some fights can be counter-intuitive or need a guide in order to progress.
*Starting new games is complex at an "in-game" perspective.
*Few side quests.
*The flow of the game can be interrupted many times from NPCs talking for a long time.
