This is one of those games where you really don't think it'll be good because of the style, the hype, or maybe even the community it's associated with. I doubted it as well for those reasons, but my doubts were misplaced. It's actually a joy to play, and there's quite a bit of content to this little pixel indie game.
To break it down bit by bit:
The gameplay is that of a normal RPG, but there's a little more to it. It's like a blend of Shin Megami Tensei and Barkley: Shut up and Jam Gaiden. You have to time normal attacks and the different weapons alter your timing as well as the damage, similar to B:SUaJG. You also have to talk to enemies to change the outcome of the battle or Spare them after using certain actions, similar to SMT.
The graphics are more or less what you expect of an 8bit/16bit/however many bits you can consider this so I won't say much about them.
The story is pretty good as well, there's a lot of layers and lore to find in the three different paths (Genocide, where you kill everyone and everything, Neutral, where you do some killing and fighting, and Pacifist, where you spare everything) to match up and tell you the backstory to the game. The characters are all unique and relatable, and I actually felt myself connected to them. It's tough to think of doing a Genocide run after getting the Pacifist run because I feel like the characters are, more or less, friends. I can't bring myself to think of killing them, even if the boss fights in that route are cool. It's normally suggested to do NPG (Neutral, Pacifist, Genocide) since there's no true reset after a Genocide run until after you do a Pacifist run, but I suggest going NGP, if you can, because you'll more than likely be too attached to the characters after P to think of killing them, but keep in mind I'm only suggesting N first because G is the hardest route to do and it's probably best for you to learn the game first.
The soundtrack is actually pretty cool for a pixel indie, and the final boss themes are pretty powerful. I don't normally cry or get emotional when it comes to games, but I had tingly feels all over in the final boss fights (not including the Neutral finale boss, that fight is the bane of my existence.) I'd say to look some of them up but the videos are pretty spoilerish, it's best if you just experience them with the boss.
tl;dr You should probably buy this. Don't even wait for a sale. It's worth it.

Rust Is a Fantastic Survival game that fits almost any person's interest in generic video games.
Rust can be wedged into almost every single genre of gaming.
Rust Can Be horrific due to being jumpscared at night by all the dangerous animals and humans that lurk in the darkness.
Rust can be placed into and RPG-like game because of the people who make clans that work together and raid eachother as if it were a real life war
Rust can be survival, Since you spawn near water with nothing but a rock and a torch, in which you must build yourself up to the mightiest player to be known.
Rust can be a Moba-game, because of it's significance in Mass-Mulitplay.
Rust can be a Shooter, due to the ability to craft guns, find guns, and use them to your advantage when it comes to
mass raids against others, who wont back down without fighting back.
Rust may as well be a creative game, because of it allowing you to have very little limitation to what, where. and how you may build structures, machines, and even towns!
As you can see, Rust fits everyone's style of gaming, which allows it to be perfect for everyone.
Here are some Pros And Cons to the Game.
-+=Pros=+-
Fantastic Graphics.
Beautiful Terrain
Large Crafting System.
Realistic Features.
Awesome Mic System that goes by Distance.
Huge World Gens.
Challenging.
Large Servers 50-200 People) to Small Servers (1-10)
(Rare Cases) Opens up to making New Friends
Great Topography.
Unlimited Possibilities.
Mods.
Large Veriety of Animals.
Raiding/Defending.
Great Concept of how the real challenge is dealing with the humans, and not the harsh conditions and obstacles that come with surviving in the wild.
-=+Cons+=-
(Some of these may vary depending on your computer)
Very low FPS game
Lag is common (in some cases)
Hackers Are a possibility but they a rare to find and they usually dont cause much Impact
Horrible Community, you are least likely to find someone to trust when ingame. (Although it does open up a new challenge to survive and defend against them).
--------------------------------------------------------
Conclusion:
Rust is probably one of the best survival games that I've ever played and it probably has better value to it than of a $60 game. I recommend this to anyone of any style of gaming

This is one of those games where you really don't think it'll be good because of the style, the hype, or maybe even the community it's associated with. I doubted it as well for those reasons, but my doubts were misplaced. It's actually a joy to play, and there's quite a bit of content to this little pixel indie game.
To break it down bit by bit:
The gameplay is that of a normal RPG, but there's a little more to it. It's like a blend of Shin Megami Tensei and Barkley: Shut up and Jam Gaiden. You have to time normal attacks and the different weapons alter your timing as well as the damage, similar to B:SUaJG. You also have to talk to enemies to change the outcome of the battle or Spare them after using certain actions, similar to SMT.
The graphics are more or less what you expect of an 8bit/16bit/however many bits you can consider this so I won't say much about them.
The story is pretty good as well, there's a lot of layers and lore to find in the three different paths (Genocide, where you kill everyone and everything, Neutral, where you do some killing and fighting, and Pacifist, where you spare everything) to match up and tell you the backstory to the game. The characters are all unique and relatable, and I actually felt myself connected to them. It's tough to think of doing a Genocide run after getting the Pacifist run because I feel like the characters are, more or less, friends. I can't bring myself to think of killing them, even if the boss fights in that route are cool. It's normally suggested to do NPG (Neutral, Pacifist, Genocide) since there's no true reset after a Genocide run until after you do a Pacifist run, but I suggest going NGP, if you can, because you'll more than likely be too attached to the characters after P to think of killing them, but keep in mind I'm only suggesting N first because G is the hardest route to do and it's probably best for you to learn the game first.
The soundtrack is actually pretty cool for a pixel indie, and the final boss themes are pretty powerful. I don't normally cry or get emotional when it comes to games, but I had tingly feels all over in the final boss fights (not including the Neutral finale boss, that fight is the bane of my existence.) I'd say to look some of them up but the videos are pretty spoilerish, it's best if you just experience them with the boss.
tl;dr You should probably buy this. Don't even wait for a sale. It's worth it.

Undertale plays with many conventions of video games, especially old school RPGs, in mostly great ways. You play as a human child on an adventure to the underground, where monsters of various designs, combat style, and personalities flourish.
Pros:
*Very endearing characters with few obnoxious ones.
*Different gameplay styles can be used, including one where you can avoid killing anything.
*Unique combat system that involves bullet-hell playing for spans of around 5 seconds per turn.
*Music is varied, catchy, and usually full of 16 bit charm.
*Skill curve is usually well-paced.
*Humorous and silly, but can provide meaningful conflict and emotional moments.
Cons:
*Some fights can be counter-intuitive or need a guide in order to progress.
*Starting new games is complex at an "in-game" perspective.
*Few side quests.
*The flow of the game can be interrupted many times from NPCs talking for a long time.
Its a fun game even with the bugs you can just injoy the game with friends.

This is one of those games where you really don't think it'll be good because of the style, the hype, or maybe even the community it's associated with. I doubted it as well for those reasons, but my doubts were misplaced. It's actually a joy to play, and there's quite a bit of content to this little pixel indie game.
To break it down bit by bit:
The gameplay is that of a normal RPG, but there's a little more to it. It's like a blend of Shin Megami Tensei and Barkley: Shut up and Jam Gaiden. You have to time normal attacks and the different weapons alter your timing as well as the damage, similar to B:SUaJG. You also have to talk to enemies to change the outcome of the battle or Spare them after using certain actions, similar to SMT.
The graphics are more or less what you expect of an 8bit/16bit/however many bits you can consider this so I won't say much about them.
The story is pretty good as well, there's a lot of layers and lore to find in the three different paths (Genocide, where you kill everyone and everything, Neutral, where you do some killing and fighting, and Pacifist, where you spare everything) to match up and tell you the backstory to the game. The characters are all unique and relatable, and I actually felt myself connected to them. It's tough to think of doing a Genocide run after getting the Pacifist run because I feel like the characters are, more or less, friends. I can't bring myself to think of killing them, even if the boss fights in that route are cool. It's normally suggested to do NPG (Neutral, Pacifist, Genocide) since there's no true reset after a Genocide run until after you do a Pacifist run, but I suggest going NGP, if you can, because you'll more than likely be too attached to the characters after P to think of killing them, but keep in mind I'm only suggesting N first because G is the hardest route to do and it's probably best for you to learn the game first.
The soundtrack is actually pretty cool for a pixel indie, and the final boss themes are pretty powerful. I don't normally cry or get emotional when it comes to games, but I had tingly feels all over in the final boss fights (not including the Neutral finale boss, that fight is the bane of my existence.) I'd say to look some of them up but the videos are pretty spoilerish, it's best if you just experience them with the boss.
tl;dr You should probably buy this. Don't even wait for a sale. It's worth it.

Undertale plays with many conventions of video games, especially old school RPGs, in mostly great ways. You play as a human child on an adventure to the underground, where monsters of various designs, combat style, and personalities flourish.
Pros:
*Very endearing characters with few obnoxious ones.
*Different gameplay styles can be used, including one where you can avoid killing anything.
*Unique combat system that involves bullet-hell playing for spans of around 5 seconds per turn.
*Music is varied, catchy, and usually full of 16 bit charm.
*Skill curve is usually well-paced.
*Humorous and silly, but can provide meaningful conflict and emotional moments.
Cons:
*Some fights can be counter-intuitive or need a guide in order to progress.
*Starting new games is complex at an "in-game" perspective.
*Few side quests.
*The flow of the game can be interrupted many times from NPCs talking for a long time.

Rust Is a Fantastic Survival game that fits almost any person's interest in generic video games.
Rust can be wedged into almost every single genre of gaming.
Rust Can Be horrific due to being jumpscared at night by all the dangerous animals and humans that lurk in the darkness.
Rust can be placed into and RPG-like game because of the people who make clans that work together and raid eachother as if it were a real life war
Rust can be survival, Since you spawn near water with nothing but a rock and a torch, in which you must build yourself up to the mightiest player to be known.
Rust can be a Moba-game, because of it's significance in Mass-Mulitplay.
Rust can be a Shooter, due to the ability to craft guns, find guns, and use them to your advantage when it comes to
mass raids against others, who wont back down without fighting back.
Rust may as well be a creative game, because of it allowing you to have very little limitation to what, where. and how you may build structures, machines, and even towns!
As you can see, Rust fits everyone's style of gaming, which allows it to be perfect for everyone.
Here are some Pros And Cons to the Game.
-+=Pros=+-
Fantastic Graphics.
Beautiful Terrain
Large Crafting System.
Realistic Features.
Awesome Mic System that goes by Distance.
Huge World Gens.
Challenging.
Large Servers 50-200 People) to Small Servers (1-10)
(Rare Cases) Opens up to making New Friends
Great Topography.
Unlimited Possibilities.
Mods.
Large Veriety of Animals.
Raiding/Defending.
Great Concept of how the real challenge is dealing with the humans, and not the harsh conditions and obstacles that come with surviving in the wild.
-=+Cons+=-
(Some of these may vary depending on your computer)
Very low FPS game
Lag is common (in some cases)
Hackers Are a possibility but they a rare to find and they usually dont cause much Impact
Horrible Community, you are least likely to find someone to trust when ingame. (Although it does open up a new challenge to survive and defend against them).
--------------------------------------------------------
Conclusion:
Rust is probably one of the best survival games that I've ever played and it probably has better value to it than of a $60 game. I recommend this to anyone of any style of gaming

Undertale is a very hard game to describe, but regardless, I'll do it anyways.
Undertale is a game where you play as a human kid named "Frisk". The world is split in two, with the surface inhabited by humans, and the underground inhabited by inferior monsters. Undertale follows the adventure of Frisk, who gets lost in the Underground and has to find her way back to the surface. Both worlds are separated by a barrier, which I won't discuss any more for spoiler reasons.
So, Frisk sets on her adventure, and meets a massive cast of lovable characters along the way, each with their own unique quirks and personality, but that's not as far as the personalities stretch. Every single monster you meet has its own personality, and you can beat them merely by abusing that personality. For example, there's a monster who constantly tells jokes. If you let it tell a joke, and then you decide to laugh at it afterwards, that monster will be satisfied and leave you be.
The entire game can be ran through without killing a single creature, or you can play as a genocidal maniac and kill everything you meet, and it affects the ending massively. Undertale has a surprising moral lesson for you all, and really did make me question my motives behind sparing every single creature I encountered.
The game also has great comedic value, with plenty of fourth wall breaking; Metal Gear style, a lot of puns, and a ton of jokes. A skele-ton.

This is, unequivocally, my favorite game of all time. I've been playing video games for 15 of my 17 years on this earth, and I've said that phrase many times, but... this is number one. Forever. Nothing can top this game. It's, in my opinion, one of the few perfect games of all time. There's nothing about this game that I dislike. Anyway, let's get to the nitty gritty. There will be spoilers, so skip to the bottom if you want to not be spoiled.
Story
The story of this game is on the surface simple but the deeper you go the more complex it gets. The story starts with the intro, which explains a war between monsters and humans hundreds of years ago that led to the monsters being forced into the underground and sealed in with a magical barrier. However, the barrier didn't encompass the entire underground, as there is still an entrance in Mt. Ebott. In the year 201X, Mt. Ebott has become a point of mystery and myth, with stories of people going there and never coming back. The intro then shows a human falling down a hole in Mr. Ebott and landing on a patch of flowers in the underground, before going to the title screen. You start a new game, pick a name for The Fallen Human, and then you play as a young human who's ended up in the underground. As you go forward, you meet a talking flower named Flowey. He seems friendly at first, claiming to be your best friend and explaining the basics of gameplay, putting your SOUL into a white box and explaining that your SOUL grows with EXP and LOVE and all that, but then he says that he want to share LOVE with you by giving you "friendliness pellets". These are white projectiles that he then shoots at your SOUL and... they reduce your health to 1/20, he reveals he was planning on killing you, and he says "Down here, it's kill or be killed." Thankfully, before he can finish you off, he's attacked from offscreen by a motherly monster named Toriel. She acts as a tutorial, showing you how to go through encounters, solve puzzles, and basically teaching you the rest of the basics of the game. She also acts like a motherly figure, protecting you, teaching you, and being as kind as she can to you. Eventually, she has to leave you alone and tells you to wait in a room while she runs errands, giving you a cell phone so you can stay in touch. ...Of course, you can't wait in that room. If you do, the game never progresses. So you go through The Ruins. You eventually get into random encounters with monsters, but you have the option of not fighting. You can ACT, which allows you to complete encounters with non-violence. This gives you no EXP, but it does give you money. Eventually, you get to the end of The Ruins after solving puzzles, having random encounters, and meeting a depressed ghost named Napstablook, and find Toriel was shopping to accommodate you in her home, having baked you a pie, prepared a room for you, and created a curriculum for your education. Eventually, however, you have to leave. You want to go home, to leave the underground. This leads to her going down the stairs and down a hallway to the exit to The Ruins, which she plans to destroy. In order to leave you have to prove to her that you are strong enough to survive without her help. This is the first "boss" fight. She's the first truly challenging monster you've fought so far... But you can still complete the fight without attacking. Either way, if you kill her or spare her, you leave the ruins. You embark on a journey to a place called "The Core", going through the regions of Snowdin, Waterfall, and Hotland before you get there. Along the way, you meet a cast of interesting characters. Sans and Papyrus, two skeleton brothers who are sentries in the Snowdin Forest; Undyne, captain of the Royal Guard; Alphys, Royal Scientist to King Asgore; Mettaton, a robot designed for entertainment; and King Asgore himself. I won't summarize the entire story, as I don't want to spoil it all, but it's one of the funniest and most well-written stories in gaming, with surprising depth and moments of heartfelt warmth and crushing sadness. There are three paths to take, Neutral (which is what your first run will always be if you're not doing the No Mercy run. Sort of like the good ending of Silent Hill 3), Pacifist (2nd playthough killing nobody and backtracking after you get through the fight with Mettaton EX and into The Core), and No Mercy (killing literally everyone you come across.). I won't tell you how to play the game, but just know that doing the No Mercy run will taint your game and make it impossible to do a Pacifist Run ever again.
Gameplay
The game plays like Earthbound mixed with Ikaruga. It's a top down adventure outside of combat, interacting with things for humorous flavor text, talking to people, buying stuff from shops, etc. In combat, however, it changes. You can fight, act, use items, and use Mercy (either sparing your opponent or fleeing the battle), but when the monsters you fight attack, it becomes a different game. It becomes a bullet hell where you have to memorize the patterns of monster attacks and try your hardest to avoid them, with later monsters throwing more complex patterns and boss monsters throwing new gameplay mechanics to change the way you have to avoid their attacks. It's very fun, and definitely one of my favorite parts of the game.
Writing
The writing is genuinely some of the best I've ever seen. It can be hilarious, thoughtful, heartfelt, tearjerking, or nightmarish and it never once seems out of place. All of the writing is spot-on and perfect for the story.
Well, that's pretty much all I can explain without spoiling the experience. Buy this game. It's 10 bucks and it might be the best game you play this year or EVER.
10/10

Walked around for half an hour without seeing another soul - alive or dead.
I came across a derelict ship, and climbed aboard. I then proceeded to fall off a gangway into the cargo hold, breaking both legs in the process.
Despite my injuries, I was relieved that I had been spared from a cruel death.
I set about making an escape from the empty bowels of the ship and started to drag myself across the floor towards the solitary exit.
Upon reaching the exit I was confronted with a small staircase consisting of about 3 steps leading up to the exit door. I was horrified to learn that the builders of the ship had not considered disabled access and found myself trapped in the empty hold unable to drag my tired, broken body up the steps to sweet freedom.
Learning of my predicament caused me to go through several emotions:
First there was anger. "How could these idiots not have considered disabled access?!?"
Then there was denial, Not accepting my fate, I frantically crawled around the hold searching, hoping for another exit.
Next came despair. My vision went blurry as tears filled my eyes and a deep sadness came over me as I came to the realization that I would die down here, alone in a dank, rusty cargo hold.
And finally acceptance. My fate was sealed, I knew I was gonna die, and that there was nothing I could do.
I made the decision to try and speed up my fate and attempted to find a way to kill myself. Unfortunately in a bare cargo hold, with no weapons, and no energy to perform the task, I could find no way of ending my suffering. Again in despair I cried out. Fortunately someone must have heard my suffering as after a further few minutes, of waiting, some kind soul came and put me out of my misery with a 2x4.
10/10 would recomend

This is, unequivocally, my favorite game of all time. I've been playing video games for 15 of my 17 years on this earth, and I've said that phrase many times, but... this is number one. Forever. Nothing can top this game. It's, in my opinion, one of the few perfect games of all time. There's nothing about this game that I dislike. Anyway, let's get to the nitty gritty. There will be spoilers, so skip to the bottom if you want to not be spoiled.
Story
The story of this game is on the surface simple but the deeper you go the more complex it gets. The story starts with the intro, which explains a war between monsters and humans hundreds of years ago that led to the monsters being forced into the underground and sealed in with a magical barrier. However, the barrier didn't encompass the entire underground, as there is still an entrance in Mt. Ebott. In the year 201X, Mt. Ebott has become a point of mystery and myth, with stories of people going there and never coming back. The intro then shows a human falling down a hole in Mr. Ebott and landing on a patch of flowers in the underground, before going to the title screen. You start a new game, pick a name for The Fallen Human, and then you play as a young human who's ended up in the underground. As you go forward, you meet a talking flower named Flowey. He seems friendly at first, claiming to be your best friend and explaining the basics of gameplay, putting your SOUL into a white box and explaining that your SOUL grows with EXP and LOVE and all that, but then he says that he want to share LOVE with you by giving you "friendliness pellets". These are white projectiles that he then shoots at your SOUL and... they reduce your health to 1/20, he reveals he was planning on killing you, and he says "Down here, it's kill or be killed." Thankfully, before he can finish you off, he's attacked from offscreen by a motherly monster named Toriel. She acts as a tutorial, showing you how to go through encounters, solve puzzles, and basically teaching you the rest of the basics of the game. She also acts like a motherly figure, protecting you, teaching you, and being as kind as she can to you. Eventually, she has to leave you alone and tells you to wait in a room while she runs errands, giving you a cell phone so you can stay in touch. ...Of course, you can't wait in that room. If you do, the game never progresses. So you go through The Ruins. You eventually get into random encounters with monsters, but you have the option of not fighting. You can ACT, which allows you to complete encounters with non-violence. This gives you no EXP, but it does give you money. Eventually, you get to the end of The Ruins after solving puzzles, having random encounters, and meeting a depressed ghost named Napstablook, and find Toriel was shopping to accommodate you in her home, having baked you a pie, prepared a room for you, and created a curriculum for your education. Eventually, however, you have to leave. You want to go home, to leave the underground. This leads to her going down the stairs and down a hallway to the exit to The Ruins, which she plans to destroy. In order to leave you have to prove to her that you are strong enough to survive without her help. This is the first "boss" fight. She's the first truly challenging monster you've fought so far... But you can still complete the fight without attacking. Either way, if you kill her or spare her, you leave the ruins. You embark on a journey to a place called "The Core", going through the regions of Snowdin, Waterfall, and Hotland before you get there. Along the way, you meet a cast of interesting characters. Sans and Papyrus, two skeleton brothers who are sentries in the Snowdin Forest; Undyne, captain of the Royal Guard; Alphys, Royal Scientist to King Asgore; Mettaton, a robot designed for entertainment; and King Asgore himself. I won't summarize the entire story, as I don't want to spoil it all, but it's one of the funniest and most well-written stories in gaming, with surprising depth and moments of heartfelt warmth and crushing sadness. There are three paths to take, Neutral (which is what your first run will always be if you're not doing the No Mercy run. Sort of like the good ending of Silent Hill 3), Pacifist (2nd playthough killing nobody and backtracking after you get through the fight with Mettaton EX and into The Core), and No Mercy (killing literally everyone you come across.). I won't tell you how to play the game, but just know that doing the No Mercy run will taint your game and make it impossible to do a Pacifist Run ever again.
Gameplay
The game plays like Earthbound mixed with Ikaruga. It's a top down adventure outside of combat, interacting with things for humorous flavor text, talking to people, buying stuff from shops, etc. In combat, however, it changes. You can fight, act, use items, and use Mercy (either sparing your opponent or fleeing the battle), but when the monsters you fight attack, it becomes a different game. It becomes a bullet hell where you have to memorize the patterns of monster attacks and try your hardest to avoid them, with later monsters throwing more complex patterns and boss monsters throwing new gameplay mechanics to change the way you have to avoid their attacks. It's very fun, and definitely one of my favorite parts of the game.
Writing
The writing is genuinely some of the best I've ever seen. It can be hilarious, thoughtful, heartfelt, tearjerking, or nightmarish and it never once seems out of place. All of the writing is spot-on and perfect for the story.
Well, that's pretty much all I can explain without spoiling the experience. Buy this game. It's 10 bucks and it might be the best game you play this year or EVER.

DayZ is a very enjoyqable open world survival game, set in a post-apocalyptic world. Development is still ongoing (ALPHA), so you can expect many bugs and poor optimization. Besides that, there are many people who abuse glitches and the weak anti-cheat system. Zombies are not your primary concern yet. In short, the game is far from being completed.
Does this disqualify the game? In my opinion: certainly not! The strength of the game currently lays in the massive open world and the randomness of encounters with other players. Will you engage them for a trade? Can you even trust those guys? Should you try to avoid their attention? Or perhaps you should kill them and go through their pockets. Making the wrong choice may end up in death, or perhaps even torture. Encounters with other people always raise your heartbeat.
The lack of any pre-determined goals is what makes the game so enjoyable. You are free to wander in this world and explore it's beautiful scenery, towns and secrets. Don't forget to look over your shoulders though.

I have quite the (true) story to tell of Dayz's incredible gameplay, and i will try my best to make it understandable for those who have never played the game.
I am a survivor. I have been surviving for 2 weeks. I am in a town along the coast, it is know as "elektro" by most. I am rummaging through the tattered houses in search of more food. I plan on heading to the wilderness to live off the land. I find a ripe apple and decide that i am ready to leave. So i pick up my rifle, which i proped against the wall, and i head out the door. I walk down the street a few meters towards the hospital and see a man on the roof. He is in a tattered sweatshirt and a pair of ruined canvas pants. He waves in a friendly manner and i wave back. I faintly hear him shout "Wait down there, for just a second!". But i am nervous that he may be hostile so i pull out my gun and keep it firmly at my side. He eagerly climbs down the ladder of the building and runs out into the street. He says "Hey there sir!" with a smile on his face. I camly relpy "Hello." i notice that he is not armed so i put my gun on my back. He says "My name is Terry and i need to ask you a favour." and i tell him to continue. He tells me "I have been robbed time and time again. I have been beaten and thrown to the curb. i have been shown nothing but hate in this world. and i just need it to stop. Can you help me?" Curious by what he means i tell him that we should talk over a quick meal. So we go inside the hospital and go into a room on the second floor. I opened my back pack and layed out some food for us to eat. He seemed very happy about the food and thanked me many times. I asked him again to tell me what he needed. He smiled and nodded as if he forgot about it and just now remembered it. He took a golden compas out of his pocket. It was beautiful, in pristine condition. He looked at it and then quickly handed it to me. "Take it," he said "Not many people are friendly anymore. Not many people are able to be kind and share a meal. I want you to take this compas." i look down at it in my hands, and my eyes glow greedily. "What do you want me to do with it?" i asked. "I want you to pass it on. I want you to give it to the next friendly player that you meet and i want him to pass it on." he continued "i want it to be a sign of kindess." i laughed a little and told him that i would do my very best to pass it on.
We finnished eating and he said that he needed one more favour. I nod at him and he asks that i follow. He takes me to the top of a large hill that over looks the city. There is a bench at the top and he sits on it. I stand behind him and he sighs with what sounds like peace. He says, "Sir i want to thank you for all that you have done, but i need you to end my life. I want my final view to be the city." I am stunned for a bit but... after a while i raise my gun. "Thank you" he says one more time. I put the barrel of my rifle a foot from his head. I tighten my grip. "Youre Welcome Terry." I close my eyes.
And i pull the trigger.
So that was what happened to me this friday :P obviously it was a little exagerated but hey! This game is a beautiful representation of a post apocolyptic war zone. You will be frustated. You will be angry. You will find happiness. You will make both friends and enemies. You will have the ultimate survivor expierience.

[spoiler-free review]
I really, REALLY expected not to like this one.
I, like many others, was put off by the obnoxious fanbase. The fandom for Undertale is so bad that I almost didn't pick it up on principal alone. However, I, against my better judgment, decided to buy it and give it a whirl, if only so I could know what I was talking about when I called it crap. For once, I'm glad that I was wrong. Oh, so horribly wrong.
Undertale is art. There's no two ways around it. The soundtrack is worth the price of admission alone, but what accompanies it is a gorgeous game, with some really interesting visual design behind its pixelated art style. It has a story filled with larger-than-life characters, shockingly unexpected twists, and a bucketful of emotions that overpower you in ways that are really hard to explain.
It is a game that will make you regularly laugh. It is a game that will make you smile. It is a game that will warm your heart. Yet, it is also a game that will make you feel sad. It will make you feel empathy for the characters you interact with. It will make you feel guilt and remind you of your mistakes. It will make you feel regret. And that's great.
It doesn't help that surrounding all this excellent writing and music is a damn good game, too. It's awfully challenging, but also creative in its design. The combat is a mix between simple turn-based RPG mechanics and bullet-hell gameplay, and I'd be lying if I said I didn't enjoy it more than either system alone. It helps that the combat music is insanely catchy and that the game's amazing writing continues on in many of the combat scenarios. I refuse to spoil any more than that, it's truly something unique and deserves to be played first-hand.
Undertale is amazing. Undoubtedly one of the best games released this year, I can recommend it to anyone, especially fans of the Mother series. Filled to the brim with detail, charm, and quirk, it does more than pay homage to the games that inspired it; in many ways, it exceeds them. On top of that, it's only $10. For the price of ten gumballs, you can experience a game that will blow you away and leave you feeling fulfilled from head to toe.
In all, ignore the fandom and get this game. It's a game of the year contender that is well deserving of every cent it costs.

This game is very much a game to play for the story, though.

Rust has been an enjoyable game for me since day 1, though the most recent changes made me rethink my review because the current state of the game is unbalanced and many of the "veterans" think the same way. Starting for the Legacy version, Rust was a great survival game, where raiding was a great thing to establish and you kind of worked hard for it. Now, after the new shape of the game, with the graphics (which I am pleased of and most are likely too) and the updates, which some are good and some are bad, I'd have to say that it is still a lot to work on.
I know that some of you might say that "oh hey, it is still in Alpha", but the Rust developers should also think twice before putting in an update which may make things go unbalanced. A good example would be the heavy armor which was nerfed a month later, and now nobody uses it, and another recent example would be the twig update, where you can build and place ladders in building blocked zones. Why do we have cupboards for then? I find it very irritating, I've spent 10 hours in one day, to build, protect and collect all of the resources that I needed, and at the blink of an eye, I've lost everything because somebody could jump over 4 layers of high external stone walls and stone gates, build around the house to climb up and eventually use 20 rockets, going upside down, and then ladder their way back up with the loot. It is the most unbalanced thing and the worst update that I've ever seen in a game, which made the things turn the way around.
I also believe that the walls and ceilings, even foundations should be harder to break, that way raiders are forced to use the doors, that way we can use some type of creativy to prevent a raid and defend the base properly. There is a lot to think about now honestly, and raiding just became the most easiest thing, when defending is just impossible unless you have a great clan that can stay on 24/7. I love raiding, but when you make it that easy, I can't enjoy raiding someone because I know how much they've worked to establish a base and work for the resourses, nor I if I get raided and I know how much effort I've put into the game.
Bring back the old Rust, make raiding a great thing to accomplish and then we'll speak about changing my review and the recommendation note. Peace.

This game is quite a lot of fun, but there are too many elements lacking to recommend this game for the current asking price on steam(yes it is an Alpha stage game). I do however recommend this game based upon how fun it is because I like survival type games.
Game: I love the ability to craft in this game, as a survivor of war I am also fond of survival themed games, this is definitely more of a survivor game than it is a zombie game(more on that soon). There is no hand holding in this game, you have to figure out everything through google(crafting, map, what you can and can't do, and basic game knoweldge); except for the control scheme which you can look at in game via the menus.
Zombie population seems to be very random and some servers spawn them at different rates than others. The Zombie ai is absolute crap, but when did a Zombie ever have ai to begin with...this game is in Alpha stage and not a finished product; as such Zombies glitch through walls like ghosts even when you shut every door to a room/house. This didn't really annoy me, but it needs fixing of course. I play this game to hunt other human players, and this part is fun. You are forced to do so since the Zombie mechanics are poor, and because all other players will kill you on sight so they can loot your corpse in the hopes of obtaining a few bullets or a can of tuna; others will kill you just for the sake of being blood thirsty morons who have never stepped outside of their mothers basement.
My first play was very enjoyable for me. Having known that this game is rife with murderous bandit human players before purchasing, I knew in advance what to expect. I saw two human players in the town streets...teamed up and fully geared up with backpacks and loaded rifles. I decided it would be fun to manipulate them. I had no weapons whatsoever, and had just spawned in the area...
They did not see me initially, I ran in between both of them quickly and then started zig zagging my character around them as they kept firing their rifles and missing, I then punched one of them in the face a few times as I was moving around them. I then ran off in between two houses nearby and circled around the other side of the area and off to an angle towards a nearby treeline. Before reaching the tree line I immediately went into a prone position into the low grass which was tall enough to hide me. I was wearing green tshirt and brown pants to aid in my camoflauge for the game.
At this point the 2 human players thought that I was still in town and hiding inside of a building. I watched them for about 10-15mins furiously run around the houses and go inside each and every one of them. About 20 houses total. I just laid comfortably on my stomach in the prone position from the treeline/grass and enjoyed the show as these two knuckleheads kept searching for me in a bloody thirsty running frenzy. I had my character eat a can of tuna while enjoying the show!

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Good-
-Beautiful graphics and 3d models
-Survival game, finding weapons and items.
-Sneaking up on another human player to kill them.
-Semi-Realistic in item dispersion and crafting
-Large Beautiful countryside map(Chernarus)
-Looting other players
-Hiding and watching other players in groups as they desperately try to find and kill you, the ability to go prone works well and you can hide in low grass and not be seen if you are wearing appropriate camoflauge colors for the surroundings you're in. This aspect I found pretty realistic and my knowledge of real life combat aids me in this game.
-Picking off and killing afformentioned "kill on sight" groups one by one
-Watching the last remaining team mate of the murderous group "panic" as he discovers he is alone and his companion/s have been eliminated by the person they were hunting.
-Watching people team up because of their inherent mental weakness and co dependance, especially when they choose to be murderous bandits.
Bad-
-This game is more like a deathmatch versus other humans than it is a Zombie game
-Kill on sight(KOS) , other human players will immediately kill you on sight. Most do not have/use a mic to speak.
-No incentive to teamup, you are rewarded when you kill people because you can loot all their items.
-You lose all your items when you die
-You start/spawn with nothing but a useless flashlight(using it will get you spotted by other human players)
-You will die often, from other players not Zombies
-You have to find weapons, ammo, and magazines for ammo; all seperately(there is a lot of inventory manipulation to ensure you have room once you do find all the components)
-Open world map is too large, and there is only 1 map, albeit it is very very large. (vehicles would alleviate this)
-No vehicle populations, there are apparently a total of 8-10 vehicles spread across the giant map somewhere.(google for locations)
-Loot/items are too sparse, especially guns.
-Price for  this Alpha game is too high, a 20$ ranged price point would be accetable to the general public.
-Inventory menu is ugly and basic
-Houses and rooms repeat themsevles across the map, but in different combinations
Feedback for the Developer-
-Smaller map, more maps

Re-reviewing this now that I've fully completed the game through one ending.
This game is absolutely brilliant, witty and suprisingly very emotional. You don't realise what you're getting into until the very situation arises and you become quickly attached to the characters. You have a variety of choices which can determine the smallest of things and it's very rewarding to see something that you did earlier causes a difference much later on.
The humour in this game is one of the best i've ever seen in a game. I've actually had to stop playing because of how funny it has become...certain skeletons come to mind. It really puts a smile on your face and there are mini games as well, including a dating simulator which is absolutely hilarious if you've ever felt like you could try your luck on chatting up a monster and seeing where the date takes you.
The story as previously mentioned is very impressive and little decisions can create different variables. There is nothing stopping you sparing every monster or killing every creature, but I won't spoil anything about the story but it is very well written and works perfectly with the humour. After the ending, you can continue on and the story takes quite a turn in turns of the emotion but it works perfectly. Not going to spoil that either!
One of the final things to talk about is the soundtrack. Oh boy, I heard the soundtrack was good from many different sources but wow it is incredible. Of all the games i've played (enough to affect a social life) it's in the top 5 for me of soundtracks. They're very catchy, very entertaining and with certain bosses it can actually be very eery.
Overall if you're looking to buy a game that is reasonably cheap and worth the value, this game, hands down is recommended. If you enjoy RPG's, Drama, Humour, Emotion and Skeletons (Especially that last one ;) ) I recommend Undertale.

First of all, I am not a fan of RPGs myself but I do have my own exceptions. Undertale just entered in this list in the past night, as I am writting this review.
In this game, you play in the skin of a human girl that has fell into the depths of a mountain, where there is a world with monsters sealed away from the surface for many years due to a war where humans ended victorious. In order to the monsters be able to return back to the surface, they need a last human soul out of 7... and that's you. What are you going to do? Will you fight back and destroy them?... Or will you spare them with hopes they won't harm you and understand that humans aren't necessairly murderers? Well, you will be pleased to know that you can actually decide which destiny you want in this game: you can optate to kill every monster you find, you can kill ones and give mercy to others and you can give mercy to everyone. And every little action you do in the game has got consequences in the story. This is the only RPG I know where you can win without killing opponents and that was one of the main reasons I got interested in trying out this game. I went for a Pacifist Route as I really did not want to finish the life of the creatures and let survivors thinking that every human is equal and I can guarantee that your actions are rewarded in surprising ways! You also end up getting attached to the most important characters of the game as each has got a different personality and are really memorable!
Now, I will talk about the game by parts and tell what I think about each:
Story - The essence of Undertale's story is simple as I explained above but it is impressive the level of depth it has got as I can really tell that these indie developers have put a lot of thought in it not just by having experienced the game but also by informing myself on the internet about the other kind of consequences it can bring depending of other types of actions you do. There are really many different versions of the story. There's drama but there is also a lot of humour, dark humour and references to japanese culture and I promise that this game will steal you smiles and laughters!
Graphics - Other thing that pleases me in Undertale is the retro aesthetic it has got but this is just a matter of personal taste. They are pleasant and detailed. It interestingly changes to a more minimalist graphism once you enter in a battle. There's a detail that I won't develop a lot as it involves spoilers but there is a point where I really believe you will feel disturbed by the type of visual a certain monster adquires for being distinctively "out of place".
Gameplay - In third person it works like a normal RPG: you wander around to explore the environments and you interact with characters to obtain informations. Ocasionally, you will be dragged to battle with a random monster. Fortunately, the encounters are not annoying as they do not appear a lot of times. In battle, you have four options: to fight (a graph appears and a vertical bar passes through it. The more centered the bar is by the moment you press your key, more damage you inflict), to act (this functionality is really interesting as the secondary options that appear really depend of the monster you find, and even in here the creators used a lot of humour!), to use items (like in normal RPGs, items can be used to heal HP or to increase stats) and to give mercy (monsters will be spared from harm but it won't work unless you performed necessary actions in the Act command although this rule only applies to the majority of the monsters). The way battles work has got an original mechanism as I never saw something similar before: your soul is represented with a red heart and inside a limited area you can move it to dodge yourself from enemy attacks that vary a lot. There are occasions where you have your soul limited to specific movements too or that you are exposed to special enemy attacks that force you to either freeze yourself or to move yourself to ensure you don't get harmed. You really need to have dexterity in your fingers as some enemies attacks (especially bosses) can be really difficult to dodge. A note I would like to make is that in case you want to spare every monster, is the fact that every monster you find has got a different way to be "defeated" and they are not only creative but will also surprise you and make you laugh a lot!
Controls - I don't have got a single complaint in these: they are simple and very sharp. If you are enoughly familiar with playing with a keyboard you won't have any issues.
Sound and music - Just like the graphics, these are retro-like. The sounds are varied and simple. While there is not a lot of different musical tracks in the game I found them pleasant.
Difficulty level - The level of difficulty is progressive and is challenging but not to the point of frustration.
Longevity and replay value - I finished the game in approximately 10 hours but the time of conclusion might vary depending of the player skills and the destiny you choose. It is relatively short, but the fact that your actions change the whole story course gives you extra reasons to consider returning to the game and play it again.
I am really happy that a game like this appeared in an industry overflooded with games with the same selling formulas and same conception formulas. It brought a completely new way to play an RPG and hooks you to the end. I do think the industry needs more games like this as with the technology evolution many game makers seem to forget what's most important in the conception of a videogame: its essence, its soul.
Undertale is a hidden indie gem that deserves recognization. I really can't find any complaint for it as I never found any annoyances in it nor even glitches. And this game can be yours for only 9,99€, a real bargain. Please buy it, it is worth every cent. And spread the word: Determination.

This game, is AMAZING.
I'm just going to get that out the way first up since I don't really know how to review this without spoiling EVERYTHING. And this is a game that NEEDS to be played blind. With all the jokes and story points it will not be as great of an experience if ANYTHING is spoiled for you, except for the secrets, maybe.
Alright. Time for the ACTUAL review.
Let's start with the soundtrack, since it can be described in one word: PERFECT
Honestly, this is the best soundtrack I have ever heard. I love the use of both chiptune and real (recorded samples, maybe) instruments. Every song is superb and has its own place. If you were to ask me what my favourite track from the game is, I wouldn't be able to tell you.
The graphics are very nice, reminiscent of consoles such as the Commodore 64 all the way to the Game Boy Advanced (Skipping one or two), and something else... (Not telling because it would spoil it, somewhat). They don't add or subtract anything (Except one part. You'll know what it is) but were worth mentioning anyway.
The story has got to be the defining factor for this game. Without as great a story as this, the game would probably be a "good" instead of "OMG IT'S THE BEST GAME EVER" (Sorry). It isn't one of those games where the story is incredibly rich at the very beginning. It actually starts with a very small story that could be put into a 1980s NES game. However, the more you play, the more you explore and the more you want to find, you more you will find. There are just so many details that all correlate with each other. I can't really say anymore without spoiling some of the game, so you'll just have to trust me on this one.
The gameplay is quite fun as well. Instead of having turns that bounce back between the player and the opponent, like a traditional JRPG, The player attacks with a simple QTE and dodges the enemy attacks like a Shoot em up. It's a very interesting and fun twist on the old way of battling.
Undertale is easily my Game of the Year and possibly my favourite game EVER. (It's still contending with Terraria for the number one spot). Even though it isn't a game you can play over and over and over again, the quality of this game absolutely outstanding. So good job Toby Fox for making this brilliant game, and making me spend half an hour on a review.
Final Score - 10.000000001/10

This game would be fun. It is also ruined, making it impossible to enjoy.
You see, the game has no option to actually reset. It's not just well-hidden, or even done by uninstalling and reinstalling.
It just doesn't. So if you were planning on enjoying it fully more than once, well, you're S.O.L.
And theres the fact that a game full of secrets has the gall to only give you one chance, on the first playthrough, to find them all. So I hope you can get it perfect in one! Because this game will actively endevour to make you have a worse time if you don't. It' snot that you CAN'T play it over, it's just that the game remembers your choices, and gives you no chance to find anything you missed. That, and if you enjoyed it the first time you played, well thats it. The game will never let you do that again. But I hear you: "Isn't this game all about the weight of choices?" Yes! Which is why it's bull that it never lets you see how things would have gone differently. Not to mention that it's a VIDEO GAME: the entire point is escapist entertainment, which it withholds on the basis of no more than "♥♥♥♥ you, you didn't do it right."

P.S: This is all coming from somone who played full pacifist, and just wanted to see if I missed a few things. It's even worse if you went with the alternate route.

I wake up groggy, and alone on the beach. The emptiness in my belly tells me I haven't eaten in quite some time, and after a brief survey of my surroundings- I decide to find something to sedate my growing appetite.
As I embark on my trek several things come to my attention, there aren't any cars hustling up and down the streets. Aside from the birds chirping, I hadn't stumbled across another person. "What's going on..?" I ask myself while I slowly march in the direction I think that North is.
After a few hours I come to the outskirts of a town who's name I can't make out. The characters printed on the sign looked Russian, but thats weird.. Last thing I remember is dancing and drinking on the cruise ship.
I probably would have stood there pondering my situation for hours if it weren't for the terrifying scream that cut through the silence. I shuddered, "What the f%^& was that?".
As if on cue, the culprit rounded the corner clumsily. I mean.. it LOOKED like it use to be a person. But something was seriously wrong, it's flesh was sagging and distorted, as if someone picked it up and wrung it dry. Its eyes, glossy and discolored studied it's surroundings with a slight disinterest. Until, it saw me.
It screamed, as if it was overjoyed, then suddenly broke into a mad dash in my direction. The only logical thing for me to do was turn tail and run. I darted to the left, cutting through several buildings who's doors had been conviently left open. I could hear the thing cackling and squealing as it gave chase, the fear of being overtaken by whatever it was put extra fuel into my tank.
Eventually, I managed to shake it and sought refuge in some sort of bar. After scavanging through the rooms I managed to find myself a few cans of food, a sledgehammer, a bottle of water, several cans of soda,  a rusty can opener, and most importantly someone's old hunting rifle. Not to mention a pair of cargo pants, a brown hoodie, and a child's briefcase to hold my things.
I want to say I was feeling confident, like I had felt prepared for what this strange place had in store for me. But that would be a lie. In all honesty... I was terrified. My hands were shaking as I gripped the handle of the sledge hammer, and after a bit of coaching.. I set off back into the fray.
I walked for what seemed like forever, only stopping to snack on my provisions and call out to anyone that may have been hiding in some of the buildings I'd come across. To my surprise those monsters that darted around in human disguises were numerous in number. Some of them even wore military uniforms.
Eventually I came to discover a junk yard of some sorts.. rusted husks that barely rested on deflated wheels littered the surroundings, the building seemed secure enough so without placing too much thought into it I ventured inside.
I'd immediately moved to the restroom to relieve myself. Tactical Bacon and Baked Beans didn't sit too well with me. I didn't bother flushing before I turned to leave.
That's when I saw him.
He stood in doorway silently, assessing me I suppose.
"Oh damn, man. You scared me... You alright?"
....
He didn't respond.
"You need some food or something?"
....
Still nothing.
"I have plenty man, its no big deal.."
The man tilted his head to the side, raising his right hand to fashion his fingers to mimic a gun and pointed it at his own head. I didn't understand.
"You want me to kill you?" I asked nerviously, stepping closer to him.
Big mistake.
No sooner did I make it within arm's reach he had already hit me twice. I staggered, the white hot pain that bloomed in my vision dazed me. I raised my fist out of instinct and swung a swift jab.
It sailed off mark and the stranger rained a series of blows that collided against my skull and rattled my brain.
Then everything went dark.
A few moments pass, and I could feel his hands rummaging through my pockets, relieving me of the items I had gathered. My eyes fluttered open long enough to see him heft my sledgehammer over his head.. There was no emotion in his face as he swung it down with grim intent.. I didn't even have time to scream.

I went into this game blind, despite the massive fan following it has already achieved everyone I know was very careful about spoilers. The non-spoilery things I did know, that made me want to play the game:
* You can choose to spare the lives of the creatures you meet rather than just mowing through mooks
* There are a lot of silly moments
* There are friendly skeletons in it
* Lots of the webcomic artists I respecte/follow were excited about this game
Non-spoilery reasons-to-play I can add to this post-playing through to the True Ending:
* The moral choices in this game actually feel important, because it isn't just a case of aesthetic like some games (that I also love) where taking a more evil approach changes available quests, your look and feel, some NPC reactions, and you know, how you feel about your character... the moral choices in Undertale are so well thought out. It requires more effort and commitment, generally, to do the right thing. The payoff for being a kind person is so much greater for that. Kindness can come with a lot of hardship. But man, it feels good.
* There are so many commonly accepted tropes and gameplay mechanics that this game subverts in playful, and sometimes horrifying ways, that really shake you out of your comort zone and make you exclaim "ahahaha oh my god you smartass" and I love it
* I actually care a lot about some of the NPCs, both main and support roles, because of how well their characters were built up to be someone you can empathise with
* Magnolia Porter, the creator of Monster Pulse, helped create some of the monsters in this game. If you like Monster Pulse, you will definitely enjoy this game. Magnolia is a legend.
* The True Ending - you really feel you've earned it, and there's still a bittersweet note to it that makes you unable to stop thinking about the game and characters once it is done. I want to replay the game just so I can comfort one character again... which, that's extreme. I don't know if I've ever felt that way about a character in a game before TBH. I've loved plenty, but not enough to replay a game just to be nice to them again for one scene!
* I will be buying this game for as many friends as possible because the world needs to encourage more stories like this.

You can largely bypass the endless spawnkilling and get a weapon (if you don't get ripped apart by zombies first) by joining low-populaton servers, but then it's just dull since it's next to impossible to find other players. None of this would really be as frustrating to me as it is except that you lose all your progress when you die and have to restart the process all over again. It makes the work you put into the game all for nothing. Honestly, unless they do something to disincentivize players from killing everyone simply for existing or allow you to keep SOME of the things you had before death (only like 10%-30% of your things) and give fresh spawns anything to defend themselve with, I can't see myself playing this game much longer.
Would I reccomend this game? I'm not sure. It all depends on how much rage you can handle before punching a hole through your wall or door (which I have done twice as a result of this game).

I went into this game blind, despite the massive fan following it has already achieved everyone I know was very careful about spoilers. The non-spoilery things I did know, that made me want to play the game:
* You can choose to spare the lives of the creatures you meet rather than just mowing through mooks
* There are a lot of silly moments
* There are friendly skeletons in it
* Lots of the webcomic artists I respecte/follow were excited about this game
Non-spoilery reasons-to-play I can add to this post-playing through to the True Ending:
* The moral choices in this game actually feel important, because it isn't just a case of aesthetic like some games (that I also love) where taking a more evil approach changes available quests, your look and feel, some NPC reactions, and you know, how you feel about your character... the moral choices in Undertale are so well thought out. It requires more effort and commitment, generally, to do the right thing. The payoff for being a kind person is so much greater for that. Kindness can come with a lot of hardship. But man, it feels good.
* There are so many commonly accepted tropes and gameplay mechanics that this game subverts in playful, and sometimes horrifying ways, that really shake you out of your comort zone and make you exclaim "ahahaha oh my god you smartass" and I love it
* I actually care a lot about some of the NPCs, both main and support roles, because of how well their characters were built up to be someone you can empathise with
* Magnolia Porter, the creator of Monster Pulse, helped create some of the monsters in this game. If you like Monster Pulse, you will definitely enjoy this game. Magnolia is a legend.
* The True Ending - you really feel you've earned it, and there's still a bittersweet note to it that makes you unable to stop thinking about the game and characters once it is done. I want to replay the game just so I can comfort one character again... which, that's extreme. I don't know if I've ever felt that way about a character in a game before TBH. I've loved plenty, but not enough to replay a game just to be nice to them again for one scene!
* I will be buying this game for as many friends as possible because the world needs to encourage more stories like this.
I'm the kind of person who gets off-put by fandom hype, but trust me, this game has earned the hype.

The battle just to get established can very well put people off and it's mostly a resource gathering grinding trek. There is no true way of getting to the top without some miracle. Most servers already have their top dogs, their trolls, their raiders, etc. The best spots are usually taken and if they aren't, they're not for a good reason.
The sad thing about this game is that the potential is there. I can see it, but its just out of reach.
I can't see this game as a worthy investment of time because everything you build can be so easily destroyed in a matter of minutes if the server population demands it. If grinding resources to build something is up your alley, then this game is fine. But as it stands, I can't in good conscience spend anymore time in this game, because the only ending is ultimately disappointment.
________________________
THE ADVENTURES OF TRYING TO GET THE GAME TO WORK!
My experience with this game involves everything except actually playing. While my time in this game technically is 71 or so minutes, the amount of time actually in-game and not in a bloody loading screen amounts to about less than a minute.
First off, my install somehow broke, and so I had to install it again. That Anti-Cheat software that came with it also failed to install when it popped up the first time, and so I had to find that and make sure it installed. I had to go into the files and set the executables to Admin mode. I then set the graphics settings to Fastest and waited. When the game began playing (HA!) I had to set its priority to high in Task Manager.
After ALL OF THAT, I had to sit through intensively long loading screens. Most of the time the game would crash on the loading screen for both the main menu and when connecting to the servers and loading the map.
But finally, FINALLY entered the game twice, and witnessed the glory that is Rust! For a solid 10 seconds of slideshow-rate frames and freezing before I was kicked from the server (I tried several). I tried another and it just couldn't be bothered to go into the loading screen before kicking me back to the main menu.
I have fought with this game for every minute I have played it, and it absolutely refuses to run for me, so I cannot recommend this game based on that fact. I am lucky twice-over in that I can get a refund, and that this game was a gift from a friend who thankfully can get his money back. The only redeeming quality from this fruitless endevour is that the main menu music tickled my fancy.

Undertale is one of the greatest, most emotional games I've ever played.
Now that that's out of the way let me elaborate why it earns such a title.
When i started Undertale i was not sure what i was expecting. I knew that it was famous for its characters and great storytelling, which was promptly proven to me by the first NPC i met ingame. I barely interacted with her for 30 minutes, but already  is she close to my heart. Over the course of about 15 hours (!) I met amazing characters that felt truly alive. They had their ups and downs, likes and dislikes and every moment I was able to spend with them was a joyous one.
The dialogue of this game was produced in an incredibly great quality. Sometimes witty comments made me burst out in laughter, other times i had to supress tears when hearing about someones backstory.
The soundtrack in Undertale is just as great as the characters. Never did a track feel unfitting. I would even go as far as to say the OST was as great as the one of the Hotline Miami franchise, and that is the highest praise I can give.
The only criticism I have to express is the fighting system. The bullethell part was a fun idea, but at some points it was incredibly hard and sometimes even frustrating. This is just something minor though, because what followed those hard fights was always worth it.
If you took the time to read all of this or just skipped to the bottom to read the final recommendation I won't hold you any longer. Just get this game, trust me, it will be worth it.

THE ADVENTURES OF TRYING TO GET THE GAME TO WORK!
My experience with this game involves everything except actually playing. While my time in this game technically is 71 or so minutes, the amount of time actually in-game and not in a bloody loading screen amounts to about less than a minute.
First off, my install somehow broke, and so I had to install it again. That Anti-Cheat software that came with it also failed to install when it popped up the first time, and so I had to find that and make sure it installed. I had to go into the files and set the executables to Admin mode. I then set the graphics settings to Fastest and waited. When the game began playing (HA!) I had to set its priority to high in Task Manager.
After ALL OF THAT, I had to sit through intensively long loading screens. Most of the time the game would crash on the loading screen for both the main menu and when connecting to the servers and loading the map.
But finally, FINALLY entered the game twice, and witnessed the glory that is Rust! For a solid 10 seconds of slideshow-rate frames and freezing before I was kicked from the server (I tried several). I tried another and it just couldn't be bothered to go into the loading screen before kicking me back to the main menu.
I have fought with this game for every minute I have played it, and it absolutely refuses to run for me, so I cannot recommend this game based on that fact. I am lucky twice-over in that I can get a refund, and that this game was a gift from a friend who thankfully can get his money back. The only redeeming quality from this fruitless endevour is that the main menu music tickled my fancy.

Instead of going into the many, huge reasons as to why I love the game, instead I will go into the things that Toby has overlooked or otherwise neglected in the demo alone, because anything further than that is spoilers.
First and foremost, the commands in combat are simple enough: FIGHT makes you attempt to deal damage to the enemy, ACT gives you fun commands like * Talk, * Unhug, and * Flirt, just to name a few. Each enemy has specific commands special to them. ITEM uses items, nothing special here. You can either equip a weapon / armor or outright just use an item to heal yourself. Finally, there's Mercy. In it at any point in time is the *Spare option. Usually when an enemy's name is yellow, you can choose to spare it, gaining no EXP but gaining some GP. Also there is the *Flee command, which is necessary to spam at least one point in the game if you want the 'best' ending, but otherwise, the chance of fleeing from enemies is random, and at some spots, extremely low.
The first area you will see in the game (and the ONLY area you will see in the demo) is the RUINS. This is the tutorial of the game, and it introduces you to many creatures that are already spare-able, some that require certain steps of ACT and/or combat to be able to spare. It also introduces you to the idea of puzzles that require memorization of floor layouts. This is the first of many downfalls for two reasons. The first is that you either love the RUINS or you hate it. The theme can, at times, get a bit long and arduous, especially if you keep failing particular puzzles. Secondly, compared to the rest of the game, if you think that you'll have a riot laughing hard in the demo you are sorely mistaken. Aside from maybe one other location, the ruins can be actually quite boring and off-putting. Lastly is the boss of the RUINS and of the demo. I have heard stories upon stories of people accidentally killing this boss when they expected something different, went to reset, and got chastised for fixing their mistakes, putting them off the rest of the game.
If you want to get the full experience from the game and not be put-off by a sociopathic omnicidal flower, suffer through the RUINS and mash "Spare" on the boss. You'll skip turns, yes, but the boss knows what's best for you, and in time, will see your point of view. It's unorthodox and it doesn't make much sense, but to put it in a phrase, "At some point you may have to SPARE an enemy even if their name isn't yellow."
So why am I still giving this game a solid recommendation? It's because the rest of the game is, while still not flawless, an excellent test of your knowledge of bullet-hell mechanics, your ability to listen to the words that people say, and knowing how your decisions will change the game. It's also pretty humorous, with characters ranging from an unhelpful, but really kind and supportive skeleton being your cool friend, to a cloistered otaku lizard who gushes WAY too much about anime on social media and an over-the-top homocidal robot that is best described as George Takei and David Bowie putting their consciousnesses into a robot, and the robot overusing the 'ham' function in conjunction with 'glamour' to make 'hammour'.
Point is, if you're not put-off by the game at the demo it's an enjoyable romp through to the end that, while difficult at times, may bring well-deserved tears, be they from joy or sadness.

Undertale. This game is amazing. I would go into detail about the characters and plot, but that would ruin the game for you. I am going to rate the game in different categories instead.
Music: 10/10. There isn't a single track I disliked. They were all very good.
Gameplay: 10/10. The bullet hell RPG system where you can spare enemies is VERY cool.
Plot: 11/10. The plot is AMAZING. If you make a slight change to your gameplay in a later playthrough, different things in the story can happen. For example, if you spare everyone, you get a TON of brand new scenarios and the true final boss. This could go under gameplay, but I feel like it's more important to the plot than it is the gameplay. The story is very tear-jerking at some points and is really funny at others, making a great mix.
Characters: 9/10. The characters are great. My personal favorite is Sans the skeleton, who makes bad puns all the time. I would say more about him, but that way you would have a bad time (heh heh) when you play the game. Would be 10/10 if Alphys wasn't a thing...
Endings: 10/10. The 3 main endings are good, but there are about 10 different endings depending on who you spare, kill, or hang out with. I've only seen 4 of the endings (Pacifist, Genocide, Neutral, and a minor ending that I won't go into detail about since it has spoilers).
Overall: 10/10. Can't recommend this game enough. On my 2nd pacifist run now. Buy it now. Don't wait for a sale. JUST DO IT!

THE ADVENTURES OF TRYING TO GET THE GAME TO WORK!
My experience with this game involves everything except actually playing. While my time in this game technically is 71 or so minutes, the amount of time actually in-game and not in a bloody loading screen amounts to about less than a minute.
First off, my install somehow broke, and so I had to install it again. That Anti-Cheat software that came with it also failed to install when it popped up the first time, and so I had to find that and make sure it installed. I had to go into the files and set the executables to Admin mode. I then set the graphics settings to Fastest and waited. When the game began playing (HA!) I had to set its priority to high in Task Manager.
After ALL OF THAT, I had to sit through intensively long loading screens. Most of the time the game would crash on the loading screen for both the main menu and when connecting to the servers and loading the map.
But finally, FINALLY entered the game twice, and witnessed the glory that is Rust! For a solid 10 seconds of slideshow-rate frames and freezing before I was kicked from the server (I tried several). I tried another and it just couldn't be bothered to go into the loading screen before kicking me back to the main menu.
I have fought with this game for every minute I have played it, and it absolutely refuses to run for me, so I cannot recommend this game based on that fact. I am lucky twice-over in that I can get a refund, and that this game was a gift from a friend who thankfully can get his money back. The only redeeming quality from this fruitless endevour is that the main menu music tickled my fancy.
