Undertale Review (Spoiler Free)
I don’t know where to start, other than the fact that thi is one of the greatest games of all time, if not the best of all time. Undertale is filled with emotion and heart to the core, and every human being on this planet MUST PLAY IT. I have already come to the conclusion that this is a tremendous game, as well as the game of the year, this review is simply just for the record. At first sight, this Indie JRPG may seem like a silly fandom at first, but once you play it, you will understand the high scores and abundance of recommendations.
Gameplay:
First to start, Undertale works with the JRPG style of gameplay, but takes it to the next level.
As you journey on through, you will encounter some enemies, and in battle, you have the choice to either fight and kill them, or have a friendly conversation and spare them while doing this little game where you have to dodge the enemies attacks. All of these attacks are varied and different from one another, some will even combine to make a difficult challenge.
Weapons and armor do exist in the game, with some funny choices like a tutu or an apron as armor, or a toy knife as a weapon.
Undertale is also made up of puzzles, each interesting, like the puzzles in the waterfall, where you have to use light to guide you to the end, or the shooting gallery mini game in hotland.
Also, this games covers real morality tremendously with heavy choice and consequence gameplay. For example, I killed one of the characters in the beginning, and felt bad about, so I went back and saved her. But after I saved her, I was greeted by another character who claimed he knew what I did, that I killed her before, and that he knows about my power to “save the game”
They game has plenty of 4th wall breaks such as this one, or even one where one character literally crashed my game!
Story:
Undertale’s story starts as a base concept of a young boy falling down a hole into the land of the monsters in a time where both humans and monsters are divided from each other after war. You are greeted by Toriel a sweet, mother-like character who emits powerful emotion to the player. Eventually, the player catches onto the fact that he must return home, so Toriel has a sorrow filled goodbye, and a battle with her to prove that you are ready to advance. You can either spare her by talking to her, or kill her. You later meet wonderful characters like Sans and Papyrus, two skeletons. Sans is a kind, cool, and hilarious character who constantly makes funny wisecracks. Papyrus is part of the royal guard, and while he is very stupid, he is a funny character, who gives you joy if you chose to be his friend. There are other characters along the way like Undyne, Alphys, Asgore, and more, but I don’t want to ruin your first interactions with any of these characters. The game seems like it gets into the odd fact of while these characters are monsters, they are kind and nice to you, and you have the choice to be a good friend with them or be a total jerk. The game does a great job overall with the concept of real morality in these kind of instances. Each character will think differently depending if you killed or spared specific characters.
While it seems like there are 3 endings, those endings have many different variations all depending on your interaction with the other characters, and if you are a true friend to each of them. Each ending has it charms to it, especially the Pacifist ending, which left me in tears.
Visuals:
While it is 8-bit, I found myself stopping to look at the pure art design in each diverse section of Undertale. Also, while all of the enemy sprites are black and white, the are welly illustrated, each different than one another and with it’s own unique concept matching that character’s nature.
Music:
I have literally got the entire soundtrack on my phone because I love it so much. This is easily one of the best gaming soundtracks of all time, from it’s cool battle themes like Megalovania, to the nice and emotional acoustic Undertale Theme, but other than that, there are too many great songs to name, for they are all perfect and greatly used in their specific times and areas.
Overall:
A Video Game hasn’t made me feel this amazement ever since Deus Ex in 2000, but even more is the fact of the emotional mark this game has left on me, with it’s brilliantly written characters, and incredible music and gameplay with choice, and the incredible ending. To me, I can come to the conclusion that this is personally the greatest game of all time to me. if you have not expirienced this master piece by genius Toby Fox, than you are making a huge mistake.

There's the potential for this game to be great, but it just isn't there, and it isn't worth your money at this point.
I do not recommend this game for three reasons.  1) The game is essentially a deathmatch.  2) The community is truly terrible.  3) The bugs, constant crashes, and character resets make it a waste of time.
1) You may occassionally run into someone who isn't a total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, but those encounters are rare.  Usually, they will shoot at you on sight, whether you are armed or not.  Robberies can be fun, even if you're the victim, because of the interaction, but they almost never happen.  If anyone does speak with you, there's a decent chance they'll be lying, and kill you when you're not looking.  The only chance of having fun is if you play with your friends, but that's true of everything.
2) This ties in with the first.  The broader point to be made is that for something that bills itself as a zombie survival game, it has little, if anything, to do with zombies.  There is no horde to watch out for, no real objective involving the zombies themselves, and you get nothing from killing them, save for ending the annoyance of having to deal with them in the first place.  With no common enemy, people just shoot eachother, and it gets old in a hurry.  You work for hours to gear up, gather food, procure a weapon, ammo, the works...  And then someone you don't see shoots you in the back.  That's the typical DayZ life-cycle.  If you enjoy trolling, then you'll have a blast, because there are endless opportunities for it.  Otherwise, steer clear.
3)  This game refers to itself as being in "alpha," which should deter you.  You will lose your character often, and for no fault of your own.  You'll be kicked and your client will crash, again often for no fault of your own.  And you're also at the whim of hackers and the like, who make an already frustrating experience even more frustrating.  Not to mention the new "survival" systems, which constantly glitch your character into death.  Wet shoes turn into hypothermia at an alarming rate.  Constant rain makes moving around outside - combined with the bugginess of the "system" - a death sentence.  Moreover, these sytems cause the game to look different - presumably to immerse you in the experience - but these systems also often cause your fps to slow to a crawl.  Additionally, your game may run fine, but when another player comes around the corner, they will be flying all over the screen just as your connection stutters and your fps slows again.
I've obviously played a lot of this game.  Some friends and I have had some good times too.  But this was in spite of the game, not because of it.  Your money, and more importantly, your time, is better spent elsewhere.

I have never in my life played a game that was so over-hyped that actually lived up to it. I figured I'd pop in and just leave this here for anyone that has not gotten this game yet. It is a MUST BUY! It is a MUST PLAY! It will be a staple in a class of its own and an instant classic. It really is that superb of a game. And if you have not personally played it you are doing yourself a disservice as a gamer.
* If you remember that whoa experience the 1st time you played Final Fantasy as a kid or got introduced to RPGs - Play Undertale.
* If you remember that "whoa" emotion the first time you jumped into game experiences like the first time you were introduced to the massive expanse of Halo, that "dangerous to go alone, take this" of Zelda, that "OMG, my decisions mattered?!?!" of games like Fable with surprises like Mass Effect...Play Undertale.
What I am saying here is Undertale evokes an emotion that will remain in your memory and cherished like these games, the mechanics of the game itself are different but easy to play. No sitting around figuring out for hours how to best equip yourself, no backtracking forever for that special sidequest, no achievement to tryhard or OCD into. The game is just damn enjoyable from start to finish.
It is an RPG, but it isn't a grind fest. Some of it is linear, and it can be completed in under 5 hours to those really racing through it....and there are different endings. Sometimes we get so lost in those grinds and massive worlds that we forgot the experience of the story that made games like Zelda and Final Fantasy so great. Undertale accomplishes this and even makes gamers question the very philosophy of EXP and LVL. This game grabs you, and it intelligently goes deeper in a way no game has done before. The soundtrack is amazing! Complete with nuances and nods to Earthbound, Super Smash, Zelda, and Final Fantasy, Mega Man, Mario, Metroid, - it is just incredible composing and musical scoring. The commentary is amazing, the way it is put together and crafted is art in itself. It has been a very very very very very long time since I have played a game so worthy of praise, so good at tugging at my emotions, superb in reviving the nostalgia that was my childhood...it truly is an instant classic! I have never in my life played a game that was so over-hyped that actually lived up to it. I figured I'd pop in and just leave this here for anyone that has not gotten this game yet. It is a MUST BUY! It is a MUST PLAY! It will be a staple in a class of its own and an instant classic. It really is that superb of a game. And if you have not personally played it you are doing yourself a disservice as a gamer.
* If you remember that whoa experience the 1st time you played Final Fantasy as a kid or got introduced to RPGs - Play Undertale.
* If you remember that "whoa" emotion the first time you jumped into game experiences like the first time you were introduced to the massive expanse of Halo, that "dangerous to go alone, take this" of Zelda, that "OMG, my decisions mattered?!?!" of games like Fable with surprises like Mass Effect...Play Undertale.
What I am saying here is Undertale evokes an emotion that will remain in your memory and cherished like these games, the mechanics of the game itself are different but easy to play. No sitting around figuring out for hours how to best equip yourself, no backtracking forever for that special sidequest, no achievement to tryhard or OCD into. The game is just damn enjoyable from start to finish.
It is an RPG, but it isn't a grind fest. Some of it is linear, and it can be completed in under 5 hours to those really racing through it....and there are different endings. Sometimes we get so lost in those grinds and massive worlds that we forgot the experience of the story that made games like Zelda and Final Fantasy so great. Undertale accomplishes this and even makes gamers question the very philosophy of EXP and LVL. This game grabs you, and it intelligently goes deeper in a way no game has done before. The soundtrack is amazing! Complete with nuances and nods to Earthbound, Super Smash, Zelda, and Final Fantasy, Mega Man, Mario, Metroid, - it is just incredible composing and musical scoring. The commentary is amazing, the way it is put together and crafted is art in itself. It has been a very very very very very long time since I have played a game so worthy of praise, so good at tugging at my emotions, superb in reviving the nostalgia that was my childhood...it truly is an instant classic! A true 10/10 and probably somewhere in my Top 10 games of all time I have ever played.

DayZ has a great concept but needs time in order to be fully realised. As it stands the game is clearly a long way off being finished though it still manages to be unique and entertaining.
As it is an early access title you can expect bugs and performance issues, I wont sugarcoat this, problems are constant and very much affect the gameplay. This is something that applies to all early access titles and will likely be ironed out over time.
The zombie survival elements of the game are currently minimal which leaves the game with a heavy player vs player focus in its current state. The overall theme of the game feels much closer to "The Road" than the Dawn of the Dead type scenarios you often see in other survival focused games.
Players can become bandits and cannibals which allows them to essentially perform as the main antagonists in the game, often with bizarre and humorous results. The infected that feature currently don't work well and generally take away from the game. I wouldn't be surprised if they are cut altogether down the line, they feel like a bit of a loose end.
The main draw of the game are the moments in which you encounter other players. They remain consistently tense and give the game a great atmosphere, though the game could do with giving more reasons for players to work together.
Pairing up with strangers often feels more like it is for the sake of roleplaying than it is any sort of necessity you would require in order to survive. Despite this I have had some great moments doing so and have had some very dynamic situations take place afterwards. A lot of the time there is a huge incentive to just shoot each other and no real reason to utilise teamwork.
I would like to see more focus on both making the world itself more dangerous and on the interaction between players which is easily the most enjoyable part of the game.
I am interested to see where the game goes, it's not really like anything else on the market and has a lot of potential.

TRUST IN RUST.
I came back to completely rewrite my comical review of this game for several reasons, which I must share with you all so you can better understand this game - also, I really wish there was a "Proceed with caution" reccomendation. This game falls under that category.
Here in Rust, there is one singular objective: survive.
At first glance, this sounds intense, from hearing how Garry describes it, intense, viceral, brutal - and, it is, however that's not all this game is anymore. With complete rehauls from the legacy, and even more encouragement towards cooperative play... Things get interesting.
For the past month now (July, 2015) I have been completely binging on this game as I had come from playing the legacy previously, and the rehauls completely engrossed me and sucked me in for 3 weeks straight. I♥♥♥♥♥♥you not, I was up for 3 days straight playing this ♥♥♥♥ing thing.
Yes, this game is a blast. This game is fun, very.
But, it will also completely devastate you and destroy you and tear down your ideas and hopes about life. In my short 3 weeks so far playing it, I discovered the only way to 'win' this game is to have fun. There are no winners or losers in Rust, only players, and player interactions.
This game is a hyper paraody on the human state of mind. Playing this, you will realize that people are terribly wrong all the time even though they and 10 others will say they are right (their friends). And, then, you begin to get engrossed.. And all of a sudden you're in there trying to raid people because you think they're 'wrong' for some reason.. Suddenly you're not raiding a base for fun - you're out on a vendetta. You're out for revenge, you begin to lose sight of the fact that it is all just a game.
The truth is, we're all wrong. If you've read this far into my scatterbrain thoughts on this game I commend you, and this is exactly why I say proceed with caution. Bloody brilliant game though.

Wow, what a fantastic game.
The writing is absolutely fantastic, with interesting characters abound (My favorite is by far Papyrus).The battle mechanics are interesting enough to not get boring because of how each enemy is like a puzzle in and of itself, keeping you on your toes when multiple enemies ambush you and you are forced to think about the best way to dispatch them. The music is also excellent, in and out of fights.
The kill/spare mechanic is amazing with the way it affects the story (which is awesome). The story itself is engaging and kept me interested throughout the entire thing, even when late-game bosses were giving me major headaches. The game is tough enough to be satisfying, but not too overbearing.
In my playthrough, I tried to spare as many as I could, and my mistakes had pretty dire consequences. It was really interesting (and usually pretty emotional) when you see the consequences of your actions.
And holy toledo, let me just say, the ending to this game was like nothing I've really played before, maybe ONE single exception which I won't name as it would spoil what makes it... insane. Really creative stuff here.
Negatives: There's a boss and setting that gets recycled a few times in samey areas that, while not detrimental story-wise, was just a little bit stale by the end of it, at least until the final fight with said boss. Also the lack of initial explanation of the attacking/fighting mechanic (which I used rarely in my playthrough) made it a bit disorienting when I used it the first few fights. Also a personal irk, the graphic style is very charming, but I personally think the game could have benefited from full hand-drawn 2d art to flesh out the world. Sometimes it was hard to recognize what they were trying to depict in their small pixel count, but honestly, the style still works very well with the game.
Also, the lack of an options menu with volume control is a little annoying... the sound is very loud compared to anything else, so I couldn't voice chat with friends while playing.
Overall though, definitely one of my favorite games I've played. A fantastic experience that will have you laughing, tearing up, and questioning what the heck is going on. Major props to Toby Fox and the dev team for making this wonderful adventure.
TL;DR: This game deserves the hype the internet gave it. The fact it was made by such a small team is a testament to gaming as art, as this game IMO is a masterpiece. DEFINITELY pick this one up if you like RPGs, hell, even if you don't, you may just learn to love them. I can't wait to go through another playthrough making different choices and seeing how the game plays out.

This game is, without a doubt, one of my favorite games of all time. With it's open gameplay, loveable characters and immersive storyline, this game is a steal for the price. I'm looking forward to more of Toby's games.

TL;DR It's a great game, awe-inspiringly terrible community, wonderful outlet for sick power fantasies.
Rust is a mixed bag of a game, and wether or not I recommend it is the hardest review decisions I've made. (after playing it some more, It isn't as hard as I first thought. more on that later) The gameplay is simple and not bad at all, the game flows nicely and makes sense, and it looks good, too. Resources are usually pretty self-explanatory to gain, or they flat-out tell you how to make them. The base-building aspect is well balanced and executed, the resources are spread out competently, what you and your characters learn is carried over from server to server, and charactyer to character (ex. a new player may not know how to make an AR, but someone who's 15th out of 83rd character saw it can) the backstory is mysterious and in the background without being nonexistent, and overall the game is quite compitent. This leaves one question left. Why am I relatively turned off from this game? Well, let me answer my own question with another question: have you ever played public Payday 2? Without anyone you knew, just random scrubs who own the server that you're on? If so, this game will feel like a return to the olden days. That's not a good thing. Raiders, pillagers, creeps, and noob-abuse is not only common, it's something you plan for and still fall beneat hthe mighty tread of. The way to start a solo game or even a game with one or two friends is to take your rocks and run for the hills off of spawn beach, to build the beginnings of a base hidden from the prying eyes of nude greifers. The "nakeds" act like savages, the people with guns imitate natural disasters on player populations, and being in between the two phases just means that you get targeted by both. I have fond memories of paying someone for killing one of my earlier nude pursuers only for the guy to break into my house and kill me twice. Yes, you Ex0. You suck. Later, I met a man of similar tastes and tried to start a clan with him. The server died, we moved on, built a new home, learned technologies, had a nooby base of loyal soldiers, and then got ravagted by the server's equivalent of Donald Trump. The reason for this was that we'd killed their newest emmber after he was caught sneaking up on our base, and they sent ROCKETS after us, while we had what we'd found on the dead guy and basic handguns for protection. We died, got killed again by a different group at the second base, then I gave up this pile of♥♥♥♥♥♥forever. Here's the deal, should you decide that you want to check the game out further, ask yourself if you can alternate between murderous paranoia and phsycotic rampages. If so, Rust is the game for you. Otherwise you better be able to do one of those things really well.

Alright time to tackle this elephant in the room. Probably the most hyped up RPG this year, and one that's suckered me in like plenty of others out there. And for good reason, it's an incredibly well crafted RPG along the likes of RPG legends like Square and Atlus.
But Undertale for me, was something very special. I consider it one of the few games that touched my heart.
But first, a bit of backstory.
I used to be very involved with another community. Due to language barriers (it was a game in Japanese), it was best we stayed on good behavior and try to seem like good guests to the sever. For nearly the first year of people migrating, it was great. People where happy, people made friends, hell I almost became a modertor for the one big forum the community had for people migrating to the Japanese servers (there where English servers, but they closed down).
But then all of that joy and fun took a near polar opposite turn.
Suddenly, everyone was full of hatred, wanting to crush everyone who seemed weaker in their eyes, to be the best but just seem vain and selfish in the long run, refusing to help others that where lower than them. Why or how this happened I'll never know. Despite all this I tried my best to keep spreading kind words and positive attitudes, knowing that despite differences, we could work for a greater good, and those who did good would be rewarded and those who where foul and hateful would be punished.
I was eventually shunned out, despite my best efforts. I simply couldn't fit with the new attitude of "Kill or Be Killed" that was floating around. Friends left me, people treated my words like sin, I was mentally kicked out by the majority essentially, seen as a forbidden person in a community I once loved.
So when Undertale came along, I wasn't too impressed. I wanted to hate it so bad like the little♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off hipster I wanted to be.  Overhyped material just wasn't my thing after so long (thanks 5+ years of tumblr). Plus the fact everyone was like "quirky RPG inspired by earthbound" didn't sell me at first since to be fair, I was never the biggest buff on Earthbound.
But then I started to play it after giving a "sure why not" with 10 dollars.
I started to fall in love, with the mechanics, characters, and the music. It took a while, but it all grew on me.
Though, the most emotion came from the game's true ending. Not to give anything away, but I was bawling my eyes out for the first time in YEARS. Not to give anything away, I was overjoyed that something with an incredibly small team of people could bring such passion and well craftsmanship to a game with a strong message to stay positive, to stay determined, and to not give up despite all odds, because out there, some people believe in you very strongly.
It was a good feeling to know that I wasn't the only one who was trying to spread such a message to others. Before I played Undertale, I wanted to loose all hope, I wanted to give up with being positive. I knew there was nothing I could do to help anyone anymore, my words were being ignored. I lost friends, people feared me, and it all felt so unreasonable.
But, a little game like this managed to keep my determination for positive thinking going. I knew that even I only changed a few, it was for the better. I remember the few that they did, they have given me a heartfelt "thank you for everything you've done, please keep doing what you do" over voice chat at least once.
Not to mention this game's music, characters, writing, and fighting system with (Shin Megami Bullet Hell Tensei kind of play style) are all wonderfully done, especially considering the fact mostly just two people worked on it and it was originally asking for only 5,000 USD on kickstarter way back. The amount of work and passion that went into this game is speechless.
Do I have anything to complain about? Not really, it's a very hard game to nitpick. It can be a little tricky doing the combat at first, but you'll get the hang of it.
Quick Review
The Good:
-Writing and Story. If a game can make me cry really hard for over half and hour, it's doing something right. Please scroll above for me gushing about how this game changed me.
-Characters. Probably goes within writing, but honestly everyone was so well written and likable I can never see myself doing a genocide route other than completion purposes.
-Music and Sound Design. Probably one of the strongest points in the game, the music and sound convey an emotion at the right time and place, and ranging from various genres of music. Though the fight themes in this game are my favorite, they're all so great and fitting for what you're fighting, great stuff to listen to and I'd love a hard copy of the game's OST.
-Fight System. As a wise man once said, "Indie Games need something unique to bring otherwise it'll fail and be forgotten with time", and while I've praised this game's ability to bring such emotion to me, the fighting mechanics are very fun and original. It's like a blend of the JRPG Shin Megami Tensei with the ability to negotiate with monsters rather than just kicking them down for XP, and shoot em ups for when an enemy attacks. Plus almost every monster has their own unique challenge attacks, it's really cool.
Graphics: Alright not the best in the world, but I believe only one person did 98% of the spritework. So I give them a lot of props. Plus the game, while drawing inspiration from the cult classic Earthbound, does feel very unique and distinctive.
The Bad:
-The combat system can be a little bit to grasp at first. Though you'll get the hang of it overtime. It's very hard to find negatives about this game in all honesty.
Final Verdict: I had never slammed the "yes" on recommend so fast and so hard on a title before. Not only is it a beautiful game crafted with plenty of love and creativity, but it's a game that honestly touched my heart to keep being a good person, and improve myself in my weaker areas. If I had to make a favorite RPGs top 10, Undertale would definitely be in my top three, perhaps at the #2 slot. One of the finest, heart touching games this year, certainly my personal pick for 2015. Please play this game by legal means if you can, because Toby Fox deserves nearly every cent in my eyes for giving us such a well crafted masterpiece done with so little.

This game. I have so many words to say. With the perfect combination of storytelling and character development, this game introduces new tactics for RPGs in an exciting and original way. Even with it's simple style, Undertale throws surprises at the player left and right, all moving the story forward. I have to say that the characters are the most memorable, and I would give anything to experience the joy of playing it for the first time. Even in different runs than the Pacifist, the game breaks the fourth wall in such a way that it sent a shiver up my spine on multiple occasions. Before undertale, RPGs had never interested me in the slightest. Even after the beginning I was skeptical why I was playing. The characters are so much deeper than wat they seem, they all have so many secrets to explore and so many ways to interact with, they truely are the  best part of the game besides the incredible storytelling. As soon as you think you figured it all out, beat the game, BOOM, it slams you down with something new to figure out. As of now, I have finished the game multiple times and continue to show people the magical world of undertale. All in all, I would extremely reccomend this game to anyone and everyone, it's a one-of-a-time game, and I'm glad that I was here in time for this. Thanks you for making this, it has brought me sadness, laughter, joy, but most of all, it leaves the game in a special place in my heart. Undertale is so much more than a game.

Undertale is, in a word, brilliant. In more words, it's funny, heartfelt, and a ton of fun. If you have $10 dollars, a Steam account, and a computer, buy it. If you don't have a Steam account, buy it on the official website.

This game. I have so many words to say. With the perfect combination of storytelling and character development, this game introduces new tactics for RPGs in an exciting and original way. Even with it's simple style, Undertale throws surprises at the player left and right, all moving the story forward. I have to say that the characters are the most memorable, and I would give anything to experience the joy of playing it for the first time. Even in different runs than the Pacifist, the game breaks the fourth wall in such a way that it sent a shiver up my spine on multiple occasions. Before undertale, RPGs had never interested me in the slightest. Even after the beginning I was skeptical why I was playing. The characters are so much deeper than wat they seem, they all have so many secrets to explore and so many ways to interact with, they truely are the  best part of the game besides the incredible storytelling. As soon as you think you figured it all out, beat the game, BOOM, it slams you down with something new to figure out. As of now, I have finished the game multiple times and continue to show people the magical world of undertale. All in all, I would extremely reccomend this game to anyone and everyone, it's a one-of-a-time game, and I'm glad that I was here in time for this. Thanks you for making this, it has brought me sadness, laughter, joy, but most of all, it leaves the game in a special place in my heart. Undertale is so much more than a game.

I've played rust for a long time, though I find myself quitting for months on end.  Overall I think it's got some entertaining mechanics, and can easily eat up a lot of your time, but you've got to really lower your expectations.
There are some core issues that keep me from recommending the game.  First and foremost, the development team is simply slow. This game has been in alpha forever, and is still barely together.
In no particular order:
+ Map generation is very buggy, pieces of the map can be found floating all over the world
+ Laughabily bad looking water
+ The worlds are boring and consist mostly of vast empty space.
+ Tons of animation issues, especially with animals.
+ Pretty much 0 sense of balance, this is hidden behind the "chaos of survival" style of play.  But once you've played long enough to get past simply surviving, things are just wacky.
+ No sense of progression past basic survival.  Again, progress on the dev side is just reallllly slow.  There are a couple of guns, a couple of sets of clothing, a few random items...  Very little in terms of upgrades, with the exception of walls for your house.
There is enough here to call it a game, but it's all very very unfinished and lacking in depth.  Which considering the length of time it's been in alpha, is pretty silly.
I keep waiting for the big 1.0 patch, where all the secret stuff they have been working on is magically done.  But I think they are working at capacity now, and the plan is to just keep adding a handful of things at a time until it is eventually "done".
If you like survival style games, you can squeeze entertaining out of this.  But it falls flat fairly quickly.

One of the most unique games I've played.
Toby Fox really outdid himself with just about everything in here. Very interesting gameplay, amazing and memorable music, a fantastic sense of humour, characters that will no doubt stick with you for a long time . . . It's one of those games that can be difficult to describe to someone who hasn't played it. Some fans like to compare it somewhat to Earthbound, and while I haven't played much of that myself, I can definitely see what they mean.
There are two primary ways to go about playing this game: being a pacifist or being a genocidal maniac. There seems to be a number of fans who unfortunately forgo the latter because they feel they've become too attached to the characters. Personally, I think doing this unnecessarily excludes yourself from some great experiences that I'd like to see more folks enjoy, so, please, if you do play this, try to remember it's only a video game and you should really get everything you can out of it.
Would certainly recommend this to anyone, particularly those interested in quirky games that do things quite differently.

One of the worst games and concepts ever developed. This game focuses primarily on wasting your real-life time, performing tasks in-game that you could perform faster in real life. Once you've wasted a sufficient amount of time, you will start being killed by other players for no apparent reason and with no given explanation; even if you do not actually possess any materials or have completed any tasks. Whether this is the developers' implicit intentions or not; it actually serves as a perfect equivalent for the Milgram experiment. The assailant rarely has a motive beyond "b-but I was supposed to do it, because that's what I was told to do".
The procedurally generated landscapes are extremely poorly crafted, with thousands of collision errors every square meter, extraordinarily lazy methods of clarifying territorial distinction and numerous other nigh-terminal, extremely blatant flaws. The fauna that inhabit the procedurally generated landscapes possess essentially deific powers to defy the game's internal physics systems and the temporal nature of reality as it stands; often bounding hundreds of meters up a mountain in a single step, or moving backwards whilst their models' actions imply they are moving forward.
The central aim of the game appears to be to gain power by ruining other players' experiences in the game. Anyone who legitimately takes a vested interest in playing this game is most likely sociopathic; and would be much better off working in a biological studies lab, tricking rats into traps to ascertain data on behavioral traits, or working as an abusive (yet not reprimanded) low-security prison officer (with, of course, an ulterior motive of being able to feel superior to their victim in both scenarios).

The fauna that inhabit the procedurally generated landscapes possess essentially deific powers to defy the game's internal physics systems and the temporal nature of reality as it stands; often bounding hundreds of meters up a mountain in a single step, or moving backwards whilst their models' actions imply they are moving forward.

I played the dayz mod for 2 years and besides it's problems and glitches(wich it had a few) it was way more fun, stable and balanced then the standalone ever was.
Take the zombies for once: In the mod, they are slow, easy to trick, not as strong and you can break line-of-sight but there are many of them in exchange of that.
In the standalone, they are fast as hell, will find your exact position 5-10 minutes after a shot even if you moved 1km, you can't really break line-of-sight and they hit you through walls/from meters away so hard that you will die after a few hits.
The performance is ridicoulusly bad, even if your hardware exceeds the recommended specifications, wich is a joke since the required specs stated by the devs are basically a lie.
This either leads to the conclusion that they are willingly tricking potential buyers or they just have no idea how their game performs on an average hardware setting.
The character movement and animations feel clunky and odd at best, often leading to animations blocking other actions and your immediat reaction to a new situation...wich will lead to a quick death eventually.
I never had this problem with the mod, although the animations from arma 2/dayz mod are not the best, they at least don't prevent you from reacting to situations.
This game is a bad joke in the moment and one of the worst games of bohemia interactive i have played so far, that including early days arma 2(wich was just bad and filled with problems/bugs) and arma 3(wich shows a lot similarities to dayz standalone in terms of optimizing).
EDIT:
To all the people stating this game in its current state is a good game:
EDIT 18. of March 2016:
So, i came back after several months not playing the game at all.
Me and a friend decided to give the game another chance to see if the recent patches and the new renderer had done at least something to the performance.
My first spawn was at Solnichny, where i was greeted with a blasting 26FPS on medium/low graphic settings.
After setting everything to low and changing "graphic memory" from auto to 2048mb i got around 28-30 FPS stable in Solnichny.
So far the usual i guess.
I anyway started to pick up some houses, looking for loot and started gearing up a bit.
After around 10 minutes, i started to notice that there where no zombies at all and wondered if that may have been a glitch or a server hiccup or anything so i asked my friend, which had spawned in Kamyshovo if he had seen any zombies.
None on his part either.
We deciced to meet up and have a look at the map and the loot spawning on our way and perhaps maybe find some zombies.
As soon as my friend reached the outskirts of Cherno, his FPS dropped to 16-20 but he found some zombies(yay) but further FPS drops in the city made it impossible for him to properly fight and after a couple of minutes, he died due to him fighting not only the zombies but the FPS which had gone down to 10-15 in the inner parts of the city(he played on the lowest settings).
As soon as i reached Elektro, my FPS dropped down to 20-24 as well and that was the point where we decided to stop our little experiment, since we anyway didn't know what to do in a zombie apocalypse game with no zombies on a server where PvP wasn't wanted and two other people on it.
So yeah, this game just got worse performance wise.
I went from usually 30-36 FPS on this system:
R7 260 2048MB Graphic
8GB DDR3 1333mhz RAM
AMD Phenom II X4 965 4-Core 3400MHz CPU
to this system now:
R9 390X 8192 MB GDDR5
16GB DDR3 1666mhz RAM
AMD FX-8350 8-Core 4000 MHz CPU
and i still get a worse performance with the current version of the game compared to what i got back with my old system and the old version of the game, despite their new renderer.
Like really, if you still want to buy this game, at least wait until its released, its just not worth the trouble.

I played the dayz mod for 2 years and besides it's problems and glitches(wich it had a few) it was way more fun, stable and balanced then the standalone ever was.
Take the zombies for once: In the mod, they are slow, easy to trick, not as strong and you can break line-of-sight but there are many of them in exchange of that.
In the standalone, they are fast as hell, will find your exact position 5-10 minutes after a shot even if you moved 1km, you can't really break line-of-sight and they hit you through walls/from meters away so hard that you will die after a few hits.
The performance is ridicoulusly bad, even if your hardware exceeds the recommended specifications, wich is a joke since the required specs stated by the devs are basically a lie.
This either leads to the conclusion that they are willingly tricking potential buyers or they just have no idea how their game performs on an average hardware setting.
The character movement and animations feel clunky and odd at best, often leading to animations blocking other actions and your immediat reaction to a new situation...wich will lead to a quick death eventually.
I never had this problem with the mod, although the animations from arma 2/dayz mod are not the best, they at least don't prevent you from reacting to situations.
This game is a bad joke in the moment and one of the worst games of bohemia interactive i have played so far, that including early days arma 2(wich was just bad and filled with problems/bugs) and arma 3(wich shows a lot similarities to dayz standalone in terms of optimizing).

EDIT 18. of March 2016:
So, i came back after several months not playing the game at all.
Me and a friend decided to give the game another chance to see if the recent patches and the new renderer had done at least something to the performance.
My first spawn was at Solnichny, where i was greeted with a blasting 26FPS on medium/low graphic settings.
After setting everything to low and changing "graphic memory" from auto to 2048mb i got around 28-30 FPS stable in Solnichny.
So far the usual i guess.
I anyway started to pick up some houses, looking for loot and started gearing up a bit.
After around 10 minutes, i started to notice that there where no zombies at all and wondered if that may have been a glitch or a server hiccup or anything so i asked my friend, which had spawned in Kamyshovo if he had seen any zombies.
None on his part either.
We deciced to meet up and have a look at the map and the loot spawning on our way and perhaps maybe find some zombies.
As soon as my friend reached the outskirts of Cherno, his FPS dropped to 16-20 but he found some zombies(yay) but further FPS drops in the city made it impossible for him to properly fight and after a couple of minutes, he died due to him fighting not only the zombies but the FPS which had gone down to 10-15 in the inner parts of the city(he played on the lowest settings).
As soon as i reached Elektro, my FPS dropped down to 20-24 as well and that was the point where we decided to stop our little experiment, since we anyway didn't know what to do in a zombie apocalypse game with no zombies on a server where PvP wasn't wanted and two other people on it.
So yeah, this game just got worse performance wise.
I went from usually 30-36 FPS on this system:
R7 260 2048MB Graphic
8GB DDR3 1333mhz RAM
AMD Phenom II X4 965 4-Core 3400MHz CPU
to this system now:
R9 390X 8192 MB GDDR5
16GB DDR3 1666mhz RAM
AMD FX-8350 8-Core 4000 MHz CPU
and i still get a worse performance with the current version of the game compared to what i got back with my old system and the old version of the game, despite their new renderer.
Like really, if you still want to buy this game, at least wait until its released, its just not worth the trouble.

DayZ Standalone started production in somewhere around late 2012 I believe. I bring this point up because the game has made painfully slow progress to move forward since its start. The slow progress made by the development team and numerous glitches have been the bane of every player since the game released in Alpha.
Please keep in mind that the game IS indeed in the infant stage of production, despite the time and effort that has been put into it. Anyone curious to play DayZ SA should be aware that the game is buggy and will continue to have problems as production moves forward.
Now, lets talk about the game itself
The game places you in a sandbox style map of what I believe to be a post apocalyptic Russian territory called "Chernarus", and you simply have to survive. Now, that being said, the game is at times fun and at times incredibly frustrating.
Upon makign a character, your "survivor" spawns with nothing but a flashlight and a battery. From that moment on, your experience is what you make it. Will you search nearby buildings for potential supplies? or do you head into the hills to avoid human and zombie contact? Either way, dont get to attached to any gear that you do happen to find. The game has what is known as "perma-death". Thats right gents, upon death, that childs backpack and can of beans you worked so hard for are gone forever. Some people do not enjoy the idea of losing all the gear they have worked so hard for, but thats what puts your heart through the roof at times. The adrenaline and dread that washes over you as a round splits the air by your head, the absolute joy of finding water while suffering from dehydration. The possibility of losing everything and hours of work will certainly keep you on your toes.
Speaking of gear, have you seen people play this game yet? Clown masks, aviator sunglasses, track suit pants, and cowboy hats... I have been held up at gunpoint by a girl in her underwear. The development team is always adding some new item of clothing, which adds a great deal of creativity when your walking around.
The biggest downfall for this game right now is, its infested with terrible people. I dont know what it is about this game that attracts the absolute WORST players. Most people will simply shoot you on sight, but whats that you say? "But I only have my starting clothes and a pitchfork" doesnt matter. If your not shot on sight, your marched away like some prisoner of war, usually to fight someone to the death or so someones girlfriend can kill you.
Not everyone you meet is going to try and rob you of your soul though. Every now and then, you run into the "Heroes of Chernarus". Players that have dedicated their hard earned time and items to saving every poor soul they meet. They dont wear capes or have a Bat signal, but when your lost and starving, having someone give you food and show you to a nearby town makes them someone your would die for... and to be honest, you just might.
Lets wrap this up, shall we
PRO's:
-the game is gritty looking and gives off a good "apocalypse" feeling
-easy to use inventroy/crafting system
-controls are simple enough that most players will find them familiar and friendly
-limitless exploring gives you the potential to go anywhere and do nearly anything
-perma death mechanic will cause your heart to race at times
CON's:
-game has constant bugs/glitches (remember, its an early access Alpha)
-playing with friends can be frustrating, the game currently has no group/party system
-players new to the game will need to read wiki's or play with a friend that can teach them the ropes

At the end of October my father passed away unexpectedly. .He and I had always been really close and I had learned of his death in a very traumatic fashion. Needless to say I was pretty messed up about it. Two days later, after mentioning to my best friend in passing that I wanted to play this game, I got a email notification. Said friend gifted me with a copy along with a note that simply read "Here, a distraction".
From the moment I booted up the game for the first time I was set on my first playthrough being one where no one died. At least in this game I could save everyone.
I'm not going to lie, it was hard. Incredibly hard. I have the coordination of a drunk moose and have never played a bullet hell game in my life. I died... a lot. But I kept playing. I was filled with determination. Eventually, I was able to get the pacifist ending and immediatly cried like a big baby.
Long and short of it? This game helped me heal. Being able to actively save and befriend all of these amazingly written characters... it was wonderful. At a time where my life felt like it had been yanked completely out from under me I had this amazing game that allowed me to feel control, and like I mattered.
10/10 Will replay many, many, more times

Undertale is a throwback to the simpler days of RPGs/JRPGs towards the SNES/NES era that seems to be inspired by series like Mother/Earthbound, Final Fantasy, among other 8/16-bit titles. What Undertale does well is it's homage to old-school videogaming, innovative story telling with an emphasis on morals along with decision-making, an amazing OST, and refreshing gameplay mechanics for RPG fans. I think if you're someone that enjoys unique storytelling, and just RPGs in general then this is a game you must give a go. However if you're a gamer that heavily relies on the latest 3D visuals, and enjoy games primarily games in the action genre, then this may not be your cup of tea (Don't get upset at purchasing a game that's not inside your niche of gaming genres and not enjoy it). Although I really think Undertale at it's core in it's silly, heart-wrenching, and joyful moments has something for everyone. I know there's a lot of hype behind the game, but it deserves it's praise in a time where the gaming market in my opinion is heavily saturated in 3D open-world action oriented games or FPS games (Could be good or bad depending on your gaming genre preferences but I digress). Anyways overall this game is worth a playthrough if not twice give it a go! And support Toby Fox for making such an amazing gem of a game.

DayZ Standalone started production in somewhere around late 2012 I believe. I bring this point up because the game has made painfully slow progress to move forward since its start. The slow progress made by the development team and numerous glitches have been the bane of every player since the game released in Alpha.
Please keep in mind that the game IS indeed in the infant stage of production, despite the time and effort that has been put into it. Anyone curious to play DayZ SA should be aware that the game is buggy and will continue to have problems as production moves forward.
Now, lets talk about the game itself
The game places you in a sandbox style map of what I believe to be a post apocalyptic Russian territory called "Chernarus", and you simply have to survive. Now, that being said, the game is at times fun and at times incredibly frustrating.
Upon makign a character, your "survivor" spawns with nothing but a flashlight and a battery. From that moment on, your experience is what you make it. Will you search nearby buildings for potential supplies? or do you head into the hills to avoid human and zombie contact? Either way, dont get to attached to any gear that you do happen to find. The game has what is known as "perma-death". Thats right gents, upon death, that childs backpack and can of beans you worked so hard for are gone forever. Some people do not enjoy the idea of losing all the gear they have worked so hard for, but thats what puts your heart through the roof at times. The adrenaline and dread that washes over you as a round splits the air by your head, the absolute joy of finding water while suffering from dehydration. The possibility of losing everything and hours of work will certainly keep you on your toes.
Speaking of gear, have you seen people play this game yet? Clown masks, aviator sunglasses, track suit pants, and cowboy hats... I have been held up at gunpoint by a girl in her underwear. The development team is always adding some new item of clothing, which adds a great deal of creativity when your walking around.
The biggest downfall for this game right now is, its infested with terrible people. I dont know what it is about this game that attracts the absolute WORST players. Most people will simply shoot you on sight, but whats that you say? "But I only have my starting clothes and a pitchfork" doesnt matter. If your not shot on sight, your marched away like some prisoner of war, usually to fight someone to the death or so someones girlfriend can kill you.
Not everyone you meet is going to try and rob you of your soul though. Every now and then, you run into the "Heroes of Chernarus". Players that have dedicated their hard earned time and items to saving every poor soul they meet. They dont wear capes or have a Bat signal, but when your lost and starving, having someone give you food and show you to a nearby town makes them someone your would die for... and to be honest, you just might.
Lets wrap this up, shall we
PRO's:
-the game is gritty looking and gives off a good "apocalypse" feeling
-easy to use inventroy/crafting system
-controls are simple enough that most players will find them familiar and friendly
-limitless exploring gives you the potential to go anywhere and do nearly anything
-perma death mechanic will cause your heart to race at times
CON's:
-game has constant bugs/glitches (remember, its an early access Alpha)
-playing with friends can be frustrating, the game currently has no group/party system
-players new to the game will need to read wiki's or play with a friend that can teach them the ropes

Undertale isn't your average RPG/Bullet Hell Shooter.
First off the main thing people notice is the 8 bit style which has an appeal to many folks like with Shovel Knight, Cave Story, etc. It also proves that a great game does not have to have amazing graphics etc as it has to rely on core game mechanics to impress the player which it does amazingly.
Second, the story is like an old 8bit game so don't expect something like Bioshock infinite, it's more widdled down like a Zelda game but still has a great twist at the end so yeah.
Third, the gameplay is what most people base a game's "Fun Factor" on and Undertale does not disappoint. It's starts like an average RPG but there's 2 phases to a battle in which your phase is to either FIGHT with a timely button pressing minigame or ACT and talk your way out of the battle. When the enemy attacks is when it gets fun because you are usually in a box as a heart dodging everything with tons of other features to liven things up such as using the enemy's attack against them or not moving to avoid taking damage. It sounds simple but aren't all the best games that way?
The rest of the game is just exploring and making choices like any other RPG and trying to progress towards an ultimate goal of leaving the underground monster infested world. Plenty of side quest like things you just have to look which rewards the patient gamer but doesn't detract from the gameplay value if you like to rush things.
Fourth, the atmosphere which incorporates the Music, tone, and mood is great as it is a rather odd mixture of Comedy, Puzzle solving, and the ocassional WTF? moment thrown in for good measure. There's a point where your game might crash and I suggest booting it back up but don't try messing with the game files or else you get a special ending which isn't so great.
The final thing that I'd like to add is what makes this game so different from everything else.
That part is: You can complete the game, without killing anything.
That's rare in a game as almost everything from GTA:V to Mario has you perform some act of beridding your enemy in a way that relates to death and is a nice change of pace since the last RPG I played that gave you the choice of not killing anything was.....wait no I don't remember an RPG like that, I rest my case.
For the quality of this game and all the replay value it's definitely worth the price of $10 at release unlike all these buggy AAA titles with game breaking glitches priced at $60.
Definitely one of my all time favorites.

Pros:  -Amazing co-op and group play, PvP included.
- Very immersive features.  You really feel like you have to survive.
- Weekly Devblog that's both informative and fun to read.  Seriously, check it out!  That's what won me over.
- Updates are fairly large, especially given most early access games.
- It's pretty.
- If there is something that needs work or tweaking, the dev team is probably already on it.
- Very good "sandbox" for all sorts of imaginative creations.
Cons: -Bloom is not toggleable (for a good reason), but there is WAY too much of it.  Deserts look like tundra because it is so bright.
- It isn't done yet, and it shows.  Most of the cons are because of this.
- Frame rate is very jumpy, even on Gtx760 and i5-4670k, because it isn't done yet.
- Some features just feel empty, because it isn't done yet.
- The "survival" mechanics could use some work, not building and living in a home mechanics but actually living in the wild mechanics.  And again, it isn't done yet.
Rust is probably the safest Early Access game to buy, it has a great Dev team who is always working on anything that needs to be fixed, balanced, added, or scrapped.  It's fairly cheap at 20 dollars and offers a lot of playtime (especially with friends, I highly recommend friends if you haven't got any).
Usually Early Access gives me buyers remorse after a month or so, but not Rust.  Reading those weekly updates and experiencing them and all the changes is fun, it feels like a new game every month.   Don't like the game right now?  Just wait a month!

I know I only have 84 hours in game, but I don't idle like a lot of the other players, so it's still reasonable. Either way, Rust has been amazing to me, and more frequently than not, I find you want to build a small base and lay low. The game is actually impossible until you can find a keypad blueprint though. Someone will sit outside your house day and night waiting for you to either leave or come back so they can take your keys and raid everything. It doesn't matter how well-armored you are, if you don't have the blueprint, it's awful. it took me about 45ish hours in before I finally got one. Most servers start you off with it now but be aware that, to start, you have to get blueprints.
This game revolves around the collection of blueprints as they are the only thing that persists through death. Once you get a few, though, you can really get the ball rolling with collecting more things. You can find them via barrels or by researching one that you found (although at best that has a 33% yield). Finally, if you transfer servers, you will lose all of your blueprints, so make sure that after you get raided (and you will) to stay on the same server.
I find it odd that very few of the reviews mention this very crucial aspect to the game.
My only other issue with the game is just how few official servers there are because on a normal day, you'll find that most of them are full at 100/100 or 250/250.
All of that out of the way, Rust is an amazing game, and the sheer fact that it pits man against man in this epic tale of human corruption in order to satisfy the need for goods really helps illustrate the dynamic of culture. If you play this game for long enough, you'll really begin to understand, in a better way than Lord of the Flies could possibly illustrate, just exactly the true nature of man. Some people will be willing to help you, some will actively♥♥♥♥♥♥on your body just to watch the world burn.
You'll learn to trust no one. For example, one time I had a man offer me a free house, keypads and all, because it was a second house of his (most likely, one he raided and then changed the locks on) and allowed newbies to stay in free-of-charge. All of this, he told me to do, however, because he was holding an AK-47 to my head and told me that if I run away, he will shoot me. Knowing full well that he would take my valuables the second I logged off, I ran as soon as I had the chance.
Finally, the most important piece of advice: When you play with friends, you don't have to find each other like in DayZ. One of you needs to make a sleeping bag and place it in the name of the other person, and then they need to kill themselves. It makes everything much easier.
Overall, though, can't recommend this game enough.The more you play, the faster you can play. It has a slow start but with friends, or alone, the game is amazing.

Also the fact that it's still in early access means that the developers update the game regularly adding new things such as colour rending, new weapons, new animations, so you get to watch the game improve and develop as you play, which is pretty cool. Also there are monthly server wipes on official servers which sounds annoying? But actually it isn't because nobody gets too overpowered and it keeps the game fresh. I have no clue how one guy, with such a small team, could create a game that feels so ALIVE! The characters are likable and unique, and depending on your choices, they will change along with your choices, you shape what they become, and some characters are VERY interesting, with theories about their backstories and origins. The story, even if it may seem simple at the beggining, it gets so much more interesting and complex as you play, you discover the truth in the world of Undertale and what has happened before your arrival... and how what you are doing now relates to it all in the bigger picture. The music... god, every song gets better and better as you progress, and each theme for each character fits perfectly, and they all have such awesome melodies, basically this game has the best soundtrack ive ever heard in a video game.
This is the first game ive ever played that has delivered such an emotional impact to me, in any game ever. Overall, Undertale is an amazing game!

I don't say this lightly, because there are a LOT of games out there-- many of which have affected me deeply and stuck with me for my whole life-- but Undertale is one of the best games I've ever played. The reasons why are kind of... complicated.
I mean, sure, it's charming, it's adorable, it has an amazing soundtrack and a WICKED sense of humor, but that's not really the reason.
This is the kind of game where you CANNOT go in expecting an experience like something else you've played. People compare it to a lot of things, but Undertale is its own kind of beast.
It's not something meant to be enjoyed passively-- if you want tune into a game and turn your brain off for a while, this game probably isn't for you. Undertale asks a lot out of you. It asks you to think about why you do what you do. It asks you to make decisions about how you play-- whether to kill or not to kill-- and it never lets you act like you didn't have a choice. It not only asks you to make that decision, but it TESTS your commitment to that decision. It asks you to CARE.
It will NOT do these things FOR you.
But the more you care, the more you approach your decisions like they actually matter, the more the game will reward you. I think this is what resonated with me about Undertale.
It's not all sweetness and light, but it's still one of the most unabashedly optimistic stories I have EVER seen. It's not a game where you have to be kind or good to get to the end; it's a game where you do those things because you WANT to. And that was SUCH a breath of fresh air. But you get out of it what you put into it.
So stay determined.

I have never had feelings during a game this hard in a very very long time. It's fairly easy to see an RPG maker esque game on your top recommended games on steam and say "Wow, that looks like crap" or "Oh my god, Tumblr will not shut the ♥♥♥♥ up about this game." Every descision that you make matters whether you defend yourself against the inhabitants of the underground and end their lives or if you choose to understand them and become a companion with unyielding comradery.
The battle system is turn based but is in no means a slow paced grind fest. On the player's turn, they have four options"
- Fight: Timing Based combat where you have to hit the action button when indicators line up with the center for maximum damage. This will KILL a citizen of the underground.
-Act: You fidget and figure out how to convince a monster to stop fighting. Encourage, pick on, tell funny joke, flex, tell terrible joke, are examples. This ends your turn.
-Item: You have items that buff you, debuff monsters, and restore your health. This also ends your turn.
-Mercy: The main gimmick of the battle system. Once you have whittled down the monster's heath (Please do not kill goat Mom)  or convinced them to not fight anymore, their names will appear yellow. You may then use 'spare' to end the engagment, earning you cash to spend at the BAKE SALE!!
- On the Monster's turn: Your soul appears in a box of varying sizes and monsters send oodles of crap at you ranging from flexing biceps to vegitables. You then have to SIMPLY dodge whatever they throw at you. I'll let you figure out the rest.
More or less, there are dogs, puzzles, minor dating sims, dogs and lots of interesting and very funny dialogue depending on what and how you deal with the people living in this world. It can go from funny and cute straight into sad and creepy as every boss character will leave some sort of impression on your soul.
Throughout my 6 hour playthrough I have experienced laughter, frustration, and ate the largest ♥♥♥♥ing bowl of honey nut feelios. Tumblr Flavor of the week "OFF" left a bad taste in my mouth, but this one...Undertale has dragged me in, comforted me, humored me, THEN CHEWED ME UP AND SPAT ME OUT. That only left me comming back for more.

6 MONTHS LATER: Still crap.
2017 Edit: So here's my new honest review.
Firstly I would like to congratulate the development team at Bohemia for fixing a lot of the bugs within the game, I am fairly disappointing it took so long but after Bryan came down to Melbourne Pax and told us why, I can understand it.
D-sync is significantly less, zombies rarely walk through walls, and the engine has been updated (gettings over 100 fps at Ultra with a GTX 1070 now). On top of this lag spikes are rarely seen as well.
Now here's my problem and I'll be as blunt as possible so readers don't read a rambling on review.
The development team's priorities are unforgivable. I can forgive a game taking over three years of development, which can actually be seen as reasonable for some games (mainly A grade games). However, they have spent the last few years focusing their development on areas that the community didn't need, things that rarely add any value to the game. I'm assume this was because the bigger areas to improve on in this game are taking quite a while and they've been adding these little 'features' to keep players interested. Unfortunately this attempt has failed, and the population in Australia for DayZ has dropped by, I'm assuming, over 50% in Australia.
My second issue is,
DayZ has some of the most passionate players I have ever seen for a game, real commitment to it. They are excited when a new awesome patch comes out, they follow the game religiously, and of course when they feel the game isn't heading the right direction they get frustrated. Unfortunely, for those that have a platform to shout their opinion (youtube), the development team has found it fitting to block these 'players' that are driving people to play DayZ from their game and their social media platform.
I can understand that developers can feel un-motivated when people shame their efforts, but this 'work' field is no different then others, and you still should be expected to retaliate well accordingly.
I think it's unreasonable, if you aren't prioritising features that should be prioritised in a game, to expect players to agree, then to retaliate poorly when those players that people watch on a platform such as youtube, voice their opinions.
So unfortunely, I still can not recommend this game and I don't see it improving either. Between a lack of community, a poor attitude and priorities from the development team, and too much time 'wasting' player's time, I'll be looking out to DayZ's successors.
2016 Review -
Welcome to DayZ!
Where Kill on Sight is more common than actual player interaction and the term "bandit" means a person who does so.
Where zombies walk through walls and on occasion are blessed with an invisible cloak.
Where "wizards" are practically more common than heros, and fairies run free taking your supplies when you drop them in buildings.
DayZ has a many bunch of problems they need to address. Along those already mentioned we have a overwhelming issue where the engine just sucks, making anyone who doesn't run a god computer not able to enjoy the experience, or at least not on anything but low settings.
Topped with d-sync that I've never seen so bad, and lag spikes every 10 minutes, a lot of time you'll want to throw your mouse at your computer & that's not even half of the bugs.
However! DayZ always seems to make me want to come back. I've come to enjoy running through fields with the sun on my back, feeling more like I'm hiking in Russia than staring at a computer screen.
I've come to love those heart-pumping gun-fights with friends, frantically trying to get laggy shots on the enemy.
And hey! sometimes the bugs you encounter can be funny, like how I was un-able to move my truck that had become wedged on a small stone.
And on that rare occasion you do meet someone who's more interested in player interaction, the journey you go on and the things you accomplish is quite amazing! So props to Bohemia for that.
Unfortunately I can't give this game my blessing just yet.
It's been in alpha for a year, which isn't a long time, but I honestly expected more to be accomplished in the way of mechanics by the start of 2015. Some of the features that have been added are amazing and make that survival experience better, but as a regular player of the game, I feel as though they haven't prioritised well enough.
Truthfully, I play this game for those small experiences that you get out of it, but it hasn't been worth all the fuss just yet.
Instead I hold onto my hopes for the game in the near future, pushing past the bugs and bad engine in order to continue watching it grow.
For now, I can't recommend DayZ and I really wish they thought through the mechanics and gameplay a bit better earlier back, however maybe in the future near or far I'll be able to give it my blessing.
-GunnyG.

This review is coming from a year's worth of playing, rather than a first glance so I can narrow down recurring problems. Yes I know it's still technically listed as  "Early Alpha", but honestly I expected the devs to get A LOT more done in a year than what they have. I will credit them with fixing the zombs phasing through walls, add new weapons and balancing weapon spawns but there's no sign of other additions that were announced and there are still outside issues, regarding the server system. For example, we're all familiar with the counter-measure against server hopping. Hop servers too soon, face a 60 second wait penalty before entering the next server. However, their prerequisite for server hopping is a bit broad. Failed server connections, server admin kicks (simply for joining a server regardless of being "public"), and immediate server restarts get counted so the next server brings forth that time penalty. Well, at the end of that penalty, there's still no joining as it remains stuck on the "Please Wait" screen (an issue that should come before added content, I must say). The only remedy for this is to exit and restart the game which takes a LONG time. In that timeframe I could've played a round on an FPS. The game is good with little complaints, once I can join a server that is,  so with the degree and recurrence of the server issue it's just not worth it right now. The game could be great and my review may change later on, but right now just hold your $35 until they fix it

This review was a joke review, I'll try to do my best to make it an actual review.
First off, Rust is a survival game you have to invest time into, my review will be broken into 3 sections, Survival, Crafting/Building and the PvP.
Survival:
The survival aspect of Rust is what makes it challenging, the Hunger and Thirst can get you when you least expect it to.
The godly animals that can warp from the ground to a rock they are standing next to are hard to hunt but yield good rewards.
Each tool you use in order to gather resources is different, PickAxes are used to break down Nodes you find around Rock clusters to gain Stone, Metal, Sulfur and High Quality metal ores.
Hatchets are used to gather Wood.
The best way to gather leather and animal fat in this game is with bone knives.
If you use a wrong tool(for example, hatchet on a node) your aim will shift up by a considerable amount.
Crafting/Building:
The Crafting and Building part of this game is what requires you to invest time into the game.
Crafting takes time unlike other games, and the materials required for certain weapons and armour are hard to find.
The buildings you make are always vulnerable, They can either  be taken down with C4 or Rockets.
There are a variety of building parts to choose from that may or may not make your building more resistant to explosives or gunfire.
The best part about building in Rust is the Stability system.
Stability ranges from 0% to 100%, 100% being the most stable.
PvP:
The PvP aspect of this game makes it all the more thrilling.
There are a variety of weapons to choose from, from Clubs made from broken Femurs to modern day Light Machine Guns.
I won't go into depth with all of these weapons.
You know how Counter Strike has Recoil patterns? Rust has them too but the Horizontal recoil(The one that goes left and right) is completely RnG. There is a bit of luck to controlling your
Recoil in this game.
The hunting bow is probably the hardest ranged weapon to master in this game, it shoots slow moving projectiles but is highly rewarding when you hear that headshot hitsound. Best of all, it is a default weapon, you don't need to learn it to craft it.
The Crossbow is a non-default weapon, which means you have to find it from blueprint pages or barrels scattered accross roads and monuments. It is way better than the hunting bow, since it fires the arrows faster and has more base damage.
Over all this game gets a 7/10 for me, there are some optimization issues but anyone with a computer made within 5 years can run this game at atleast 30 fps.

6 MONTHS LATER: Still crap.
2017 Edit: So here's my new honest review.
Firstly I would like to congratulate the development team at Bohemia for fixing a lot of the bugs within the game, I am fairly disappointing it took so long but after Bryan came down to Melbourne Pax and told us why, I can understand it.
D-sync is significantly less, zombies rarely walk through walls, and the engine has been updated (gettings over 100 fps at Ultra with a GTX 1070 now). On top of this lag spikes are rarely seen as well.
Now here's my problem and I'll be as blunt as possible so readers don't read a rambling on review.
The development team's priorities are unforgivable. I can forgive a game taking over three years of development, which can actually be seen as reasonable for some games (mainly A grade games). However, they have spent the last few years focusing their development on areas that the community didn't need, things that rarely add any value to the game. I'm assume this was because the bigger areas to improve on in this game are taking quite a while and they've been adding these little 'features' to keep players interested. Unfortunately this attempt has failed, and the population in Australia for DayZ has dropped by, I'm assuming, over 50% in Australia.
My second issue is,
DayZ has some of the most passionate players I have ever seen for a game, real commitment to it. They are excited when a new awesome patch comes out, they follow the game religiously, and of course when they feel the game isn't heading the right direction they get frustrated. Unfortunely, for those that have a platform to shout their opinion (youtube), the development team has found it fitting to block these 'players' that are driving people to play DayZ from their game and their social media platform.
I can understand that developers can feel un-motivated when people shame their efforts, but this 'work' field is no different then others, and you still should be expected to retaliate well accordingly.
I think it's unreasonable, if you aren't prioritising features that should be prioritised in a game, to expect players to agree, then to retaliate poorly when those players that people watch on a platform such as youtube, voice their opinions.
So unfortunely, I still can not recommend this game and I don't see it improving either. Between a lack of community, a poor attitude and priorities from the development team, and too much time 'wasting' player's time, I'll be looking out to DayZ's successors.

Welcome to DayZ!
Where Kill on Sight is more common than actual player interaction and the term "bandit" means a person who does so.
Where zombies walk through walls and on occasion are blessed with an invisible cloak.
Where "wizards" are practically more common than heros, and fairies run free taking your supplies when you drop them in buildings.
DayZ has a many bunch of problems they need to address. Along those already mentioned we have a overwhelming issue where the engine just sucks, making anyone who doesn't run a god computer not able to enjoy the experience, or at least not on anything but low settings.
Topped with d-sync that I've never seen so bad, and lag spikes every 10 minutes, a lot of time you'll want to throw your mouse at your computer & that's not even half of the bugs.
However! DayZ always seems to make me want to come back. I've come to enjoy running through fields with the sun on my back, feeling more like I'm hiking in Russia than staring at a computer screen.
I've come to love those heart-pumping gun-fights with friends, frantically trying to get laggy shots on the enemy.
And hey! sometimes the bugs you encounter can be funny, like how I was un-able to move my truck that had become wedged on a small stone.
And on that rare occasion you do meet someone who's more interested in player interaction, the journey you go on and the things you accomplish is quite amazing! So props to Bohemia for that.
Unfortunately I can't give this game my blessing just yet.
It's been in alpha for a year, which isn't a long time, but I honestly expected more to be accomplished in the way of mechanics by the start of 2015. Some of the features that have been added are amazing and make that survival experience better, but as a regular player of the game, I feel as though they haven't prioritised well enough.
Truthfully, I play this game for those small experiences that you get out of it, but it hasn't been worth all the fuss just yet.
Instead I hold onto my hopes for the game in the near future, pushing past the bugs and bad engine in order to continue watching it grow.
For now, I can't recommend DayZ and I really wish they thought through the mechanics and gameplay a bit better earlier back, however maybe in the future near or far I'll be able to give it my blessing.
